Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|0.source_text: Pattern box: (noun) ini / itu (adjective). / (noun) ini tidak (adjective).

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|1.source_text: 1. A: Teh ini manis atau pahit? B: Manis.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|2.source_text: 2. A: Kopi ini pahit? B: Ya, pahit. Saya mahu gula.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|3.source_text: 3. A: Cili itu merah atau hijau? B: Cili itu hijau.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|4.source_text: 4. A: Bungkusan ini berat? B: Tidak, bungkusan ini ringan.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|5.source_text: 5. A: Pejabat encik besar? B: Tidak, pejabat saya sempit.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|6.source_text: Explanation: An adjective follows the noun and stands alone as the description: there is no word for "is". To say "not", put tidak in front of the adjective (tidak manis). bukan is for nouns (Ini bukan teh.). The adjective never changes.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|7.source_text: 説明：形容詞は名詞のあとに置き、そのまま述語になります。「〜は」にあたる語は要りません。否定は形容詞の前に tidak を置きます（tidak manis）。bukan は名詞用です（Ini bukan teh.）。形容詞の形は変わりません。

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|8.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese i-adjectives and na-adjectives change form (辛い / 辛くない / 静かな); Malay has no such groups. pedas stays pedas; only tidak is added.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|9.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語のイ形容詞・ナ形容詞は形が変わります（辛い／辛くない／静かな）が、マレー語にはその区別がありません。pedas は pedas のままで、tidak を足すだけです。

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|11.source_text: Pattern box: Bagaimana rasa ___ ? / ___ , tetapi ___ . (spoken: Macam mana, tapi)

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|12.source_text: 1. A: Bagaimana rasa mi goreng ini? B: Sedap, tetapi pedas.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|13.source_text: 2. A: Bagaimana rasa teh ini? B: Manis, tetapi sedap.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|14.source_text: 3. A: Bagaimana rasa mangga ini? B: Masam, tetapi segar.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|15.source_text: 4. A: Bagaimana rasa kopi ini? B: Pahit. Saya mahu gula.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|16.source_text: 5. A: Macam mana? Sedap? (spoken) B: Sedap! Tetapi pedas sedikit.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|17.source_text: Explanation: Bagaimana rasa …? asks how something tastes. Answer with an adjective. tetapi joins two ideas that pull against each other; the second one is what you want to stress. sedikit after an adjective softens it: pedas sedikit. In speech, macam mana replaces bagaimana and tapi replaces tetapi.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|18.source_text: 説明：Bagaimana rasa …? は味をたずねる表現で、形容詞で答えます。tetapi は反対の内容をつなぎ、あとに来る方が言いたいことです。形容詞のあとに sedikit を付けると和らぎます：pedas sedikit。話し言葉では bagaimana の代わりに macam mana、tetapi の代わりに tapi を使います。

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|0.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese puts the contrast on the first clause (辛いけどおいしい). Malay puts tetapi between the two: Pedas, tetapi sedap. Hear the order: the last idea wins.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|1.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語は前の節に「けど」を付けます（辛いけどおいしい）。マレー語は二つの間に tetapi を置きます：Pedas, tetapi sedap. 最後に言う方が主役です。

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|3.source_text: Pattern box: Saya mahu ___ yang ___ . / ___ atau ___ ? (spoken: nak)

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|4.source_text: 1. A: Encik mahu payung yang biru atau yang hitam? B: Saya mahu yang hitam.
target_spans: Encik mahu payung yang biru atau yang hitam?

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|5.source_text: 2. A: Puan mahu fail yang merah atau yang hijau? B: Yang hijau, ya.
target_spans: Puan mahu fail yang merah atau yang hijau?

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|6.source_text: 3. A: Encik mahu buku yang tebal atau yang nipis? B: Yang nipis.
target_spans: Encik mahu buku yang tebal atau yang nipis?

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|7.source_text: 4. A: Awak mahu mangga yang besar atau yang kecil? B: Yang besar. Berapa harga?
target_spans: Awak mahu mangga yang besar atau yang kecil?

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|8.source_text: 5. A: Panas atau sejuk? B: Sejuk.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|9.source_text: Explanation: yang means "the one that is": yang biru is the blue one. Once everyone knows the noun you can drop it: Saya mahu yang hitam. atau offers a choice. mahu is "want"; in speech you will hear nak.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|10.source_text: 説明：yang は「〜なもの」。yang biru は青いものです。相手が名詞を分かっていれば省けます：Saya mahu yang hitam. atau は選択肢を出します。mahu は「欲しい・〜したい」で、話し言葉では nak も聞きます。

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|11.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: yang biru works like the 青いの in 青いのをください: it points at one thing among several. For a plain description the bare adjective is enough (payung biru).

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|12.source_text: 日本語との比較：yang biru は「青いのをください」の「青いの」に近く、いくつかの中から一つを指します。ただ描写するだけなら形容詞だけで十分です（payung biru）。

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|14.source_text: Pattern box: Saya rasa ___ . / Kenapa (= mengapa, apa sebab) ___ ? Sebab (or kerana) ___ .

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|15.source_text: 1. A: Encik rasa bagaimana hari ini? B: Saya rasa penat.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|16.source_text: 2. A: Kenapa encik penat? B: Sebab semalam saya tidur lewat.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|17.source_text: 3. A: Kenapa awak tidak makan? B: Sebab saya belum lapar.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|18.source_text: 4. A: Apa sebab bos marah? B: Sebab saya lambat.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|19.source_text: 5. A: Kenapa encik gembira? B: Sebab hari ini hari cuti.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|20.source_text: 6. A: Mengapa awak lambat? B: Kerana hujan.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|0.source_text: Explanation: rasa before an adjective means "feel": Saya rasa penat. Kenapa, mengapa and apa sebab all ask "why" and are interchangeable: kenapa is the everyday one. Answer with sebab or kerana, mainly; the reason follows the word.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|1.source_text: 説明：形容詞の前の rasa は「感じる」：Saya rasa penat. Kenapa・mengapa・apa sebab はどれも「なぜ」で、言い換えられます（日常でよく使うのは kenapa）。答えは主に sebab か kerana で、理由はそのあとに続きます。

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|2.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese puts the reason first and から after it (疲れたから). Malay does the reverse: Sebab (or kerana) comes first and the reason follows. kenapa ≈ どうして・なぜ; mengapa and apa sebab say the same thing.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|3.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語は理由を先に言い、あとに「から」を付けます（疲れたから）。マレー語は逆で、Sebab（または kerana）が先に来て理由があとに続きます。kenapa ≈ どうして・なぜで、mengapa と apa sebab も同じ意味です。

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|5.source_text: Pattern box: Saya mahu ___ , kurang manis, ais sedikit. / Panas atau sejuk?

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|6.source_text: 1. A: Encik mahu minum apa? B: Saya mahu teh tarik, kurang manis.
target_spans: Saya mahu teh tarik, kurang manis.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|7.source_text: 2. A: Panas atau sejuk? B: Sejuk. Ais sedikit.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|8.source_text: 3. A: Makan sini atau tapau? B: Makan sini.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|9.source_text: 4. A: Mi goreng ini pedas? B: Pedas sedikit, tetapi sedap.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|10.source_text: 5. A: Ada apa lagi? B: Air kosong satu, ya.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|11.source_text: 6. A: Roti canai, dengan kuah? B: Ya, kuah banyak.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|12.source_text: Explanation: An order is built in a fixed order: the drink, how sweet it is, hot or cold, and how much ice. kurang manis is a fixed phrase for less sugar; use it only for ordering. air kosong is plain water.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|13.source_text: 説明：注文は決まった順番で組み立てます：飲み物、甘さ、温度（熱い・冷たい）、氷の量。kurang manis は砂糖控えめを頼む決まった言い方で、注文のときだけ使います。air kosong はお水です。

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|14.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: It matches the way you customise a drink in Japan (甘さ控えめ、氷少なめ): same slots, same order. Do not build kurang into other sentences yet; comparing things comes in chapter 6.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|15.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本で飲み物をカスタムする言い方（甘さ控えめ、氷少なめ）と同じ項目・同じ順番です。kurang を他の文に広げるのは待ちましょう。比較は第6章で学びます。

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|0.source_text: Model each A line; learners answer as B, then swap. Explain the rule only after they have used the pattern.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|2.source_text: Pattern 1: if a learner says bukan manis, model tidak manis and ask "Is it a noun or a description?"

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|3.source_text: Pattern 2: macam mana and tapi are spoken forms; accept them in pair work once bagaimana and tetapi have been practised.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|4.source_text: Pattern 4 covers Kata-Kata frames f04 and f06 together (f06 is the Kenapa …? Sebab … frame from the Kata-Kata clean-up), so it is tagged with both; the stage review brings f06 back. Kenapa, mengapa and apa sebab are one question; accept sebab or kerana as the answer.

Unit 5 · Culture and usage note|3|0.source_text: A mamak stall is a casual eatery, traditionally run by Indian-Muslim families and often open late, so it is also where people lepak and sembang after work. Use the word for the stall, not for a person. A drink order is built in a short sequence: the drink, how sweet it is, and hot or cold with a little ice: teh tarik, kurang manis, ais sedikit. The Kata-Kata scene and the ledger add the rest: makan sini or tapau (take away), Kira! for the bill, and roti canai dengan kuah (with gravy).
target_spans: teh tarik, kurang manis, ais sedikit

Unit 5 · Culture and usage note|3|1.source_text: Drink names are short. Kata-Kata notes that teh O is tea without milk, and the ledger lists kopi O as black coffee with sugar, so kurang manis is how you ask for less sugar. Air kosong is plain water; Kata-Kata links kosong to the chapter 3 word for zero and empty.

Unit 5 · Culture and usage note|3|2.source_text: Colour words are easy to meet on the street. The national flag, the Jalur Gemilang, is red, white, blue and yellow: merah, putih, biru and kuning. Pink is merah jambu, literally "jambu-fruit red" (Kata-Kata card ms-c05-025). Yang lets you point at one thing among several: yang merah is "the red one" (card ms-c05-004).

Unit 5 · Culture and usage note|3|3.source_text: Malaysia is hot and humid throughout the year, so panas and sejuk are everyday words for the weather as well as for drinks. At the counter you will often hear nak for mahu (Saya nak teh tarik); Kata-Kata marks nak as spoken (card ms-c05-005).

Unit 5 · Culture and usage note|3|5.source_text: mamak の店は気軽な食堂で、昔からインド系ムスリムの家族が営むことが多く、遅くまで開いていることもあるので、仕事のあとに lepak（ぶらぶらする）や sembang（おしゃべり）をする場所でもあります。この語は店に使い、人には使いません。飲み物の注文は、短い順番で組み立てます：飲み物、甘さ、熱い・冷たい、そして氷を少し：teh tarik, kurang manis, ais sedikit。Kata-Kata の場面と台帳には、ほかに makan sini（店内で食べる）か tapau（持ち帰り）、お会計の Kira!、そして roti canai dengan kuah（カレーなどのたれ付き）があります。
target_spans: teh tarik, kurang manis, ais sedikit

Unit 5 · Culture and usage note|3|6.source_text: 飲み物の名前は短いです。Kata-Kata の注記では teh O はミルクなしの紅茶で、台帳では kopi O が砂糖入りのブラックコーヒーとされているので、砂糖を減らしたいときは kurang manis と言います。Air kosong はお水です。Kata-Kata は kosong を第3章の「ゼロ・空」の語とつなげています。

Unit 5 · Culture and usage note|3|7.source_text: 色の言葉は街でよく目にします。国旗 Jalur Gemilang は赤・白・青・黄色：merah、putih、biru、kuning です。ピンクは merah jambu で、直訳すると「jambu（果物）の赤」です（Kata-Kata カード ms-c05-025）。Yang は複数の中から一つを指します：yang merah は「赤いもの」です（カード ms-c05-004）。

Unit 5 · Culture and usage note|3|8.source_text: マレーシアは一年を通して暑くて湿度が高いので、panas と sejuk は飲み物だけでなく天気の話でも毎日使う言葉です。カウンターでは mahu の代わりに nak をよく聞きます（Saya nak teh tarik）。Kata-Kata は nak を話し言葉としています（カード ms-c05-005）。

Unit 5 · Teaching plan and answer key|3|.source_text: Before Block A: Kata-Kata Sedia Kelas c05 (27 cards, frames ms-c05-f01 and ms-c05-f02).
Before Block E: Kata-Kata Dunia "Masak nasi goreng", "Di klinik", "Gambar bayi" and "Lepak di kedai mamak"; learners only need to recognise the scene words.

After Block D: the Kata-Kata chapter 5 deck with spaced review, frames ms-c05-f01, ms-c05-f02, ms-c05-f03, ms-c05-f04, ms-c05-f05, ms-c05-f06 in the frame drill and Susun Ayat; about 3 hours of self-study for this unit (planning figure).
Hanashishou starts at A2, so there is no Hanashishou scene for this unit. Listening uses the teacher-read script.
■ Block A · Words and patterns (45 min)
Goal: I can describe food, drink, colours, sizes and feelings with an adjective after the noun.
0–5 Recall: chapter 4 (Sudah makan?, the time, a weekly habit) from the opener prompts.
5–10 Tanya Cikgu questions from Kata-Kata.
10–20 Vocabulary focus: core words first; Dunia and revision words are only pointed out.
20–40 Pattern focus: patterns 1 to 5, question and answer first, rule second; teach the six word groups across Blocks A to C (not all in one sitting).
40–45 First substitutions (Drill 2, items 1 to 3).
■ Block B · Drills and conversation (45 min)
Goal: I can ask Bagaimana …? and Kenapa …? and answer with an adjective, tetapi or sebab.
0–5 Recall: colours in the room: Warna apa? round the class.
5–25 Drill ladder in order: pattern table, substitution, transformation, question and answer, question-word choice, short dialogues, then the markers drill.
25–40 Model conversation, gapped form, then the changed-facts variant.
40–45 Pair rehearsal without the script.
■ Block C · Listening and task (45 min)
Goal: I can follow a short talk about a weekend and use a menu to order a drink the way I like it.
0–5 Recall: learners describe one thing they ate this week: taste and temperature.
5–20 Listening: read the questions, two readings, check, then shadow three lines.
20–30 Reading and writing.

Unit 5 · Teaching plan and answer key|4|.source_text: 30–45 Task with role cards; announce the change of plan halfway.
■ Block D · Review and test (45 min)
Goal: I can check adjectives, colours and question words in a short test.
0–15 Mixed review: cumulative question-word drill (chapters 1 to 5, including bagaimana and kenapa), then the markers drill with new cues.
35–45 Preview: chapter 6 Kata-Kata set (comparatives); the writing block for unit 5 comes first if time allows.
Goal: I can recognise words for cooking, the clinic, a baby photo and the mamak in four Kata-Kata Dunia scenes.
0–5 Recall: order a drink: sweetness, hot or cold, ice.
5–15 Kata-Kata Dunia scenes "Masak nasi goreng", "Di klinik", "Gambar bayi" and "Lepak di kedai mamak" as listening (teacher reads, learners point to pictures or words).
30–40 Free variation: the dish is finished, or the friend wants something that is not spicy.
■ What to listen for · 注意点

Load: 63 core words in six groups. Route 1 (whole unit): tastes and the question and linking words in Block A; colours, size and shape in Block B; feelings and states, hot, cold, food and drink in Blocks C and D; Block E recycles all of them in the Dunia scenes. Route 2 (A/B in the pilot): split the same plan into two halves, Blocks A and B on tastes, the question and linking words, hot, cold, food and drink and ordering, then Blocks C and D on colours, size and shape and feelings. Note which route needs fewer repeats. The Dunia words are for recognition only.

Standard first: mahu, tetapi, bagaimana. The spoken forms nak, tapi and macam mana are marked spoken; accept them in pair work once the standard form is on the board. jingga and oren are both correct for orange (Sam, 12 Nov 2026).
tidak negates adjectives and verbs; bukan negates nouns (chapter 3). Ask: "Is it a noun or a description?"
No comparatives or superlatives (chapter 6): do not teach lebih, paling or kurang … daripada. kurang manis is a fixed ordering phrase only.

Unit 5 · Teaching plan and answer key|5|.source_text: rasa is a noun (taste: Bagaimana rasa …?) and a verb (to feel: Saya rasa penat.). Kenapa, mengapa and apa sebab are equivalents (Sam, 12 Nov 2026); answer with sebab or kerana, mainly. Use kenapa in everyday talk and let learners hear mengapa as the same question. tawar is "bland" here; learners met it as "to bargain" in chapter 3. seronok and tawar were recognition words earlier and are core here because the ledger places them in chapter 5.

Clinic scene: symptoms only (demam, batuk, sakit kepala, perut, tekak). Do not teach diagnoses, medicines or doses. hospital is the recognition word for the hospital here and a taught word in chapter 7; the Indonesian-leaning rumah sakit is not taught (Sam, 12 Nov 2026).
No food rules or religious expressions are taught in this unit. Ask Sam before adding any. The culture note says who traditionally runs a mamak stall, as Sam approved on 12 Nov 2026.
Dunia words from the four scenes are for recognition in Block E only.

Unit 5 · Writing block · A short descrip.source_text: Part 1 (15 min): choose a drink, a dish or a place you know. Write four to six sentences: colour, size, taste, hot or cold. Use tetapi once and sebab once.
Part 2 (15 min): swap with your partner and read aloud. Your partner asks Bagaimana …? and Kenapa …?.
Part 3 (15 min): rewrite your text after the questions, adding one adjective for colour or size.
パート1：飲み物・料理・場所を選び、4〜6文で描写（色・大きさ・味・温度）。tetapi と sebab を一回ずつ。パート2：交換して音読し、Bagaimana …?・Kenapa …? で質問。パート3：質問を受けて、色か大きさの形容詞を一つ足して書き直す。
☐ Each adjective comes after its noun and does not change.
☐ tidak (not bukan) stands before an adjective.
☐ tetapi joins two contrasting ideas; sebab (or kerana) comes before the reason.
☐ Standard forms (mahu, tetapi) are used in writing; spoken forms are not.
Model: Hari Sabtu saya makan mi goreng di mamak. Mi goreng itu pedas, tetapi sedap. Teh tarik saya sejuk dan kurang manis. Saya kenyang dan gembira sebab makanan sedap.
target_spans: Hari Sabtu saya makan mi goreng di mamak. Mi goreng itu pedas, tetapi sedap. Teh tarik saya sejuk dan kurang manis. Saya kenyang dan gembira sebab makanan sedap.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|0.source_text: Pattern box: (A) lebih (adjective) daripada (B). / (A) kurang (adjective) daripada (B).

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|1.source_text: 1. A: Kondo A lebih luas daripada kondo B? B: Ya, kondo A lebih luas. Kondo A ada tiga bilik.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|4.source_text: 4. A: Komputer baru lebih cepat daripada komputer lama? B: Ya, lebih cepat sedikit.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|5.source_text: 5. A: Hari ini lebih panas daripada semalam? B: Ya, semalam hujan.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|6.source_text: 6. A: Soalan ini kurang susah daripada soalan semalam? B: Ya, soalan ini lebih mudah.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|7.source_text: Explanation: lebih goes before the adjective and means "more" or "-er": lebih besar. daripada introduces the thing you compare with: lebih besar daripada kondo B. When both people know the other thing you can leave daripada out: Kondo B lebih murah. kurang before an adjective means "less" or "not so": kurang besar. The adjective itself never changes. sedikit after the adjective makes the difference small: lebih cepat sedikit. mudah is the standard word for easy; senang is the spoken one.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|8.source_text: 説明：lebih は形容詞の前に置き「もっと」「〜より」の意味です：lebih besar。daripada は比べる相手を導きます：lebih besar daripada kondo B。相手が分かっていれば daripada は省けます：Kondo B lebih murah. 形容詞の前の kurang は「より少ない・あまり〜ない」：kurang besar。形容詞の形は変わりません。形容詞のあとに sedikit を付けると、差が小さいことを表します：lebih cepat sedikit。「易しい」は標準語では mudah、話し言葉では senang です。

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|9.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese puts the standard first (Bより大きい). Malay puts it last: A lebih besar daripada B. Japanese adjectives change form (大きい / 大きくない), Malay adjectives never do; lebih and kurang are separate words in front.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|10.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語は比べる相手を先に言います（Bより大きい）。マレー語は最後です：A lebih besar daripada B。日本語の形容詞は形が変わります（大きい／大きくない）が、マレー語の形容詞は変わらず、lebih と kurang は前に置く別の語です。

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|0.source_text: Explanation: sama + adjective + dengan says two things are equal, as … as: sama besar dengan kondo C. The adjective sits between sama and dengan. setinggi (as tall as) and semahal (as expensive as) are single ledger words: learn them as whole words. For every other adjective use sama … dengan. Building new words like these is a later chapter, so do not make new ones yet.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|1.source_text: 説明：sama + 形容詞 + dengan は「〜と同じくらい〜」です：sama besar dengan kondo C。形容詞は sama と dengan の間に入ります。setinggi（同じくらい高い）と semahal（同じくらい高価）は台帳の一語なので、そのまま覚えます。ほかの形容詞には sama … dengan を使います。この形の新しい語を作るのはあとの章なので、まだ作りません。

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|2.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese says Bと同じくらい高い: dengan (と) comes last in Malay, after the adjective: sama tinggi dengan B. The whole words setinggi and semahal need no dengan and no sama.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|3.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語は「Bと同じくらい高い」と言います。マレー語の dengan（と）は最後で、形容詞のあとです：sama tinggi dengan B。setinggi と semahal は一語で、sama も dengan も要りません。

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|12.source_text: Explanation: paling before any adjective means "the most": paling murah, paling ramai. Four ledger words say the same in one word: termurah (cheapest), terbesar (biggest), terbaik (best), tercantik (most beautiful). Learn these four as whole words. paling is the way to make the rest. yang terbaik means "the best one".

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|13.source_text: 説明：paling は形容詞の前に付いて「一番〜」の意味です：paling murah、paling ramai。台帳には一語で同じ意味の語が四つあります：termurah（一番安い）、terbesar（一番大きい）、terbaik（一番良い）、tercantik（一番きれい）。この四つは一語としてそのまま覚えます。ほかは paling で作ります。yang terbaik は「一番良いもの」です。

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|14.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 一番 is also a word in front of the adjective (一番安い = paling murah), so the order matches. termurah is one word, like 最安.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|0.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「一番」も形容詞の前に来るので、語順は同じです（一番安い＝paling murah）。termurah は「最安」のような一語です。

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|9.source_text: Explanation: yang mana means "which one" and stands where the answer will stand: Yang mana lebih selesa? Kondo D. After a noun it means "which …": kondo yang mana. pilih is "to choose": Saya pilih yang ini. lain means "other": Ada kondo lain? yang ini is "this one", yang itu is "that one".

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|10.source_text: 説明：yang mana は「どれ」で、答えが入る位置に置きます：Yang mana lebih selesa? Kondo D. 名詞のあとでは「どの〜」：kondo yang mana。pilih は「選ぶ」：Saya pilih yang ini. lain は「他の」：Ada kondo lain? yang ini は「これ」、yang itu は「それ」です。

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|11.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese separates どれ (three or more) from どちら (two); Malay uses yang mana for both. pilih is one plain verb, like 選ぶ.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|12.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語はどれ（3つ以上）とどちら（2つ）を使い分けますが、マレー語はどちらも yang mana です。pilih は「選ぶ」にあたる普通の動詞です。

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|21.source_text: Explanation: sangat goes before an adjective and means "very": sangat selesa. sekali goes after it and means the same: bising sekali. amat is also "very", but formal. terlalu means "too": more than is good. Compare sangat panas (very hot) with terlalu panas (too hot to enjoy).

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|0.source_text: 説明：sangat は形容詞の前に置き「とても」：sangat selesa。sekali は形容詞のあとに置いて同じ意味です：bising sekali。amat も「とても」ですが、改まった言い方です。terlalu は「〜すぎる」で、よくない程度を表します。sangat panas（とても暑い）と terlalu panas（暑すぎる）を比べましょう。

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|1.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: 「暑すぎる」has すぎる attached to the adjective stem; in Malay terlalu is a separate word in front, and the adjective does not change: terlalu panas. とても ≈ sangat.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|2.source_text: 日本語との比較：「暑すぎる」は形容詞の語幹に「すぎる」が付きますが、マレー語の terlalu は前に置く別の語で、形容詞は変わりません：terlalu panas。とても ≈ sangat です。

Unit 6 · Culture and usage note|2|0.source_text: Read about comparing places and things in Malaysia. Word-building notes come only from Kata-Kata card notes.

Unit 6 · Culture and usage note|3|0.source_text: Kondo is the everyday Malaysian word for a condominium: a block of homes with shared areas. Kamus Dewan lists it as a headword (the ledger's check). In Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan, the Strata Management Act 2013 sets out who looks after those shared areas: first a joint management body of the owners and later, once strata titles are issued, a management corporation. So talking about a kondo often means talking about the whole building too: is it bersih, sunyi or bising?

Unit 6 · Culture and usage note|3|1.source_text: The Klang Valley, the urban area around Kuala Lumpur, has a rail network that includes LRT, MRT, monorail and KTM Komuter lines, so stesen is a word you read on signs and hear on the platform. When you say where you live or work, a station is an easy thing to describe: Stesen sangat ramai pukul lapan.

Unit 6 · Culture and usage note|3|2.source_text: Kata-Kata's card notes show how some comparing words are made. setinggi is se- + tinggi and semahal is se- + mahal; terbaik comes from baik with ter-. Learn them as whole words for now. For other adjectives, say sama … dengan or paling. bersih is a root word that only looks like a ber- word.

Unit 6 · Culture and usage note|3|3.source_text: Two small words change meaning. After an adjective, sekali means "very" (cantik sekali); it is the same word as "once" in chapter 4. baru is "new" here and "just" in chapter 4. In the Kata-Kata scene the agent says Kondo B kurang besar: kurang with an adjective means "less" or "not so".

Unit 6 · Culture and usage note|3|5.source_text: Kondo は、マレーシアで日常的に使う「コンドミニアム」の言葉で、共用部分のある集合住宅を指します。Kamus Dewan に見出し語として載っています（台帳の確認）。半島マレーシアとラブアンでは、Strata Management Act 2013 が共用部分の管理者を定めています：最初は所有者による共同管理組織、分譲登記が発行されたあとは管理法人です。そのため kondo の話は建物全体の話にもなりがちです：bersih か、sunyi か、bising か。

Unit 6 · Culture and usage note|3|6.source_text: クランバレー（クアラルンプール周辺の都市圏）には LRT、MRT、モノレール、KTM Komuter などの鉄道網があるので、stesen は標識で目にし、ホームで耳にする言葉です。住んでいる場所や職場を話すとき、駅は説明しやすい題材です：Stesen sangat ramai pukul lapan.

Unit 6 · Culture and usage note|3|7.source_text: Kata-Kata のカード注記から、比べる言葉のでき方が分かります。setinggi は se- + tinggi、semahal は se- + mahal で、terbaik は baik に ter- が付いた形です。今は一語としてそのまま覚えましょう。ほかの形容詞には sama … dengan か paling を使います。bersih は接頭辞の付いた語に見えるだけの、語根の単語です。

Unit 6 · Culture and usage note|3|8.source_text: 二つの小さな語は意味が変わります。形容詞のあとの sekali は「とても」の意味です（cantik sekali）。第4章の「一度」と同じ語です。baru はここでは「新しい」、第4章では「〜したばかり」です。Kata-Kata の場面で不動産担当者は Kondo B kurang besar と言います。形容詞の前の kurang は「より少ない」「あまり〜ない」の意味です。

Unit 6 · Teaching plan and answer key|3|.source_text: Before Block A: Kata-Kata Sedia Kelas c06 (22 cards, frames ms-c06-f01 and ms-c06-f02).
Before Block E: Kata-Kata Dunia scene "Main badminton"; learners only need to recognise the scene words.

After Block D: the Kata-Kata chapter 6 deck with spaced review, frames ms-c06-f01, ms-c06-f02, ms-c06-f03, ms-c06-f04, ms-c06-f05, ms-c06-f06, ms-c06-f07 in the frame drill and Susun Ayat; about 3 hours of self-study for this unit (planning figure).
Hanashishou starts at A2, so there is no Hanashishou scene for this unit. Listening uses the teacher-read script.
■ Block A · Words and patterns (45 min)
Goal: I can compare two things with lebih or kurang and daripada, and say they are the same with sama … dengan.
0–5 Recall: chapter 5 (taste, hot or cold, Kenapa …? Sebab …) from the opener prompts.
5–10 Tanya Cikgu questions from Kata-Kata.
10–20 Vocabulary focus: core words first; Dunia and revision words are only pointed out.
20–40 Pattern focus: patterns 1 and 2, question and answer first, rule second; teach the first two word groups and the describing words in Blocks A and B, not all in one sitting.
40–45 First substitutions (Drill 2, items 1 to 3).
■ Block B · Drills and conversation (45 min)
Goal: I can say which is the most with paling, use sangat and terlalu, and ask and answer Yang mana …? with pilih.
0–5 Recall: two things in the room: Yang mana lebih besar? round the class.
5–25 Drill ladder in order: pattern table, substitution, transformation, question and answer, question-word choice, short dialogues, then the markers drill.
25–40 Model conversation, gapped form, then the changed-facts variant.
40–45 Pair rehearsal without the script.
■ Block C · Listening and task (45 min)
Goal: I can follow a talk about a new home and use a short listing to choose a condo.
0–5 Recall: learners compare two drinks or two foods from last week: lebih manis, kurang pedas.
5–20 Listening: read the questions, two readings, check, then shadow three lines.

Unit 6 · Teaching plan and answer key|4|.source_text: 30–45 Task with role cards; announce the change of plan halfway.
■ Block D · Review and test (45 min)
Goal: I can check comparing words, sangat and terlalu, and place words in a short test.
0–15 Mixed review: cumulative question-word drill (chapters 1 to 6, including yang mana), then the markers drill with new cues.
35–45 Preview: the review block for chapters 1 to 6 (45 minutes) comes next, then the chapter 7 Kata-Kata set (places and directions).
Goal: I can recognise words for the game, the court and the body in the Kata-Kata Dunia scene "Main badminton" and compare two players.
0–5 Recall: compare two condos with lebih, paling and terlalu.
5–15 Kata-Kata Dunia scene "Main badminton" as listening (teacher reads, learners point to pictures or words).
15–30 Role-play of the scene in pairs.
30–40 Free variation: two players compare height and speed (a pair role-play), then they change who wins.
■ What to listen for · 注意点

Load: 35 core words in six groups (comparing and equal 6; the most 5; very and too 3; choosing 3; describing places and things 14; places 4). Suggested order: Block A the comparing and equal words, paling and the four whole words; Block B sangat, terlalu, choosing words and the describing words, with sewa, bilik and luas in the condo scene; Block C and D recycle them in the condo listing, the listening and the test; Block E recycles the comparing words in "Main badminton". If the pilot shows 32 is too many for one unit, the natural cut is A/B: comparing, equal and most first; very, too, choosing and the describing words second.

sekali and baru were taught in chapter 4 with other meanings (sekali once, baru just). Chapter 6 adds sekali = very after an adjective and baru = new. They are revision with a note (the ledger places them in chapters 4 and 6).

Unit 6 · Teaching plan and answer key|5|.source_text: termurah, terbesar, terbaik, tercantik, setinggi and semahal are taught as whole ledger words. Do not drill making new ter- or se- words: productive ter- is chapter 16. paling + adjective is the way to make a new superlative, and sama … dengan the way to say equal.

Standard first: mudah (standard) and senang (spoken) are shown together (decided by Sam on 12 Nov 2026, ledger L-0285); accept both in speech. Kamus Dewan was not opened for this. senang is also heard in a different meaning ("at ease"); that is not taught here.

The Kata-Kata scene uses dekat, jauh and the abbreviation LRT, which are outside chapters 1 to 6 (dekat and jauh are chapter 7), so the scene here compares rent, rooms, size, noise, age and comfort. sewa (rent), bilik (room) and luas (spacious) were added to the ledger at the request of Sam (12 Nov 2026) for these scenes. The rent is said per month with setiap bulan; sebulan, which the ledger gloss of sewa mentions, is a chapter 7 word (L-1063), so it is not used here. menyewa (to rent) waits for chapter 11. Do not add words from chapter 7 or later to the condo scenes.
terlalu is "too" and carries a complaint; sangat is "very" and does not. amat is the formal "very"; it fits a letter or a speech more than a chat.
"Main badminton" is for recognition. The body words (lengan, bahu, siku, lutut, pinggang) are labels in a sports scene: no injuries, advice or medicine. kurang before a noun is not taught.
Cumulative question words now include yang mana (chapters 1 to 6). Chapter 5 words bagaimana and kenapa (= mengapa = apa sebab, answered with sebab or kerana) return in drill 5 and in the listening.

■ Your turn · 自分で

Part 1 (10 min): without notes, ask your partner one question from each chapter: a greeting (1), a name or where they live (2), a price or a phone number (3), a time or a day (4), a taste or Kenapa …? (5), a comparison or Yang mana …? (6).

Part 2 (20 min): write six sentences about a home or a place you know: where it is, the rent or a price, how many rooms, one comparison with lebih … daripada or paling, one word with sangat or terlalu, and which one is the best (yang terbaik or Saya pilih …). Fictional details are fine.
Part 3 (15 min): read your partner's sentences aloud and ask two questions: one with Yang mana …? and one with Kenapa …?.
パート1：各章から一つずつ質問します。パート2：住まいや知っている場所について6文を書きます（場所、家賃や値段、部屋数、比較、「とても」か「〜すぎる」、一番良いものか選ぶもの）。パート3：相手の文を読み上げ、Yang mana …? と Kenapa …? で質問します。
■ Peer check · 互いに確認
☐ The greeting fits the time of day and the title comes before the name (chapters 1 and 2).
☐ Numbers and prices are correct (chapter 3).
☐ pukul for the clock and the marker fits the time word (chapter 4).
☐ The adjective comes after the noun and tidak stands before it (chapter 5).
☐ lebih, paling, sangat and terlalu come before the adjective; daripada comes after it (chapter 6).

Model: Saya tinggal di kondo di Mont Kiara. Kondo saya ada dua bilik. Sewa kondo saya dua ribu lima ratus ringgit setiap bulan. Kondo saya lebih luas daripada kondo kawan saya, tetapi kondo kawan saya lebih murah. Kondo saya sangat sunyi, tetapi pagi ini stesen terlalu ramai. Kondo saya yang terbaik.
target_spans: Saya tinggal di kondo di Mont Kiara. Kondo saya ada dua bilik. Sewa kondo saya dua ribu lima ratus ringgit setiap bulan. Kondo saya lebih luas daripada kondo kawan saya, tetapi kondo kawan saya lebih murah. Kondo saya sangat sunyi, tetapi pagi ini stesen terlalu ramai. Kondo saya yang terbaik.

Unit 7 · Chapter opener|3|5.source_text: ■ Setting and recall · 場面と復習

Unit 7 · Chapter opener|3|6.source_text: A new office: Encik Tanaka asks the way to a bank and to a bus stop, then follows Puan Aini's directions to her office. All places, routes and times are fictional.

Unit 7 · Chapter opener|3|7.source_text: 新しいオフィス：田中さんが銀行とバス乗り場への道をたずね、アイニ先生の道案内でオフィスに向かいます。場所・道順・時間はすべて架空です。

Unit 7 · Chapter opener|3|8.source_text: Without notes, from chapter 6: compare two places or two homes with lebih … daripada and say which is paling …. / 第6章の復習：二つの場所や家を lebih … daripada で比べ、paling … で一番を言いましょう。

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|0.source_text: Pattern box: Saya pergi ke (place). / (title) pergi ke mana? / datang dari mana?

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|1.source_text: 1. A: Encik pergi ke mana? B: Saya pergi ke pejabat.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|2.source_text: 2. A: Awak mahu pergi ke mana? B: Saya mahu pergi ke bank.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|3.source_text: 3. A: Puan datang dari mana? B: Saya datang dari rumah.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|4.source_text: 4. A: Encik balik ke rumah sekarang? B: Ya, saya balik ke rumah pukul enam.
target_spans: Ya, saya balik ke rumah pukul enam.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|5.source_text: 5. A: Dari mana? B: Dari pasar. Sekarang saya pergi ke stesen.
target_spans: Dari pasar. Sekarang saya pergi ke stesen.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|6.source_text: 6. A: Saya pergi kerja. Awak pergi ke mana? B: Saya pergi ke sekolah.
target_spans: Saya pergi kerja. Awak pergi ke mana?

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|7.source_text: Explanation: ke comes before the place you are going to: pergi ke bank. ke mana? asks where to, and dari mana? asks where from; the answer starts with ke or dari. di is for being at a place (di bank), ke is for going to it. You have already heard pergi kerja and balik rumah with no ke: that is everyday speech. pergi ke pejabat and balik ke rumah are the standard forms, and the ones you will read.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|8.source_text: 説明：ke は行き先の前に置きます：pergi ke bank。ke mana? は「どこへ」、dari mana? は「どこから」で、答えは ke か dari で始まります。di は場所にいること（di bank）、ke はそこへ行くことです。これまでに聞いた pergi kerja・balik rumah は ke のない日常の話し言葉です。pergi ke pejabat・balik ke rumah が標準の形で、読むときに出てくるのはこちらです。

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|9.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese marks the goal after the noun (銀行へ・銀行に); Malay puts ke before it. dari (から) also comes first: dari rumah. di matches で・に of location, but again comes first.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|10.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語は目的地のあとに「へ・に」を付けますが、マレー語は ke を名詞の前に置きます。「から」にあたる dari も前です：dari rumah。場所の「で・に」にあたる di も前に置きます。

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|13.source_text: 1. A: Bank di mana? B: Bank di depan stesen.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|14.source_text: 2. A: Sekolah di mana? B: Sekolah di utara stesen, pasar di selatan.
target_spans: Sekolah di utara stesen, pasar di selatan.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|15.source_text: 3. A: Tandas di mana? B: Tandas di sebelah lif, di tingkat dua.
target_spans: Tandas di sebelah lif, di tingkat dua.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|16.source_text: 4. A: Pasar di antara stesen dan sekolah? B: Ya, di antara stesen dan sekolah.
target_spans: Pasar di antara stesen dan sekolah?
Ya, di antara stesen dan sekolah.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|17.source_text: 5. A: Bank di sini atau di sana? B: Di sana, di seberang jalan.
target_spans: Bank di sini atau di sana?

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|18.source_text: 6. A: Kereta encik di mana? B: Di bawah, di tempat letak kereta.
target_spans: Di bawah, di tempat letak kereta.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|19.source_text: Explanation: The position word comes after di and before the landmark: di depan stesen, di sebelah bank, di antara A dan B. kiri and kanan follow sebelah: di sebelah kiri. di sini is here, di situ there near you, di sana over there. The compass words work the same way: di utara stesen, di selatan, di timur, di barat. No word for "is" is needed.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|0.source_text: 説明：位置を表す語は di のあと、目印の前に置きます：di depan stesen、di sebelah bank、di antara A dan B。kiri と kanan は sebelah のあとに付きます：di sebelah kiri。di sini はここ、di situ はそこ（近く）、di sana はあそこです。方位の語も同じです：di utara stesen、di selatan、di timur、di barat。「ある」にあたる語は要りません。

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|1.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese says 駅の前に: the landmark comes first and the position word after (の前に). Malay reverses it: di depan stesen, the position word first. Japanese also needs ある/います; Malay does not.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|2.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語は「駅の前に」と、目印が先で位置の語があとです。マレー語は逆で、di depan stesen のように位置の語が先に来ます。日本語の「ある・いる」にあたる語もマレー語には要りません。

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|4.source_text: Pattern box: Jalan terus, kemudian belok kiri / kanan di (landmark). / Jangan belok kiri / kanan.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|5.source_text: 1. A: Maaf, tumpang tanya, stesen di mana? B: Jalan terus, kemudian belok kanan di lampu isyarat.
target_spans: Maaf, tumpang tanya, stesen di mana?
Jalan terus, kemudian belok kanan di lampu isyarat.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|6.source_text: 2. A: Bank di mana? B: Belok kiri di simpang. Bank di sebelah kanan.
target_spans: Belok kiri di simpang. Bank di sebelah kanan.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|7.source_text: 3. A: Kedai itu di mana? B: Jalan terus sampai bulatan, kemudian belok kiri.
target_spans: Jalan terus sampai bulatan, kemudian belok kiri.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|8.source_text: 4. A: Hospital di mana? B: Terus depan. Hospital di seberang gereja.
target_spans: Terus depan. Hospital di seberang gereja.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|9.source_text: 5. A: Pasar di mana? B: Pergi terus. Jangan belok di lampu isyarat. Pasar di sebelah kiri, selepas tokong.
target_spans: Pergi terus. Jangan belok di lampu isyarat. Pasar di sebelah kiri, selepas tokong.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|10.source_text: 6. A: Tandas di mana? B: Naik tangga ke tingkat dua, kemudian belok kiri.
target_spans: Naik tangga ke tingkat dua, kemudian belok kiri.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|11.source_text: Explanation: A route is a list of short steps joined by kemudian (then): Jalan terus, kemudian belok kanan di lampu isyarat. terus means straight on: jalan terus, pergi terus or terus depan (straight ahead). belok is the verb to turn, kiri or kanan says which way, and di names the landmark where you do it. Jangan before a verb means do not: Jangan belok kiri. jalan is the road and also the verb to go on foot. For up, down, in and out use naik, turun, masuk and keluar: naik tangga is to go up the stairs. lurus only describes a straight road or line (Jalan ini lurus.); it is not used to say go straight on.
target_spans: Jalan terus, kemudian belok kanan di lampu isyarat.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|0.source_text: 説明：道順は短い手順を kemudian（それから）でつなぎます：Jalan terus, kemudian belok kanan di lampu isyarat. terus は「まっすぐ」で、jalan terus・pergi terus・terus depan（まっすぐ前）と言います。belok は「曲がる」、kiri か kanan で方向を言い、di のあとに曲がる目印を置きます。動詞の前の jangan は「〜しないで」の意味です：Jangan belok kiri. jalan は「道」でも「歩く・進む」でもあります。上る・下りる・入る・出るには naik・turun・masuk・keluar を使い、naik tangga は階段を上ることです。lurus は道や線の形（まっすぐな）を表すだけで、「まっすぐ進む」の意味では使いません：Jalan ini lurus.
target_spans: Jalan terus, kemudian belok kanan di lampu isyarat.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|1.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese joins steps with て (まっすぐ行って、曲がって); Malay keeps each verb plain and adds kemudian, or just a comma. The landmark comes after di, not before を. A Japanese "do not" ends the verb (曲がらないで); Malay puts jangan first.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|2.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語は「まっすぐ行って、曲がって」と動詞を「て」でつなぎますが、マレー語は動詞の形を変えずに kemudian かコンマでつなぎます。目印は di のあとに置きます。日本語の「曲がらないで」は動詞の終わりで禁止を表しますが、マレー語は jangan を動詞の前に置きます。

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|4.source_text: Pattern box: Berapa jauh (place) dari sini? / Lebih kurang (distance).

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|5.source_text: 1. A: Berapa jauh stesen dari sini? B: Lebih kurang lima ratus meter.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|6.source_text: 2. A: Jauh dari sini? B: Tidak jauh. Dekat sahaja.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|7.source_text: 3. A: Bank dekat dengan pejabat? B: Ya, dekat. Jalan kaki lebih kurang dua minit.
target_spans: Ya, dekat. Jalan kaki lebih kurang dua minit.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|8.source_text: 4. A: Berapa jauh hospital dari kondo? B: Lebih kurang dua kilometer.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|9.source_text: 5. A: Rumah awak jauh dari pejabat? B: Jauh. Lebih kurang sepuluh kilometer. Saya naik kereta api.
target_spans: Jauh. Lebih kurang sepuluh kilometer. Saya naik kereta api.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|10.source_text: 6. A: Berapa sewa kondo itu sebulan? B: Tiga ribu ringgit sebulan. Kondo itu dekat dengan stesen.
target_spans: Tiga ribu ringgit sebulan. Kondo itu dekat dengan stesen.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|11.source_text: Explanation: berapa jauh asks how far; answer with lebih kurang (about) and a distance in meter or, for a longer distance, kilometer. dekat (near) goes with dengan (dekat dengan stesen); jauh (far) goes with dari (jauh dari sini). Say tidak jauh for not far. kalau (if) starts a condition: Kalau jauh, naik teksi. sebulan (per month, a month) comes after the amount: tiga ribu ringgit sebulan. It is one whole word; do not build other words like it.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|0.source_text: 説明：berapa jauh は「どのくらい遠いか」で、lebih kurang（約）と meter、長い距離なら kilometer で答えます。dekat（近い）は dengan と、jauh（遠い）は dari と使います：dekat dengan stesen、jauh dari sini。遠くないときは tidak jauh と言います。kalau（もし）は条件を始めます：Kalau jauh, naik teksi. sebulan（1か月につき）は金額のあとに置きます：tiga ribu ringgit sebulan。ひとかたまりの語で、同じ形の語を自分で作ることはしません。

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|1.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese says 駅に近い / 駅から遠い with different particles (に・から); Malay likewise uses dengan and dari. 約 comes first in Malay: lebih kurang before the number. 月3000リンギット is amount first, then the period, in both languages.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|2.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語は「駅に近い」「駅から遠い」と助詞を使い分けますが、マレー語も dengan と dari を使い分けます。「約」にあたる lebih kurang は数字の前に置きます。「月3,000リンギット」のように、金額が先で期間があとに来る点は両言語で同じです。

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|4.source_text: Pattern box: Berapa lama ke (place)? / Lebih kurang (number) minit naik (transport).

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|5.source_text: 1. A: Berapa lama ke pejabat? B: Lebih kurang dua puluh minit naik bas.
target_spans: Lebih kurang dua puluh minit naik bas.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|6.source_text: 2. A: Berapa lama jalan kaki ke stesen? B: Lebih kurang sepuluh minit.
target_spans: Berapa lama jalan kaki ke stesen?

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|7.source_text: 3. A: Berapa lama ke sekolah naik kereta? B: Lebih kurang lima belas minit, kalau tidak jam / sesak.
target_spans: Berapa lama ke sekolah naik kereta?
Lebih kurang lima belas minit, kalau tidak jam / sesak.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|8.source_text: 4. A: Berapa lama ke hospital naik teksi? B: Lebih kurang sepuluh minit. Kalau jam / sesak, lebih lama.
target_spans: Berapa lama ke hospital naik teksi?
Lebih kurang sepuluh minit. Kalau jam / sesak, lebih lama.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|9.source_text: 5. A: Encik naik apa ke pejabat? B: Saya naik kereta api, kemudian jalan kaki.
target_spans: Saya naik kereta api, kemudian jalan kaki.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|10.source_text: 6. A: Berapa lama encik tunggu bas? B: Lebih kurang lima minit.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|11.source_text: Explanation: berapa lama asks how long; the answer is lebih kurang with minit or jam (hour, chapter 4). naik takes the vehicle: naik bas, naik teksi, naik kereta api. You get off with turun: Turun di stesen. Walking is jalan kaki. In speech jam also means heavy traffic, so kalau tidak jam could be heard as an hour; pair it with sesak (crowded, jammed): kalau tidak jam / sesak. (satu jam is an hour.)

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|12.source_text: 説明：berapa lama は「どのくらい時間がかかるか」で、lebih kurang と minit か jam（時間、第4章）で答えます。乗り物は naik のあとに置きます：naik bas、naik teksi、naik kereta api。降りるのは turun です：Turun di stesen. 歩くのは jalan kaki です。話し言葉では jam に「渋滞」の意味もあり、kalau tidak jam は「一時間」と聞き違えられるので、sesak（混んでいる・渋滞している）と並べて kalau tidak jam / sesak と言います。（satu jam は「一時間」）

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|0.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese uses 乗る for all vehicles (バスに乗る); Malay naik also means to go up, and the vehicle follows with no particle. 降りる ≈ turun. Japanese 渋滞 is one word; Malay has two, spoken jam and sesak.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|1.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「乗る」にあたる naik は「上がる」の意味もあり、乗り物は助詞なしでそのあとに来ます。「降りる」は turun です。日本語の「渋滞」は一語ですが、マレー語では話し言葉の jam と sesak の二つがあります。

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|0.source_text: Model each A line; learners answer as B, then swap. Explain the rule only after they have used the pattern.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|1.source_text: Pattern IDs are the Kata-Kata chapter 7 frames, one pattern for each of f01 to f05. Explanations and Japanese comparisons are drafts.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|2.source_text: Pattern 1: if a learner says pergi kerja, accept it as everyday speech and model pergi ke pejabat as the standard form. ke goes before the place, never after.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|3.source_text: Pattern 2: the position word comes straight after di. If a learner puts it after the landmark (Japanese order), model di depan stesen again and tap the order. Use all six places of worship in turn as landmarks, and no one of them more often than the others.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|4.source_text: Pattern 3: a route is short steps joined by kemudian. Accept a comma instead. belok needs kiri or kanan.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|5.source_text: Pattern 4: dekat dengan and jauh dari are the two partners. lebih kurang comes before the distance.

Unit 7 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|6.source_text: Pattern 5: naik takes the vehicle with no word between. jam (traffic) is spoken; if a learner says it as an hour, check which meaning they want.

■ Say it with the marker · マーカーを付けて言う
1. Saya pergi ke bank. (marker: sudah)
2. Dia balik ke rumah. (time cue: esok, marker: akan)
3. Kami sampai di stesen. (marker: belum)
4. Encik tunggu di luar. (marker: masih)
5. Saya naik bas ke pejabat. (time cue: semalam)
6. Mereka datang dari pasar. (marker: baru)
7. Answer Sudah sampai? (marker: belum)
8. Kami turun di bulatan. (time cue: nanti, marker: akan)
■ Japanese bridge · 日本語との橋渡し
sudah pergi ≈ もう行った · belum sampai ≈ まだ着いていない · masih tunggu ≈ まだ待っている · akan turun ≈ 降りる予定
Japanese changes the verb (行く / 行った); Malay keeps pergi and changes only the marker or the time word. / 日本語は動詞が変わりますが、マレー語は pergi のままで、前の語だけが変わります。

Chapters 1 to 7: apa / siapa / di mana / Siapakah (-kah) / Apakah (-kah) / di manakah (-kah) / Adakah / Bolehkah / berapa / bila / pukul berapa / hari apa / bagaimana (spoken: macam mana) / kenapa (= mengapa, apa sebab; answer: sebab or kerana) / yang mana / ke mana / dari mana / berapa jauh / berapa lama

New in chapter 7: ke mana (where to; answer with ke and the place: Ke pejabat.), dari mana (where from; answer with dari and the place: Dari rumah.), berapa jauh (how far; answer with lebih kurang and metres) and berapa lama (how long; answer with lebih kurang and minutes or hours). Chapter 6 added yang mana (which one) with pilih in the answer. / 第7章で増えた疑問語：ke mana（どこへ。ke と場所で答える）、dari mana（どこから。dari と場所で答える）、berapa jauh（どのくらい遠い。lebih kurang と距離で答える）、berapa lama（どのくらいの時間。lebih kurang と分や時間で答える）。第6章の yang mana（どれ）と pilih（選ぶ）も引き続き使います。
1. Ask a colleague how they are. (apa)
2. Ask who is in the office. (siapa)
3. Ask where the bank is. (di mana)
4. Ask formally whether the station is near. (Adakah)
5. Ask politely whether you may go in. (Bolehkah)
6. Ask the price of a taxi to the station. (berapa)
7. Ask when the bus comes. (bila)
8. Ask what time you leave for the office. (pukul berapa)
9. Ask what day your colleague goes to the office. (hari apa)
10. Ask how the new station is. (bagaimana; spoken macam mana)
11. Ask why a colleague does not take the bus. (kenapa; also mengapa or apa sebab; the answer starts with sebab or kerana)
12. Ask which exit your friend means. (yang mana)
13. Ask where your colleague is going. (ke mana)
14. Ask where a visitor comes from. (dari mana)
15. Ask how far the station is. (berapa jauh)
16. Ask how long it takes to walk to the station. (berapa lama)

No Malay explainer for Stage 1 units: explainers and rubrics are in Japanese or English (Sam, 11 Nov 2026). Select 日本語 or English.
The teacher reads the script twice; read the questions first, listen for the details, then shadow.
On Monday morning Encik Tanaka phones Puan Aini from the station to ask the way to her office. / 月曜の朝、田中さんが駅からアイニ先生に電話をして、オフィスへの道をたずねます。
Predict: which route words will Aini use? Write three guesses (for example terus, belok, sebelah). / アイニ先生が使いそうな道案内の言葉を三つ予想しましょう。
Read the nine questions below before the first listening. / 1回目の前に下の9つの質問を読みます。
■ While listening · 聞きながら
1. Where is Tanaka at the start?
2. What does he do at the roundabout?
3. How far does he go straight on after the roundabout, and which way must he not turn?
4. What is next to Aini's office building?
5. Which floor is the office on, and how can he go up?
6. How long is the walk from the station, and why does Aini say not to take a taxi?
7. Where does Tanaka come from this morning, how far is it and how does he come?
8. How long is the train ride, and is the train late?
9. How much is the rent of a condo near the station?
■ After listening · 聞いたあと
Compare answers, then shadow lines 3, 5 and 7 after the teacher. / 答えを比べ、3・5・7行目をシャドーイングします。
Tell your partner the way from the station to your home or office: jalan terus, kemudian belok and one landmark. / 駅から自分の家や職場までの道を、jalan terus・kemudian belok・目印を一つ使って話しましょう。
The teacher reads the script twice at natural speed. No audio file.

■ Role card B · Bのカード

You live nearby. From the station: straight on 300 metres, turn left at the traffic lights; the hospital is on the right, opposite the gurdwara; about 800 metres, about fifteen minutes on foot; the bus takes five minutes.
Give the route with jalan terus, kemudian belok and a landmark.
Bは近所の人です。駅から：まっすぐ300メートル、信号を左、病院は右側でグルドワラの向かい。約800メートル、歩いて約15分、バスなら5分。jalan terus・kemudian belok・目印で道を教えます。
■ Change of plan · 予定変更
Halfway, B says: Hari ini jam. Bas lambat. A asks Kalau jalan kaki, berapa lama? and decides how to go.
途中でBが Hari ini jam. Bas lambat. と言います。Aは Kalau jalan kaki, berapa lama? とたずね、どうやって行くかを決めます。

☐ A asks where, how far and how long (di mana, berapa jauh, berapa lama).
☐ B gives the route with jalan terus, kemudian belok and a landmark.
☐ After the change, A asks Kalau jalan kaki, berapa lama? and says how they will go.

Unit 7 · Culture and usage note|3|0.source_text: Earlier chapters used pergi kerja and balik rumah. They are everyday speech, and perfectly normal. Now that you have ke, you can say the standard forms, pergi ke pejabat and balik ke rumah, which are the ones you will read. Ask ke mana? or dari mana? and the answer starts with ke or dari.

Unit 7 · Culture and usage note|3|1.source_text: Traffic in Malaysia keeps to the left, a legacy of British rule according to guidebooks and news sources. That is worth knowing when you give a route to someone in a car: belok kanan crosses the other lane.

Unit 7 · Culture and usage note|3|2.source_text: This unit uses six places of worship as ordinary landmarks, like a bank or a station: a masjid, a gereja, a kuil (Hindu temple), a tokong (Chinese temple), a gurdwara (Sikh temple) and a surau (a small prayer hall). Reports of the 2020 census name Muslim, Buddhist, Christian and Hindu communities among the largest groups, so all of them are part of the street scene. You only need to say where they are.

Unit 7 · Culture and usage note|3|3.source_text: Kata-Kata's card notes explain some words. lebih kurang is literally "more-less"; kereta api is "fire carriage"; bulatan comes from bulat (round); belok is a root word, not a ber- form; hadapan is the more formal depan. To say straight on, Malaysians use terus, jalan terus, pergi terus or terus depan; lurus describes a straight road or line. In speech jam has a third meaning, heavy traffic, so it is paired with sesak: kalau tidak jam / sesak.

Unit 7 · Culture and usage note|3|5.source_text: 前の章では pergi kerja と balik rumah を使いました。どちらも日常の話し言葉で、ごく普通の言い方です。ke が使えるようになったので、標準の形である pergi ke pejabat・balik ke rumah も言えます。読むときに出てくるのはこちらです。ke mana? や dari mana? とたずねると、答えは ke か dari で始まります。

Unit 7 · Culture and usage note|3|6.source_text: マレーシアの車は左側通行で、旅行や報道の情報源によればイギリス統治時代の名残です。車の人に道を教えるときは覚えておくとよいでしょう：belok kanan（右折）は反対車線を横切ります。

Unit 7 · Culture and usage note|3|7.source_text: このユニットでは、銀行や駅と同じ普通の目印として、六つの礼拝の場を使います：masjid、gereja、kuil（ヒンドゥー教寺院）、tokong（中国寺院）、gurdwara（シク教寺院）、surau（小さな礼拝所）です。2020年の国勢調査の報道では、イスラム教徒、仏教徒、キリスト教徒、ヒンドゥー教徒が大きな集団に挙げられているので、どれも街の風景の一部です。ここでは、それがどこにあるかを言えれば十分です。

Unit 7 · Culture and usage note|3|8.source_text: Kata-Kata のカード注記が、いくつかの語のなりたちを説明しています。lebih kurang は文字どおり「もっと・より少ない」、kereta api は「火の車」、bulatan は bulat（丸い）から、belok は語根の単語で接頭辞の付いた形ではなく、hadapan は depan の改まった形です。「まっすぐ進む」はマレーシアでは terus・jalan terus・pergi terus・terus depan と言い、lurus は道や線の形を表します。話し言葉の jam には「渋滞」という三つ目の意味もあるので、sesak と並べて kalau tidak jam / sesak と言います。

Unit 7 · Teaching plan and answer key|3|.source_text: Before Block A: Kata-Kata Sedia Kelas c07 (28 cards, frames ms-c07-f01 and ms-c07-f02).
Before Block E: Kata-Kata Dunia scenes "Di ruang tamu", "Telefon baru" and "Lintas jalan"; learners only need to recognise the scene words.

After Block D: the Kata-Kata chapter 7 deck with spaced review, frames ms-c07-f01, ms-c07-f02, ms-c07-f03, ms-c07-f04, ms-c07-f05 in the frame drill and Susun Ayat; about 3 hours of self-study for this unit (planning figure).
Hanashishou starts at A2, so there is no Hanashishou scene for this unit. Listening uses the teacher-read script.
■ Block A · Words and patterns (45 min)
Goal: I can say where something is with di and a position word, and where I am going and coming from with ke and dari.
0–5 Recall: chapter 6 (comparing two homes, Yang mana paling …?) from the opener prompts.
5–10 Tanya Cikgu questions from Kata-Kata.
10–20 Vocabulary focus: core words first; Dunia and revision words are only pointed out.

20–40 Pattern focus: patterns 1 and 2, question and answer first, rule second; teach the position words and the distance and direction words in Blocks A and B, and the landmarks and transport in Block C, not all in one sitting.
40–45 First substitutions (Drill 2, items 1 to 3).
■ Block B · Drills and conversation (45 min)
Goal: I can give and follow a route with jalan terus, kemudian belok kiri or kanan, say jangan belok and name a landmark, and ask Berapa jauh? and Berapa lama?.
0–5 Recall: two things in the room: Yang mana di sebelah kiri? round the class.
5–25 Drill ladder in order: pattern table, substitution, transformation, question and answer, question-word choice, short dialogues, then the markers drill.
25–40 Model conversation, gapped form, then the changed-facts variant.
40–45 Pair rehearsal without the script.
■ Block C · Listening and task (45 min)
Goal: I can follow directions to an office and read a building directory.
0–5 Recall: learners say where five things in the room are: Telefon di atas meja.
5–20 Listening: read the questions, two readings, check, then shadow three lines.
20–30 Reading and writing.

Unit 7 · Teaching plan and answer key|4|.source_text: 30–45 Task with role cards; announce the change of plan halfway.
■ Block D · Review and test (45 min)
Goal: I can check position words, route words and the distance and time questions in a short test.
0–15 Mixed review: cumulative question-word drill (chapters 1 to 7, including ke mana, dari mana, berapa jauh, berapa lama), then the markers drill with new cues.
35–45 Preview: the writing block for unit 7 (directions by message, 45 minutes) comes next; then unit 8 (counters) and the chapter 8 Kata-Kata set.
Goal: I can recognise words for the living room, the new phone and crossing the road in the Kata-Kata Dunia scenes and say where things are.
0–5 Recall: give a route from the door to another room with terus, kemudian belok and a landmark.
5–15 Kata-Kata Dunia scenes "Di ruang tamu", "Telefon baru" and "Lintas jalan" as listening (teacher reads, learners point to pictures or words).
15–30 Role-play of the scene in pairs.
30–40 Free variation: a pair role-play: one learner hides a phone in the room and gives clues (di atas, di bawah, di sebelah), the other finds it.
■ What to listen for · 注意点

Load: 62 core words in five groups (position words 13; distance, time and direction 11; turning and moving 11; landmarks and transport 23; compass points 4). Suggested order: Block A position words and the distance, time and direction words; Block B the turning and moving words and the route pattern; Block C the landmarks and transport (the six places of worship together, as one set of landmarks) and the compass points; Block D and E recycle them. If the pilot shows 62 is too many for one unit, the natural cut is A/B: position, distance, direction and turning words first; landmarks, transport and compass points second.

Going straight on (Sam, 12 Nov 2026): say terus, jalan terus, pergi terus or terus depan. jalan lurus is not used for directions; if a learner says it, give the Malay form and move on. lurus (L-0318) is only the adjective "straight" for a road or line: Jalan ini lurus. The Kata-Kata card ms-c07-024 and its frame still teach jalan lurus; they are being fixed there.

Unit 7 · Teaching plan and answer key|5|.source_text: ke is now taught. Earlier chapters used pergi kerja and balik rumah and mentioned ke only to explain why it was not used. Show pergi ke pejabat and balik ke rumah as the standard written form and the earlier forms as everyday speech: both are right.

Traffic (Sam, 12 Nov 2026): say kalau tidak jam / sesak so that jam (traffic, spoken) is not read as jam (hour, chapter 4). sesak (L-0620) is a core word beside jam (L-0342); sesak is standard and jam is everyday speech (Sam, 12 Nov 2026). satu jam is still an hour.

Places of worship (Sam, 12 Nov 2026): masjid, gereja, kuil, tokong, gurdwara and surau are one set, used as plain landmarks. Show no bias: rotate them evenly in examples and drills, never single one out, and do not add worship, dress or etiquette content. The spelling gurdwara is confirmed. There is no separate word for a Buddhist temple; tokong stays.

Ledger notes: L-0592 pintu masuk is Retired as a duplicate of L-0330 pintu masuk / pintu keluar (Sam, 12 Nov 2026). L-0304 depan / hadapan is depan, taught in chapter 4 (L-0173); hadapan is the formal form. hospital and kapal terbang were placed as recognition words in chapters 5 and 4, so they are revision here. tumpang tanya (L-0019) is chapter 1 revision, used to start a question to a stranger.

New in step 5f (Sam, 12 Nov 2026): kilometer (long distances; meter for short ones), terus, tangga, jangan and sebulan. sebulan is a whole word, like seminggu sekali in chapter 4; this unit does not drill making se- words (chapter 8 teaches se- with every counter). jangan is only used with root verbs (Jangan belok kiri.). tengok is everyday speech for "to look"; the standard word is not in the ledger.

Do not use words placed after chapter 7 (the rest of the ledger from chapter 8 and 9). The Kata-Kata chapter 7 scene uses several words outside the ledger, a rail line, a ride-hailing service and real shopping-centre names, so the scenes here use a bank, a station and an office instead. All routes, distances, rents and times are fictional.
"Di ruang tamu", "Telefon baru" and "Lintas jalan" are for recognition. The phone words are labels (no passwords or accounts are asked for); the road words are labels, not safety rules.

Cumulative question words now include ke mana, dari mana, berapa jauh and berapa lama (chapters 1 to 7). The writing block for unit 7 (directions by message) is the separate 45-minute block that follows this unit.

Unit 7 · Teaching plan and answer key|6|.source_text: Answer keys are on each component. Japanese text awaits native review.
Standard forms first; spoken forms are labelled. No productive ber- or me- verbs (root verbs only).

Unit 7 · Writing block · Directions by m.source_text: ■ Your turn · 自分で
Part 1 (15 min): read the model reply. Underline the route steps (jalan terus, belok), the landmarks after di, the distance, the time and the jangan.

Part 2 (15 min): write a two-sentence message to a friend or a colleague asking the way to their home or office (where it is, how far). Swap with your partner and write the reply: four or five sentences with one landmark, one distance with lebih kurang, one time in minit and one jangan.
Part 3 (15 min): read the reply you received and check it with the list below. Write one line back (Terima kasih! Saya sampai pukul …) and correct your own reply once.
パート1：見本の返信を読み、道順の語・目印・距離・時間・jangan に線を引く。パート2：友だちか同僚に家や職場への行き方をたずねる2文を書く（どこか、どのくらい遠いか）。ペアと交換し、目印・lebih kurang の距離・minit の時間・jangan を一つずつ入れた4〜5文の返信を書く。パート3：もらった返信を下のリストで確認し、お礼と到着時刻を一行返す。自分の返信も一度直す。
■ Peer check · 互いに確認
☐ Going straight on is terus, jalan terus or pergi terus (not jalan lurus).
☐ Every turn has kiri or kanan and a landmark after di; the position word comes straight after di.
☐ The distance has lebih kurang and meter or kilometer; the time has minit or jam.
☐ jangan stands before a verb (Jangan belok kiri.).
☐ In writing, traffic is sesak; spoken jam is left for speech. ke goes before the place you are going to.

Model: Kondo saya lebih kurang dua kilometer dari stesen. Dari stesen, jalan terus lebih kurang tiga ratus meter. Jangan belok kiri di lampu isyarat. Belok kanan di bulatan. Kondo saya di sebelah gereja, di depan bank. Naik lif ke tingkat lima. Jalan kaki lebih kurang sepuluh minit, kalau tidak sesak.
target_spans: Kondo saya lebih kurang dua kilometer dari stesen. Dari stesen, jalan terus lebih kurang tiga ratus meter. Jangan belok kiri di lampu isyarat. Belok kanan di bulatan. Unit 8 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|7.source_text: Explanation: The number comes first, then the counter, then the noun: dua ekor ikan (two fish). The counter says what kind of thing you are counting: ekor for animals, biji for small round things, batang for long thin things, helai for clothes and sheets of paper, kuntum for flowers, pasang for pairs, orang for people, buah for large or general things. The noun never changes for plural. mahu is the standard word for "want"; in speech you will also hear nak (spoken).

Unit 8 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|8.source_text: 説明：数・助数詞・名詞の順です：dua ekor ikan（魚2匹）。助数詞は数えるものの種類を表します：動物は ekor、小さくて丸いものは biji、細長いものは batang、衣類や紙は helai、花は kuntum、対のものは pasang、人は orang、大きいものや一般のものは buah。名詞は複数でも形が変わりません。「ほしい」の標準の語は mahu で、話し言葉では nak も聞きます。

Unit 8 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|9.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese has the same idea (匹, 個, 枚, 本) but puts the number and counter after the noun (魚を二匹); Malay puts them before it. Japanese counters change sound (一本, 二本, 三本); a Malay counter never changes.

Unit 8 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|10.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語にも同じ考え方（匹・個・枚・本）がありますが、数と助数詞は名詞のあとに置きます（魚を二匹）。マレー語は名詞の前です。日本語の助数詞は音が変わります（一本・二本・三本）が、マレー語の助数詞は形が変わりません。

Unit 8 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|0.source_text: Explanation: se- joins "one" to the counter: sehelai = satu helai, sebatang = satu batang. It works with every counter: seekor, sebiji, sebuah, sebatang, sehelai, sekeping, sepucuk, sekuntum, sepasang, seulas, senaskhah, sebungkus, secawan, sepinggan, semangkuk, sebotol, setin, sekotak and seorang. Say sehelai baju or satu helai baju: both are right and you will hear both. The noun follows: sehelai baju. Use se- only for "one"; for two or more say the number and the counter: dua helai baju. Three of them, seekor, sebiji and sebuah, are also whole words in the ledger.

Unit 8 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|1.source_text: 説明：se- は「1」と助数詞をひとつにします：sehelai = satu helai、sebatang = satu batang。どの助数詞にも使えます：seekor・sebiji・sebuah・sebatang・sehelai・sekeping・sepucuk・sekuntum・sepasang・seulas・senaskhah・sebungkus・secawan・sepinggan・semangkuk・sebotol・setin・sekotak・seorang。sehelai baju でも satu helai baju でも正しく、どちらもよく聞きます。名詞はそのあとに続きます：sehelai baju。se- は「1」のときだけ使い、2つ以上は数と助数詞で言います：dua helai baju。seekor・sebiji・sebuah の三つは台帳ではひとつの語としても載っています。

Unit 8 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|2.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 一匹, 一枚, 一本 fuse the number and the counter, and so does Malay: se- is the Malay 一 fused to the counter. The order is the difference: Japanese puts it after the noun (卵を一個), Malay before it (sebiji telur). Malay se- only ever means one; Japanese changes the sound of the counter for other numbers (一本, 二本, 三本).

Unit 8 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|3.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「一匹・一枚・一本」も数と助数詞がひとつになりますが、マレー語の se- はそれにあたる「一」です。違いは語順で、日本語は名詞のあと（卵を一個）、マレー語は名詞の前（sebiji telur）です。マレー語の se- は「1」の意味だけで、日本語のように助数詞の音が数によって変わる（一本・二本・三本）ことはありません。

Unit 8 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|12.source_text: Explanation: berapa before a counter asks how many: Berapa biji telur? The answer is a number and the counter: Sepuluh biji. berapa on its own asks a price or a plain number (chapter 3): Berapa harga? The counter is what makes it a count. At a restaurant door the staff ask Berapa orang? (how many people?) and you answer Tiga orang.

Unit 8 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|0.source_text: 説明：助数詞の前の berapa は「いくつ」をたずねます：Berapa biji telur? 答えは数と助数詞です：Sepuluh biji. 助数詞のない berapa は値段や数だけをたずねます（第3章）：Berapa harga? 助数詞が付くと「数」の質問になります。レストランの入口では Berapa orang?（何名様？）とたずねられ、Tiga orang. と答えます。

Unit 8 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|1.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese asks with 何 + counter (何個, 何匹, 何枚, 何名); Malay asks with berapa + counter. The order is the same, question word first. Japanese puts it after the noun (卵は何個?), Malay before the noun.

Unit 8 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|2.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語は「何」＋助数詞（何個・何匹・何枚・何名）でたずね、マレー語は berapa ＋助数詞でたずねます。疑問語が先に来る順は同じです。日本語は名詞のあと（卵は何個？）、マレー語は名詞の前です。

Unit 8 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|11.source_text: Explanation: To give the price of one, say the amount first and then se- and the counter: lima ringgit sekuntum (five ringgit a flower), lima puluh sen sebiji (fifty sen an egg). To ask, put berapa before it: berapa sekuntum? satu + counter works too: lima ringgit satu kuntum. semua means all or everything, and Berapa harga semua? asks for the total. The answer begins with Semua: Semua dua puluh ringgit.

Unit 8 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|12.source_text: 説明：1つあたりの値段は、金額が先で、そのあとに se- と助数詞を言います：lima ringgit sekuntum（花1輪5リンギット）、lima puluh sen sebiji（卵1個50セン）。たずねるときは前に berapa を置きます：berapa sekuntum? satu ＋ 助数詞でも言えます：lima ringgit satu kuntum。semua は「全部」で、Berapa harga semua? は合計をたずねます。答えは Semua で始まります：Semua dua puluh ringgit.

Unit 8 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|13.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese says 1個50セン, counter first; Malay says the price first: lima puluh sen sebiji. The total is 全部で in Japanese and Semua in Malay, both at the start.

Unit 8 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|14.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語は「1個50セン」と助数詞が先ですが、マレー語は lima puluh sen sebiji と値段が先です。合計は日本語の「全部で」にあたる Semua を文の初めに置きます。

Unit 8 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|7.source_text: Explanation: At a stall you hear Makan sini atau bungkus? (eat here or take away?). To take food away say Tolong bungkus and the amount: Tolong bungkus dua roti canai. tolong (please, help me) goes in front of the verb. To order more, say Tambah (add): Tambah satu lagi. means one more. At a stall people usually drop the counter and say dua teh tarik or mi goreng satu: that is everyday speech. The careful form is dua cawan teh tarik and sepinggan mi goreng. In speech tapau is another word for bungkus (spoken). At a gerai you may see pisang goreng; the everyday name is goreng pisang.

Unit 8 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|8.source_text: 説明：店では Makan sini atau bungkus?（店内ですか、持ち帰りですか）とたずねられます。持ち帰りは Tolong bungkus と量で言います：Tolong bungkus dua roti canai. tolong（お願いします）は動詞の前に置きます。追加で頼むときは Tambah（足す）を使います：Tambah satu lagi. は「もう一つ」の意味です。店では助数詞を落として dua teh tarik や mi goreng satu と言うのがふつうで、これは日常の話し言葉です。ていねいな形は dua cawan teh tarik、sepinggan mi goreng です。話し言葉では tapau も bungkus と同じ意味で使います。gerai（屋台）では pisang goreng と書いてあることがあり、日常の呼び方は goreng pisang です。

Unit 8 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|9.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese also drops the counter when ordering (ラーメン二つ, コーヒーひとつ) and puts the number after the noun. Malay stalls say teh tarik dua or dua teh tarik; both orders are heard. 持ち帰り is a noun in Japanese; Malay uses the verb bungkus. 追加で (「もう一つ追加で」) matches Tambah satu lagi.

Unit 8 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|10.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語でも注文のときは助数詞を省いたり簡単にしたりして、数を名詞のあとに置きます（ラーメン二つ、コーヒーひとつ）。マレーシアの屋台でも teh tarik dua と dua teh tarik のどちらも聞きます。日本語の「持ち帰り」は名詞ですが、マレー語では動詞 bungkus を使います。「もう一つ追加で」にあたるのが Tambah satu lagi です。

Unit 8 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|1.source_text: Pattern IDs are the Kata-Kata chapter 8 frames, one pattern for each of f01 to f05. Explanations and Japanese comparisons are drafts.

Unit 8 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|2.source_text: Pattern 1: the counter sits between the number and the noun. If a learner puts the number after the noun (Japanese order), model dua ekor ikan again. Accept nak in pair work, as spoken.

Unit 8 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|3.source_text: Pattern 2: se- + any counter is normal Malay (Sam, 12 Nov 2026). Drill it with every counter, beside satu + counter, and accept both as right. se- is for "one" only; two or more is the number and the counter.

Unit 8 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|4.source_text: Pattern 3: berapa + counter asks a count; berapa alone asks a price. Ask Berapa harga? and Berapa biji? one after the other.

Unit 8 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|5.source_text: Pattern 4: price first, then the counter: lima ringgit satu kuntum. semua starts the total.

Unit 8 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|6.source_text: Pattern 5: at a stall the counter is often dropped; accept dua teh tarik as everyday speech and model dua cawan teh tarik. Tambah satu lagi adds one more. tapau is everyday speech.

Say each sentence again with the marker or time cue in brackets. The verb, the number and the counter never change; only the marker does. / かっこ内のマーカーか時の言葉を付けて言い直します。動詞・数・助数詞は変わらず、前に付く語だけが変わります。
■ Say it with the marker · マーカーを付けて言う
1. Saya beli dua ekor ikan. (marker: sudah)
2. Dia bayar semua. (marker: belum)
3. Ada tiga botol air. (marker: masih)
4. Saya beli seekor ayam. (time cue: esok, marker: akan)
5. Mereka beli sebuah kereta. (time cue: semalam)
6. Dia beli satu pasang kasut. (marker: baru)
7. Answer Sudah bayar? (marker: belum)
8. Kami ambil dua botol air. (time cue: nanti, marker: akan)
■ Japanese bridge · 日本語との橋渡し
sudah beli ≈ もう買った · belum bayar ≈ まだ払っていない · masih ada ≈ まだある · akan beli ≈ 買う予定
Japanese changes the verb (買う / 買った); Malay keeps beli and changes only the marker or the time word. / 日本語は動詞が変わりますが、マレー語は beli のままで、前の語だけが変わります。
Answers in order:
1 Saya sudah beli dua ekor ikan. 2 Dia belum bayar semua. 3 Masih ada tiga botol air. 4 Esok saya akan beli seekor ayam.
target_spans: Saya sudah beli dua ekor ikan.

Chapters 1 to 8: apa / siapa / di mana / Siapakah (-kah) / Apakah (-kah) / di manakah (-kah) / Adakah / Bolehkah / berapa / bila / pukul berapa / hari apa / bagaimana (spoken: macam mana) / kenapa (= mengapa, apa sebab; answer: sebab or kerana) / yang mana / ke mana / dari mana / berapa jauh / berapa lama / berapa with a counter (Berapa biji?)

New in chapter 8: berapa with a counter, to ask how many of a thing: Berapa biji telur? (answer with a number and the counter: Sepuluh biji.), Berapa ekor?, Berapa orang?. berapa alone still asks the price or a number (chapter 3); with a counter it asks for a count. Chapter 7 added ke mana, dari mana, berapa jauh and berapa lama; chapter 6 added yang mana (which one) with pilih in the answer. / 第8章で増えた疑問語：数える語（助数詞）の付いた berapa。ものがいくつあるかをたずねます：Berapa biji telur?（数と助数詞で答える：Sepuluh biji.）、Berapa ekor?、Berapa orang?。助数詞のない berapa は、これまでどおり値段や数をたずねます（第3章）。第7章の ke mana・dari mana・berapa jauh・berapa lama と、第6章の yang mana も引き続き使います。
1. Ask a friend how they are. (apa)
2. Ask who is at the stall. (siapa)
3. Ask where the market is. (di mana)
4. Ask formally whether this fish is fresh. (Adakah)
5. Ask politely whether you may try a shirt. (Bolehkah)
6. Ask the price of a box of tissues. (berapa)
7. Ask when the stall opens. (bila)
8. Ask what time you go to the market. (pukul berapa)
9. Ask what day your friend goes to the market. (hari apa)
10. Ask how the roti canai is. (bagaimana; spoken macam mana)
11. Ask why a friend does not buy the fish. (kenapa; also mengapa or apa sebab; the answer starts with sebab or kerana)
12. Ask which shirt your friend likes. (yang mana)
13. Ask where your friend is going. (ke mana)
14. Ask where these eggs come from. (dari mana)
15. Ask how far the market is. (berapa jauh)
16. Ask how long it takes to walk to the market. (berapa lama)
17. Ask how many eggs your friend wants. (berapa with a counter)

Unit 8 · Culture and usage note|2|0.source_text: Read about how things are counted and ordered in Malaysia. Word-building notes come only from Kata-Kata card notes.

Unit 8 · Culture and usage note|3|0.source_text: Malay counters, penjodoh bilangan, are the small words between a number and a noun: dua ekor ikan, tiga helai baju. For "one", Malay joins se- to the counter: sehelai baju, sekeping roti, secawan teh, sebungkus nasi lemak. satu helai baju means the same. Both forms are right, and you will hear both. At a stall or a mamak, people often drop the counter and just say dua teh tarik or roti canai tiga; that is everyday speech, and perfectly normal.

Unit 8 · Culture and usage note|3|1.source_text: Prices use the same words: lima ringgit sekuntum (five ringgit a flower) and lima puluh sen sebiji (fifty sen an egg). To ask how many you want, put berapa before the counter: Berapa biji telur?

Unit 8 · Culture and usage note|3|2.source_text: Kata-Kata's card notes show where some counters come from: ekor is literally "tail", biji "seed", batang "stem", helai "strand", kuntum "bud" and pucuk "shoot". pucuk and naskhah are formal counters, mostly seen in writing.

Unit 8 · Culture and usage note|3|3.source_text: At a gerai (a food or market stall) you may see nasi lemak, pisang goreng (banana fritters) and keropok lekor, a fish snack that the ledger calls a Terengganu speciality. pisang goreng is the standard order of the words, with the noun first; goreng pisang is the everyday name at the stall, and both are understood. At a food stall you will also hear Makan sini atau bungkus? (eat here or take away?); Kata-Kata's card for it says it is heard at every food stall. In speech many people say tapau for bungkus.

Unit 8 · Culture and usage note|3|5.source_text: マレー語の助数詞（penjodoh bilangan）は、数と名詞のあいだに入る小さな語です：dua ekor ikan、tiga helai baju。「1」のときは助数詞に se- を付けます：sehelai baju、sekeping roti、secawan teh、sebungkus nasi lemak。satu helai baju も正しく、どちらもよく聞きます。屋台やママック（mamak）の店では、助数詞を落として dua teh tarik や roti canai tiga と言うことがよくあります。これは日常の話し言葉で、ごく普通の言い方です。

Unit 8 · Culture and usage note|3|6.source_text: 値段にも同じ語を使います：lima ringgit sekuntum（花1輪5リンギット）、lima puluh sen sebiji（卵1個50セン）。いくつほしいかをたずねるときは、助数詞の前に berapa を置きます：Berapa biji telur?

Unit 8 · Culture and usage note|3|7.source_text: Kata-Kata のカード注記が、助数詞のなりたちをいくつか示しています：ekor は文字どおり「しっぽ」、biji は「種」、batang は「茎」、helai は「ひとすじ」、kuntum は「つぼみ」、pucuk は「新芽」です。pucuk と naskhah は改まった助数詞で、おもに書き言葉で見かけます。

Unit 8 · Culture and usage note|4|0.source_text: gerai（食べ物や市場の屋台）では、nasi lemak、pisang goreng（揚げバナナ）、keropok lekor などを見かけます。keropok lekor は魚のすり身のおやつで、台帳ではトレンガヌ名物とされています。pisang goreng が名詞を先に置く標準の語順で、屋台での日常の呼び方は goreng pisang です。どちらも通じます。食べ物の屋台では Makan sini atau bungkus?（店内ですか、持ち帰りですか）ともたずねられます。Kata-Kata の該当カードには、どの屋台でも聞くと書かれています。話し言葉では bungkus の代わりに tapau と言う人も多くいます。

Unit 8 · Culture and usage note|5|1.source_text: Sources: Sam's brief of 12 Nov 2026 (the counter is often dropped in everyday speech: Mi goreng satu, dua epal; the careful form keeps it) and Sam's answers of 12 Nov 2026 (se- + any counter is normal Malay; pucuk and naskhah are formal counters mostly seen in writing; tapau is everyday speech; Journal rows 75 to 80); Kata-Kata chapter 8 cards ms-c08-002 (ekor, lit. tail), -004 (biji, lit. seed), -005 (batang, lit. stem), -006 (helai, lit. strand), -008 (pucuk, lit. shoot), -009 (kuntum, lit. bud), and ms-c08-043 (Makan sini atau bungkus?, note: "Heard at every food stall"); ledger L-0937 (tapau, to take away, Dunia "Lepak di kedai mamak"); ledger L-1068 (Sam's note: pisang goreng follows the Malay noun-then-modifier order and is standard, goreng pisang is the everyday name; Journal row 77, which records a Sinar Harian column on Peraturan D-M and recipe sites, not reopened in this session); ledger L-1069 (the gloss: a Terengganu speciality). The note makes no claim about any real stall, price or law; the practice stalls, prices and names are fictional.
