Unit 8 · Teaching plan and answer key|3|.source_text: Before Block A: Kata-Kata Sedia Kelas c08 (14 cards, frames ms-c08-f01 and ms-c08-f02).
Before Block E: Kata-Kata Dunia scenes "Beli baju"; learners only need to recognise the scene words.

After Block D: the Kata-Kata chapter 8 deck with spaced review, frames ms-c08-f01, ms-c08-f02, ms-c08-f03, ms-c08-f04, ms-c08-f05 in the frame drill and Susun Ayat; about 3 hours of self-study for this unit (planning figure).
Hanashishou starts at A2, so there is no Hanashishou scene for this unit. Listening uses the teacher-read script.
■ Block A · Words and patterns (45 min)
Goal: I can say how many of something I want with a number, a counter and the noun, and say "one" with se- and the counter (sehelai, secawan) or satu and the counter.
0–5 Recall: chapter 7 (asking the way to the market) from the opener prompts.
5–10 Tanya Cikgu questions from Kata-Kata.
10–20 Vocabulary focus: core words first; Dunia and revision words are only pointed out.

20–40 Pattern focus: patterns 1 and 2, question and answer first, rule second; teach the classifiers with their se- forms in Block A, the containers, the things counted and the gerai words in Block B, not all in one sitting.
40–45 First substitutions (Drill 2, items 1 to 3).
■ Block B · Drills and conversation (45 min)
Goal: I can ask Berapa biji? or Berapa ekor?, ask and give the price of one and of everything, order Tolong bungkus …, add Tambah satu lagi, or eat here.
0–5 Recall: count three things in the room: Ada tiga batang pen.
5–25 Drill ladder in order: pattern table, substitution, transformation, question and answer, question-word choice, short dialogues, then the markers drill.
25–40 Model conversation, gapped form, then the changed-facts variant.
40–45 Pair rehearsal without the script.
■ Block C · Listening and task (45 min)
Goal: I can follow a market order and a price board and write a short order.
0–5 Recall: learners order two things at an imaginary stall: Saya mahu dua ekor ikan.
5–20 Listening: read the questions, two readings, check, then shadow three lines.
20–30 Reading and writing.
30–45 Task with role cards; announce the change of plan halfway.

Unit 8 · Teaching plan and answer key|4|.source_text: Goal: I can check counters, containers and se- forms in a short test.
0–15 Mixed review: cumulative question-word drill (chapters 1 to 8, including berapa with a counter), then the markers drill with new cues.
35–45 Preview: chapter 9 (the passive, signs and notices): set the Kata-Kata chapter 9 Sedia Kelas cards and frames ms-c09-f01 and ms-c09-f02 before the next class.
Goal: I can recognise the clothes-shop words in the Kata-Kata Dunia scene "Beli baju" and count shirts and shoes with the right counter.
0–5 Recall: order a drink, then a plate of food, with the careful form and the everyday form.
5–15 Kata-Kata Dunia scenes "Beli baju" as listening (teacher reads, learners point to pictures or words).
15–30 Role-play of the scene in pairs.
30–40 Free variation: a pair role-play in a clothes shop: A asks for two shirts and a pair of shoes, B asks the size; they change the colour.
■ What to listen for · 注意点

Load: 41 core words in five groups (classifiers 14; containers and portions 7; the things counted 12; the gerai 5; semua, tolong and Makan sini atau bungkus? 3), plus 11 Dunia recognition words. It is the heaviest unit after unit 7. Suggested order: Block A the classifiers with their se- forms; Block B the containers and portions, the things counted and the gerai words; Block C the shopping and ordering scenes; Block D and E recycle them. If the pilot shows 41 is too many, the natural cut is A/B: ekor, biji, batang, helai, orang, buah, seekor, sebiji, sebuah, the containers, semua, tolong and tambah first; keping, pucuk, kuntum, pasang, ulas, naskhah and the gerai foods second.

se- + any counter is normal Malay and is the chapter 8 pattern (Sam, 12 Nov 2026; this corrects the step 5f brief). Teach and drill it with every counter, beside satu + counter: sehelai baju = satu helai baju. Accept both as right. se- means "one" only. seekor, sebiji and sebuah are also whole ledger words (L-0360 to L-0362).

Earlier units deliberately avoided counters. Unit 3B has dua epal and unit 5 has Mi goreng satu and roti canai dua; these are everyday speech and stay as they are. This unit shows the counter form beside them: dua biji epal, sepinggan mi goreng. Do not correct the earlier units.

Unit 8 · Teaching plan and answer key|5|.source_text: Register (Sam, 12 Nov 2026): pucuk and naskhah are formal counters, mostly seen in writing; tapau is everyday speech; nak is spoken for mahu. pisang goreng is standard and goreng pisang is the everyday name (ledger L-1068). Do not mark goreng pisang as an error.

Counter cards in the Kata-Kata chapter 8 deck that the ledger placed earlier: orang (card ms-c08-001, ledger chapter 2, now with the counter sense in its note). The Kata-Kata card ms-c08-010 kaki (counter: umbrellas) was removed in the clean-up because kaki is not a counter (Sam: too rare). The counter buah is ledger row L-1067 and its card now points there; buah as fruit stays L-0514.

Scenes: a fish, egg and chicken stall at a morning market, a flower stall, a gerai (nasi lemak, pisang goreng, keropok lekor, teh tarik) and a mamak stall. All stalls, prices and names are fictional. No food rules or religious expressions are taught; ask Sam before adding any.
"Beli baju" is for recognition. The clothes words are labels; the size and fit sentences (Saiz berapa?, Baju ini ketat., Boleh saya cuba baju ini?) are chunks to recognise and say, not new grammar.
Cumulative question words now include berapa with a counter (chapters 1 to 8). Chapter 9 adds no new question word; siapa returns in the passive.

Unit 8 · Teaching plan and answer key|6|.source_text: Answer keys are on each component. Japanese text awaits native review.
Standard forms first; spoken forms are labelled. No productive ber- or me- verbs (root verbs only).

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|7.source_text: Explanation: In a di- sentence the thing comes first and the doer comes after oleh: Kek ini dibuat oleh isteri saya. (This cake was made by my wife.) To ask who did it, put siapa after oleh: dibuat oleh siapa? If the doer is not important, leave oleh and the doer out: Kek ini dibuat. The verb is the root with di- in front, and it never changes for who or when. In everyday speech the active sentence uses the bare root: Isteri saya buat kek ini. tadi marks a time that has just passed: pagi tadi (this morning).
target_spans: Kek ini dibuat oleh isteri saya.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|8.source_text: 説明：di- の文では、物が先に来て、動作主は oleh のあとに置きます：Kek ini dibuat oleh isteri saya.（このケーキは妻が作りました）。誰がしたかをたずねるときは oleh のあとに siapa を置きます：dibuat oleh siapa? 動作主が大事でなければ、oleh と動作主をはぶきます：Kek ini dibuat. 動詞は語根の前に di- を付けた形で、誰が・いつしたかで形が変わりません。日常会話の能動文では語根をそのまま使います：Isteri saya buat kek ini. tadi は少し前に過ぎた時を表します：pagi tadi（けさ）。
target_spans: Kek ini dibuat oleh isteri saya.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|9.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 受身 (作られた, 買われた) often carries a feeling that someone was affected. The Malay di- passive is neutral: it simply puts the thing first, and it is very common in everyday speech, not just in writing. The doer comes after oleh, like に / によって in 妻によって作られた, but oleh is easier to leave out than the Japanese に.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|10.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の受身（作られた・買われた）には、誰かが影響を受けた気持ちがこもることがよくあります。マレー語の di- は中立で、物を先に出すだけです。書き言葉だけでなく日常会話でもとてもよく使います。動作主は oleh のあとに置き、「妻によって作られた」の「によって」にあたりますが、oleh は日本語の「に」よりはぶきやすい語です。

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|13.source_text: 1. A: Nasi lemak ini dibeli di mana? B: Dibeli di gerai dekat stesen.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|14.source_text: 2. A: Surat khabar dijual di mana? B: Surat khabar dijual di kedai itu.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|2.source_text: Explanation: After a di- verb you can add where: Nasi lemak ini dibeli di gerai. The place word di is the preposition you know from chapter 2; do not confuse it with the di- that is stuck to the verb (dibeli). Ask dibeli di mana? for where and dihantar ke mana? for where to. You can use di- with any root verb you already know, not only the 18 on the list: digoreng (fried), dipilih (chosen), ditunggu (waited for), dijemput (invited), ditanya (asked). Only roots that are verbs work this way.
target_spans: Nasi lemak ini dibeli di gerai.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|3.source_text: 説明：di- の動詞のあとに場所を足せます：Nasi lemak ini dibeli di gerai. 場所を表す di は第2章で学んだ前置詞で、動詞にくっついた di-（dibeli）とは別のものです。場所は dibeli di mana?、行き先は dihantar ke mana? とたずねます。di- は一覧の18語だけでなく、すでに知っている動詞の語根ならどれにでも付けられます：digoreng（揚げられた）、dipilih（選ばれた）、ditunggu（待たれた）、dijemput（招かれた）、ditanya（たずねられた）。動詞の語根だけがこのように使えます。
target_spans: Nasi lemak ini dibeli di gerai.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|4.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese marks the place with で (市場で買われた) after the noun; Malay puts di and the place after the verb (dibeli di gerai). Because Malay verbs do not conjugate, you only learn the root once: beli becomes dibeli, goreng becomes digoreng.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|5.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語は名詞のあとに「で」を付けて場所を表します（市場で買われた）が、マレー語は動詞のあとに di と場所を置きます（dibeli di gerai）。マレー語の動詞は活用しないので、語根を一度覚えれば足ります：beli → dibeli、goreng → digoreng。

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|7.source_text: Pattern box: ___ sudah / belum di-(verb). / ___ sudah saya (verb).

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|8.source_text: 1. A: Teh tarik sudah diminum? B: Sudah. Teh tarik sudah diminum semua.
target_spans: Sudah. Teh tarik sudah diminum semua.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|9.source_text: 2. A: Harga sudah dibayar? B: Belum. Harga belum dibayar.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|10.source_text: 3. A: Kek sudah dimakan? B: Belum. Kek belum dimakan.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|11.source_text: 4. A: Surat sudah dihantar? B: Sudah. Surat dihantar semalam.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|12.source_text: 5. A: Pinggan sudah dicuci? B: Belum. Pinggan saya bawa ke dapur.
target_spans: Belum. Pinggan saya bawa ke dapur.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|13.source_text: 6. A: Pintu sudah ditutup? B: Belum. Pintu masih dibuka.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|0.source_text: Explanation: Put sudah (already) or belum (not yet) in front of the di- verb: Teh tarik sudah diminum. Pintu masih dibuka (still open) and Pintu akan ditutup (will be closed) use the chapter 4 markers in the same place. When you did it yourself, the doer goes straight in front of the verb and di- drops away: Pinggan saya bawa ke dapur. (I will take the plates to the kitchen.) Kek saya beli. (I bought the cake.) This is Kata-Kata frame f06: the thing, then the doer, then the verb; it works with saya, awak, kami or a name.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|1.source_text: 説明：di- の動詞の前に sudah（もう）か belum（まだ）を置きます：Teh tarik sudah diminum. 第4章のマーカーも同じ位置です：Pintu masih dibuka（まだ開いている）、Pintu akan ditutup（閉められる予定）。自分でするときは、動作主を動詞の直前に置き、di- は付けません：Pinggan saya bawa ke dapur.（お皿は私が台所へ持っていきます）、Kek saya beli.（ケーキは私が買いました）。Kata-Kata の文型 f06（物、動作主、動詞の順）にあたり、saya・awak・kami や名前で使えます。

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|2.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese もう / まだ…ていない map to sudah / belum and the Japanese verb changes (食べられた / 食べられていない). In Malay only the marker changes: sudah dimakan, belum dimakan. The "I did it myself" form is close to Japanese はから topic order: ケーキは私が買った = Kek saya beli.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|3.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「もう」「まだ…ていない」は sudah / belum にあたり、日本語は動詞が変わります（食べられた / 食べられていない）。マレー語は前の語だけが変わります：sudah dimakan、belum dimakan。「自分でした」形は日本語の「は…が」の語順に近く、「ケーキは私が買った」＝Kek saya beli. です。

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|5.source_text: Pattern box: Kedai ini dibuka / ditutup pada pukul ___.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|6.source_text: 1. A: Kedai ini dibuka pada pukul berapa? B: Kedai ini dibuka pada pukul sembilan pagi.
target_spans: Kedai ini dibuka pada pukul berapa?
Kedai ini dibuka pada pukul sembilan pagi.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|7.source_text: 2. A: Pejabat ditutup pada pukul berapa? B: Ditutup pada pukul enam petang.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|8.source_text: 3. A: Bank dibuka pada pukul berapa? B: Dibuka pada pukul sepuluh pagi.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|9.source_text: 4. A: Jamuan itu pada pukul berapa? B: Pada pukul lima petang.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|10.source_text: 5. A: Kedai dibuka pada hari Ahad? B: Tidak. Kedai ditutup pada hari Ahad.
target_spans: Tidak. Kedai ditutup pada hari Ahad.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|11.source_text: 6. A: Pasar dibuka pada hari apa? B: Pasar dibuka pada hari Sabtu.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|12.source_text: Explanation: dibuka and ditutup are what shops and offices say about their hours: Pejabat dibuka pada pukul sembilan. pada goes in front of a time or a day: pada pukul sembilan, pada hari Sabtu. In speech people often drop it (dibuka pukul sembilan); a sign or a notice keeps it. Ask pada pukul berapa? (at what time?) or pada hari apa? (on what day?).

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|0.source_text: 説明：dibuka（開いている）と ditutup（閉まっている）は、店や事務所が営業時間を言うときの言い方です：Pejabat dibuka pada pukul sembilan. pada は時刻や曜日の前に置きます：pada pukul sembilan、pada hari Sabtu。話すときは省くことも多い（dibuka pukul sembilan）ですが、掲示や案内では省きません。たずねるときは pada pukul berapa?（何時に）、pada hari apa?（何曜日に）です。

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|1.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 9時に開きます uses に after the time; Malay pada comes before it. Japanese says 開く / 閉まる with a plain verb; Malay says dibuka / ditutup ("is opened", "is closed"), which is exactly what a shop sign says.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|2.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「9時に開きます」は時刻のあとに「に」を付けますが、マレー語の pada は時刻の前です。日本語は「開く・閉まる」と普通の動詞を使いますが、マレー語は dibuka・ditutup（開けられる・閉められる）で、店の掲示そのままの言い方です。

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|5.source_text: 1. A: Papan tanda ini apa? B: Dilarang masuk.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|6.source_text: 2. A: Boleh makan di sini? B: Tidak boleh. Dilarang makan dan minum.
target_spans: Tidak boleh. Dilarang makan dan minum.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|7.source_text: 3. A: Boleh masuk? B: Boleh. Sila masuk.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|8.source_text: 4. A: Kenapa pintu itu ditutup? B: Sebab dilarang masuk.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|9.source_text: 5. A: Pintu ini tolak atau tarik? B: Tarik, bukan tolak.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|10.source_text: 6. A: Kedai itu dibuka bila? B: Ditutup hingga hari Isnin. Perhatian di pintu.
target_spans: Ditutup hingga hari Isnin. Perhatian di pintu.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|11.source_text: Explanation: Signs and notices use Dilarang (forbidden) in front of what is not allowed: Dilarang masuk. (No entry.) Dilarang makan dan minum. (No eating or drinking.) Dilarang merokok. (No smoking) is a sign to recognise only. Sila (please) in front of a verb is a polite instruction: Sila masuk. Sila duduk. A sign leaves out the doer: it says what is forbidden or welcome, not who must do it. A papan tanda is the signboard itself. A door says TOLAK (push) or TARIK (pull). A notice often opens with PERHATIAN (attention), then gives the news: Ditutup hingga hari Isnin. hingga (until) is the written word on notices and timetables (Dibuka Isnin hingga Jumaat); in speech say sampai.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|12.source_text: 説明：掲示や案内では、してはいけないことの前に Dilarang（禁止）を置きます：Dilarang masuk.（立入禁止）、Dilarang makan dan minum.（飲食禁止）。Dilarang merokok.（禁煙）は見て分かればよい掲示です。動詞の前の Sila（どうぞ）は丁寧な指示です：Sila masuk.、Sila duduk. 掲示は動作主をはぶき、禁止か歓迎かだけを書きます。papan tanda は看板そのものです。ドアには TOLAK（押す）か TARIK（引く）と書いてあります。掲示は PERHATIAN（注意）で始まり、そのあとに知らせが続くことが多いです：Ditutup hingga hari Isnin. hingga（〜まで）は掲示や時刻表で使う書き言葉で、話すときは sampai を使います。

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|0.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese signs say 立入禁止 and 禁煙 with nouns; Malay uses the passive Dilarang + a verb. Sila is like どうぞ + verb, or ください in a notice (ご自由にお取りください).

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|1.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の掲示は「立入禁止」「禁煙」のように名詞で書きますが、マレー語は受け身の Dilarang ＋動詞です。Sila は「どうぞ」＋動詞にあたり、掲示の「ご自由にお取りください」の「ください」に近い言い方です。

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|0.source_text: Model each A line; learners answer as B, then swap. Explain the rule only after they have used the pattern.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|1.source_text: Pattern IDs are the Kata-Kata chapter 9 frames f01 to f05; frame f06 (the doer before the verb, no di-) sits inside pattern 3. Explanations and Japanese comparisons are drafts.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|2.source_text: Pattern 1: thing first, then oleh and the doer. If a learner puts the doer first (Japanese-style subject, Isteri saya dibuat kek), model Kek ini dibuat oleh isteri saya again. Let learners swap the doer: isteri saya, suami saya, anak saya, kawan saya. Do not teach active me- verbs: the active sentences in this unit use root verbs only, including the new roots buat, panggil, cuci and larang (Isteri saya buat kek ini.).
target_spans: Kek ini dibuat oleh isteri saya

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|3.source_text: Pattern 2: di before a place is the preposition; di- stuck to the verb makes the passive. Write both on the board. Let learners try digoreng, dipilih, ditunggu and dijemput from roots they know; correct only roots that are not verbs. A quick active-to-passive check: Gerai itu jual kuih. → Kuih dijual di gerai itu. Saya hantar surat itu. → Surat itu dihantar.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|4.source_text: Pattern 3: sudah and belum go before the di- verb; the chapter 4 markers (masih, akan, baru) take the same place. The saya + verb form (Pinggan saya bawa ke dapur) has no di-; accept it as the natural way to say "I will do it".

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|5.source_text: Pattern 4: dibuka and ditutup with pada and a time. Accept dibuka pukul sembilan in speech; a notice keeps pada. In everyday speech people also use the plain roots: Kedai buka pukul sembilan. Kedai tutup pukul enam.

Unit 9 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|6.source_text: Pattern 5: signs. Dilarang merokok is for recognition only. Let learners read the signs in the reading text aloud as if they were a guard. TOLAK and TARIK are the door signs: have learners say which way a door opens before they touch it. PERHATIAN is a whole word at the head of a notice (do not build other words from perhatian; word-building with affixes is later). hingga is the formal word on notices (Ditutup hingga hari Isnin.); sampai (chapter 4) is what people say.

Unit 9 · Culture and usage note|3|0.source_text: The Malay passive is neutral and very common. Kek ini dibuat oleh isteri saya puts the cake first and the doer after oleh. When the doer does not matter, it is simply left out: Pejabat ditutup pada pukul enam. Japanese 受身 often carries a feeling of being affected; the Malay di- passive does not. It is how people talk about food, shops, mail and rules every day.
target_spans: Kek ini dibuat oleh isteri saya

Unit 9 · Culture and usage note|3|1.source_text: Signs and notices use the same form without saying who: Dilarang masuk (no entry), Dilarang makan dan minum. Sila before a verb is a polite instruction: Sila masuk. Dilarang merokok is a sign to recognise only; the Kata-Kata card note says it contains a me- verb. Doors say TOLAK or TARIK, and a notice may begin PERHATIAN and end Ditutup hingga ….

Unit 9 · Culture and usage note|3|2.source_text: Kata-Kata's card notes name the roots: dibuat is di- + buat, dicuci is di- + cuci (wash), dipanggil comes from panggil (call) and dilarang from larang (forbid). In everyday speech the roots work alone: Saya cuci pinggan. The note on jamuan says jamu (treat a guest) → jamuan. With a root verb you already know, you can make a new one: digoreng, dipilih, ditunggu.

Unit 9 · Culture and usage note|3|3.source_text: When you do something yourself, the doer goes straight in front of the verb and di- drops away: Pinggan saya bawa ke dapur. (Kek saya beli.) This is Kata-Kata frame f06. In the open-house scene of Block E, the notes for each festival are on a separate sheet.

Unit 9 · Culture and usage note|3|5.source_text: マレー語の受け身は中立で、とてもよく使われます。Kek ini dibuat oleh isteri saya はケーキを先に出し、動作主を oleh のあとに置きます。動作主が大事でないときは、単にはぶきます：Pejabat ditutup pada pukul enam. 日本語の受身には「影響を受けた」気持ちがこもることがよくありますが、マレー語の di- にはありません。食べ物、店、郵便、決まりごとを毎日の会話で話すときの言い方です。
target_spans: Kek ini dibuat oleh isteri saya

Unit 9 · Culture and usage note|3|6.source_text: 掲示や案内も、誰がするかを言わずに同じ形を使います：Dilarang masuk（立入禁止）、Dilarang makan dan minum。動詞の前の Sila は丁寧な指示です：Sila masuk。Dilarang merokok は見て分かればよい掲示で、Kata-Kata のカード注記によると me- の動詞を含みます。ドアには TOLAK か TARIK と書かれ、掲示は PERHATIAN で始まり Ditutup hingga … で終わることがあります。

Unit 9 · Culture and usage note|3|7.source_text: Kata-Kata のカード注記が語根を示しています：dibuat は di- ＋ buat、dicuci は di- ＋ cuci（洗う）、dipanggil は panggil（呼ぶ）、dilarang は larang（禁じる）から来ています。日常会話では語根だけでも使います：Saya cuci pinggan.jamuan の注記には jamu（客をもてなす）→ jamuan とあります。すでに知っている動詞の語根から、新しい語を作れます：digoreng、dipilih、ditunggu。

Unit 9 · Culture and usage note|3|8.source_text: 自分でするときは、動作主を動詞の直前に置き、di- は付けません：Pinggan saya bawa ke dapur.（Kek saya beli.）。これは Kata-Kata の文型 f06 です。ブロックEの rumah terbuka の場面で出てくる行事ごとのメモは、別のシートにあります。

Unit 9 · Culture note · Open houses in M.source_text: rumah terbuka の場面で出てくる行事ごとに、短い文化メモを読みます。宗教の授業ではなく、マレーシアの習慣の紹介です。
（日本語は下書きです。ネイティブ・スピーカーの確認待ち）
No Malay explainer for Stage 1 units: explainers and rubrics are in Japanese or English (Sam, 11 Nov 2026). Select 日本語 or English.
Read a short note for each festival in the general rumah terbuka scene. It is culture, not a religious lesson.

A rumah terbuka (open house) is a gathering where the host (tuan rumah) welcomes relatives, friends, neighbours and colleagues during a festival, and people of other communities are often invited too. Guests hear Jemput masuk and Mari makan (spoken: Jom makan). It is culture, not a lesson in belief. Greetings: Selamat Hari Raya, Selamat Tahun Baru Cina (no Hari), Selamat Hari Deepavali, Selamat Hari Krismas, Selamat Hari Gawai and Selamat Pesta Kaamatan (Bernama, 30 May 2026). The fuller formal greeting is Selamat Menyambut Pesta Kaamatan (a me- verb, shown only as a quotation).

Hari Raya (the festival at the end of Ramadan): Kata-Kata lists ketupat, rendang and kuih as the food, duit raya as the money gift for children, pelita as oil lamps, baju Melayu as the men's outfit and balik kampung for going back to your hometown. Maaf zahir dan batin asks forgiveness for past wrongs.

Tahun Baru Cina (Chinese New Year) is the everyday name; Tahun Baharu Cina is the official one, in the federal public-holiday list. Open houses are widely held, and guides list angpau (red packets with money; English-language newspapers often write "ang pow") among the customs.
Deepavali (the Hindu festival of lights): newspapers list Deepavali open houses for all Malaysians, with families welcoming Malay and Chinese friends and neighbours.
Krismas (Christmas) is celebrated by Malaysia's Christian communities.

Gawai (Sarawak, 1 June) and Kaamatan (Sabah and Labuan, 30 and 31 May) are harvest festivals and public holidays there. Gawai was gazetted as a holiday on 25 September 1964 and first celebrated on 1 June 1965. The communities' own greetings are not Malay, so they are not taught here.
■ 日本語

rumah terbuka（オープンハウス）は、行事のときに主催者（tuan rumah）が親戚、友人、近所の人、同僚を迎える集まりで、別の民族の人もよく招かれます。客は Jemput masuk・Mari makan（話し言葉：Jom makan）と声をかけられます。これは文化の紹介であり、信仰の授業ではありません。挨拶：Selamat Hari Raya、Selamat Tahun Baru Cina（Hari は付けない）、Selamat Hari Deepavali、Selamat Hari Krismas、Selamat Hari Gawai、Selamat Pesta Kaamatan（ベルナマ通信、2026年5月30日）。より改まった形は Selamat Menyambut Pesta Kaamatan（me- の動詞を含むため、引用として示すだけ）。
Hari Raya（断食明けのお祭り）：Kata-Kata は、食べ物として ketupat・rendang・kuih、子どもへの贈り物として duit raya、pelita は灯油ランプ、男性の装いとして baju Melayu、故郷へ帰ることを balik kampung と挙げています。Maaf zahir dan batin は、これまでの非礼の許しを願う言葉です。
Tahun Baru Cina（旧正月）は日常の呼び方で、Tahun Baharu Cina は連邦の祝日一覧にある公式の呼び方です。オープンハウスが広く開かれ、ガイドは angpau（お金入りの赤い封筒。英字紙では英語式のつづりで書かれることが多い）を習慣のひとつに挙げています。
Deepavali（ヒンドゥー教の光のお祭り）：新聞はすべてのマレーシア人に開かれたディーパバリのオープンハウスを紹介し、家族がマレー系や中華系の友人や近所の人を迎える様子も報じています。
Krismas（クリスマス）はマレーシアのキリスト教徒の人々が祝います。
Gawai（サラワク州、6月1日）と Kaamatan（サバ州とラブアン、5月30日と31日）は収穫祭で、その地域の祝日です。Gawai は1964年9月25日に祝日として官報に告示され、1965年6月1日に初めて祝われました。各民族の言葉の挨拶はマレー語ではないため、ここでは教えません。

Unit 9 · Teaching plan and answer key|3|.source_text: Before Block A: Kata-Kata Sedia Kelas c09 (16 cards, frames ms-c09-f01 and ms-c09-f02).

Before Block E: Kata-Kata Dunia scenes "Rumah terbuka" and "Simpulan bahasa harian"; learners only need to recognise the scene words. The festival notes (Culture note · Open houses) are read in Block E.

After Block D: the Kata-Kata chapter 9 deck with spaced review, frames ms-c09-f01, ms-c09-f02, ms-c09-f03, ms-c09-f04, ms-c09-f05 in the frame drill and Susun Ayat; about 3 hours of self-study for this unit (planning figure).
Hanashishou starts at A2, so there is no Hanashishou scene for this unit. Listening uses the teacher-read script. The stage review and the A1 test come after this unit and wait for Sam.
■ Block A · Words and patterns (45 min)
Goal: I can say what was done with a di- verb and say who did it with oleh, and say a thing is sudah or belum done.
0–5 Recall: chapter 8 (ordering at a gerai) from the opener prompts.
10–20 Vocabulary focus: core words first; Dunia and revision words are only pointed out.

20–40 Pattern focus: patterns 1 and 2, question and answer first, rule second; teach the di- verbs in two lots of nine (making and buying, then eating, reading, opening and closing), and oleh, pada, tadi, siap in Block A; signs and the party words in Block B.
■ Block B · Drills and conversation (45 min)
Goal: I can ask dibuat oleh siapa?, dibeli di mana? and pada pukul berapa? and answer in the passive.
0–5 Recall: say what was done in the room: Pintu ditutup. Meja dicuci.
5–25 Drill ladder in order: pattern table, substitution, transformation, question and answer, question-word choice, short dialogues, then the markers drill.
25–40 Model conversation, gapped form, then the changed-facts variant.
■ Block C · Listening and task (45 min)
Goal: I can read signs and a notice board, follow a short party plan, and write a short notice.

Unit 9 · Teaching plan and answer key|4|.source_text: 0–5 Recall: learners say who made or bought something on their desk: Beg ini dibeli oleh saya.
5–20 Listening: read the questions, two readings, check, then shadow three lines.
30–45 Task with role cards; announce the change of plan halfway.
■ Block D · Review and test (45 min)
Goal: I can check the di- verbs, signs and oleh in a short test.
0–15 Mixed review: cumulative question-word drill (chapters 1 to 9, with siapa + oleh), then the markers drill with new cues.
35–45 Preview: the stage review and the A1 test come after this unit and wait for Sam; point learners to the Kata-Kata review of all nine chapters.
Goal: I can recognise the festival words in the general rumah terbuka scene and the idioms in the Dunia scene "Simpulan bahasa harian".
0–5 Recall: read two signs aloud and say who made the cake.
5–15 Kata-Kata Dunia scenes "Rumah terbuka" and "Simpulan bahasa harian" as listening (teacher reads, learners point to pictures or words).
15–30 Role-play of the scene in pairs.

30–40 Free variation: a pair role-play of a general open house: the tuan rumah chooses a festival from the notes, says Jemput masuk and Mari makan, and says who made each dish (Rendang ini dimasak oleh ibu saya.); the guest says the greeting and thanks the host; change the festival and the food.
target_spans: Rendang ini dimasak oleh ibu saya.

Unit 9 · Teaching plan and answer key|5|.source_text: Load: 42 core words in six groups (di- verbs 18; the roots buat, panggil, cuci, larang 4; oleh, pada, tadi, siap 4; signs and notices 9, including perhatian, hingga, tolak, tarik; a party and an open house: kek, jamuan, tuan rumah, mari, pesta 5; family: ibu, adik 2), plus 33 Dunia recognition words (the general rumah terbuka scene 19, the idioms 14). Suggested order: Block A the di- verbs in two lots with their roots, and oleh, pada, tadi, siap; Block B the signs, the party words and the drills; Block C the notice board and the party; Block D and E recycle them. If the pilot shows 42 is too many, the natural cut is A/B: dibuat, dibeli, dimakan, diminum, dibuka, ditutup, dibayar, dihantar, dilarang, oleh, pada, tadi, siap, sila and the signs first; dibaca, ditulis, diambil, dipanggil, dimasak, dicuci, dibawa, disewa, dijual, kek, jamuan second. The roots buat, panggil, cuci, larang go with their di- forms; tuan rumah, mari and pesta go with Block E; tolak, tarik, perhatian and hingga go with the signs in Block B; ibu and adik can wait for Block C.

The point of the chapter is di- + a root the learner already knows. The 18 ledger forms are core. Other di- + verb forms are taught as the rule (digoreng, dipilih, ditunggu, dijemput, ditanya): the language checks accept di- + any ledger word placed in chapters 1 to 9 and do not look at its part of speech, so check by hand that the root is a verb. buat, panggil, cuci and larang are ledger words since 12 Nov 2026 (Sam), so each di- form now has its root in the unit, and the transformation drill makes Kuih ini dibuat oleh ibu saya. from Ibu saya buat kuih ini. larang is mostly met inside dilarang. The active sentences use ledger root verbs only (no me- or ber-; the me- forms of these roots wait for chapter 11).
target_spans: Kuih ini dibuat oleh ibu saya.

Unit 9 · Teaching plan and answer key|5|.source_text: The saya + verb form (Pinggan saya bawa ke dapur.) is Kata-Kata frame f06. It is taught inside pattern 3 as the natural way to say "I will do it"; accept it and do not ask for oleh saya.
Dilarang merokok is a sign to recognise only (Kata-Kata card ms-c09-024: it contains a me- verb). No other sign in this unit uses me- or ber-.

Unit 9 · Teaching plan and answer key|6|.source_text: Open-house scene (Sam, 12 Nov 2026): the old "Rumah terbuka Hari Raya" scene is now a general rumah terbuka scene. The 13 Raya words stay as recognition; the festival-specific ones (maaf zahir dan batin, duit raya, ketupat, pelita) appear in the Hari Raya note, as culture, not as a religious lesson. Six festival words were added with Sam's approval (L-1070 to L-1075), and tuan rumah and mari (L-1080, L-1081) for the host and Mari makan (Jom makan is the spoken form). Greetings (Sam, 12 Nov 2026): Selamat Hari Raya, Selamat Tahun Baru Cina (no Hari), Selamat Hari Deepavali, Selamat Hari Krismas, Selamat Hari Gawai and Selamat Pesta Kaamatan (sourced: Bernama, 30 May 2026; pesta is ledger row L-1084). Show the fuller formal Selamat Menyambut Pesta Kaamatan only as a quotation: it contains a me- verb. Teach both Tahun Baru Cina (everyday) and Tahun Baharu Cina (official). No faith-specific greeting is taught. Every factual statement in the festival notes has a named source in the key.
The 14 idioms in "Simpulan bahasa harian" are for recognition. Give the plain meaning and one example; do not drill them, do not test them as new vocabulary, and do not ask learners to produce them.
Practice offices, notices, names and times are fictional. No productive ber- or me- (chapters 10 and 11). The stage review and the A1 test come after this unit and wait for Sam's go-ahead.
Cumulative question words now include siapa with oleh (chapters 1 to 9). Chapter 9 adds no new question word.

Unit 9 · Teaching plan and answer key|7|.source_text: Answer keys are on each component. Japanese text awaits native review.
Standard forms first; spoken forms are labelled. No productive ber- or me- verbs (root verbs only).

A 45-minute block reviewing chapters 1 to 9 through one real week: a new colleague's first week in Kuala Lumpur, spoken, read and written without notes, then a self-check of every Stage 1 can-do goal.
Can-do goal: I can use the language of chapters 1 to 9 together, without notes, to get through a real first week at work in Kuala Lumpur. / 第1〜9章の表現をノートなしで組み合わせ、クアラルンプールでの仕事の最初の一週間を乗り切れる。

Scene (fictional): Encik Kimura Kenji from Osaka starts work at an office in Kuala Lumpur. Puan Aini and Encik Rahman, his colleagues, and Puan Siti, the office manager, help him through his first week. All names, prices, numbers, times and places are invented. / 場面（架空）：大阪出身の木村健二さんがクアラルンプールの事務所で働き始めます。同僚のアイニさんとラーマンさん、事務所長のシティさんが最初の一週間を手伝います。名前、値段、番号、時刻、場所はすべて架空です。
Monday: greetings, introductions and a staff form (chapters 1, 2 and 3). / 月曜日：あいさつ、自己紹介、職員用の書類（第1・2・3章）。
Tuesday: lunch at a gerai — choosing, comparing, ordering with counters and paying (chapters 3, 5, 6 and 8). / 火曜日：gerai（屋台）で昼食。選ぶ、比べる、助数詞で注文する、払う（第3・5・6・8章）。
Wednesday: the meeting day — times, routines, done and not yet done (chapter 4). / 水曜日：会議の日。時刻、日課、済んだこと・まだのこと（第4章）。
Thursday: the way to the bank (chapter 7). / 木曜日：銀行への道（第7章）。
Friday: the office jamuan, the notices, and taking leave for the weekend (chapters 9 and 1). / 金曜日：事務所の jamuan（会食）、掲示、週末前のあいさつ（第9・1章）。

Ch 1: greet your partner for this time of day, with a title. / 今の時間帯のあいさつを、敬称を付けてしましょう。
Ch 2: say where you live and what your hobby is. / 住んでいる所と趣味を言いましょう。
Ch 3: say your phone number in Malay digits. / 電話番号をマレー語で言いましょう。
Ch 4: say what time you start work and one thing you do every day. / 仕事を始める時刻と、毎日することを一つ言いましょう。
Ch 5: describe the food you had yesterday. / きのう食べたものを説明しましょう。
Ch 6: compare two drinks with lebih … daripada. / 飲み物二つを lebih … daripada で比べましょう。
Ch 7: say where the nearest station is from here. / ここからいちばん近い駅がどこにあるかを言いましょう。
Ch 8: order two cups of tea and one plate of fried noodles. / お茶を2杯と焼きそばを1皿注文しましょう。
Ch 9: read one sign in this building aloud, or make one with Dilarang. / この建物の掲示を一つ読み上げるか、Dilarang で一つ作りましょう。

Stage 1 · Stage review · A new colleague.source_text: ■ Role card A · Aのカード

You are a new colleague in your first week (use your own name or Encik Kimura's). With your partner, go through the five days without the script, one day at a time: / あなたは最初の週の新しい同僚です（自分の名前か木村さんの名前で）。台本なしで、一日ずつ五日間を進めます：
Monday: greet B, introduce yourself and ask one question about B; give your age and phone number for the form. / 月曜日：Bにあいさつして自己紹介し、Bに一つ質問します。書類のために年齢と電話番号を言います。
Tuesday: ask how a dish tastes, compare two dishes, choose one and say why, order for two people with counters, and check the total. / 火曜日：料理の味をたずね、二つを比べ、一つを選んで理由を言い、二人分を助数詞で注文し、合計を確かめます。
Wednesday: ask the time and when the meeting starts and ends; say one thing you have not done yet. / 水曜日：時刻と会議の開始・終了時刻をたずね、まだしていないことを一つ言います。
Thursday: ask the way to the bank, how far it is and how long it takes; repeat the route. / 木曜日：銀行への道、距離、かかる時間をたずね、道順を繰り返します。
Friday: ask who made one dish and where one was bought, offer to help, read a sign, and take leave. / 金曜日：料理を誰が作ったか、どこで買ったかをたずね、手伝いを申し出て、掲示を読み、別れのあいさつをします。
■ Role card B · Bのカード

You are a colleague who has worked here for a year. Answer A in full sentences, using fictional details of your own (names, prices, times, places). Ask A at least one question each day. / あなたはここで一年働いている同僚です。架空の情報（名前、値段、時刻、場所）を使って、Aに完全な文で答えます。毎日少なくとも一つAに質問します。
Tuesday: you are also the stall holder: ask Makan sini atau bungkus? and give the total. / 火曜日：屋台の人の役もします。Makan sini atau bungkus? とたずね、合計を言います。
Friday: you organised the jamuan: say who made, bought and brought the food. / 金曜日：あなたは jamuan の幹事です。誰が作り、買い、持ってきたかを言います。

Stage 1 · Stage review · A new colleague.source_text: ■ Success criteria · できる基準
☐ Every day has at least one question and one full answer, with no notes.
☐ Titles come before names; the greeting fits the time of day (chapters 1 and 2).
☐ Prices, the age and the phone number are said correctly (chapter 3).
☐ pukul for clock times; sudah, belum, akan fit the time (chapter 4).
☐ Adjectives follow the noun; one comparison with lebih, sama … dengan or paling; one choice with Saya pilih … and one reason with Kenapa …? Sebab … (chapters 5 and 6).
☐ The route uses jalan terus, belok kiri / kanan di … and a position word (chapter 7).
☐ Every order has a number and a counter, or se- + counter (chapter 8).
☐ One sentence with a di- verb and oleh, and one sign read correctly (chapter 9).

☐ I can read common signs and notices (Dilarang …, Sila …, opening hours). / よくある掲示や案内（Dilarang …・Sila …・営業時間）を読める。

■ Task 1 · Two announcements · 二つのお知らせ
You hear an announcement in a clothes shop, then one in your office. / 洋服店のお知らせと、事務所のお知らせを聞きます。
L1. When does the shop close, and what is the discount today? / 店は何時に閉まりますか。今日の割引は何ですか。 [2 marks]
L2. When does the meeting start now, and where is it? / 会議は何時に始まることになりましたか。場所はどこですか。 [2 marks]
■ Task 2 · Meeting a new colleague · 新しい同僚に会う
Encik Tanaka meets a new colleague in the office pantry. / 田中さんが事務所の給湯室で新しい同僚に会います。
L3. What is her name, and where is she from? / 女性の名前は何ですか。出身はどこですか。 [2 marks]

Version A. Write in Malay. All names, shops, prices, times and places are fictional. / バージョンA。マレー語で書きます。名前、店、値段、時刻、場所はすべて架空です。

■ Part 1 · A form · 申込書

You are joining a Malay class at a community centre (fictional). Fill in the form in Malay about yourself. If you prefer, use this card: Kimura Kenji, 35, from Osaka, engineer, works in Bangsar, lives in Mont Kiara, phone 012-345 6789, hobby golf, class on Wednesday evening. / 地域センターのマレー語クラス（架空）に申し込みます。自分のことをマレー語で書きましょう。このカードを使ってもかまいません：木村健二、35歳、大阪出身、エンジニア、バンサーで勤務、モントキアラ在住、電話 012-345 6789、趣味はゴルフ、クラスは水曜日の夜。
Borang kelas bahasa Melayu
W1. Fill in the ten fields of the form. / 申込書の10の欄を記入しましょう。 [10 marks]
Hari kelas: Isnin / Rabu / Sabtu: ______________________
Masa kelas: pagi / petang / malam: ______________________
■ Part 2 · A message · メッセージ

Write a WhatsApp message of five to seven sentences to your colleague Encik Rahman. Invite him to lunch on Friday: greet him; say the day and the time; say where the gerai is (a position word or a short route); say what you will buy for him, with a counter; ask him one question; and take leave. / 同僚のラーマンさんに WhatsApp のメッセージを5〜7文で書きましょう。金曜日の昼ごはんに誘います：あいさつ、曜日と時刻、屋台の場所（位置のことばか短い道順）、助数詞を使ってラーマンさんに買うもの、質問を一つ、結びのあいさつ。
W2. Write the message. / メッセージを書きましょう。 [10 marks]

W1: One mark per field when the answer is true for the learner (or the card) and in Malay where a Malay word is needed; a spelling slip that does not change the word is not penalised. Card answers: 1 Kimura Kenji; 2 Jepun (or Osaka, Jepun); 3 35 tahun; 4 012-345 6789; 5 Mont Kiara; 6 jurutera; 7 Bangsar; 8 golf; 9 Rabu; 10 malam.

W2: Content 4: day and time 1; the place 1; what you will buy, with a counter 1; a greeting and taking leave 1. Language 4: pukul with the time 1; di + a position word, or jalan terus / belok 1; a number + counter + noun, or se- + counter 1; one more Stage 1 pattern used correctly (a question word or -kah, yang, lebih … daripada, sudah / belum, a di- verb) 1. Accuracy 2: 2 = Malaysian standard forms and the meaning always clear; 1 = a few slips, the meaning clear; 0 = the meaning often unclear. Model: Selamat pagi, Encik Rahman. Hari Jumaat ini, kita makan tengah hari di gerai dekat stesen, pukul satu? Gerai itu di sebelah bank. Saya beli sebungkus nasi lemak untuk encik. Encik suka teh tarik yang kurang manis? Jumpa hari Jumaat!

Stage 1 · A1 stage test · Version A · Sp.source_text: A1 段階テストの話す問題です：自己紹介とロールカード。試験官の台詞と採点基準は先生用キーにあります。日本語は未監修です。
（日本語は下書きです。ネイティブ・スピーカーの確認待ち）
No Malay explainer for Stage 1 units: explainers and rubrics are in Japanese or English (Sam, 11 Nov 2026). Select 日本語 or English.
The speaking test of the A1 stage test: a self-introduction and role-play cards. The examiner's lines and the rubric are in the teacher key.

Can-do: I can introduce myself and handle short everyday exchanges: ordering, buying, asking the way and talking at a party, including a change of plan. / 自己紹介ができ、注文、買い物、道をたずねる、パーティーでの会話など、予定変更を含む短いやりとりができる。
Version A. Speak in Malay. All names, shops, prices, times and places are fictional. / バージョンA。マレー語で話します。名前、店、値段、時刻、場所はすべて架空です。

About 7 minutes for each learner, 20 marks: the self-introduction (8) and two role-play cards (6 each). Card 2 (comparing) is always used; the examiner chooses the other card from cards 1, 3 and 4. / 一人約7分、20点：自己紹介（8点）とロールカード二枚（各6点）。カード2（比べる）は必ず使い、もう一枚は試験官がカード1・3・4から選びます。
■ Part 1 · Self-introduction · 自己紹介

S1. Self-introduction (about one minute). Introduce yourself to a new colleague: greet, your name, where you are from, your work or study, where you live, your hobby; then take leave. The examiner then asks two questions. / 自己紹介（約1分）。新しい同僚に自己紹介しましょう：あいさつ、名前、出身、仕事か勉強、住んでいる所、趣味、最後に別れのあいさつ。そのあと試験官が二つ質問します。 [8 marks]
■ Part 2 · Role-play cards · ロールカード
Read your card, then talk with the examiner without a script. The examiner will change one thing. / カードを読み、台本なしで試験官と話します。試験官が途中で一つ変更します。
■ Card 1 · At a gerai · カード1・屋台で
☐ Order lunch for yourself and a colleague: two dishes, each with a number and a counter. / 自分と同僚の昼ごはんを注文しましょう：料理二つを、それぞれ数と助数詞で。
☐ Ask for a drink kurang manis or ais sedikit. / 飲み物を kurang manis か ais sedikit で頼みましょう。
☐ Ask the total and pay. / 合計をたずねて払いましょう。
■ Card 2 · Buying fruit · カード2・果物を買う (always used · 必ず使う)
☐ Ask the price of one kind of fruit for one piece. / 果物一つの値段をたずねましょう。
☐ Compare two fruits and ask which is sweeter. / 二つの果物を比べ、どちらが甘いかたずねましょう。
☐ Buy some with a number and a counter, and check your change. / 数と助数詞で買い、おつりを確かめましょう。
■ Card 3 · Asking the way · カード3・道をたずねる
☐ Stop someone politely. / ていねいに声をかけましょう。
☐ Ask where the post office is and how far it is. / 郵便局がどこにあるか、どのくらい遠いかをたずねましょう。
☐ Repeat the route to check it. / 道順を繰り返して確かめましょう。
■ Card 4 · At the office jamuan · カード4・事務所の jamuan
☐ Ask who made one dish and where another was bought. / 料理を誰が作ったか、別の料理をどこで買ったかをたずねましょう。
☐ Say how something tastes. / 何かの味を言いましょう。
☐ Offer to help after the party. / 会のあと、手伝いを申し出ましょう。
S1 examiner: Selamat pagi. Siapa nama encik? (or puan, cik) Follow-up 1: Encik suka makan apa? Follow-up 2: Encik pergi kerja naik apa?

S1 rubric (8): Content 4: greeting and taking leave 1; name and origin 1; work or study, and home 1; hobby 1. Language 2: 2 = Nama saya …, Saya orang … / Asal saya dari …, Saya tinggal di … said correctly; 1 = some slips; 0 = mostly single words. Interaction and delivery 2: both follow-up questions answered in a sentence 1; pronunciation and pace easy to follow 1. Model: Selamat pagi. Nama saya Kimura. Saya orang Jepun. Asal saya dari Osaka. Saya kerja di Bangsar. Saya jurutera. Saya tinggal di Mont Kiara. Hobi saya golf. Saya minta diri dulu. Jumpa lagi! Follow-ups: Saya suka makan nasi lemak. Saya pergi kerja naik bas.
target_spans: Selamat pagi. Nama saya Kimura. Saya orang Jepun. Asal saya dari Osaka. Saya kerja di Bangsar. Saya jurutera. Saya tinggal di Mont Kiara. Hobi saya golf. Saya minta diri dulu. Jumpa lagi!

Stage 1 · A1 stage test · Version B · Li.source_text: A1 段階テストの聞く問題です。先生が台本を2回読みます。台本は先生用キーにあります。日本語は未監修です。
（日本語は下書きです。ネイティブ・スピーカーの確認待ち）
No Malay explainer for Stage 1 units: explainers and rubrics are in Japanese or English (Sam, 11 Nov 2026). Select 日本語 or English.
The listening paper of the A1 stage test. The teacher reads each script twice; the scripts are in the teacher key.
Can-do: I can understand short announcements and everyday conversations about people, food, prices, times and places, and note the facts I need. / 人、食べ物、値段、時刻、場所についての短いお知らせや日常会話を聞いて分かり、必要な情報を書き取れる。
Version B. Answer in English or Japanese unless a question asks for Malay. All names, shops, prices, times and places are fictional. / バージョンB。マレー語で書くよう指示がある問題以外は、英語か日本語で答えます。名前、店、値段、時刻、場所はすべて架空です。
12 minutes, 20 marks. The teacher reads each text twice. Read the questions first. / 12分、20点。先生が各文を2回読みます。先に質問を読みましょう。
■ Task 1 · Two announcements · 二つのお知らせ
You hear an announcement in a bookshop, then one in your office. / 本屋のお知らせと、事務所のお知らせを聞きます。
L1. When does the shop close, and what is the discount today? / 店は何時に閉まりますか。今日の割引は何ですか。 [2 marks]
L2. When does Friday's party start now, and where is it? / 金曜日の会は何時に始まることになりましたか。場所はどこですか。 [2 marks]
■ Task 2 · Meeting a new neighbour · 新しい隣人に会う
Encik Yamada meets a new neighbour in the lobby of his condo. / 山田さんがコンドミニアムのロビーで新しい隣人に会います。
L3. What is her name, and where is she from? / 女性の名前は何ですか。出身はどこですか。 [2 marks]
L4. What is her job, and where does she work? / 女性の仕事は何ですか。どこで働いていますか。 [2 marks]
■ Task 3 · Choosing how to go · 行き方選び
Two colleagues decide how to get to the bank. / 二人の同僚が銀行への行き方を決めます。
L5. Which is quicker, the taxi or the bus? Which way of going does Mei Ling say is the cheapest? / タクシーとバスではどちらが速いですか。メイリンさんはどの行き方が一番安いと言っていますか。 [2 marks]
A woman orders breakfast at a gerai. / 女性が屋台で朝ごはんを注文します。
L6. What food does she order? Write each number and counter in Malay. / 何を注文しましたか。数と助数詞をマレー語で書きましょう。 [2 marks]
L7. How does she want her coffee? Does she eat there or take the food away? / コーヒーはどのように頼みましたか。店で食べますか、持ち帰りですか。 [2 marks]
L8. How much is everything, and how much change does she get? / 全部でいくらですか。おつりはいくらですか。 [2 marks]
■ Task 5 · Directions on the phone · 電話で道案内
Mei Ling phones Encik Yamada, who is on his way to a kedai mamak. / メイリンさんが、ママックの店に向かう山田さんに電話します。
L9. How does he get from the post office to the kedai mamak? / 郵便局からママックの店までどう行きますか。 [2 marks]
L10. Where is the kedai mamak, and how far is it? / ママックの店はどこにありますか。どのくらい遠いですか。 [2 marks]

How to run the A1 stage test: timing, materials, procedure, scoring and the pass mark, the item maps and a result sheet.

The A1 stage test closes Stage 1 (chapters 1 to 9). It checks the charter's Stage 1 can-do goals at CEFR A1 with tasks that have a real outcome, in the Irodori and JF Standard way: understand an announcement, act on a sign, fill in a form, order and pay, ask the way. / A1 段階テストは第1段階（第1〜9章）のまとめのテストです。憲章の「できること」を CEFR A1 で、実際の目的のある課題で確かめます（いろどり・JF スタンダードの方法）。

Chapter 6 (comparing) is compulsory in both versions: one listening item on lebih … daripada and paling (L5), and speaking card 2, which is always used. / 第6章（比べる）はどちらのバージョンでも必須です：聞く問題の1問（L5）と、必ず使うスピーキングのカード2。

Two parallel versions, A and B, with the same sections, tasks, marks and chapter spread. Use A for the main sitting; use B for a second group, a re-sit or the next course. Do not give both versions to one learner in the same week. / 同じ構成のバージョンAとBがあります。本試験はA、別のグループ・再試験・次の講座はBを使います。

The test is summative but kept low-stakes in spirit (charter rule 9): the result tells the learner which can-do goals to revisit. A pass means the learner has met the Stage 1 goals at A1 as this course defines them; it is not an official CEFR certificate. / 合格は、この講座の定める A1 の第1段階の目標を達成したという意味で、公式の CEFR 証明ではありません。
The test takes two extra 45-minute blocks (Sam, 12 Nov 2026), which brings the Stage 1 plan to 76 blocks (the charter gives the hours). / テストには45分のブロックが2つ加わり（Sam、2026年11月12日）、第1段階は全76ブロックになります。
Block 1, the written papers: listening 12 minutes, reading 15, writing 18 (45 minutes in all). Collect each paper before the next one.
Block 2, speaking: about 7 minutes for each learner, one at a time or in pairs (six learners fill about 45 minutes). The others can do the stage review self-check or Kata-Kata review meanwhile.
Do the stage review block before the test, in an earlier class.
For each learner: the listening, reading and writing papers of the version you use (without the teacher keys).
For the speaking test: the speaking sheet, with the four role-play cards cut apart; the teacher key with the examiner's lines and the rubric.
For the teacher: the listening scripts sheet, the four teacher keys, this sheet and one result sheet per learner. No audio is needed: the teacher reads the scripts.

Listening: read the instructions, give one minute to read the questions, then read each text twice at a natural speed. Learners answer in English or Japanese, or in Malay where the question asks for it.
Reading and writing: learners work alone without notes or dictionaries. Answer questions about the instructions only.

Speaking: greet the learner first (Selamat pagi. Apa khabar?; not marked). Part 1, the self-introduction, then the two follow-up questions. Part 2: always card 2 (comparing), then one of cards 1, 3 and 4 (change it from learner to learner so that the cards cannot be learnt by heart); give 30 seconds to read the card; play your part from the key and bring in the change of plan halfway. Mark with the rubric straight after each part.
■ Scoring and pass mark · 採点と合格基準
Four sections of 20 marks: 80 in all. Listening and reading: one mark for each fact in the key. Writing and speaking: the rubric in each key (content, language, accuracy or interaction).

Pass: 48 or more out of 80 (60 per cent), and at least 10 out of 20 in every section. This is Sam's decision of 12 Nov 2026; it is not taken from a JF, Irodori or CEFR document. / 合格：80点中48点以上（60％）、かつ各セクション20点中10点以上。これはSamの決定（2026年11月12日）で、JF・いろどり・CEFRの基準ではありません。
A pass is recorded as "Malay A1 · Stage 1 complete" (CEFR A1). "Not yet": go back to the chapters of the items that were missed (item map below), then sit the other version.
Accept any natural answer with the same meaning. In listening and reading, a spelling slip that does not change the meaning loses no mark. No half marks.

Unit 10A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|7.source_text: Explanation: A ber- verb is a root with ber- in front: sarapan → bersarapan, kerja → bekerja, tolak → bertolak. These verbs have no object: say what you do, then when (pukul tujuh) or where (di rumah). Like every Malay verb, a ber- verb never changes for who or when; the time words of chapter 4 do that job. ber- has no nasal sound changes: only be- before a root that starts with r (berehat, berenang) and in bekerja, and bel- in belajar (chapter 2). In everyday talk people often use the bare root (Saya kerja di KL, Sudah sarapan?); the ber- form is the standard one, so learn it first. Finishing work for the day is habis kerja.

Unit 10A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|8.source_text: 説明：ber- の動詞は、語根の前に ber- を付けた形です：sarapan → bersarapan、kerja → bekerja、tolak → bertolak。目的語をとらないので、何をするかを言い、そのあとにいつ（pukul tujuh）やどこで（di rumah）を続けます。マレー語の動詞と同じく、ber- の動詞も人や時で形が変わりません。時は第4章の時の言葉で表します。ber- には鼻音の変化がありません。r で始まる語根の前（berehat・berenang）と bekerja で be- になり、belajar（第2章）だけが bel- です。日常会話では語根だけを使うことも多い（Saya kerja di KL・Sudah sarapan?）ですが、ber- の形が標準なので、まずこちらを覚えます。その日の仕事が終わることは habis kerja です。

Unit 10A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|9.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Many ber- verbs match Japanese する verbs (bersenam 運動する, berlatih 練習する), which helps. But ber- is not ます: it does not make a verb polite or past, and you cannot add it to any word you like. Learn each ber- verb as a whole word.

Unit 10A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|1.source_text: 日本語との比較：多くの ber- の動詞は日本語の「〜する」動詞にあたります（bersenam 運動する、berlatih 練習する）。ただし ber- は「ます」ではなく、ていねいさや過去を表しません。また、どの語にでも付けられるわけではありません。ber- の動詞は一語ずつ覚えましょう。

Unit 10A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|2.source_text: 2. A: Pukul berapa kita bertolak? B: Kita bertolak pukul dua.

Unit 10A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|4.source_text: 4. A: Bas ini berhenti di stesen? B: Ya. Bas ini berhenti di depan stesen.
target_spans: Ya. Bas ini berhenti di depan stesen.

Unit 10A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|5.source_text: 5. A: Encik sudah bersedia? B: Sudah. Kita boleh bertolak sekarang.

Unit 10A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|6.source_text: 6. A: Mesyuarat sudah bermula? B: Belum. Mesyuarat bermula pukul sepuluh.

Unit 10A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|7.source_text: Explanation: bermula is what an event does: Mesyuarat bermula pukul sembilan. bertolak is setting off on a trip or for work: Pukul berapa kita bertolak? Its root tolak is the door sign PUSH from chapter 9, but with ber- the meaning changes, so never use bertolak for pushing. berhenti is to stop (Bas berhenti di depan pejabat.); careful: berhenti kerja means to quit a job, not to stop work for the day (habis kerja). bersiap is getting ready (the action); bersedia is being ready (the state): Saya sedang bersiap. → Saya sudah bersedia.

Unit 10A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|8.source_text: 説明：bermula は行事が始まることです：Mesyuarat bermula pukul sembilan. bertolak は旅行や仕事に出発することです：Pukul berapa kita bertolak? 語根の tolak は第9章のドアの表示「押す」ですが、ber- が付くと意味が変わるので、押す意味では使いません。berhenti は止まることです（Bas berhenti di depan pejabat.）。注意：berhenti kerja は仕事を辞めることで、その日の仕事が終わること（habis kerja）ではありません。bersiap は準備をすること（動作）、bersedia は準備ができていること（状態）です：Saya sedang bersiap. → Saya sudah bersedia.

Unit 10A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|9.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 始まる and 出発する are the same kind of verb as bermula and bertolak, so the word order is easy. Two Japanese words mislead: やめる covers both stopping and quitting, but berhenti kerja is only quitting; 準備する / 準備ができた is the same pair as bersiap / sudah bersedia.

Unit 10A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|1.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「始まる」「出発する」は bermula・bertolak と同じ種類の動詞なので、語順はやさしいです。ただし二つの日本語に注意：「やめる」は止めることにも辞めることにも使いますが、berhenti kerja は「辞める」だけです。「準備する／準備ができた」は bersiap と sudah bersedia の組み合わせにあたります。

Unit 10A · Pattern and grammar focus|5|3.source_text: Explanation: suka goes straight in front of the verb, with nothing in between: Saya suka berenang. (I like swimming.) bermain takes the game: bermain badminton, bermain golf; in everyday talk main badminton is just as common. Tidak juga is the natural, gentle "not really"; lebih suka means prefer ("I like cycling more"). Say how often with the chapter 4 words: selalu, biasanya, kadang-kadang, jarang, setiap hari Sabtu. berlatih is practising a skill or a sport, and it can take a verb: berlatih bercakap bahasa Melayu.

Unit 10A · Pattern and grammar focus|5|4.source_text: 説明：suka は動詞の直前に置き、間に何も入れません：Saya suka berenang.（泳ぐのが好きです）。bermain のあとに競技名を置きます：bermain badminton・bermain golf。日常会話では main badminton もよく使います。Tidak juga は「そうでもない」にあたる自然なやわらかい言い方で、lebih suka は「〜のほうが好き」です。頻度は第4章の言葉で言います：selalu・biasanya・kadang-kadang・jarang・setiap hari Sabtu。berlatih は技術やスポーツを練習することで、動詞を続けることもできます：berlatih bercakap bahasa Melayu。

Unit 10A · Pattern and grammar focus|5|5.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese needs 〜するのが好き or 〜することが好き; Malay needs no の or こと: suka + verb. Japanese 遊ぶ is for children and fun, but bermain is also the normal verb for sports and games (ゴルフをする = bermain golf).

Unit 10A · Pattern and grammar focus|5|6.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語は「〜するのが好き」「〜することが好き」と言いますが、マレー語は「の」や「こと」にあたる語がいらず、suka ＋動詞です。日本語の「遊ぶ」は子どもや楽しみに使いますが、bermain はスポーツやゲームを「する」ときのふつうの動詞でもあります。

Unit 10A · Pattern and grammar focus|6|0.source_text: Explanation: bercakap is to speak: the language follows straight after it (bercakap bahasa Melayu), and the person comes after dengan (bercakap dengan Puan Aini). berbual is a relaxed chat. berjumpa dengan is to meet someone. In everyday talk you will hear the roots: cakap, jumpa (Jumpa lagi! is the fixed goodbye from chapter 1). Use kita when the listener is included (Kita berjumpa esok.) and kami when not (Kami berbual setiap pagi.).

Unit 10A · Pattern and grammar focus|6|1.source_text: 説明：bercakap は話すことで、言語はすぐあとに置き（bercakap bahasa Melayu）、話す相手は dengan のあとに置きます（bercakap dengan Puan Aini）。berbual は気軽なおしゃべりです。berjumpa dengan は人に会うことです。日常会話では語根の cakap・jumpa も聞きます（Jumpa lagi! は第1章の決まった別れの言葉）。聞き手を含むときは kita（Kita berjumpa esok.）、含まないときは kami（Kami berbual setiap pagi.）です。

Unit 10A · Pattern and grammar focus|6|2.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 〜と話す matches bercakap dengan. But 〜に会う uses に, and learners often say *berjumpa di pengurus: the person always takes dengan, never di (which is only for places). 〜語を話す: no word for を, the language follows the verb.

Unit 10A · Pattern and grammar focus|6|3.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「〜と話す」は bercakap dengan にあたります。ところが「〜に会う」は「に」を使うので、*berjumpa di pengurus と言いがちです。人には必ず dengan を使い、di は場所だけです。「〜語を話す」の「を」にあたる語はなく、言語は動詞のすぐあとに来ます。

Unit 10A · Pattern and grammar focus|7|1.source_text: Pattern IDs are the Kata-Kata chapter 10 frames f01 to f04 (f04 returns in unit 10B with neighbours; f05 and f06 are unit 10B). Explanations and Japanese comparisons are drafts.

Unit 10A · Pattern and grammar focus|7|2.source_text: Pattern 1: one ber- verb, then the time. If a learner adds an object (Saya bersarapan roti), accept the meaning and model Saya makan roti untuk sarapan or Saya bersarapan di rumah; ber- verbs here take no object. Accept the everyday roots (kerja, sarapan) in speech, but write the ber- form on the board.

Unit 10A · Pattern and grammar focus|7|3.source_text: Pattern 2: bermula for events, bertolak for people setting off. Ask the class what tolak means on a door before you show bertolak. Contrast berhenti (stop) and berhenti kerja (quit a job) with habis kerja (finish for the day).

Unit 10A · Pattern and grammar focus|7|4.source_text: Pattern 3: suka + verb, nothing in between. bersukan (to do sport) is a practice-pool word (ledger L-1307, not taught in class): say bersenam or bermain + the sport. Practise the frequency words from chapter 4 with each answer.

Unit 10A · Pattern and grammar focus|7|5.source_text: Pattern 4: dengan for the person, nothing before the language. Listen for *berjumpa di + person and *bercakap dengan bahasa Melayu.

Unit 10A · Culture and usage note|2|0.source_text: Read about hearing the standard ber- form and the everyday root, the spelling of ber-, and two verbs whose meaning changes.

Unit 10A · Culture and usage note|3|0.source_text: In Malaysia you will hear the same verb in two forms. News, forms, notices and polite speech use the ber- form: Saya bekerja di Kuala Lumpur, Encik sudah bersarapan? In a relaxed chat many people use the root alone: Saya kerja di KL, Sudah sarapan?, Saya cakap bahasa Melayu. Both are correct Malaysian Malay. This course teaches the ber- form first, as the standard, and you will understand the short form when you hear it.

Unit 10A · Culture and usage note|3|1.source_text: ber- is the easiest Malay verb prefix: it has no nasal sound changes. Its only spelling variants are be- before a root that starts with r (berehat, berenang) and in bekerja, and bel- in belajar, the one exception. Learners from Japan often write *berrehat or *berkerja: say the word aloud and you hear only one r.

Unit 10A · Culture and usage note|3|2.source_text: Two verbs change their meaning with ber-. tolak on a door means push, but bertolak means set off: Pukul berapa kita bertolak? berhenti means stop, so Bas berhenti di sini, but berhenti kerja means to quit your job. To say that you finish work for the day, use habis kerja: Saya habis kerja pukul enam.

Unit 10A · Culture and usage note|3|3.source_text: Malaysian colleagues often chat about breakfast and the weekend. Sudah sarapan? is a friendly greeting, not a real question about food, as in chapter 4.

Unit 10A · Culture and usage note|3|5.source_text: マレーシアでは、同じ動詞を二つの形で耳にします。ニュース、書類、掲示、ていねいな会話では ber- の形を使います：Saya bekerja di Kuala Lumpur、Encik sudah bersarapan? くだけたおしゃべりでは、語根だけを使う人も多いです：Saya kerja di KL、Sudah sarapan?、Saya cakap bahasa Melayu。どちらも正しいマレーシアのマレー語です。このコースでは標準として ber- の形を先に教え、短い形は聞いて分かるようにします。

Unit 10A · Culture and usage note|3|6.source_text: ber- はマレー語の動詞の接頭辞でいちばんやさしいもので、鼻音の変化がありません。つづりの違いは、r で始まる語根の前（berehat・berenang）と bekerja の be-、そして例外の belajar の bel- だけです。日本の学習者は *berrehat や *berkerja と書きがちですが、声に出すと r は一つしか聞こえません。

Unit 10A · Culture and usage note|3|7.source_text: ber- が付くと意味が変わる動詞が二つあります。ドアの tolak は「押す」ですが、bertolak は「出発する」です：Pukul berapa kita bertolak? berhenti は「止まる」なので Bas berhenti di sini と言いますが、berhenti kerja は「仕事を辞める」です。その日の仕事が終わることは habis kerja と言います：Saya habis kerja pukul enam.

Unit 10A · Culture and usage note|3|8.source_text: マレーシアの同僚は、朝ごはんや週末の話をよくします。第4章と同じく、Sudah sarapan? は食べ物について本当にたずねる質問ではなく、親しみのこもったあいさつです。

Unit 10A · Teaching plan and answer key|.source_text: 先生用：45分×5ブロックの進め方、注意点、宿題です。答えは各シートのキーにあります。
（日本語は下書きです。ネイティブ・スピーカーの確認待ち）
No Malay explainer for Stage 2 units: explainers and rubrics are in Japanese or English only, as in Stage 1 (Sam, 13 Nov 2026). Select 日本語 or English.
Teacher plan: five 45-minute blocks with timings, what to listen for and homework. Answers are on each sheet.
Before Block A: Kata-Kata Sedia Kelas c10 (33 cards, frames ms-c10-f01 and ms-c10-f02).

After Block D: the Kata-Kata chapter 10 deck with spaced review, frames ms-c10-f01, ms-c10-f02, ms-c10-f03, ms-c10-f04 in the frame drill and Susun Ayat; about 3 hours of self-study for this unit (planning figure).

Hanashishou (Stage 2): the plan links chapter 10 to the daily-life scene grab_ride_chat and the home-condo scene new_neighbour, both for unit 10B. Their Malay is not yet tagged by chapter (build step 6), so do not assign them yet.
Next: unit 10B (background and neighbours), then the writing block after 10B.
■ Block A · Words and patterns (45 min)
Goal: I can say when I do things on a working day with a taught ber- verb and pukul.
0–5 Recall: chapters 4 and 9 (a morning routine with root verbs; the door signs) from the opener prompts.
5–10 Tanya Cikgu questions from Kata-Kata.
10–20 Vocabulary focus: core words first, with each root; recognition and revision words are only pointed out.

20–40 Pattern focus: patterns 1 and 2 first, question and answer before the rule; then the vocabulary in three groups with each root (a working day 10, talking and meeting 4, exercise and free time 6). Write ber-, be- and bel- on the board.
40–45 First substitutions (Drill 2, items 1 to 3).
■ Block B · Drills and conversation (45 min)
Goal: I can ask and answer about routines: Pukul berapa …?, … bermula, … bertolak, suka + a ber- verb.
0–5 Recall: say the time you do three things with Setiap pagi saya … pukul ….
5–25 Drill ladder in order: pattern table, substitution, transformation (everyday to standard first), question and answer, question-word choice, short dialogues, then the markers drill.
25–40 Model conversation, gapped form, then the changed-facts variant.
40–45 Pair rehearsal without the script.
■ Block C · Listening and task (45 min)
Goal: I can follow a colleague's day and a team message, and plan a time that fits two routines.
0–5 Recall: each learner says when they set off today and one weekend activity.
5–20 Listening: read the questions, two readings, check, then shadow three lines.
20–30 Reading and writing.
30–45 Task with role cards; announce the change of plan halfway.
■ Block D · Review and test (45 min)
Goal: I can check the ber- verbs, their roots and their spelling, and correct a routine description.
0–15 Mixed review: cumulative question-word drill (chapters 1 to 10), then the markers drill with new cues and a spelling check of berehat, berenang, bekerja, belajar.
15–25 Unit test (low-stakes).
25–35 Self-check and feedback.
35–45 Preview: unit 10B: background and neighbours (Kata-Kata c10 cards ms-c10-021 to ms-c10-041 and frames f05, f06).
■ Block E · Scene transfer (45 min)
Goal: I can explain a changed workday in a short role-play.
0–5 Recall: say three things from your Monday and one thing from your weekend.
5–15 Scene listening: read the Kata-Kata scenario lines ms-c10-s01 to ms-c10-s09 (Tanaka and Puan Aini, the working day) twice; learners tick the ber- verbs they hear.
15–30 Role-play in pairs: pairs play the same scene with their own routine, without the script.

30–40 Changed situation: a changed workday: today A works from home (Hari ini saya bekerja dari rumah), the meeting starts at two and the bus does not stop at the office; A explains the new day, B asks Pukul berapa …?
target_spans: Hari ini saya bekerja dari rumah

Unit 10A · Teaching plan and answer key|.source_text: 40–45 Culture and usage note discussion, and the home-practice briefing.
■ What to listen for · 注意点

Load: 24 core words in three groups (a working day 11; talking and meeting 4; exercise and free time 9), no recognition word (no Dunia scene primes chapter 10), and revision of the roots, the time words and the office words. Suggested order: Block A the working-day group with patterns 1 and 2; Block B talking and meeting with pattern 4; exercise and free time with pattern 3 in Block B or C. If the pilot shows 24 is too many, the natural cut is A/B: bekerja, bersarapan, bertolak, bermula, berehat, berhenti, bercakap, berjumpa, bermain, bersenam first; the rest second.

ber- rule (charter section 5, Sam 13 Nov 2026): no nasal sound changes; be- before r (berehat, berenang) and in bekerja; bel- only in belajar (revision, chapter 2). Every ber- word here is its own ledger row; do not let learners build new ones (bersukan is a practice-pool word, not taught here; *bermesyuarat is not taught). No meN- verb (chapter 11).

Common traps from the Kata-Kata cards: berhenti kerja means to quit a job (card ms-c10-015); for finishing work for the day say habis kerja. bertolak means to set off, not to push (card ms-c10-020): tolak alone is the door sign PUSH from chapter 9. bersarapan is standard; sarapan alone is everyday (card ms-c10-013).

Where Japanese learners usually slip: (1) treating ber- like ます and adding it to any verb (*bermakan does not exist); (2) *berjumpa di + a person, from 〜に会う: the person takes dengan; (3) *bercakap dengan bahasa Melayu, from 〜語で話す: the language follows the verb directly; (4) spelling *berrehat, *berkerja; (5) 休む covers both berehat (rest) and taking a day off (bercuti, unit 10B): ask which they mean; (6) やめる covers stop and quit.
Standard first: teach the ber- form, accept the everyday root in speech (kerja, sarapan, cakap, jumpa, main), and never mark it wrong in a speaking task. No spoken contraction is needed in this unit.
The scene follows Kata-Kata c10 (scenario lines ms-c10-s01 to s09, frames f01 to f04). All names, times and routines are fictional; learners may use their real week or an invented one.
Cumulative question words: chapters 1 to 10. Chapter 10 adds no new question word.
Answer keys are on each component. Japanese text awaits native review.
Standard forms first; spoken forms are labelled. ber- verbs are taught as whole ledger forms, each with its root; no meN- verb (chapter 11) and no suffixed verb form (chapter 12).

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|7.source_text: Explanation: Background in standard Malay uses ber- verbs: Saya berasal dari Osaka. (I am from Osaka.) Saya bekerja di … (I work at …). Chapter 2 gave you the everyday forms, and they are still right in speech: Asal saya dari Osaka, Nama saya …, Umur saya …. bernama and berumur are formal: you will meet them in writing, on forms and when someone introduces a third person: Anak saya bernama Yuki. Dia berumur lapan tahun. For yourself, Nama saya Tanaka is the natural spoken line. berniaga is to run a business; the answer to Bekerja di mana? can be Saya berniaga.
target_spans: Anak saya bernama Yuki. Dia berumur lapan tahun.

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|8.source_text: 説明：標準のマレー語では、背景を ber- の動詞で言います：Saya berasal dari Osaka.（大阪の出身です）、Saya bekerja di …（〜で働いています）。第2章で学んだ日常の形（Asal saya dari Osaka・Nama saya …・Umur saya …）も、話すときはそのまま正しい言い方です。bernama と berumur は改まった言い方で、書き言葉や書類、ほかの人を紹介するときに出てきます：Anak saya bernama Yuki. Dia berumur lapan tahun. 自分のことは Nama saya Tanaka と言うのが自然です。berniaga は商売をすることで、Bekerja di mana? に Saya berniaga と答えることもできます。
target_spans: Anak saya bernama Yuki. Dia berumur lapan tahun.

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|9.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 〜出身です and 〜で働いています give the same order: berasal dari + place, bekerja di + place. Watch the little word: 出身 takes dari (from), work takes di (at). Japanese 〜という名前です sounds formal too, so bernama is a good match for it.

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|1.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「〜出身です」「〜で働いています」と語順は同じです：berasal dari ＋場所、bekerja di ＋場所。小さな語に注意：出身は dari（〜から）、働く場所は di（〜で）です。日本語の「〜という名前です」も改まった響きなので、bernama によく合います。
Pattern box: Saya sudah / belum (ber- verb).
1. A: Encik sudah berkahwin? B: Sudah. Saya tinggal berdua dengan isteri saya.
target_spans: Sudah. Saya tinggal berdua dengan isteri saya.

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|1.source_text: 2. A: Puan sudah berkeluarga? B: Sudah. Saya ada dua orang anak.

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|1.source_text: 3. A: Anak puan masih bersekolah? B: Ya. Dua orang anak saya masih bersekolah.
target_spans: Ya. Dua orang anak saya masih bersekolah.

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|0.source_text: 4. A: Encik baru berpindah ke sini? B: Ya. Saya baru berpindah minggu lepas.
target_spans: Ya. Saya baru berpindah minggu lepas.

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|1.source_text: 5. A: Encik sudah bercuti tahun ini? B: Belum. Saya bercuti bulan Disember.

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|2.source_text: 6. A: Encik sudah berkenalan dengan jiran? B: Belum. Saya mahu berkenalan dengan mereka.

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|3.source_text: Explanation: Life events and states take the chapter 4 markers: sudah berkahwin (married), belum berkahwin (not married yet), masih bersekolah (still at school), baru berpindah (have just moved). To the question Sudah berkahwin? the usual short answers are Sudah. and Belum.; you do not have to say more. berdua means the two of you together: Saya tinggal berdua dengan isteri saya. (My wife and I live here, just the two of us.) In speech you will hear pindah for berpindah: recognise it, but say berpindah.
target_spans: Saya tinggal berdua dengan isteri saya.

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|4.source_text: 説明：人生のできごとや状態には第4章のマーカーを使います：sudah berkahwin（結婚している）、belum berkahwin（まだ結婚していない）、masih bersekolah（まだ学校に通っている）、baru berpindah（引っ越してきたばかり）。Sudah berkahwin? への短い答えは Sudah.・Belum. がふつうで、それ以上言う必要はありません。berdua は二人一緒にという意味です：Saya tinggal berdua dengan isteri saya.（妻と二人で住んでいます）。話し言葉では berpindah の代わりに pindah も聞きます。聞いて分かればよく、言うときは berpindah を使います。
target_spans: Saya tinggal berdua dengan isteri saya.

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|5.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 結婚しています is a state, and sudah berkahwin is the same idea: sudah marks that the event has happened. まだ… ていない is belum; do not answer Tidak berkahwin, which sounds like a firm "I don't marry". 二人で is berdua, not dua orang.

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|6.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「結婚しています」は状態を表し、sudah berkahwin も同じ考え方です。sudah はできごとがすでに起きたことを表します。「まだ〜ていない」は belum です。Tidak berkahwin と答えると「結婚しない」ときっぱり言う響きになります。「二人で」は berdua で、dua orang ではありません。

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|8.source_text: Pattern box: Saya bercakap / berbual dengan ___. / Kami berjiran / berkawan.

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|9.source_text: 1. A: Encik selalu berbual dengan jiran? B: Ya. Saya berbual dengan Puan Siti setiap petang.
target_spans: Ya. Saya berbual dengan Puan Siti setiap petang.

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|1.source_text: 2. A: Encik berkawan dengan Encik Lim? B: Ya. Kami sudah lama berkawan.
3. A: Puan Siti jiran encik? B: Ya, kami berjiran. Rumah dia di sebelah rumah saya.
target_spans: Ya, kami berjiran. Rumah dia di sebelah rumah saya.

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|1.source_text: 4. A: Pada hari Ahad kita berkumpul di mana? B: Kita berkumpul di rumah saya pukul empat.
target_spans: Pada hari Ahad kita berkumpul di mana?
Kita berkumpul di rumah saya pukul empat.

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|1.source_text: 5. A: Encik bercakap bahasa Melayu dengan jiran? B: Ya. Saya bercakap bahasa Melayu dengan jiran saya.
target_spans: Encik bercakap bahasa Melayu dengan jiran?
Ya. Saya bercakap bahasa Melayu dengan jiran saya.

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|0.source_text: 6. A: Encik sudah berkenalan dengan Encik Lim? B: Sudah. Kami berkenalan di rumah Puan Siti.
target_spans: Encik sudah berkenalan dengan Encik Lim?
Sudah. Kami berkenalan di rumah Puan Siti.

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|1.source_text: Explanation: Some ber- verbs need two people: berkawan (be friends), berjiran (be neighbours), berkenalan (get to know each other), berkumpul (gather). Put both people before the verb (Kami berkawan., Saya dan Puan Siti berjiran.) or one person and dengan the other (Saya berkenalan dengan Encik Lim.). You know Selamat berkenalan! from chapter 1: it is the same verb. hidup berjiran (living as neighbours) is the ledger's phrase for good neighbourly life. bercakap and berbual come back from unit 10A.

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|2.source_text: 説明：二人以上を必要とする ber- の動詞があります：berkawan（友達である）、berjiran（隣同士である）、berkenalan（知り合いになる）、berkumpul（集まる）。二人とも動詞の前に置く（Kami berkawan.・Saya dan Puan Siti berjiran.）か、一人を前に、もう一人を dengan のあとに置きます（Saya berkenalan dengan Encik Lim.）。第1章の Selamat berkenalan! も同じ動詞です。hidup berjiran（隣同士として暮らすこと）は、台帳にある近所付き合いの言い方です。bercakap・berbual はユニット10Aから戻ってきます。

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|3.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese says 友達です or 隣同士です with a noun; Malay uses a verb: Kami berkawan., Kami berjiran. Japanese と in 田中さんと知り合う is dengan in Malay, the same as 〜と話す.

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|4.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語は「友達です」「隣同士です」と名詞で言いますが、マレー語は動詞を使います：Kami berkawan.、Kami berjiran. 「田中さんと知り合う」の「と」は、「〜と話す」と同じく dengan です。

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|6.source_text: Pattern box: Saya suka (ber- verb). / Saya berminat untuk (verb).

target_spans: Pada hujung minggu puan buat apa?

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|8.source_text: 2. A: Isteri encik berminat untuk belajar apa? B: Dia berminat untuk belajar masak.

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|9.source_text: 3. A: Encik bercuti bila? B: Saya bercuti minggu depan. Saya balik ke Jepun.

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|1.source_text: 4. A: Puan suka berbelanja di mana? B: Saya suka berbelanja di pasar pagi.

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|1.source_text: 5. A: Di pejabat encik berpakaian bagaimana? B: Kami berpakaian kemas.
6. A: Ini pengalaman pertama encik di Malaysia? B: Ya. Ini pengalaman pertama saya.
target_spans: Ini pengalaman pertama encik di Malaysia?

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|1.source_text: Explanation: Frame f03 from unit 10A comes back with the 10B verbs: Saya suka berbelanja. berminat untuk + a verb says what you are interested in doing: Saya berminat untuk belajar bahasa Melayu. berbelanja is to shop or spend money; belanja alone means to treat someone (chapter 17), so do not shorten it. bercuti is to be on leave or on holiday; cuti (chapter 2) is the noun. berpakaian is mostly heard in berpakaian kemas (neatly dressed). pengalaman (experience) is one whole word.
target_spans: Saya berminat untuk belajar bahasa Melayu.

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|6|0.source_text: 説明：ユニット10Aの文型 f03 が10Bの動詞で戻ってきます：Saya suka berbelanja. berminat untuk ＋動詞で、したいと興味を持っていることを言います：Saya berminat untuk belajar bahasa Melayu. berbelanja は買い物をする・お金を使うことです。belanja だけだと「おごる」（第17章）なので、短くしないでください。bercuti は休暇をとる・休暇中であることで、cuti（第2章）は名詞です。berpakaian はたいてい berpakaian kemas（きちんとした服装）で聞きます。pengalaman（経験）は一語まるごと覚えます。
target_spans: Saya berminat untuk belajar bahasa Melayu.

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|6|1.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 休む is berehat (rest, unit 10A) and also 休みを取る, which is bercuti. Ask yourself which one you mean. 〜に興味があります with a noun is harder in Malay; at this stage use berminat untuk + a verb, or suka + a verb.

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|6|2.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「休む」は berehat（休憩、ユニット10A）にも「休みを取る」にもなり、後者は bercuti です。どちらの意味か考えましょう。「〜に興味があります」を名詞で言うのはマレー語では難しいので、この段階では berminat untuk ＋動詞か、suka ＋動詞を使います。

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|7|2.source_text: Pattern 1: berasal dari and bekerja di. Accept the chapter 2 forms in speech (Asal saya dari …, Nama saya …); use bernama and berumur when introducing someone else or in writing.

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|7|3.source_text: Pattern 2: sudah / belum + a ber- verb. Belum. is the natural "not yet" for marriage; a learner never has to give personal details. Offer the persona cards on the task page.

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|7|4.source_text: Pattern 3: two-person verbs. Check that both people come before the verb, or one before and one after dengan.

Unit 10B · Pattern and grammar focus|7|5.source_text: Pattern 4: suka + ber- verb, berminat untuk + verb. Do not teach berminat + a noun at this stage (see the report).

The teacher reads the script twice; read the questions first, listen for the details, then shadow.
On Sunday afternoon Encik Tanaka goes to Puan Siti's gathering. She introduces her family and a neighbour. / 日曜の午後、田中さんがシティさんの集まりに行きます。シティさんが家族と隣人を紹介します。
Predict: which background words will you hear? Write three guesses (for example berasal, bekerja, berumur). / 聞こえそうな背景の言葉を三つ予想しましょう。
Draw three boxes, one for each person (Rashid, Farah, Encik Lim), and read the eight questions below. / 三人（ラシッドさん、ファラさん、リムさん）の欄を作り、下の8つの質問を読みます。
■ While listening · 聞きながら
1. Where is Encik Rashid from?
2. Where does he work, and what is his job?
3. Who is Farah, and what does she do?
4. How long has Tanaka been in Malaysia?
5. Where does Encik Lim live?
6. What is the name of Encik Lim's child, and how old is the child?
7. What does Encik Lim do at the weekend?
8. When will they get together again?

Unit 10B · Culture and usage note|3|0.source_text: Many Japanese professionals in Malaysia live in a condominium or a terrace house, with neighbours from several communities. The ledger's phrase hidup berjiran means living as good neighbours, and the Kata-Kata card gives Kami berjiran for "we are neighbours". A short introduction at the lift or the door is a good start: Selamat berkenalan! Saya baru berpindah ke sini.
target_spans: Selamat berkenalan! Saya baru berpindah ke sini.

Unit 10B · Culture and usage note|3|1.source_text: In chapter 9 you met the rumah terbuka: during a festival, families welcome friends and neighbours from other communities. Puan Siti's Sunday gathering is smaller, but it is the same spirit: Pada hari Ahad, kami berkumpul di rumah saya. Encik datang, ya!
target_spans: Pada hari Ahad, kami berkumpul di rumah saya. Encik datang, ya!

Unit 10B · Culture and usage note|3|2.source_text: Standard and everyday forms again: a form or a letter says Saya berasal dari Osaka, Anak saya bernama Yuki and Dia berumur lapan tahun; in speech people usually say Asal saya dari Osaka, Nama dia Yuki, Umur dia lapan tahun. berpindah is standard; pindah is spoken. berbelanja is to shop; belanja alone means to treat someone (chapter 17).

Unit 10B · Culture and usage note|3|3.source_text: New neighbours may ask about your family. Sudah. or Belum. is a complete answer, and in class you may use an invented persona.

Unit 10B · Culture and usage note|3|5.source_text: マレーシアに住む日本人の多くは、コンドミニアムやテラスハウスに住み、いろいろな民族の隣人がいます。台帳にある hidup berjiran は、よい隣人として暮らすことを表し、Kata-Kata のカードは「隣同士です」を Kami berjiran としています。エレベーターや玄関での短いあいさつは、よい始まりです：Selamat berkenalan! Saya baru berpindah ke sini.
target_spans: Selamat berkenalan! Saya baru berpindah ke sini.

Unit 10B · Culture and usage note|3|6.source_text: 第9章で rumah terbuka を学びました。行事のとき、家族が別の民族の友人や隣人を迎えます。シティさんの日曜日の集まりはもっと小さなものですが、同じ気持ちから来ています：Pada hari Ahad, kami berkumpul di rumah saya. Encik datang, ya!
target_spans: Pada hari Ahad, kami berkumpul di rumah saya. Encik datang, ya!

Unit 10B · Culture and usage note|3|7.source_text: ここでも標準の形と日常の形があります。書類や手紙では Saya berasal dari Osaka・Anak saya bernama Yuki・Dia berumur lapan tahun と書き、話すときはふつう Asal saya dari Osaka・Nama dia Yuki・Umur dia lapan tahun と言います。berpindah は標準、pindah は話し言葉です。berbelanja は買い物をすること、belanja だけだと「おごる」（第17章）です。

Unit 10B · Culture and usage note|3|8.source_text: 新しい隣人に家族のことをたずねられることがあります。Sudah. や Belum. だけで十分な答えで、授業では架空の人物になって答えてもかまいません。
