Unit 10B · Teaching plan and answer key|.source_text: 先生用：45分×5ブロックの進め方、注意点、宿題です。答えは各シートのキーにあります。
（日本語は下書きです。ネイティブ・スピーカーの確認待ち）
No Malay explainer for Stage 2 units: explainers and rubrics are in Japanese or English only, as in Stage 1 (Sam, 13 Nov 2026). Select 日本語 or English.
Teacher plan: five 45-minute blocks with timings, what to listen for and homework. Answers are on each sheet.
Before Block A: Kata-Kata Sedia Kelas c10 (33 cards, frames ms-c10-f01 and ms-c10-f02).

After Block D: the Kata-Kata chapter 10 deck with spaced review, frames ms-c10-f05, ms-c10-f06, ms-c10-f04, ms-c10-f03 in the frame drill and Susun Ayat; about 3 hours of self-study for this unit (planning figure).

Hanashishou (Stage 2): the plan links unit 10B to the daily-life scene grab_ride_chat (Awak dari mana? small talk) and the home-condo scene new_neighbour. Their Malay is not yet tagged by chapter (build step 6), so do not assign them yet; the classroom role-play stands in for them.
Next: the writing block after unit 10B (45 minutes, below), then chapter 11.
■ Block A · Words and patterns (45 min)
Goal: I can give two background details with ber- verbs (berasal dari, bekerja di, sudah / belum berkahwin).
0–5 Recall: chapter 2 and unit 10A (a three-line introduction and the morning routine) from the opener prompts.
5–10 Tanya Cikgu questions from Kata-Kata.
10–20 Vocabulary focus: core words first, with each root; recognition and revision words are only pointed out.

20–40 Pattern focus: patterns 1 and 2, question and answer first, rule second; then the vocabulary in three groups with each root (who I am 8, neighbours and friends 6, life and interests 6) and pindah as the spoken form to recognise.
40–45 First substitutions (Drill 2, items 1 to 3).
■ Block B · Drills and conversation (45 min)
Goal: I can exchange background questions with a new neighbour and say who I live with.
0–5 Recall: introduce the person next to you in two sentences: Dia berasal dari … Dia bekerja di …

5–25 Drill ladder in order: pattern table, substitution, transformation (everyday and spoken to standard first), question and answer, question-word choice, short dialogues, then the markers drill with life events.
25–40 Model conversation, gapped form, then the changed-facts variant.
40–45 Pair rehearsal without the script.
■ Block C · Listening and task (45 min)
Goal: I can identify neighbours from a short introduction and a residents' message, and introduce myself in a role-play.
0–5 Recall: each learner says one thing they have just done or not yet done with baru or belum + a ber- verb.
5–20 Listening: read the questions, two readings, check, then shadow three lines.
20–30 Reading and writing.
30–45 Task with role cards; announce the change of plan halfway.
■ Block D · Review and test (45 min)
Goal: I can check my own introduction: ber- forms, dari / di / dengan, and the standard and everyday forms.
0–15 Mixed review: cumulative question-word drill (chapters 1 to 10), then the markers drill and a check of dari, di and dengan.
15–25 Unit test (low-stakes).
25–35 Self-check and feedback.
35–45 Preview: the writing block (background and week), then chapter 11 (meN- verbs: Kata-Kata c11).
■ Block E · Scene transfer (45 min)
Goal: I can introduce myself to a different neighbour and accept an invitation to a gathering.
0–5 Recall: say where you are from, where you work and who you live with.
5–15 Scene listening: read the Kata-Kata scenario lines ms-c10-s10 to ms-c10-s19 (Tanaka meets Puan Siti) twice; learners note three facts about Siti.
15–30 Role-play in pairs: pairs play the meeting at the lift without the script, with their own details or a persona card.
30–40 Changed situation: a different neighbour: B is a student who has just moved in with a cousin and is interested in learning Japanese; A introduces A and invites B to the Sunday gathering.
40–45 Culture and usage note discussion, and the home-practice briefing.
■ What to listen for · 注意点

Load: 20 core words in three groups (who I am 8; neighbours and friends 6; life and interests 6), one word to recognise (pindah, the spoken partner of berpindah), and revision of the roots and the chapter 2 introduction. Suggested order: Block A who I am with patterns 1 and 2; Block B neighbours and friends with pattern 3; life and interests with pattern 4 in Block B or C. If the pilot shows 20 is too many, the natural cut is A/B: berasal, berkahwin, berpindah, bersekolah, berdua, jiran, berjiran, berkenalan, berkumpul, bercuti first; the rest second.

ber- rule as in unit 10A: no nasal sound changes; every ber- word here is its own ledger row. pengalaman is a whole word (the pe- … -an family is Stage 3); do not build other words from it. No meN- verb (chapter 11).

Common traps from the Kata-Kata cards: berbelanja (shop, spend) is not belanja (treat someone, chapter 17; card ms-c10-032); bernama and berumur are formal (cards ms-c10-021 and -025): for yourself, Nama saya … is natural; pindah is spoken (card ms-c10-041, recognise only). Unit 10A traps still apply: berhenti kerja = quit a job, bertolak = set off, not push.

Where Japanese learners usually slip: (1) *berasal di Osaka from 出身 + で: the origin takes dari; (2) Tidak berkahwin for まだ結婚していない: the natural answer is Belum.; (3) *dua orang for 二人で: say berdua; (4) *berkenalan di + person: the person takes dengan; (5) 休む for taking a day off: bercuti, not berehat; (6) leaving out both people with berkawan or berjiran: say Kami berkawan or Saya berkawan dengan ….

Personal questions: a learner never has to give real marital or family details. Persona cards are on the task page; Belum. and Sudah. are complete answers. berminat is taught with untuk + a verb only (the noun pattern is a question for the native reader).
The scene follows Kata-Kata c10 (scenario lines ms-c10-s10 to s19, frames f05 and f06, with f03 and f04 returning). All names, floors, jobs and families are fictional.
Cumulative question words: chapters 1 to 10. Chapter 10 adds no new question word.
Answer keys are on each component. Japanese text awaits native review.
Standard forms first; spoken forms are labelled. ber- verbs are taught as whole ledger forms, each with its root; no meN- verb (chapter 11) and no suffixed verb form (chapter 12).

No Malay explainer for Stage 2 units: explainers and rubrics are in Japanese or English only, as in Stage 1 (Sam, 13 Nov 2026). Select 日本語 or English.
The writing block after unit 10B (45 minutes): write your background and your week in six to eight sentences with ber- verbs; an invented persona is fine.
Fictional model: a message to the residents' chat group of a condominium (all details invented):

Unit 10B · Writing block · My background.source_text: Notice: background first (from, home, who you live with), then the week (times and days), then one interest and a greeting. Standard ber- forms in writing: berasal, bekerja, bertolak. / 気づくこと：最初に背景（出身・住まい・同居の人）、次に一週間（時刻と曜日）、最後に興味と一言のあいさつ。書くときは標準の ber- の形：berasal・bekerja・bertolak。
■ Plan · 45 minutes · 進め方
0–5 Recall: say your name, where you are from and when you set off in the morning (units 10A and 10B).
5–15 Model and notice: read the model; underline every ber- verb and its root; compare Asal saya dari … (spoken) with Saya berasal dari … (written).
15–30 Guided draft: write your own message with the checklist below (a real or an invented persona).
30–40 Peer or teacher feedback with the peer check.
40–45 Rewrite one sentence and read the message aloud.
0–5 復習・5–15 例文を読んで気づく・15–30 下書き・30–40 ペアまたは先生の確認・40–45 一文を書き直して音読。
■ Your turn · 自分で
Write six to eight sentences for your own residents' chat or a new colleague. Include:
☐ where you are from, where you live and who you live with (berasal dari, tinggal, berdua or sudah / belum berkahwin, if you wish)
☐ where you work and two things from your week with times (bekerja di, Setiap pagi saya … pukul …, Pada hari … saya …)
☐ one interest (Saya suka … or Saya berminat untuk …) and a greeting (Selamat berkenalan!)
自分のコンドミニアムのグループ、または新しい同僚へのメッセージを6〜8文で書きましょう。出身・住まい・同居の人、仕事と一週間のこと二つ（時刻つき）、興味一つとあいさつを入れます。家族のことは書かなくても、架空の人物でもかまいません。
■ Peer check · 互いに確認
☐ Every ber- verb is spelt as on its card (be- in berehat, berenang, bekerja).
☐ dari after berasal, di after bekerja and tinggal, dengan before a person.
☐ Times have pukul; days have pada hari.
☐ No spoken form, no meN- verb; the partner can answer one question about the message.
☐ ber- の動詞のつづり、berasal dari・bekerja di・dengan ＋人、pukul・pada hari を確認し、パートナーが質問を一つします。

Model: Any six to eight correct sentences that cover the checklist. Model: Selamat petang semua. Nama saya Yamada Emi. Saya berasal dari Nagoya. Saya baru berpindah ke tingkat sembilan minggu lepas. Saya tinggal berdua dengan suami saya. Saya bekerja di sebuah bank di Kuala Lumpur. Setiap pagi saya bertolak pukul tujuh setengah. Pada hujung minggu saya suka berenang. Selamat berkenalan!
target_spans: Selamat petang semua. Nama saya Yamada Emi. Saya berasal dari Nagoya. Saya baru berpindah ke tingkat sembilan minggu lepas. Saya tinggal berdua dengan suami saya. Saya bekerja di sebuah bank di Kuala Lumpur. Setiap pagi saya bertolak pukul tujuh setengah. Pada hujung minggu saya suka berenang. Selamat berkenalan!

Unit 10B · Writing block · My background.source_text: Mark for the task first (background, week, interest, greeting), then for form (ber- spelling, dari / di / dengan, pukul). Accept the spoken forms a learner knows (Asal saya dari …) but ask for the standard form once in the rewrite.
Personal details are optional: a learner may write as an invented persona. Do not ask anyone to share marital or family details.
This is the extra 45-minute writing block after unit 10B.

Unit 11A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|7.source_text: Explanation: A meN- verb is a root with meN- in front: baca → membaca, tulis → menulis. The doer comes first, then the verb, then the thing, with no little word for it: Aini membaca buku itu. (the Kata-Kata frame) or Puan Aini membaca emel itu. Only the front changes shape, and the first sound of the root decides how. mem- before b (membeli, membaca, membuat, membuka, membawa, membayar); men- before c, d and j (mencari, mencuci, mendengar, menjawab, menjual); meng- before h or a vowel (menghantar, mengambil); me- before l and m (melihat, memasak: the m of masak stays). With t and p the first sound drops out: tulis → menulis, tutup → menutup, tunggu → menunggu, panggil → memanggil. Unit 11B adds s, k and one-syllable roots. In everyday speech people often leave meN- off: Puan Aini baca emel itu (spoken). The meN- form is the standard, so say it first; the verb never changes for who or when (sedang, sudah and akan do that job).

Unit 11A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|8.source_text: 説明：meN- の動詞は、語根の前に meN- を付けた形です：baca → membaca、tulis → menulis。動作主が先、次に動詞、最後に物が来て、「を」にあたる語はありません：Puan Aini membaca emel itu. 形が変わるのは前の部分だけで、語根の最初の音で決まります。b の前は mem-（membeli・membaca・membuat・membuka・membawa・membayar）、c・d・j の前は men-（mencari・mencuci・mendengar・menjawab・menjual）、h か母音の前は meng-（menghantar・mengambil）、l と m の前は me-（melihat・memasak：masak の m は残ります）。t と p は最初の音が落ちます：tulis → menulis、tutup → menutup、tunggu → menunggu、panggil → memanggil。s・k・一音節の語根は11Bで習います。日常会話では meN- を付けないこともよくあります：Puan Aini baca emel itu（話し言葉）。標準は meN- の形なので、まずこちらを言います。動詞は人や時で形が変わらず、sedang・sudah・akan が時を表します。

Unit 11A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|9.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese verbs have no prefix, so the nasal change is new, but the order doer + verb + thing matches 〜が〜を〜する. Two things mislead: meN- is not ます (it adds no politeness and no past), and there is no を: the thing follows the verb directly.

Unit 11A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|0.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の動詞には接頭辞がないので鼻音の変化は初めてですが、動作主＋動詞＋物の順は「〜が〜を〜する」と同じです。ただし二点に注意：meN- は「ます」ではなく（ていねいさも過去も表しません）、「を」にあたる語もないので、物は動詞のすぐあとに置きます。

Unit 11A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|9.source_text: Explanation: Chapter 9 gave you the di- verb: the thing comes first and oleh introduces the doer. It is the same event as the meN- line: Aini membaca buku itu. = Buku itu dibaca oleh Aini. and Puan Aini membaca emel itu. = Emel itu dibaca oleh Puan Aini. Choose by what you want to talk about: the doer first (meN-) or the thing first (di-). Notice that the nasal change disappears in the di- form because di- is added to the plain root: baca → membaca but dibaca; tulis → menulis but ditulis; panggil → memanggil but dipanggil. Not every meN- verb has a di- partner in this course: mencari, menjawab, melihat, mendengar, menunggu and menerima stay active here.
target_spans: Emel itu dibaca oleh Puan Aini.

Unit 11A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|1.source_text: 説明：第9章で習った di- の動詞は、物が先に来て、oleh のあとに動作主を置きます。meN- の文と同じできごとです：Puan Aini membaca emel itu. ＝ Emel itu dibaca oleh Puan Aini. 何について話したいかで選びます：動作主が先なら meN-、物が先なら di- です。di- の形では鼻音の変化がなくなることに注意してください。di- は元の語根に付くからです：baca → membaca ですが dibaca、tulis → menulis ですが ditulis、panggil → memanggil ですが dipanggil。このコースでは、すべての meN- の動詞に di- の相手があるわけではありません：mencari・menjawab・melihat・mendengar・menunggu・menerima は、ここでは能動のまま使います。
target_spans: Emel itu dibaca oleh Puan Aini.

Unit 11A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|1.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese passive (〜に読まれる) is the nearest idea, but the Japanese passive often suggests that something was done to you. The Malay di- form is neutral: Fail itu dihantar oleh Puan Aini only says who sent the file. Do not hear a complaint in it.
target_spans: Fail itu dihantar oleh Puan Aini

Unit 11A · Pattern and grammar focus|5|8.source_text: 説明：Siapa yang ＋ meN- の動詞で、誰がしたかをたずねます：Siapa yang menghantar fail itu? 答えも同じ形で、yang の前に動作主を置きます：Puan Aini yang menghantar fail itu.（そのファイルを送ったのはアイニさんです。）人に重点を置く言い方で、質問がたずねている点と合います。Puan Aini. だけの短い答えもかまいません。同じ型は11Bの Siapa yang menelefon? にも使えます。

Unit 11A · Pattern and grammar focus|5|1.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「誰が〜しましたか」と「〜したのはアイニさんです」はよく対応し、yang は「送ったのは」の「の」にあたります。語順も同じなので、この型は日本語話者にとってやさしいです。

Unit 11A · Pattern and grammar focus|6|0.source_text: Explanation: sedang (chapter 4) says that the action is happening now, and it goes in front of the meN- verb: Saya sedang menulis emel. The question word apa goes at the end and asks about the thing: Awak sedang menulis apa? The answer replaces apa with the thing. The other markers work the same way: Saya sudah menulis emel (done), Saya belum menulis emel (not yet), Saya akan menulis emel (will). The verb never changes.

Unit 11A · Pattern and grammar focus|6|1.source_text: 説明：sedang（第4章）は今その動作が進行中であることを表し、meN- の動詞の前に置きます：Saya sedang menulis emel. 疑問語 apa は最後に置いて物をたずね、答えでは apa を物に置き換えます：Awak sedang menulis apa? ほかのマーカーも同じです：Saya sudah menulis emel（済み）、Saya belum menulis emel（まだ）、Saya akan menulis emel（これから）。動詞は変わりません。

Unit 11A · Pattern and grammar focus|6|2.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 〜ている (書いている) is the same idea as sedang menulis, and the question 何を書いていますか puts the question word before the verb, but Malay puts apa at the end. Say the whole sentence first, then add apa.

Unit 11A · Pattern and grammar focus|6|3.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「〜ている」（書いている）は sedang menulis と同じ考え方です。ただし「何を書いていますか」は疑問語が動詞の前に来ますが、マレー語では apa が最後に来ます。まず文全体を言い、そのあとに apa を付けましょう。

Unit 11A · Pattern and grammar focus|7|2.source_text: Pattern 1: doer + meN- verb + the thing. If a learner says Puan Aini baca emel itu, accept it as everyday speech and model membaca. Write the front of each verb on the board and let the class find the rule from the first sound of the root.

Unit 11A · Pattern and grammar focus|7|3.source_text: Pattern 2: the di- partner of the same line. Check that oleh comes before the doer and that the nasal change is gone: dibaca, not *dimembaca. Unit 11A · Culture and usage note|2|0.source_text: Read about hearing the standard meN- form and the everyday short form, three verbs that need a word of warning, and how to put the doer or the thing first at work.

Unit 11A · Culture and usage note|3|0.source_text: In Malaysia you will hear most of these verbs in two forms. Writing, notices, meetings and polite speech use the meN- form: Puan Aini membaca emel itu. In a relaxed chat many people drop the front and say the root: Puan Aini baca emel itu, Saya tengok jam for Saya melihat jam. Both are correct Malaysian Malay. This course teaches the meN- form first, as the standard, and you will understand the short form when you hear it.

Unit 11A · Culture and usage note|3|1.source_text: Two verbs need a word of warning. menerima and melihat are learned as whole words, because their roots terima and lihat are not taught on their own in this course (you already know terima kasih). And menghantar has two everyday uses: to send a file, and to take someone to a place: Saya menghantar anak ke sekolah means that you take your child to school.

Unit 11A · Culture and usage note|3|2.source_text: In an office, who did what often matters, so you will hear both lines of a pair: the doer first (Puan Aini menghantar fail itu) when you ask or say who acted, and the thing first (Fail itu dihantar oleh Puan Aini) when the file is what you are talking about. Neither sounds rude or critical. Choose the one that fits the sentence you want to say.
target_spans: Fail itu dihantar oleh Puan Aini

Unit 11A · Culture and usage note|3|3.source_text: Japanese colleagues often ask Sudah dibaca? or Sudah dihantar? to check progress. A short, plain answer such as Sudah. or Belum. is polite and clear.

Unit 11A · Culture and usage note|3|5.source_text: マレーシアでは、これらの動詞の多くを二つの形で耳にします。書き言葉、掲示、会議、ていねいな会話では meN- の形を使います：Puan Aini membaca emel itu.くだけたおしゃべりでは、前の部分を落として語根だけを言う人も多いです：Puan Aini baca emel itu、Saya melihat jamの代わりにSaya tengok jam。どちらも正しいマレーシアのマレー語です。このコースでは標準として meN- の形を先に教え、短い形は聞いて分かるようにします。

Unit 11A · Culture and usage note|3|6.source_text: 注意が必要な動詞が二つあります。menerima と melihat は一語として覚えます。語根の terima と lihat は、このコースでは単独では教えないからです（terima kasih はすでに知っています）。また menghantar には日常で二つの使い方があります：ファイルを送ることと、人をある場所に連れて行くことです：Saya menghantar anak ke sekolah は、子どもを学校に送っていくという意味です。

Unit 11A · Culture and usage note|3|7.source_text: 職場では、誰が何をしたかが大切なことがよくあるので、ペアの両方の文を耳にします。誰が動いたかをたずねたり言ったりするときは動作主が先（Puan Aini menghantar fail itu）、ファイルについて話すときは物が先（Fail itu dihantar oleh Puan Aini）です。どちらも失礼でも批判的でもありません。言いたい文に合うほうを選びます。
target_spans: Fail itu dihantar oleh Puan Aini

Unit 11A · Culture and usage note|3|8.source_text: 日本人の同僚は、進み具合を確かめるために Sudah dibaca? や Sudah dihantar? とよくたずねます。Sudah. か Belum. の短くはっきりした答えで、ていねいで十分です。

Unit 11A · Teaching plan and answer key|.source_text: 先生用：45分×5ブロックの進め方、注意点、宿題です。答えは各シートのキーにあります。
（日本語は下書きです。ネイティブ・スピーカーの確認待ち）
No Malay explainer for Stage 2 units: explainers and rubrics are in Japanese or English only, as in Stage 1 (Sam, 13 Nov 2026). Select 日本語 or English.
Teacher plan: five 45-minute blocks with timings, what to listen for and homework. Answers are on each sheet.
Before Block A: Kata-Kata Sedia Kelas c11 (34 cards, frames ms-c11-f01 and ms-c11-f02).

After Block D: the Kata-Kata chapter 11 deck with spaced review, frames ms-c11-f01, ms-c11-f02, ms-c11-f03, ms-c11-f05 in the frame drill and Susun Ayat; about 3 hours of self-study for this unit (planning figure).

Hanashishou (Stage 2): the plan links chapter 11 to the office scene report_deadline for unit 11B, with mendaki from the social pack. Their Malay is not yet tagged by chapter (build step 6), so do not assign them yet.
Next: unit 11B (the draft, the deadline and the weekend), then the review block after 11B.
■ Block A · Words and patterns (45 min)
Goal: I can say who did what with a taught meN- verb and a thing: Puan Aini membaca emel itu.
0–5 Recall: chapters 9 and 10 (di- partners; ber- routines) from the opener prompts.
5–10 Tanya Cikgu questions from Kata-Kata.
10–20 Vocabulary focus: core words first, with each root; recognition and revision words are only pointed out.

20–40 Pattern focus: patterns 1 and 2 first (the active line and its di- partner), question and answer before the rule; then the vocabulary in three groups with each root, its chapter and the nasal change (reading, writing and files 7, buying, paying and carrying 6, senses, calling and everyday tasks 7). Write the six fronts mem-, men-, meng-, me- and the dropped t and p on the board.
40–45 First substitutions (Drill 2, items 1 to 3).
■ Block B · Drills and conversation (45 min)
Goal: I can ask and answer Siapa yang …? and Awak sedang … apa? with meN- verbs, and turn a meN- line into its di- partner.
0–5 Recall: say who sent the file, with the doer first and then with the thing first.
5–25 Drill ladder in order: pattern table, substitution, transformation (spoken to standard first), question and answer, question-word choice, short dialogues, then the markers drill.
25–40 Model conversation, gapped form, then the changed-facts variant.
40–45 Pair rehearsal without the script.
■ Block C · Listening and task (45 min)
Goal: I can follow a colleague's morning with files and emails, and report who sent, received and opened what.
0–5 Recall: each learner says one thing they sent and one thing they received.
5–20 Listening: read the questions, two readings, check, then shadow three lines.
20–30 Reading and writing.
30–45 Task with role cards; announce the change of plan halfway.
■ Block D · Review and test (45 min)
Goal: I can check the meN- spelling of each verb and its di- partner, and correct a short report.
0–15 Mixed review: cumulative question-word drill (chapters 1 to 11), then the markers drill with new cues and a spelling check of membeli, menulis, memanggil, mencari, menghantar.
15–25 Unit test (low-stakes).
25–35 Self-check and feedback.
35–45 Preview: unit 11B: the draft, the deadline and the weekend (Kata-Kata c11 cards ms-c11-021 to ms-c11-043 and frames f04, f06).
■ Block E · Scene transfer (45 min)
Goal: I can explain who read, sent and received a file in a short role-play, and change one fact.
0–5 Recall: say three things you did at work yesterday with meN- verbs.
5–15 Scene listening: read the Kata-Kata scenario lines ms-c11-s01 to ms-c11-s08 (Tanaka, Puan Aini and Encik Rahman, the email and the file) twice; learners tick the meN- verbs they hear.
15–30 Role-play in pairs: pairs play the same scene with their own files and names, without the script.
30–40 Changed situation: a changed morning: the file cannot be opened, so A explains who sent it, who received it and who is looking for the password; B asks Siapa yang …? and Awak sedang … apa?
40–45 Culture and usage note discussion, and the home-practice briefing.

Load: 21 core words in three groups (reading, writing and files 8; buying, paying and carrying 6; senses, calling and everyday tasks 7), no recognition word (no Dunia scene primes chapter 11), and revision of the roots, the di- partners, the office words and the markers. Suggested order: Block A the first group with patterns 1 and 2; Block B the second group with pattern 3; the third group with pattern 4 in Block B or C. If the pilot shows 21 is too many, the natural cut is: membaca, menulis, menghantar, menerima, membuka, membeli, membayar, mencari, menunggu, memanggil first; the rest second.
The scene lines ms-c11-s06 and ms-c11-s07 use menelefon, a unit 11B core word (card ms-c11-040). Gloss it as "to phone" and treat it as recognition here; it is taught in 11B.

meN- rule (plan section 3, Sam 13 Nov 2026): mem- before b; men- before c, d, j; meng- before h or a vowel; me- before l and m; t and p drop (menulis, memanggil). The nasal-change traps from the Kata-Kata cards: memanggil, not *mempanggil (card ms-c11-013); menulis, not *mentulis (ms-c11-003); menutup, not *mentutup (ms-c11-008); menunggu, not *mentunggu (ms-c11-019). memasak keeps its m (ms-c11-004): not *memmasak. Unit 11B adds s and k and the one-syllable roots (menyewa, menyapu as a mention only, mengira, mengecas).

Common traps from the cards: menerima (ms-c11-015) and melihat (ms-c11-017) are whole words; their roots are not taught alone. melihat is standard, everyday speech says tengok (ms-c11-017). menghantar (ms-c11-014) also means to take someone to a place. The di- partner appears only where the card names one (chapter 9); do not make a di- form for mencari, menjawab, melihat, mendengar, menunggu or menerima.

Where Japanese learners usually slip: (1) treating meN- like ます or like the past, and so adding it to every verb; (2) a requested action takes the plain root (Tolong baca emel ini), not the meN- form: *Tolong membaca emel ini is wrong; (3) 聞く covers mendengar (hear, listen to) and asking a question (tanya, chapter 2): ask which they mean; (4) spelling: dropping the first sound of b, c, d, j (membeli is right, *meli is wrong) or keeping it for t and p (*mentulis, *mempanggil); (5) reading the di- form as a complaint because the Japanese passive often is one; (6) 見る covers melihat and tengok: teach melihat first, accept tengok in speech.

In conversation, focus the doer with yang (Encik Tanaka yang membeli kopi itu, Siapa yang membaca emel itu?); the model conversation does this. Keep di- … oleh for the drills and for written notices (Sam, 13 Nov 2026: in speech people focus with yang).
target_spans: Encik Tanaka yang membeli kopi itu

Unit 11B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|7.source_text: Explanation: Tolong semak + the thing is the everyday request: Tolong semak draf ini. (Please check this draft.) A request takes the plain root, not the meN- form: semak, not menyemak. The same root becomes menyemak when you say what someone is doing: Cik Mei Ling sedang menyemak draf itu. The deadline is tarikh akhir in a notice or a message; in speech you will hear deadline (spoken), so the answer to Tarikh akhir bila? can be Hari Jumaat. or Deadline hari Jumaat. Say it in writing with tarikh akhir.
target_spans: Cik Mei Ling sedang menyemak draf itu.

Unit 11B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|8.source_text: 説明：Tolong semak ＋ 物は、日常のいちばん使う依頼の言い方です：Tolong semak draf ini.（この下書きを確認してください。）依頼には meN- の形ではなく、語根をそのまま使います：semak で、menyemak ではありません。同じ語根でも、誰かがしていることを言うときは menyemak になります：Cik Mei Ling sedang menyemak draf itu. 締め切りは、掲示やメッセージでは tarikh akhir で、話し言葉では deadline（話し言葉）も聞きます。Tarikh akhir bila? への答えは Hari Jumaat. でも Deadline hari Jumaat. でもよいですが、書くときは tarikh akhir を使います。
target_spans: Cik Mei Ling sedang menyemak draf itu.

Unit 11B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|9.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 〜してください (確認してください) matches Tolong semak …, and the Japanese verb stem is used without a polite ending in the plain request, much as Malay uses the bare root. The mistake is to copy a polite verb into Malay: *Tolong menyemak draf ini sounds odd; use the root.

Unit 11B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|1.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「〜してください」（確認してください）は Tolong semak … にあたります。丁寧な語尾を付けずに語根をそのまま使うところも、マレー語の語根のままの依頼に似ています。間違いやすいのは丁寧な動詞形をそのままマレー語にすることです：*Tolong menyemak draf ini は不自然なので、語根を使います。

Unit 11B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|2.source_text: Explanation: mahu + a meN- verb says what you plan to do: Hujung minggu ini saya mahu mendaki. Nothing comes between mahu and the verb, and the verb keeps its meN- form after mahu. Rancangan is the plan itself: Apa rancangan awak? (What are your plans?). In everyday talk people say nak for mahu (spoken); say mahu first. melancong is a trip for pleasure and takes no object, so melancong ke Johor Bahru uses ke for the place and has no di- form. menyewa is to rent as a tenant, meminjam to borrow for a while: the two are not the same word.
target_spans: Hujung minggu ini saya mahu mendaki.

Unit 11B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|3.source_text: 説明：mahu ＋ meN- の動詞で、したいことを言います：Hujung minggu ini saya mahu mendaki. mahu と動詞の間には何も入れず、動詞は mahu のあとでも meN- の形のままです。Rancangan は計画そのものです：Apa rancangan awak?（ご予定は？）日常会話では mahu の代わりに nak（話し言葉）とも言いますが、まず mahu を言います。melancong は楽しみの旅行で目的語をとらないので、melancong ke Johor Bahru のように場所には ke を使い、di- の形はありません。menyewa は借り手として賃借すること、meminjam は一時的に借りることで、同じ語ではありません。
target_spans: Hujung minggu ini saya mahu mendaki.

Unit 11B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|4.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 借りる covers both menyewa (rent a flat) and meminjam (borrow a pen): ask which one is meant. 〜したい (料理したい) matches mahu memasak, but Japanese puts a の/こと after the verb in some patterns; Malay never does.

Unit 11B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|5.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「借りる」は menyewa（部屋を借りる）と meminjam（ペンを借りる）の両方にあたります。どちらの意味かを確かめましょう。「〜したい」（料理したい）は mahu memasak にあたります。日本語では動詞のあとに「の・こと」が付く型がありますが、マレー語では付けません。

Unit 11B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|0.source_text: Explanation: These are the rest of the spelling changes. s drops and meny- is used: sewa → menyewa, simpan → menyimpan, semak → menyemak. k drops and meng- is used: kira → mengira. p and t drop: memilih, meminjam, memesan, menukar, menolong, menelefon. meng- before a vowel: mengisi, mengajar. A root of one syllable takes menge-: cas → mengecas. All the cases together: mem- before b; t, p, s and k drop; meng- before h or a vowel; men- before c, d and j; me- before l, m, n, r, w and y; menge- before a one-syllable root. The word menyapu (to sweep) is spelt the same way, with meny-, not *mensapu.

Unit 11B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|1.source_text: 説明：残りのつづりの変化です。s は落ちて meny- になります：sewa → menyewa、simpan → menyimpan、semak → menyemak。k は落ちて meng- になります：kira → mengira。p と t は落ちます：memilih・meminjam・memesan・menukar・menolong・menelefon。母音の前は meng-：mengisi・mengajar。一音節の語根には menge- を付けます：cas → mengecas。まとめると、b の前は mem-、t・p・s・k は落ちる、h か母音の前は meng-、c・d・j の前は men-、l・m・n・r・w・y の前は me-、一音節の語根は menge- です。menyapu（掃く）も同じで、meny- を使い、*mensapu とは書きません。

Unit 11B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|2.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese has no sound change like this, so the spelling has to be practised aloud: say the root, say the front, then the verb. Two traps for a reader of English or Japanese: the first sound of a root such as sewa or kira is not repeated (*mensewa, *mengkira are wrong), and cas needs menge-, not meng- alone.

Unit 11B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|3.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語にはこのような音の変化がないので、声に出して練習しましょう：語根を言い、前の部分を言い、そのあと動詞を言います。英語や日本語を読む人が陥りやすい二つの落とし穴：sewa や kira のような語根の最初の音は残さず（*mensewa や *mengkira は間違い）、cas には meng- だけでなく menge- が必要です。

The answer puts the doer in front of yang: Cik Mei Ling yang menyemak draf itu. The same frame asks about the plan: Siapa yang akan menelefon? (Who will phone?) with akan. For menolong, remember the difference between asking for help and talking about it: Tolong! or Tolong semak draf ini is the request (chapter 8), and Cik Mei Ling menolong saya says that she helped.

Unit 11B · Pattern and grammar focus|6|1.source_text: 説明：11Aの型が新しい動詞で戻ってきます：Siapa yang menyemak draf itu? 答えでは yang の前に動作主を置きます：Cik Mei Ling yang menyemak draf itu. 同じ型で予定もたずねられます：Siapa yang akan menelefon?（誰が電話しますか。）akan を使います。menolong は、頼むことと話すことの違いを覚えてください：Tolong! や Tolong semak draf ini が依頼（第8章）で、Cik Mei Ling menolong saya は助けてくれたという報告です。

Unit 11B · Culture and usage note|3|0.source_text: In the office you will meet tarikh akhir in a notice, a form or an email, and deadline in a chat or at a meeting: Tarikh akhir hari Jumaat and Deadline hari Jumaat mean the same. This course teaches tarikh akhir first, as the formal and written word, and you will understand deadline when you hear it. In the same way menukar (to change, to exchange) is the standard word and tukar is what people usually say: Saya mahu tukar bilik.

Unit 11B · Culture and usage note|3|1.source_text: Japanese learners are often caught by 借りる. Malay has two verbs: menyewa is to rent as a tenant, for a longer time and for money, and meminjam is to borrow something for a while: Kami menyewa rumah but Saya meminjam pen awak. Likewise 聞く and 見る each have several Malay verbs, so decide which meaning you want before you pick the verb.

Unit 11B · Culture and usage note|3|2.source_text: A request to a colleague is short and plain. Tolong semak draf ini uses the bare root semak, and the colleague answers Baik or Boleh. You do not add a long polite phrase. When you say what someone is doing, use the meN- form: Cik Mei Ling sedang menyemak draf itu.
target_spans: Cik Mei Ling sedang menyemak draf itu.

Unit 11B · Culture and usage note|3|3.source_text: mengecas telefon is the ordinary Malaysian way to say that you are charging a phone, and asking Boleh saya mengecas telefon saya di sini? is polite and normal in an office. Weekend plans such as mendaki (hiking) and melancong (travelling for pleasure) are a friendly topic: ask Hujung minggu ini awak buat apa? and listen for the plan.
target_spans: Boleh saya mengecas telefon saya di sini?
Hujung minggu ini awak buat apa?

Unit 11B · Culture and usage note|3|5.source_text: 職場では、掲示・書類・メールでは tarikh akhir、チャットや会議では deadline を目にします。Tarikh akhir hari JumaatとDeadline hari Jumaatは同じ意味です。このコースでは、あらたまった書き言葉として tarikh akhir を先に教え、deadline は聞いて分かるようにします。同じように、menukar（替える・交換する）が標準の語で、ふだんは tukar と言う人が多いです：Saya mahu tukar bilik.

Unit 11B · Culture and usage note|3|6.source_text: 日本人の学習者は「借りる」でつまずきがちです。マレー語には二つの動詞があります。menyewa は借り手として、長い期間、お金を払って借りること、meminjam は物を一時的に借りることです：Kami menyewa rumahですがSaya meminjam pen awakです。同じように「聞く」と「見る」にも、それぞれいくつかのマレー語の動詞があるので、言いたい意味を決めてから動詞を選びましょう。

Unit 11B · Culture and usage note|3|7.source_text: 同僚への依頼は短くシンプルです。Tolong semak draf ini は語根の semak をそのまま使い、同僚は Baik か Boleh と答えます。長いていねいな言い方を付け足す必要はありません。誰かがしていることを言うときは meN- の形を使います：Cik Mei Ling sedang menyemak draf itu.
target_spans: Cik Mei Ling sedang menyemak draf itu.

Unit 11B · Culture and usage note|3|8.source_text: mengecas telefon は、携帯電話を充電するときのふつうのマレーシアの言い方で、Boleh saya mengecas telefon saya di sini? と頼むのは職場でもていねいで自然です。mendaki（ハイキング）や melancong（楽しみの旅行）のような週末の予定は親しみのある話題です：Hujung minggu ini awak buat apa?とたずね、予定を聞きましょう。

Unit 11B · Teaching plan and answer key|.source_text: 先生用：45分×5ブロックの進め方、注意点、宿題です。答えは各シートのキーにあります。
（日本語は下書きです。ネイティブ・スピーカーの確認待ち）
No Malay explainer for Stage 2 units: explainers and rubrics are in Japanese or English only, as in Stage 1 (Sam, 13 Nov 2026). Select 日本語 or English.
Teacher plan: five 45-minute blocks with timings, what to listen for and homework. Answers are on each sheet.
Before Block A: Kata-Kata Sedia Kelas c11 (34 cards, frames ms-c11-f01 and ms-c11-f02).

After Block D: the Kata-Kata chapter 11 deck with spaced review, frames ms-c11-f04, ms-c11-f06, ms-c11-f01, ms-c11-f03 in the frame drill and Susun Ayat; about 3 hours of self-study for this unit (planning figure).

Hanashishou (Stage 2): the plan links chapter 11 to the office scene report_deadline for this unit, with mendaki from the social pack. Their Malay is not yet tagged by chapter (build step 6), so do not assign them yet. The full story already contains later words and suffixes.
Next: the review block after 11B (chapters 10 and 11), then chapter 12 (suffixed verb forms).
■ Block A · Words and patterns (45 min)
Goal: I can request a check with Tolong semak … and say what I want to do this weekend with mahu and a meN- verb.
0–5 Recall: unit 11A (who sent and received the file) from the opener prompts.
5–10 Tanya Cikgu questions from Kata-Kata.
10–20 Vocabulary focus: core words first, with each root; recognition and revision words are only pointed out.

20–40 Pattern focus: patterns 1 and 2 first (the request and the weekend plan), question and answer before the rule; then the vocabulary in three groups with each root and the nasal change (the draft and the deadline 6, messages, phones, money and choices 7, free time, help and renting 8). Write the full spelling table on the board.
40–45 First substitutions (Drill 2, items 1 to 3).
■ Block B · Drills and conversation (45 min)
Goal: I can ask and answer about a draft, a deadline and the weekend, and spell the meN- verbs with s, k and one-syllable roots.
0–5 Recall: say your weekend plan with Hujung minggu ini saya mahu ….
5–25 Drill ladder in order: pattern table, substitution, transformation (spoken to standard first), question and answer, question-word choice, short dialogues, then the markers drill.
25–40 Model conversation, gapped form, then the changed-facts variant.
40–45 Pair rehearsal without the script.
■ Block C · Listening and task (45 min)
Goal: I can follow a colleague's weekend plans and a message about a draft, and agree when the draft will be ready.
0–5 Recall: each learner says one thing they asked a colleague to check.
5–20 Listening: read the questions, two readings, check, then shadow three lines.
20–30 Reading and writing.
30–45 Task with role cards; announce the change of plan halfway.
■ Block D · Review and test (45 min)
Goal: I can check the spelling of the meN- verbs and correct a short message about a draft.
0–15 Mixed review: cumulative question-word drill (chapters 1 to 11), then the markers drill with new cues and a spelling check of menyewa, mengira, mengecas, memesan, meminjam.
15–25 Unit test (low-stakes).
25–35 Self-check and feedback.
35–45 Preview: the review block for chapters 10 and 11 (45 minutes), then chapter 12 (suffixed verb forms).
■ Block E · Scene transfer (45 min)
Goal: I can confirm a deadline and chat about the weekend in a short role-play, and handle a moved deadline.
0–5 Recall: say three things you do for work and one thing you want to do this weekend.

5–15 Scene listening: read the Kata-Kata scenario lines ms-c11-s09 to ms-c11-s18 (Tanaka and Cik Mei Ling: the draft, the deadline, the weekend, the coffee) twice; learners tick the meN- verbs they hear.
15–30 Role-play in pairs: pairs play the same scene with their own draft and weekend plan, without the script.
30–40 Changed situation: a moved deadline: B says the deadline is now Thursday; A says when the draft will be ready, who will check it and who will send it.
40–45 Culture and usage note discussion, and the home-practice briefing.

Load: 24 core words in three groups (the draft and the deadline 6; messages, phones, money and choices 7; free time, help and renting 11), two recognition entries (tukar and deadline), and revision of the roots, the office, free time and the markers. Suggested order: Block A the first group with patterns 1 and 2; Block B the second group with pattern 3 (the spelling table); the third group with pattern 4 in Block B or C. If the pilot shows 24 is too many, the natural cut is: menyemak, semak, draf, tarikh akhir, mesej, menelefon, mendaki, memesan, menyewa, mengecas first; the rest second.

The nasal-change traps from the Kata-Kata cards: menyewa, not *mensewa (card ms-c11-021); mengira, not *mengkira (ms-c11-027); mengecas, not *mengcas (ms-c11-041); memilih, meminjam and memesan drop the p (ms-c11-029 to -031); menolong drops the t (ms-c11-032). The same rule for menyapu (to sweep, not a ledger word, quoted only): meny-, not *mensapu. Say the root aloud first, then the front, then the whole verb.

Other traps: semak as a request takes the plain root (card ms-c11-038: Tolong semak draf ini), not the meN- form. menyewa is to rent and meminjam to borrow for a while (ms-c11-030); 借りる covers both. menolong is a verb ("to help"); tolong is the request (chapter 8, ms-c11-032). melancong takes no object and has no di- form (ms-c11-022). rancangan is learned as a whole word (ms-c11-037).

Spoken forms (recognition only): tukar for menukar (ms-c11-042) and deadline for tarikh akhir (ms-c11-043). Both are labelled spoken wherever they appear and never in a key, a dialogue or the listening. nak (spoken mahu) is a Stage 1 pair: accept it in speech.

Where Japanese learners usually slip: (1) 借りる for both menyewa and meminjam; (2) using the meN- form in a request: *Tolong menyemak draf ini; (3) repeating the first sound of the root: *mensewa, *mengkira; (4) forgetting menge- for a one-syllable root (*mengcas); (5) hearing mahu + a meN- verb as a polite future: mahu is "want", and akan is "will"; (6) 聞く, 見る and 払う have more than one Malay verb: decide the meaning first.
Standard first: teach the meN- form, accept the everyday root in speech (semak, tukar, cas, telefon), and never mark it wrong in a speaking task. The review block after this unit has no new words.

The scene follows Kata-Kata c11 (scenario lines ms-c11-s09 to s18, frames f04 and f06, with f01 and f03 returning). All names, times and plans are fictional; learners may use their real week or an invented one.
Cumulative question words: chapters 1 to 11. Chapter 11 adds no new question word.

Unit 11B · Review block · Chapters 10 an.source_text: Notice: ber- verbs have no object (bermula, bekerja, bertolak); meN- verbs take the thing directly (membaca emel); the di- partner puts the thing first (Fail itu dihantar oleh …); the markers go in front of any of them. / 気づくこと：ber- の動詞は目的語をとらず、meN- の動詞は物をすぐあとに置き、di- の相手は物が先に来て、マーカーはどれの前にも付きます。
■ Plan · 45 minutes · 進め方
0–5 Recall: say three things you do every morning (ber-) and three things you did with a file (meN-).
5–15 Mixed input: read the model; underline every ber- verb, meN- verb and di- verb and name the marker in front of each.
15–30 Alternating role task: in pairs, one is a manager who asks and one is the colleague who answers; swap after seven minutes (task below).
30–40 Changed situation: the manager says the meeting now starts earlier and the file has not arrived; the colleague explains who is doing what.
40–45 Self-check against the list below, then one thing to practise at home.
0–5 復習・5–15 混合の入力・15–30 役割交代のタスク・30–40 状況の変更・40–45 自己チェック。
■ Your turn · 自分で

Part 1 (15 min, alternating): A is the manager and asks about the morning: Pukul berapa mesyuarat bermula?, Siapa yang menghantar fail itu?, Awak sedang menulis apa?, Awak sudah bersarapan? B answers with at least one ber- verb, one meN- verb and one di- sentence. After seven minutes swap.

Part 2 (10 min, changed situation): A says Maaf, mesyuarat bermula pukul sembilan dan fail itu belum sampai. B says who will phone, who is checking the draft and who is waiting, using akan, sedang and belum.
target_spans: Maaf, mesyuarat bermula pukul sembilan dan fail itu belum sampai.

Unit 11B · Review block · Chapters 10 an.source_text: Part 3 (5 min): write three sentences about your own morning, one with each kind of verb.
パート1：交代でマネージャーと同僚を演じます。パート2：状況が変わり、同僚は誰が電話し、誰が下書きを確認し、誰が待っているかを説明します。パート3：自分の朝について、三種類の動詞を一つずつ使った3文を書きます。
■ Peer check · 互いに確認
☐ ber- verbs have no object and keep the spelling of their card (be- in bekerja, berehat).
☐ meN- verbs have the right front for the first sound of the root (membaca, menulis, memanggil, menyemak, mengecas).
☐ The di- sentence puts the thing first and oleh before the doer.
☐ A request uses the plain root (Tolong semak draf ini).
☐ The marker (sudah, belum, sedang, akan) stands in front of the verb and the verb does not change.

Model: Any natural exchange that follows the checklist. Model: Mesyuarat bermula pukul sembilan. Saya sudah membaca emel itu. Fail itu dihantar oleh Cik Mei Ling. Encik Rahman akan menelefon Osaka. Saya sedang menyemak draf itu, dan Puan Aini sedang menunggu di lif.
target_spans: Mesyuarat bermula pukul sembilan. Saya sudah membaca emel itu. Fail itu dihantar oleh Cik Mei Ling. Encik Rahman akan menelefon Osaka. Saya sedang menyemak draf itu, dan Puan Aini sedang menunggu di lif.

A review block has no new words. Every word is from chapters 1 to 11; the three core groups of 10A, 10B, 11A and 11B all return.

Unit 12A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|7.source_text: Explanation: -kan goes on the end of a root and gives the verb a new job: do it for someone, or make it happen. hantar (send, Dunia, chapter 2) becomes hantarkan (send it for me); simpan (keep) becomes simpankan (keep it for me); letak becomes letakkan (put it there). A request has Tolong first, then the -kan verb, then the thing: Tolong simpankan bungkusan ini. (the Kata-Kata frame). Everyday speech often drops the suffix: Tolong simpan bungkusan ini, Tolong tutup pintu itu. Both are correct. This course teaches the -kan form first, because it shows who the action is for, and you will understand the short form when you hear it. Watch the spelling: two k in letakkan and tunjukkan (the root ends in k and -kan starts with k), and berikan is beri + -kan, not ber- + ikan. Pastikan means to make sure. The thing follows the verb with no little word for it.

Unit 12A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|8.source_text: 説明：-kan は語根の終わりに付いて、動詞に「誰かのためにする」「そうなるようにする」という働きを加えます。hantar（送る、Dunia・第2章）は hantarkan（送ってあげる）、simpan（預かる）は simpankan（預かってあげる）、letak は letakkan（そこに置く）になります。依頼は Tolong が先で、次に -kan の動詞、最後に物：Tolong simpankan bungkusan ini.（Kata-Kata の文型）。日常会話では接尾辞を落とすことも多いです：Tolong simpan bungkusan ini.、Tolong tutup pintu itu. どちらも正しい言い方です。このコースでは、誰のための動作かが分かるので -kan の形を先に教え、短い形は聞いて分かるようにします。つづりに注意：letakkan と tunjukkan は k が二つ（語根の終わりの k と -kan の k）で、berikan は beri ＋ -kan（ber- ＋ ikan ではありません）。Pastikan は「確かめる」です。物は動詞のすぐあとに置き、「を」にあたる語はありません。

Unit 12A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|9.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 〜てください is one pattern for every verb, and 〜てあげる / 〜てくれる says who the action is for. -kan is closer to 〜てあげる, but it is part of the verb, not a separate word. It is not a politeness ending, so do not put it on every verb: Tolong baca emel ini (read this email) takes no -kan.

Unit 12A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|0.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「〜てください」はどの動詞にも使える一つの型で、「〜てあげる」「〜てくれる」は誰のための動作かを表します。-kan は「〜てあげる」に近いですが、別の語ではなく動詞の一部です。ていねいさを表す語尾ではないので、どの動詞にも付けてはいけません：Tolong baca emel ini（このメールを読んでください）に -kan は付きません。

Unit 12A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|9.source_text: Explanation: Boleh + a -kan verb + the thing is the polite question for the same idea: Boleh tunjukkan mesej itu? (the Kata-Kata frame) asks for a favour. The answer is Boleh. or Maaf, tidak boleh., and a short extra word is natural. The suffix says that the favour is for the speaker: ambilkan (get it for me), belikan (buy it for me), bawakan (bring it for me), berikan (give it to me), pulangkan (give it back). Everyday speech often has the root: Boleh bagi nombor telefon puan? (bagi is the everyday word for berikan, Dunia, chapter 4). You can put Tolong in front for a softer request: Boleh tolong hantarkan bungkusan kecil itu ke unit 8-1?
target_spans: Boleh tolong hantarkan bungkusan kecil itu ke unit 8-1?

Unit 12A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|1.source_text: 説明：Boleh ＋ -kan の動詞 ＋ 物は、同じ内容のていねいな質問です：Boleh tunjukkan mesej itu?（Kata-Kata の文型）でお願いをします。答えは Boleh. か Maaf, tidak boleh. で、短いひとことを足すと自然です。接尾辞は「話し手のために」を表します：ambilkan（取ってきて）、belikan（買ってきて）、bawakan（持ってきて）、berikan（渡して）、pulangkan（返して）。日常会話では語根だけのこともあります：Boleh bagi nombor telefon puan?（bagi は berikan の日常語、Dunia・第4章）。前に Tolong を付けるとやわらかい依頼になります：Boleh tolong hantarkan bungkusan kecil itu ke unit 8-1?
target_spans: Boleh tolong hantarkan bungkusan kecil itu ke unit 8-1?

Unit 12A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|1.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 〜てもらえますか is one pattern for every verb. In Malay the favour is in the verb: tunjukkan already means 見せてもらえますか in this question. Say Boleh tunjukkan mesej itu? and do not add anything for 〜てもらえますか.

Unit 12A · Pattern and grammar focus|5|0.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「〜てもらえますか」はどの動詞にも使える一つの型です。マレー語ではお願いの気持ちが動詞の中にあります：この質問の tunjukkan が「見せて」にあたります。Boleh tunjukkan mesej itu? と言い、「〜てもらえますか」にあたる語を足さないでください。

Unit 12A · Pattern and grammar focus|5|9.source_text: Explanation: To collect something yourself, use the plain root: Saya mahu ambil bungkusan. (the Kata-Kata frame). The root is enough because the action is for you and nobody does it on your behalf. When the guard does it for you, the verb takes -kan: Boleh ambilkan bungkusan saya? This is the whole idea of the unit: the same root, with -kan when the action is for someone else or makes something happen. Sudah sampai? asks whether it has arrived. On the label you will read penerima (recipient), nombor penjejakan (tracking number; spoken nombor tracking) and the block and unit: Blok B, unit 12-3. Pengawal, pemilik and penerima are learned as whole words; pe- words as a family come in Stage 3.

Unit 12A · Pattern and grammar focus|5|1.source_text: 説明：自分で受け取るときは語根のままです：Saya mahu ambil bungkusan.（Kata-Kata の文型）。動作が自分のためで、誰かが代わりにするわけではないので、語根で十分です。守衛さんがしてくれるときは動詞に -kan が付きます：Boleh ambilkan bungkusan saya? これがこのユニットの中心です：同じ語根に、他の人のための動作やそうなるようにする動作のとき -kan が付きます。Sudah sampai? は「もう届いていますか」とたずねます。ラベルでは penerima（受取人）、nombor penjejakan（追跡番号、話し言葉は nombor tracking）、棟と部屋番号を読みます：Blok B, unit 12-3. Pengawal・pemilik・penerima は一語として覚えます。pe- の語を仲間として習うのは第3段階です。
Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 受け取りたいのですが and 取ってきてください both use 取る. Malay separates them: ambil when you do it, ambilkan when you ask someone to do it for you.

Unit 12A · Pattern and grammar focus|6|0.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語では「受け取りたいのですが」も「取ってきてください」も「取る」を使います。マレー語は分けます：自分でするなら ambil、誰かにしてもらうなら ambilkan です。

Your information (fictional): you are the guard. Two parcels are in the guardhouse: a big one for Block B, unit 12-3 (recipient Encik Tanaka) and a small one with a torn label (the unit number is Block A, unit 8-1). The owner of unit 8-1 is not home yet.
Ask B the unit, ask B to show the message and say which parcel is for B. Offer to keep the small parcel in the guardhouse.
Aの情報（架空）：あなたは守衛です。守衛所にはB棟12-3号室（受取人は田中さん）の大きな荷物と、ラベルが破れた小さな荷物（部屋番号はA棟8-1）があります。8-1の所有者はまだ帰宅していません。Bに部屋番号をたずね、メッセージを見せてもらい、どちらがBの荷物か伝えます。小さな荷物は守衛所で預かると言います。
■ Role card B · Bのカード
You want to collect your parcel (Block B, unit 12-3). Say what you want, give your unit, show the message and thank the guard.
The small parcel is not yours: ask the guard to deliver it or keep it. Ask the guard to bring the big parcel to the lift.
Bは荷物を受け取りに来ました（B棟12-3号室）。用件を言い、部屋番号を伝え、メッセージを見せ、守衛にお礼を言います。小さな荷物は自分のものではないので、守衛に届けるか預かってもらうよう頼みます。大きな荷物をエレベーターまで持っていってもらうよう頼みます。
■ Change of plan · 予定変更
Halfway, A says: Maaf, encik. Pemilik unit 8-1 sudah ada di rumah. Boleh encik bawakan bungkusan kecil itu ke atas? B agrees and asks A to give the parcel: Boleh. Tolong berikan bungkusan itu.
target_spans: Maaf, encik. Pemilik unit 8-1 sudah ada di rumah. Boleh encik bawakan bungkusan kecil itu ke atas?

Unit 12A · Culture and usage note|2|0.source_text: Read about hearing the same request with -kan and with the bare root, the spelling points, the usual slip of Japanese learners, and the general custom of a guardhouse.

Unit 12A · Culture and usage note|3|0.source_text: Most of these -kan words have an everyday partner without the suffix. In a careful or written request you hear Tolong simpankan bungkusan ini. In a quick chat many people say the root: Tolong simpan bungkusan ini. Both are correct Malaysian Malay. This course teaches the -kan form first, because it shows who the action is for, and you will understand the short form when you hear it. Berikan works the same way: everyday speech says bagi.

Unit 12A · Culture and usage note|3|1.source_text: Two points of spelling matter. letakkan and tunjukkan have two k, because the root ends in k and the suffix begins with k. And berikan is beri + -kan, not ber- + ikan. Japanese learners often put -kan on every verb, as if it were a polite ending. It is not: Tolong baca emel ini takes the root.

Unit 12A · Culture and usage note|3|2.source_text: General knowledge, not a rule and not a checked fact: in many Malaysian condominiums a guard keeps parcels at a guardhouse and may ask to see the delivery message. Arrangements differ from one building to another, so ask at your own guardhouse.

Unit 12A · Culture and usage note|3|3.source_text: A short, plain request with Tolong or Boleh is polite and clear. Address the guard as Encik (or Cik), say Terima kasih when you have your parcel, and expect a short, friendly answer.

Unit 12A · Culture and usage note|3|5.source_text: この -kan の語の多くには、接尾辞のない日常の形があります。ていねいな依頼や書き言葉では Tolong simpankan bungkusan ini. を使い、気軽なおしゃべりでは語根だけの Tolong simpan bungkusan ini. と言う人が多いです。どちらも正しいマレーシアのマレー語です。このコースでは、誰のための動作かが分かるので -kan の形を先に教え、短い形は聞いて分かるようにします。Berikan も同じで、日常では bagi と言います。

Unit 12A · Culture and usage note|3|6.source_text: つづりには二つ注意があります。letakkan と tunjukkan は、語根の終わりが k で接尾辞の初めも k なので k が二つになります。また berikan は beri ＋ -kan で、ber- ＋ ikan ではありません。日本人の学習者は -kan をていねいな語尾のようにどの動詞にも付けがちですが、そうではありません：Tolong baca emel ini は語根のままです。

Unit 12A · Culture and usage note|3|7.source_text: 一般的な知識であり、規則でも確認済みの事実でもありません：マレーシアの多くのコンドミニアムでは、守衛さんが守衛所で荷物を預かり、配達のメッセージを見せるように言われることがあります。建物によって違うので、自分の建物の守衛所で聞きましょう。

Unit 12A · Culture and usage note|3|8.source_text: Tolong か Boleh を使った短くて簡単な依頼で、ていねいさは十分です。守衛さんには Encik（女性なら Cik）と呼びかけ、荷物を受け取ったら Terima kasih と言いましょう。短くて親しみのある返事が返ってきます。

■ Block A · Words and patterns (45 min)
Goal: I can ask for a favour with Tolong or Boleh and a -kan verb: Tolong simpankan bungkusan ini., Boleh tunjukkan mesej itu?

20–40 Pattern focus: patterns 1 and 2 first (the request and the polite question), question and answer before the rule; then the vocabulary in three groups with each root, its chapter and what -kan adds (for someone, or to make it happen 12, the guardhouse 6, the parcel 5 and the spoken nombor tracking). Write the root and the suffix side by side (hantar + -kan) and point out the two k in letakkan and tunjukkan.

■ Block B · Drills and conversation (45 min)
Goal: I can ask and answer about a parcel at the guardhouse, and choose between the root (ambil) and the -kan form (ambilkan).
0–5 Recall: say one request with Tolong and one with Boleh, first with the -kan form and then with the everyday root.

25–40 Model conversation, gapped form, then the changed-facts variant.
40–45 Pair rehearsal without the script.
Goal: I can follow a guard's questions about a parcel and read a notice and a message about a parcel on a label.
0–5 Recall: each learner says one thing they would ask a guard to keep, bring or show.
5–20 Listening: read the questions, two readings, check, then shadow three lines.
20–30 Reading and writing.
30–45 Task with role cards; announce the change of plan halfway.

Goal: I can check the spelling of the -kan verbs (two k in letakkan and tunjukkan) and correct a short request.

Goal: I can collect a parcel in a short role-play and handle a torn label.

5–15 Scene listening: read the Kata-Kata scenario lines ms-c12-s01 to ms-c12-s10 (Tanaka and the guard: the parcel, the torn label) twice; learners tick the -kan verbs they hear.

30–40 Changed situation: a parcel in the wrong place: the big parcel is at the lobby and the small one is still in the guardhouse; B asks A to bring one and keep the other, and A confirms with Saya bawakan … and Saya simpankan ….

Load: 23 core words in three groups (for someone, or to make it happen 12; the guardhouse 6; the parcel 5), one recognition word (nombor tracking), and revision of the roots, the parcel and the building, asking politely and the markers. Suggested order: Block A the first group with patterns 1 and 2; Block B the second group with pattern 3; the third group in Block B or C. If the pilot shows 23 is too many, the natural cut is: simpankan, hantarkan, tunjukkan, bawakan, ambilkan, letakkan, pengawal, pondok pengawal, unit, penerima first; the rest second.

The scene lines ms-c12-s09 (and s14 and s17 in unit 12B) use hubungi, a unit 12B core word (card ms-c12-027). Gloss it as "contact" and treat it as recognition here; it is taught in 12B with the other -i verb.

The -kan choice (plan section 3, Sam 13 Nov 2026): -kan means to do it for someone or to make it happen (simpankan, hantarkan, tunjukkan, matikan, bersihkan); -i means to or at a person or place (unit 12B). Show the root, its chapter and what the suffix adds in every vocabulary entry. Spelling: two k in letakkan and tunjukkan (card ms-c12-008 and -011); berikan is beri + -kan, not ber- + ikan (card ms-c12-010). The pe- and ke-an words (pengawal, pemilik, penerima, kebocoran, kerosakan) are whole words: their roots (kawal, milik, terima) are not taught alone (cards ms-c12-013, -017, -019).

Where Japanese learners usually slip: (1) putting -kan on every verb as if it were a polite ending: Tolong baca emel ini takes the root, and so does Saya mahu ambil bungkusan (card ms-c12-003 is for another person); (2) forgetting the double k: *letakan, *tunjukan; (3) hearing berikan as ber- + ikan; (4) a full meN- + -kan form (*menyimpankan, *menghantarkan) is not natural and is not taught: see the -kan rule below; (5) 〜てください covering both Tolong + root and Tolong + -kan: ask for whom the action is.

the -kan rule (Sam, 13 Nov 2026): use the bare -kan verb for a request (Tolong simpankan …, Boleh bawakan …?) and for a first-person offer or reply (Saya hantarkan sekarang., Baik, saya matikan sekarang.); in a statement with a third-person doer or with sudah, sedang, belum, akan, baru or masih, use the meN- verb the course has (Pengawal menyimpan bungkusan itu., Pengawal menghantar bungkusan itu., Pengawal membuka pintu itu., Saya sedang membawa bungkusan itu ke lif.); where the course has no meN- verb (letakkan, bukakan, matikan, bersihkan), rephrase: Saya letakkan bungkusan itu di sini sekarang., Saya bersihkan lantai itu sekarang. Do not teach forms such as *menyimpankan or *menghantarkan: they are not natural.
target_spans: Saya sedang membawa bungkusan itu ke lif.
Saya letakkan bungkusan itu di sini sekarang.

■ Your turn · 自分で
Write six to eight sentences: a message to your residents' chat about a parcel, and a note asking the guard to do two things. Include:

Unit 12B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|7.source_text: Explanation: -i goes on the end of a root and points the action at a person or a place: hubungi is hubung + -i, and it means to get in touch with someone. The person follows the verb directly, with no little word between them: Boleh hubungi juruteknik? (the Kata-Kata frame), not a word like dengan before the person. On notices you read Sila hubungi pejabat pengurusan. With meN- in front, hubungi becomes menghubungi (meng- before h): Kami akan menghubungi juruteknik. Choose the form by the sentence: after Tolong, Boleh or Sila, and in a first-person reply (Saya hubungi sekarang.), use hubungi; after a doer such as kami or pejabat pengurusan, or after sudah, belum, sedang or akan, use menghubungi. This is the same rule as for the -kan verbs. menelefon (chapter 11) means to phone, and hubungi does not say how you get in touch. The suffix -i does not mean the same as -kan: -i is to or at a person or place, -kan is for someone or to make it happen.

Unit 12B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|8.source_text: 説明：-i は語根の終わりに付いて、動作を人や場所に向けます：hubungi は hubung ＋ -i で、誰かと連絡を取るという意味です。人は動詞のすぐあとに置き、間に小さな語は入りません：Boleh hubungi juruteknik?（Kata-Kata の文型）。「に」にあたる語は入りません。掲示では Sila hubungi pejabat pengurusan. と読みます。前に meN- が付くと hubungi は menghubungi（h の前は meng-）になります：Kami akan menghubungi juruteknik. 使い分けは文で決まります：Tolong・Boleh・Sila のあと、また一人称の返事（Saya hubungi sekarang.）では hubungi、kami や pejabat pengurusan のような動作主のあと、また sudah・belum・sedang・akan のあとでは menghubungi を使います。-kan の動詞と同じ規則です。menelefon（第11章）は電話をかけることで、hubungi は連絡の手段を言いません。-i と -kan は同じではありません：-i は人や場所へ向かう動作、-kan は誰かのため・そうなるようにする動作です。

Unit 12B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|9.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 連絡する takes に: 技術者に連絡する. Malay has no に-word after hubungi: the person follows the verb directly. Do not add kepada or dengan.

Unit 12B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|0.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「連絡する」は「技術者に連絡する」のように「に」を取ります。マレー語の hubungi のあとには「に」にあたる語がなく、人は動詞のすぐあとに来ます。kepada や dengan を足さないでください。

Unit 12B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|9.source_text: Explanation: baiki is baik + -i. It looks like baik (good) but means to repair. With meN- in front, mem- before b gives membaiki: Juruteknik sedang membaiki paip. (the Kata-Kata frame). sedang goes in front of the verb, as in chapter 11. A request uses the root form: Tolong baiki paip ini. This course uses baiki and membaiki for a repair in Malaysian Malay. Gantikan (ganti + -kan) means to replace something: Tolong gantikan lampu itu., and ganti alone means to replace or to stand in for someone. Notice that the doer comes first and the thing follows the verb: Juruteknik membaiki paip.

Unit 12B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|1.source_text: 説明：baiki は baik ＋ -i です。baik（良い）に似ていますが、修理するという意味です。前に meN- が付き、b の前は mem- なので membaiki になります：Juruteknik sedang membaiki paip.（Kata-Kata の文型）。sedang は第11章と同じく動詞の前に置きます。依頼は語根の形です：Tolong baiki paip ini. このコースでは、マレーシアのマレー語として baiki・membaiki を使います。Gantikan（ganti ＋ -kan）は何かを取り替えることで、Tolong gantikan lampu itu.、ganti だけなら取り替える・誰かの代わりをするです。動作主が先で、物は動詞のすぐあとに来ることに注意：Juruteknik membaiki paip.
Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 直す and 修理する both fit membaiki. But 直す also covers correcting a mistake, and Malay does not use baiki for that. Do not mix it up with baik (good).
日本語との比較：日本語の「直す」「修理する」はどちらも membaiki にあたります。ただし「直す」は間違いを直す意味でも使いますが、マレー語ではその意味に baiki は使いません。baik（良い）と混同しないでください。

Unit 12B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|5.source_text: Explanation: To report a problem in your own home, say what is wrong and where: Ada kebocoran di siling saya. (the Kata-Kata frame). kebocoran (a leak) and kerosakan (damage, a fault) are learned as whole words, as are aduan (a complaint or problem report) and tempahan (a booking). Start the call with your name, block and unit, as Encik Tanaka does. The office answers with a question and then a request: Tolong matikan lampu itu dulu. and gives you a slot with the technician (juruteknik) or the contractor (kontraktor). Say the place after di: di siling bilik air saya, di paip dapur saya.

Unit 12B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|6.source_text: 説明：自分の家の問題を伝えるときは、何がどこでおかしいかを言います：Ada kebocoran di siling saya.（Kata-Kata の文型）。kebocoran（水漏れ）と kerosakan（故障・破損）は一語として覚え、aduan（苦情・問題の報告）と tempahan（予約）も同じです。田中さんのように、まず名前・棟・部屋番号を言って電話を始めます。事務所は質問のあとに依頼で答えます：Tolong matikan lampu itu dulu. そして技術者（juruteknik）か業者（kontraktor）の slot を教えてくれます。場所は di のあとに言います：di siling bilik air saya、di paip dapur saya。

Unit 12B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|7.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 〜が漏れています uses the verb 漏れる. Malay says Ada kebocoran (there is a leak), with ada and a noun, and di for the place. Do not look for a verb meaning to leak.

Unit 12B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|8.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「水漏れしています」は動詞を使いますが、マレー語は Ada kebocoran（水漏れがある）のように ada と名詞を使い、場所は di で言います。漏れるという動詞を探さないでください。

Unit 12B · Pattern and grammar focus|6|0.source_text: Explanation: These are the -kan verbs of 12A again, now for things in the home: matikan (switch off), hidupkan (switch on), bersihkan (clean), kosongkan (empty), isikan (fill in) and perlahankan (lower, slow down). Each is a root with -kan: mati + -kan, hidup + -kan, bersih (chapter 6) + -kan (it is bersih + -kan, not ber- + sih), kosong (chapter 3) + -kan, isi (Dunia, chapter 3) + -kan, perlahan (chapter 6) + -kan. Everyday speech: tutup lampu for matikan lampu and buka lampu for hidupkan lampu (also for the aircon); Sila isi borang ini for isikan. Both forms are correct; teach the -kan form first and recognise the everyday one.

Unit 12B · Pattern and grammar focus|6|1.source_text: 説明：12A の -kan の動詞が、今度は家の中の物に使われます：matikan（消す）、hidupkan（つける）、bersihkan（きれいにする）、kosongkan（空にする）、isikan（記入する）、perlahankan（小さくする・ゆっくりにする）。どれも語根に -kan が付いた形です：mati ＋ -kan、hidup ＋ -kan、bersih（第6章）＋ -kan（bersih ＋ -kan で、ber- ＋ sih ではありません）、kosong（第3章）＋ -kan、isi（Dunia・第3章）＋ -kan、perlahan（第6章）＋ -kan。日常会話では matikan lampu の代わりに tutup lampu、hidupkan lampu の代わりに buka lampu（エアコンも同じ）、isikan の代わりに Sila isi borang ini と言います。どちらも正しいので、-kan の形を先に教え、日常の形は聞いて分かるようにします。

Unit 12B · Pattern and grammar focus|6|2.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese uses one verb for each: 消す, つける, 掃除する. In Malay the suffix does the work: matikan is "make it dead", hidupkan is "make it alive". The meaning of -kan here is cause: you make something happen.

Unit 12B · Pattern and grammar focus|6|3.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語では「消す」「つける」「掃除する」とそれぞれ別の動詞を使います。マレー語では接尾辞が働きます：matikan は「死んだ状態にする」、hidupkan は「生きた状態にする」です。ここでの -kan の意味は「そうなるようにする」です。

Unit 12B · Pattern and grammar focus|7|2.source_text: Pattern 1: Boleh or Tolong + hubungi + the person. Check that nothing comes between the verb and the person (no dengan and no kepada). Accept Saya hubungi and Kami menghubungi in a reply.

Unit 12B · Pattern and grammar focus|7|3.source_text: Pattern 2: sedang membaiki + the thing. Check mem- before b. Keep baiki for a repair and baik for good, and do not use baiki for correcting a mistake.

Unit 12B · Pattern and grammar focus|7|4.source_text: Pattern 3: Ada kebocoran / kerosakan di + the place + saya. Check di before the place.

Unit 12B · Pattern and grammar focus|7|5.source_text: Pattern 4: Tolong + a -kan verb + the thing. Check matikan and hidupkan, and the spelling of bersihkan. Accept tutup lampu and buka lampu in speech.

Unit 12B · Markers with ‹-kan› and ‹-i›.source_text: 第4章の sudah・belum・sedang・masih・akan・baru を言い、素の -i の動詞を meN- の動詞（menghubungi・membaiki・mengisi）に直します。
（日本語は下書きです。ネイティブ・スピーカーの確認待ち）
No Malay explainer for Stage 2 units: explainers and rubrics are in Japanese or English only, as in Stage 1 (Sam, 13 Nov 2026). Select 日本語 or English.
Say the chapter 4 markers and change the bare -i verb to the meN- verb (menghubungi, membaiki, mengisi) after a marker.

Say each sentence again with the marker in brackets. After sudah, sedang, belum, akan, baru or masih, or with a third-person doer, use menghubungi and membaiki, not the bare hubungi and baiki. / かっこ内のマーカーを付けて言い直します。sudah・sedang・belum・akan・baru・masih のあと、または三人称の動作主のときは、hubungi・baiki ではなく menghubungi・membaiki を使います。
■ Say it with the marker · マーカーを付けて言う
1. Saya hubungi juruteknik. (marker: sudah)
2. Kontraktor membaiki siling itu. (marker: belum)
3. Juruteknik membaiki paip. (marker: sedang)
4. Kami menghubungi kontraktor. (marker: akan)
5. Saya mengisi borang aduan. (marker: baru)
6. Saya tunggu juruteknik. (marker: masih)
7. Answer Juruteknik sudah sampai? (marker: belum)
8. Pejabat pengurusan menghubungi juruteknik. (marker: sedang)
■ Japanese bridge · 日本語との橋渡し
sudah menghubungi ≈ もう連絡した · belum membaiki ≈ まだ修理していない · sedang membaiki ≈ 修理している · akan menghubungi ≈ 連絡する予定 · baru mengisi ≈ 記入したばかり

Japanese changes the verb ending (連絡した / 連絡していない); Malay puts the marker in front and uses the meN- verb (menghubungi), not the bare hubungi. / 日本語は動詞の語尾が変わります。マレー語はマーカーを前に置き、素の hubungi ではなく meN- の動詞（menghubungi）を使います。
Answers in order:
1 Saya sudah menghubungi juruteknik. 2 Kontraktor belum membaiki siling itu. 3 Juruteknik sedang membaiki paip. 4 Kami akan menghubungi kontraktor.
5 Saya baru mengisi borang aduan. 6 Saya masih tunggu juruteknik. 7 Belum. Juruteknik belum sampai. 8 Pejabat pengurusan sedang menghubungi juruteknik.

Unit 12B · Cumulative question-word dril.source_text: 第1章から第12章までの疑問語をすべて使って質問します。
（日本語は下書きです。ネイティブ・スピーカーの確認待ち）
No Malay explainer for Stage 2 units: explainers and rubrics are in Japanese or English only, as in Stage 1 (Sam, 13 Nov 2026). Select 日本語 or English.
Ask questions with every question word taught so far (chapters 1 to 12).

Chapters 1 to 12: apa / siapa / di mana / Siapakah (-kah) / Apakah (-kah) / di manakah (-kah) / Adakah / Bolehkah / berapa / bila / pukul berapa / hari apa / bagaimana (spoken: macam mana) / kenapa (= mengapa, apa sebab; answer: sebab or kerana) / yang mana / ke mana / dari mana / berapa jauh / berapa lama / berapa with a counter (Berapa biji?) / siapa with oleh (Kek ini dibuat oleh siapa?)

Chapter 12 adds no new question word. The -kan and -i verbs fit every question you know: Siapa yang menghubungi juruteknik?, Ada kebocoran di mana?, Bila juruteknik boleh datang?, Pukul berapa juruteknik sampai?, Berapa lama awak tunggu? / 第12章で新しい疑問語は増えません。-kan・-i の動詞は知っている疑問語すべてと使えます：Siapa yang menghubungi juruteknik?、Ada kebocoran di mana?、Bila juruteknik boleh datang?、Pukul berapa juruteknik sampai?、Berapa lama awak tunggu?
1. Ask what the technician is repairing. (apa)
2. Ask who contacts the technician. (siapa)
3. Ask where the leak is. (di mana)
4. Ask formally whether the technician has arrived. (Adakah)
5. Ask politely whether you may switch the light off. (Bolehkah)
6. Ask how many slots there are. (berapa)
7. Ask when the technician can come. (bila)
8. Ask what time the technician arrives. (pukul berapa)
9. Ask on what day the contractor comes. (hari apa)
10. Ask how you contact the management office. (bagaimana; spoken macam mana)
11. Ask why the light is damaged. (kenapa; also mengapa or apa sebab; the answer starts with sebab or kerana)
12. Ask which pipe is broken. (yang mana)
13. Ask where the water goes. (ke mana)
14. Ask where the water comes from. (dari mana)
15. Ask how far the management office is. (berapa jauh)
16. Ask how long you wait for the technician. (berapa lama)
17. Ask how many lamps are damaged. (berapa)
18. Ask who wrote the complaint form. (siapa with oleh)

Unit 12B · Culture and usage note|2|0.source_text: Read about the difference between -kan and -i, the everyday forms, the general way of reporting a problem to a management office, and the usual slip of Japanese learners.

Unit 12B · Culture and usage note|3|0.source_text: Two suffixes, two jobs. -kan is for someone or to make it happen (matikan, bersihkan); -i is to or at a person or place (hubungi). A few roots take either one, and the meaning changes, so each verb is learned with its object: hubungi juruteknik, baiki paip, matikan lampu. Notices say Sila hubungi pejabat pengurusan, and for a repair Malaysian Malay uses baiki and membaiki.

Unit 12B · Culture and usage note|3|1.source_text: Everyday speech often uses the plain verb: buka lampu and tutup lampu for hidupkan lampu and matikan lampu (also for the aircon), and Sila isi borang ini for isikan. Both are correct. This course teaches the -kan form first and you will understand the everyday form when you hear it.

Unit 12B · Culture and usage note|3|2.source_text: General knowledge, not a rule and not a checked fact: in many Malaysian condominiums residents report a problem such as a leak to the management office, which may book a technician for a time slot. Buildings differ, so ask the office about your own case.

Unit 12B · Culture and usage note|3|3.source_text: Japanese learners often put -kan on every verb. Here that is a mistake: Tolong baca emel ini and Saya hubungi juruteknik do not need it. Start the call with your name and unit, say plainly what is wrong, and thank the office at the end.

Unit 12B · Culture and usage note|3|5.source_text: 二つの接尾辞に二つの働きがあります。-kan は誰かのため・そうなるようにする動作（matikan・bersihkan）、-i は人や場所へ向かう動作（hubungi）です。語根によってはどちらも取れて、意味が変わるので、動詞は目的語と一緒に覚えます：hubungi juruteknik・baiki paip・matikan lampu。掲示では Sila hubungi pejabat pengurusan と書かれ、修理にはマレーシアのマレー語で baiki・membaiki を使います。

Unit 12B · Culture and usage note|3|6.source_text: 日常会話では素の動詞がよく使われます：hidupkan lampu・matikan lampu の代わりに buka lampu・tutup lampu（エアコンも同じ）、isikan の代わりに Sila isi borang ini です。どちらも正しいので、このコースでは -kan の形を先に教え、日常の形は聞いて分かるようにします。

Unit 12B · Culture and usage note|3|7.source_text: 一般的な知識であり、規則でも確認済みの事実でもありません：マレーシアの多くのコンドミニアムでは、水漏れなどの問題は管理事務所に連絡し、事務所が技術者を時間帯で予約することがあります。建物によって違うので、自分の場合は事務所に聞いてください。

Unit 12B · Culture and usage note|3|8.source_text: 日本人の学習者は -kan をどの動詞にも付けがちですが、ここでは間違いです：Tolong baca emel ini や Saya hubungi juruteknik には要りません。電話は名前と部屋番号から始め、何がおかしいかをはっきり言い、最後に事務所にお礼を言いましょう。

Unit 12B · Culture and usage note|4|0.source_text: English note: 205 words. The Japanese is a full translation (draft).

Unit 12B · Culture and usage note|4|1.source_text: Sources: Kata-Kata chapter 12 card notes ms-c12-025 and -026 (baiki, membaiki; same spelling as baik), -027 and -028 (hubungi, menghubungi; common on notices), -030, -032 and -033 (everyday isi, buka and tutup for lights and aircon), -034 (bersihkan is bersih + -kan), -035, -041 and -042 (whole words); stage 2 plan section 3 (-kan is not a universal politeness ending; -i has no one English or Japanese equivalent). The paragraph on the management office is general knowledge of condominium life in Malaysia, labelled as such and not source-checked; the note states no figure or rule.

Unit 12B · Teaching plan and answer key|.source_text: 先生用：45分×5ブロックの進め方、注意点、宿題です。答えは各シートのキーにあります。
（日本語は下書きです。ネイティブ・スピーカーの確認待ち）
No Malay explainer for Stage 2 units: explainers and rubrics are in Japanese or English only, as in Stage 1 (Sam, 13 Nov 2026). Select 日本語 or English.
Teacher plan: five 45-minute blocks with timings, what to listen for and homework. Answers are on each sheet.
Before Block A: Kata-Kata Sedia Kelas c12 (36 cards, frames ms-c12-f01 and ms-c12-f02).

After Block D: the Kata-Kata chapter 12 deck with spaced review, frames ms-c12-f05, ms-c12-f04, ms-c12-f06, ms-c12-f01 in the frame drill and Susun Ayat; about 3 hours of self-study for this unit (planning figure).

Hanashishou (Stage 2): the plan links chapter 12 to the home-condo scenes (a leak, the management office, a technician). Their Malay is not yet tagged by chapter (build step 6), so do not assign them yet.
Next: the review block after 12B (chapters 10 to 12), then chapter 13 (health situations).
■ Block A · Words and patterns (45 min)
Goal: I can ask someone to contact a person with Boleh hubungi …? and say that a technician is repairing something with sedang membaiki.
0–5 Recall: unit 12A (-kan requests and the parcel) from the opener prompts.
5–10 Tanya Cikgu questions from Kata-Kata.
10–20 Vocabulary focus: core words first, with each root; recognition and revision words are only pointed out.

20–40 Pattern focus: patterns 1 and 2 first (hubungi, then sedang membaiki), question and answer before the rule; then the vocabulary in three groups with each root, its chapter and what the suffix adds (the leak and the report 8, repair and contact 7, switch, empty, clean, fill 6). Write -kan (for someone, or make it happen) and -i (to or at a person or place) side by side on the board.
40–45 First substitutions (Drill 2, items 1 to 3).
■ Block B · Drills and conversation (45 min)
Goal: I can report a leak with Ada kebocoran di … saya, answer the office's questions and book a slot.
0–5 Recall: say one request with Tolong + a -kan verb and one with hubungi.
5–25 Drill ladder in order: pattern table, substitution, transformation (standard to everyday first), question and answer, question-word choice, short dialogues, then the markers drill.
25–40 Model conversation, gapped form, then the changed-facts variant.
40–45 Pair rehearsal without the script.
■ Block C · Listening and task (45 min)
Goal: I can follow a call to the management office and read a complaint form and a notice about a repair.
0–5 Recall: each learner says one problem at home and who they would contact.
5–20 Listening: read the questions, two readings, check, then shadow three lines.
20–30 Reading and writing.
30–45 Task with role cards; announce the change of plan halfway.
■ Block D · Review and test (45 min)
Goal: I can choose between -kan and -i and spell membaiki, menghubungi, bersihkan correctly.
0–15 Mixed review: cumulative question-word drill (chapters 1 to 12), then the markers drill with new cues and a spelling check of membaiki, menghubungi, bersihkan, hidupkan, matikan.
15–25 Unit test (low-stakes).
25–35 Self-check and feedback.
35–45 Preview: the review block for chapters 10 to 12 (45 minutes), then chapter 13 (negation, permission and advice in health situations).
■ Block E · Scene transfer (45 min)
Goal: I can report a problem and agree a repair time in a short role-play, and handle a changed time.
0–5 Recall: say three things you can ask the management office to do.

5–15 Scene listening: read the Kata-Kata scenario lines ms-c12-s11 to ms-c12-s19 (Tanaka and the management office: the ceiling leak, the slot, the complaint form) twice; learners tick the -kan and -i verbs they hear.
15–30 Role-play in pairs: pairs play the same scene with their own block, unit and problem, without the script.
30–40 Changed situation: a changed time: the office says the technician now comes at two; the resident agrees, says what to switch off and asks to be contacted.
40–45 Culture and usage note discussion, and the home-practice briefing.
■ What to listen for · 注意点

Load: 25 core words in three groups (the leak and the report 10; repair and contact 9; switch, empty, clean, fill 6), no recognition word (no Dunia scene primes chapter 12), and revision of the roots, the home, asking and feelings, and the markers. Suggested order: Block A the first group with patterns 1 and 2; Block B the second group with pattern 3; the third group with pattern 4 in Block B or C. If the pilot shows 25 is too many, the natural cut is: hubungi, membaiki, baiki, kebocoran, siling, juruteknik, matikan, hidupkan, aduan, slot first; the rest second.

The -kan and -i choice (plan section 3, Sam 13 Nov 2026): -kan is to do it for someone or to make it happen (matikan, bersihkan, kosongkan); -i is to or at a person or place (hubungi). Spelling traps from the cards: baiki has the same spelling as baik but means to repair (card ms-c12-025); membaiki has mem- before b (ms-c12-026); menghubungi has meng- before h (ms-c12-028); bersihkan is bersih + -kan, not ber- + sih (ms-c12-034). The pe-, ke-an and -an words (pengawal, kebocoran, kerosakan, aduan, tempahan) are whole words (cards ms-c12-029, -035, -041, -042).

Where Japanese learners usually slip: (1) putting -kan on every verb as if it were a polite ending; (2) adding a に-word such as dengan after hubungi; (3) *perbaiki for a repair (Indonesian): the course uses baiki and membaiki; (4) *bersihan or *berbersih for bersihkan; (5) treating baiki as baik (good); (6) 直す covers membaiki and correcting a mistake: only the first is baiki.

the -kan rule (Sam, 13 Nov 2026): use the bare -kan verb for a request (Tolong simpankan …, Boleh bawakan …?) and for a first-person offer or reply (Saya hantarkan sekarang., Baik, saya matikan sekarang.); in a statement with a third-person doer or with sudah, sedang, belum, akan, baru or masih, use the meN- verb the course has (Pengawal menyimpan bungkusan itu., Juruteknik akan membaiki paip itu., Kami akan menghubungi juruteknik., Saya sedang membawa bungkusan itu ke lif.); where the course has no meN- verb (letakkan, bukakan, matikan, bersihkan), rephrase: Saya letakkan bungkusan itu di sini sekarang., Saya bersihkan lantai itu sekarang. The same goes for -i verbs: hubungi and baiki are for requests and first-person replies, menghubungi and membaiki for the rest. Do not teach forms such as *menyimpankan or *menghantarkan: they are not natural.
target_spans: Saya sedang membawa bungkusan itu ke lif.
Saya letakkan bungkusan itu di sini sekarang.

Unit 12B · Teaching plan and answer key|.source_text: Management office (general knowledge, not a rule and not source-checked; no figure): in many Malaysian condominiums residents report a leak or a fault to the management office, which may book a technician for a time slot. Buildings differ, so tell learners to ask the office about their own case.

Spoken forms: buka lampu and tutup lampu for hidupkan and matikan (card notes ms-c12-032 and -033), and isi for isikan (ms-c12-030). They are everyday words; accept them in speech and never mark them wrong. Standard first: teach the -kan form.

The scene follows Kata-Kata c12 (scenario lines ms-c12-s11 to s19, frames f04, f05 and f06, with f01 returning). All names, blocks, units and times are fictional; learners may use their real building or an invented one.
Cumulative question words: chapters 1 to 12. Chapter 12 adds no new question word.
Answer keys are on each component. Japanese text awaits native review.
Standard forms first; spoken forms are labelled. ber- verbs are taught as whole ledger forms, each with its root; no meN- verb (chapter 11) and no suffixed verb form (chapter 12).
