Unit 12B · Review block · Chapters 10 to.source_text: Notice: ber- verbs have no object; meN- verbs take the thing directly; -kan is for someone or makes it happen; -i points at a person or place; the markers go in front of any of them. / 気づくこと：ber- の動詞は目的語をとらず、meN- の動詞は物をすぐあとに置き、-kan は誰かのため・そうなるようにする動作、-i は人や場所へ向かう動作で、マーカーはどれの前にも付きます。
■ Plan · 45 minutes · 進め方
0–5 Recall: say one request with Tolong + a -kan verb and one thing you did with a meN- verb at the office.
5–15 Mixed input: read the model; underline every ber- verb, meN- verb, -kan verb and -i verb and name the marker in front of each.
15–30 Alternating role task: in pairs, one is a resident who asks and one is the office who answers; swap after seven minutes (task below).
30–40 Changed situation: the office says the technician now comes earlier; the resident explains who contacts whom and what they switch off.
40–45 Self-check against the list below, then one thing to practise at home.
0–5 復習・5–15 混合の入力・15–30 役割交代のタスク・30–40 状況の変更・40–45 自己チェック。
■ Your turn · 自分で

Part 1 (15 min, alternating): A is a resident and reports a problem (Ada kebocoran di siling saya.), asks the office to do two things (Tolong …, Boleh hubungi …?) and answers Bila …?. B is the office and asks the block and unit, says what to switch off and offers a slot. After seven minutes swap.
Part 2 (10 min, changed situation): B says Maaf, juruteknik datang pukul dua, bukan pukul tiga. A says who will contact the technician, what A is switching off and what A is emptying.
target_spans: Maaf, juruteknik datang pukul dua, bukan pukul tiga.

Unit 12B · Review block · Chapters 10 to.source_text: Part 3 (5 min): write three sentences about your own home, one with a meN- verb, one with a -kan verb and one with hubungi.
パート1：交代で住民と事務所を演じます。パート2：状況が変わり、住民は誰が技術者に連絡し、何を消し、何を空にするかを説明します。パート3：自分の家について、meN- の動詞・-kan の動詞・hubungi を一つずつ使った3文を書きます。
■ Peer check · 互いに確認
☐ meN- verbs have the right front for the first sound of the root (membaiki, menghubungi, menyemak).
☐ -kan verbs keep the spelling of their card (two k in letakkan and tunjukkan; bersihkan, not *berbersih).
☐ The person follows hubungi directly, with no extra word.
☐ A request uses Tolong or Boleh and the thing follows the verb.
☐ The marker (sudah, belum, sedang, akan) stands in front of the verb, and a bare hubungi or baiki becomes menghubungi or membaiki after it.

Model: Any natural exchange that follows the checklist. Model: Ada kebocoran di siling saya. Tolong hubungi juruteknik. Saya matikan lampu itu sekarang dan kosongkan meja dulu. Juruteknik sedang membaiki paip, dan Encik Rahman akan menelefon saya.
target_spans: Ada kebocoran di siling saya. Tolong hubungi juruteknik. Saya matikan lampu itu sekarang dan kosongkan meja dulu. Juruteknik sedang membaiki paip, dan Encik Rahman akan menelefon saya.

Unit 13 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|7.source_text: Explanation: belum goes in front of the verb and means not yet, so it also says that you expect to do it later: Saya belum makan. (the Kata-Kata frame) is "I haven't eaten yet". The verb does not change. Belum. alone is a full answer to Sudah …? (chapter 4). tidak is a plain no or not, with no "yet": Saya tidak demam. says that you do not have a fever. For a noun use bukan (chapter 3). After belum the standard verb is mendaftar (meN- + daftar, chapter 11), and everyday speech also drops the prefix: Saya belum isi borang. Both are correct; this course teaches the meN- form first.

Unit 13 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|8.source_text: 説明：belum は動詞の前に置いて「まだ〜ていない」を表し、あとでする予定があることも示します：Saya belum makan.（Kata-Kata の文型）は「まだ食べていません」。動詞の形は変わりません。Belum. だけで Sudah …?（第4章）への答えになります。tidak は「いいえ・〜ない」で、「まだ」の意味がありません：Saya tidak demam. は「熱がない」という意味です。名詞には bukan（第3章）を使います。belum のあとの標準形は mendaftar（meN- ＋ daftar、第11章）で、日常会話では接頭辞を落として Saya belum isi borang. とも言います。どちらも正しく、このコースでは meN- の形を先に教えます。

Unit 13 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|9.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese まだ〜ていません is one pattern and 〜ません is another. Malay matches them: belum is まだ〜ていません, tidak is 〜ません. The verb ending does not change in Malay.

Unit 13 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|10.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「まだ〜ていません」と「〜ません」は別の型で、マレー語では belum と tidak が対応します。マレー語の動詞は形が変わりません。

Unit 13 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|0.source_text: Explanation: To ask permission put Bolehkah saya or Boleh saya in front of the verb: Bolehkah saya masuk? (the Kata-Kata frame). Bolehkah is the careful, polite form (chapter 2); Boleh saya …? is just as correct in everyday speech, and the course teaches the first and recognises the second. The answer is Boleh. or Maaf, tidak boleh., and a short extra word makes it friendly: Boleh. Sila masuk. kebenaran means permission and nothing else here: minta kebenaran bos is to ask the boss for permission. No little word for "to" or "if" goes between saya and the verb.

Unit 13 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|1.source_text: 説明：許可を求めるときは、動詞の前に Bolehkah saya か Boleh saya を置きます：Bolehkah saya masuk?（Kata-Kata の文型）。Bolehkah はていねいな言い方（第2章）で、Boleh saya …? も日常会話で正しい言い方です。このコースでは前者を教え、後者は聞いて分かるようにします。答えは Boleh. か Maaf, tidak boleh. で、ひとこと足すと親しみやすくなります：Boleh. Sila masuk. kebenaran はここでは「許可」の意味だけです：minta kebenaran bos は「上司に許可をもらう」。saya と動詞の間に「〜ても」にあたる語は入りません。

Unit 13 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|2.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese asks permission with the て-form: 入ってもいいですか, 座ってもいいですか. Malay has no て-form and no もいい: put Boleh saya before the plain verb, Boleh saya masuk?. Answer 〜てもいいです with Boleh.

Unit 13 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|3.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語は「入ってもいいですか」のように て形で許可を求めます。マレー語には て形も「〜てもいい」にあたる語もなく、Boleh saya を素の動詞の前に置いて Boleh saya masuk? と言います。「〜てもいいです」への答えは Boleh. です。

Unit 13 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|12.source_text: Explanation: perlu + a verb says what you need to do or what is needed: Saya perlu berjumpa doktor. (the Kata-Kata frame). It is a plain fact about a step, not a threat and not advice. Tidak perlu means you do not have to: Tidak perlu tunggu lama. It does not mean it is forbidden. The standard verb after perlu can be mendaftar or the everyday daftar: Encik perlu daftar dulu. (the Kata-Kata line). The fixed phrase bila perlu (when needed) is learned whole: Tanya penyambut tetamu bila perlu. A short answer is Perlu. or Tidak perlu.

Unit 13 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|0.source_text: 説明：perlu ＋ 動詞は、しなければならないこと・必要なことを表します：Saya perlu berjumpa doktor.（Kata-Kata の文型）。これは手順についての事実で、おどしでも助言でもありません。Tidak perlu は「しなくてよい」で、禁止ではありません：Tidak perlu tunggu lama. perlu のあとの標準形は mendaftar ですが、日常の daftar も使います：Encik perlu daftar dulu.（Kata-Kata の文）。決まり文句 bila perlu（必要なときに）は一まとまりで覚えます：Tanya penyambut tetamu bila perlu. 短い答えは Perlu. か Tidak perlu. です。

Unit 13 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|1.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 〜なければならない (must) and 必要がある (need) are close, and 〜なくてもいい is the opposite. Malay uses perlu for the need and tidak perlu for 〜なくてもいい. Do not say tidak boleh for 〜なくてもいい: that means 〜てはいけません.

Unit 13 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|2.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「〜なければならない」と「必要がある」は近く、「〜なくてもいい」はその反対です。マレー語は必要に perlu、「〜なくてもいい」に tidak perlu を使います。「〜なくてもいい」に tidak boleh を使わないでください。それは「〜てはいけません」です。

Unit 13 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|7.source_text: 3. A: Kita patut sampai pukul berapa? B: Kita patut sampai pukul sembilan.

Unit 13 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|10.source_text: 6. A: Saya mesti daftar dulu? B: Ya, awak mesti daftar dulu.

Unit 13 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|11.source_text: Explanation: patut + a verb is advice: it says what is a good idea, and you may choose: Encik patut berehat. (the Kata-Kata frame, said by the doctor). nasihat is the advice itself. mesti is must, with no choice: Encik mesti baca arahan di label. mesti is a root, not me- + sti. wajib is must on a form or a notice: Borang ini wajib diisi. So the three steps are: perlu (a step you take), patut (advice) and mesti or wajib (must). This course teaches the language of advice only; for your health follow your own doctor and pharmacist. Elakkan (avoid) belongs to notices and requests: Tolong elakkan lif itu. To tell someone not to make a noise, say Tolong jangan bising.
target_spans: Encik mesti baca arahan di label.

Unit 13 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|0.source_text: 説明：patut ＋ 動詞は助言で、よいことを言うだけで、選ぶのは本人です：Encik patut berehat.（Kata-Kata の文型、医者の言葉）。nasihat は助言そのものです。mesti は「しなければならない」で選べません：Encik mesti baca arahan di label. mesti は語根で、me- ＋ sti ではありません。wajib は用紙や掲示での「必須」です：Borang ini wajib diisi. つまり三つの段階は perlu（する手順）、patut（助言）、mesti・wajib（義務）です。このコースが教えるのは助言のことばだけで、健康については自分の医者と薬剤師の指示に従ってください。Elakkan（避ける）は掲示や依頼に使います：Tolong elakkan lif itu. 音を立てないでと言うときは Tolong jangan bising. です。
target_spans: Encik mesti baca arahan di label.

Unit 13 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|1.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 〜たほうがいい is advice and 〜なければならない is must. Malay keeps them apart: patut is 〜たほうがいい, mesti and wajib are 〜なければならない, perlu is 必要がある. Do not use mesti for advice: it sounds like an order.

Unit 13 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|2.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「〜たほうがいい」は助言、「〜なければならない」は義務です。マレー語も分けます：patut が「〜たほうがいい」、mesti・wajib が「〜なければならない」、perlu が「必要がある」です。助言に mesti を使わないでください。命令のように聞こえます。

Unit 13 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|11.source_text: Explanation: On a sign or a rule, tidak dibenarkan + a verb says that something is not allowed: Tidak dibenarkan minum di sini. (the Kata-Kata frame). dibenarkan is di- + benar + -kan, the opposite of dilarang (chapter 9): Dilarang makan dan minum di bilik menunggu. Both are written, rather formal words; in speech people say tidak boleh. A notice about a form says Borang ini wajib diisi. (the Kata-Kata frame): wajib + the passive diisi says that it must be filled in, and the thing comes first. wajib is used here for forms and notices only, a plain rule of the place and nothing about religion. The notices in this course are fictional.
target_spans: Dilarang makan dan minum di bilik menunggu.

Unit 13 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|0.source_text: 説明：掲示や決まりでは、tidak dibenarkan ＋ 動詞で「〜は許可されていない」を表します：Tidak dibenarkan minum di sini.（Kata-Kata の文型）。dibenarkan は di- ＋ benar ＋ -kan で、dilarang（第9章）の反対です：Dilarang makan dan minum di bilik menunggu. どちらも書き言葉でやや改まった語で、話すときは tidak boleh と言います。用紙についての掲示は Borang ini wajib diisi.（Kata-Kata の文型）：wajib ＋ 受け身の diisi で「記入が必須」を表し、物が先に来ます。ここでの wajib は用紙や掲示の決まりだけで、宗教とは関係ありません。このコースの掲示は架空です。
target_spans: Dilarang makan dan minum di bilik menunggu.

Unit 13 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|1.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 〜てはいけません and 禁止 cover both the sign dilarang and the spoken tidak boleh. Malay chooses by place: dilarang and tidak dibenarkan on signs, tidak boleh in speech, jangan for a command to a person. 記入必須 on a form is wajib diisi.

Unit 13 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|2.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「〜てはいけません」「禁止」は、掲示の dilarang と話し言葉の tidak boleh の両方にあたります。マレー語は場所で選びます：掲示では dilarang・tidak dibenarkan、話すときは tidak boleh、人への命令は jangan です。用紙の「記入必須」は wajib diisi です。

sudah mendaftar ≈ もう受付した · belum mengisi ≈ まだ記入していない · sedang berjumpa ≈ 診察を受けているところ · akan menelefon ≈ 電話する予定 · masih menunggu ≈ まだ待っている · baru memanggil ≈ 呼んだばかり

The clinic sentences fit every question you know: Siapa yang sudah mendaftar?, Saya perlu bawa apa?, Kaunter di mana?, Pukul berapa temu janji saya?, Berapa lama saya tunggu? / 第13章で新しい疑問語は増えません。クリニックの文は知っている疑問語すべてと使えます：Siapa yang sudah mendaftar?、Saya perlu bawa apa?、Kaunter di mana?、Pukul berapa temu janji saya?、Berapa lama saya tunggu?
1. Ask what you need to bring. (apa)
2. Ask who must register. (siapa)
3. Ask where the counter is. (di mana)
4. Ask formally whether the patient has an appointment. (Adakah)
5. Ask politely whether you may sit here. (Bolehkah)
6. Ask how many forms there are. (berapa)
7. Ask when the clinic closes. (bila)
8. Ask what time the appointment is. (pukul berapa)
9. Ask on what day the clinic is closed. (hari apa)
10. Ask how you register. (bagaimana; spoken macam mana)
11. Ask why drinking is not allowed. (kenapa; also mengapa or apa sebab; the answer starts with sebab or kerana)
12. Ask which form is compulsory. (yang mana)
13. Ask where you go after registering. (ke mana)
14. Ask where this card is from. (dari mana)
15. Ask how far the pharmacy is. (berapa jauh)
16. Ask how long you wait. (berapa lama)
17. Ask how many chairs are in the waiting room. (berapa with a counter)
18. Ask who filled in the form. (siapa with oleh)

Use the role cards without a script; deal with the change of plan halfway through.

Your information (fictional): you are the receptionist, and later the pharmacist. The patient has no appointment and has not registered. The form is compulsory. Drinking is not allowed in the waiting room.

As the receptionist: ask about an appointment, say the patient must register and fill in the form, and answer the permission questions. As the pharmacist: if B does not understand the instruction, point to the label and say to ask you again. Do not name any medicine, any dose or any time to take it.
Aの情報（架空）：あなたは受付係で、あとで薬剤師にもなります。患者は予約がなく、まだ受付をしていません。用紙は必須で、待合室では飲んではいけません。受付係として予約をたずね、受付をして用紙に記入するよう言い、許可の質問に答えます。薬剤師としては、Bが指示を分からないときにラベルを指して、もう一度聞くように言います。薬の名前・用量・飲む時間は言いません。
■ Role card B · Bのカード
You are the patient (fictional). You have a fever and a sore throat and no appointment. Register, ask whether you may fill in the form here and whether you may drink water.
At the pharmacy you do not understand the instruction: ask the pharmacist to say it once more, then say you will read the label.
Bは患者です（架空）。熱とのどの痛みがあり、予約はありません。受付をし、ここで用紙に記入してよいか、水を飲んでよいかをたずねます。薬局では指示が分からないので、薬剤師にもう一度言ってもらい、ラベルを読むと言います。
■ Change of plan · 予定変更

Halfway, A says: Maaf, doktor belum ada. Encik boleh tunggu, atau datang pukul empat. Sesuai? B decides, says what is suitable and asks whether B may leave a bag here: Pukul empat sesuai. Boleh saya tinggalkan beg di sini?
target_spans: Maaf, doktor belum ada. Encik boleh tunggu, atau datang pukul empat. Sesuai?
Pukul empat sesuai. Boleh saya tinggalkan beg di sini?

Unit 13 · Culture and usage note|3|0.source_text: Need, advice and must are three different strengths. perlu is a step you have to take (Encik perlu daftar dulu), patut is advice that leaves the choice to you (Encik patut berehat), and mesti or wajib is a must with no choice (Encik mesti baca arahan di label, Borang ini wajib diisi). A doctor in this course only says patut berehat and gives sick leave; a pharmacist only points to the label and says tanya saya lagi. The course teaches language, not medical knowledge: for your health follow your own doctor and pharmacist.
target_spans: Encik mesti baca arahan di label

Unit 13 · Culture and usage note|3|1.source_text: Signs and speech differ. Tidak dibenarkan and dilarang are written words for signs and rules; in speech people say tidak boleh, and jangan is a command to a person. To ask permission, say Bolehkah saya masuk? or Boleh saya masuk? with the plain verb after saya. In this course kebenaran means permission and nothing else (minta kebenaran bos), and wajib is a plain rule about a form or a notice.

Unit 13 · Culture and usage note|3|2.source_text: General knowledge, not a rule and not a checked fact: many Malaysian employers have an agreement with a panel clinic, and staff may be asked for a company card or letter. A doctor may give sick leave, called cuti sakit (everyday: MC), but who accepts it and how differs by employer, so ask your own company.

Unit 13 · Culture and usage note|3|3.source_text: Japanese learners ask permission with the て-form (入ってもいいですか). Malay has none: put Boleh saya before the plain verb. They also say tidak boleh when they mean 〜なくてもいい; that is tidak perlu.

Unit 13 · Culture and usage note|3|5.source_text: 必要・助言・義務は強さが違います。perlu はしなければならない手順（Encik perlu daftar dulu）、patut は選ぶのは本人に任せる助言（Encik patut berehat）、mesti と wajib は選べない義務（Encik mesti baca arahan di label、Borang ini wajib diisi）です。このコースの医者は patut berehat と言って病気休暇を出すだけで、薬剤師はラベルを指して tanya saya lagi と言うだけです。このコースが教えるのは医学の知識ではなくことばです。健康については自分の医者と薬剤師の指示に従ってください。
target_spans: Encik mesti baca arahan di label

Unit 13 · Culture and usage note|3|6.source_text: 掲示と話し言葉は違います。Tidak dibenarkan と dilarang は掲示や決まりの書き言葉で、話すときは tidak boleh、jangan は人への命令です。許可を求めるときは、saya のあとに素の動詞を置いて Bolehkah saya masuk? か Boleh saya masuk? と言います。このコースの kebenaran は「許可」の意味だけ（minta kebenaran bos）で、wajib は用紙や掲示についての単なる決まりです。

Unit 13 · Culture and usage note|3|7.source_text: 一般的な知識であり、規則でも確認済みの事実でもありません：マレーシアの多くの雇用主はパネルクリニックと契約しており、会社のカードや書類を求められることがあります。医者は病気休暇（cuti sakit、日常は MC）を出すことがありますが、受け付けるかどうかは雇用主によって違うので、自分の会社に聞いてください。

Unit 13 · Culture and usage note|3|8.source_text: 日本人の学習者は て形で許可を求めがちです（入ってもいいですか）。マレー語には て形がなく、素の動詞の前に Boleh saya を置きます。また「〜なくてもいい」の意味で tidak boleh と言いがちですが、それは tidak perlu です。

Unit 13 · Teaching plan and answer key|3.source_text: Before Block A: Kata-Kata Sedia Kelas c13 (27 cards, frames ms-c13-f01 and ms-c13-f02).

After Block D: the Kata-Kata chapter 13 deck with spaced review, frames ms-c13-f01, ms-c13-f02, ms-c13-f03, ms-c13-f04, ms-c13-f05, ms-c13-f06 in the frame drill and Susun Ayat; about 3 hours of self-study for this unit (planning figure).

Hanashishou (Stage 2): the plan links chapter 13 to the clinic scenes (clinic_visit, pharmacy_advice, clinic_registration). Their Malay is not yet tagged by chapter (build step 6), so do not assign them yet.
Next: unit 14 (reasons, conditions and sequence; Kata-Kata c14), with its writing block.
■ Block A · Words and patterns (45 min)
Goal: I can say what I have not done yet with belum, ask permission with Bolehkah saya …? and say what I need with perlu.
0–5 Recall: chapters 2, 4 and 12 (Boleh …?, sudah, Tolong + a -kan verb) from the opener prompts.
10–20 Vocabulary focus: core words first, with each root; recognition and revision words are only pointed out.

20–40 Pattern focus: patterns 1 and 2 first (belum, Bolehkah saya …?), question and answer before the rule; then the vocabulary in three groups with each whole word and its root (need, advice and rules 10, the panel clinic 11, the pharmacy 4). Draw the ladder perlu (a step), patut (advice), mesti / wajib (must) and the pair tidak perlu against tidak boleh.
■ Block B · Drills and conversation (45 min)
Goal: I can register at a panel clinic, answer the receptionist and ask the doctor for sick leave.
0–5 Recall: say one thing you have not done yet with belum and one permission question.
5–25 Drill ladder in order: pattern table, substitution, transformation (sudah to belum first), question and answer, question-word choice, short dialogues, then the markers drill.
25–40 Model conversation, gapped form, then the changed-facts variant.

Unit 13 · Teaching plan and answer key|4.source_text: Goal: I can follow a call to a panel clinic, read a clinic notice and a message about sick leave, and ask a pharmacist to repeat an instruction.
0–5 Recall: each learner says one thing they must do before a visit to a clinic.
5–20 Listening: read the questions, two readings, check, then shadow three lines.
30–45 Task with role cards; announce the change of plan halfway.
■ Block D · Review and test (45 min)
Goal: I can choose between belum and tidak, and between perlu, patut and mesti, and correct a short sentence.
0–15 Mixed review: cumulative question-word drill (chapters 1 to 13), then the markers drill with new cues and a check of belum against tidak and perlu against patut.
35–45 Preview: unit 14: reasons, conditions and sequence (Kata-Kata c14 cards ms-c14-001 onward and its frames).
Goal: I can handle a short role-play at a panel clinic and a pharmacy, including a change of time.
0–5 Recall: say three permission questions you could ask in a clinic.

5–15 Scene listening: read the Kata-Kata scenario lines ms-c13-s01 to ms-c13-s18 (Tanaka at the panel clinic, with the doctor and at the pharmacy) twice; learners tick belum, perlu, patut, mesti, dibenarkan and dilarang when they hear them.
15–30 Role-play in pairs: pairs play the same scene with their own fictional symptom, form and name, without the script; A never names a medicine or a dose.
30–40 Changed situation: a changed time: the doctor is not in yet; B chooses to wait or to come at four, says the time suits and asks permission to leave a bag.
40–45 Culture and usage note discussion, and the home-practice briefing.

Unit 13 · Teaching plan and answer key|5.source_text: Load: 29 core words in three groups (need, advice and rules 11; the panel clinic 13; the pharmacy 5), no recognition word, and revision of not and not yet, health and the clinic, forms and the counter, signs and rules, and asking and thanking. Suggested order: Block A the first group with patterns 1 to 3; Block B the second group with patterns 4 and 5; the third group in Block B or C. If the pilot shows 29 is too many, the natural cut is: perlu, patut, mesti, wajib, dibenarkan, daftar, mendaftar, temu janji, klinik panel, cuti sakit first; the rest second.

Safety (read first): the unit writes no diagnosis, no treatment advice, no medicine name with a dose and no dosing instruction. The doctor only says patut berehat and gives sick leave; the pharmacist only points to the label and says tanya saya lagi. dos is taught for reading a label. Tell learners to follow their own doctor and pharmacist, and do not answer medical questions in class. Use fictional names and symptoms; assess the language, not medical knowledge.

belum against tidak: belum is not yet (it will happen); tidak is not, a plain no; bukan is for nouns. Saya belum makan means I have not eaten yet; Saya tidak makan means I do not eat. The answer to Sudah …? is Sudah. or Belum., not Tidak. The verb does not change after belum.

perlu (need: a step) against patut (should: advice, you choose) against mesti or wajib (must: no choice; wajib is secular here, on forms and notices, with no reference to religion). tidak perlu is not having to; tidak boleh is not allowed; jangan is a command; dilarang and tidak dibenarkan are for signs. mesti is a root, not me- + sti (card ms-c13-021). kebenaran is permission only (card ms-c13-005); the other meaning is not taught.

Where Japanese learners usually slip: (1) asking permission with the て-form idea (入ってもいいですか): there is no て-form, say Boleh saya masuk?; (2) tidak boleh for 〜なくてもいい (it is tidak perlu); (3) patut or mesti for every 〜ほうがいい or 〜なければならない: patut is advice, mesti an order; (4) tidak for まだ〜ていない (it is belum); (5) a particle or a word for "to" between saya and the verb; (6) putting the sentence-final particles of speech into an answer: they are recognition only, never in a key.

Panel clinics and cuti sakit / MC (general knowledge, not a rule and not source-checked; no figure): many Malaysian employers have an agreement with a panel clinic, and a doctor may give sick leave, called cuti sakit or, in speech, MC. Employers differ, so tell learners to ask their own company.

The -kan rule from chapter 12 (Sam): Tolong elakkan … is a request, so the bare -kan verb is right. No meN- + -kan form is taught. Standard first: mendaftar in careful speech and writing, daftar and isi borang in everyday speech; the course teaches mendaftar first and never marks the everyday form wrong. MC is spoken, recognition only, never in a key.

Unit 13 · Teaching plan and answer key|6.source_text: Natural speech: Boleh saya …? and tidak boleh in conversation; tidak dibenarkan, dilarang and wajib diisi on signs and forms. Keep ialah, di- … oleh and rulings out of casual turns. The scene follows Kata-Kata c13 (scenario lines ms-c13-s01 to s18, frames f01 to f06). All names, clinics and times are fictional; learners may use an invented clinic.
Cumulative question words: chapters 1 to 13. Chapter 13 adds no new question word.

Unit 13 · Teaching plan and answer key|7.source_text: Answer keys are on each component. Japanese text awaits native review.
Standard forms first; spoken forms are labelled. ber- verbs are taught as whole ledger forms, each with its root; no meN- verb (chapter 11) and no suffixed verb form (chapter 12).

Unit 14 · Chapter opener|3|2.source_text: Block C: I can follow a phone call about a changed plan, read a message in written Malay, and put a plan off or cancel it with a reason. / 予定変更の電話が分かり、書き言葉のメッセージを読め、理由をつけて予定を延期・中止できる。

Unit 14 · Chapter opener|3|3.source_text: Block D: I can choose between kalau and walaupun, kerana and supaya, and between the everyday and the written words, and correct a short sentence. / kalau と walaupun、kerana と supaya、日常の語と書き言葉の語を使い分け、短い文を直せる。

Unit 14 · Chapter opener|3|4.source_text: Block E: I can handle a short role-play about a changed outing, including a second change of plan. / 外出の変更についての短いロールプレイができ、もう一度の変更にも対応できる。

Unit 14 · Chapter opener|3|5.source_text: ■ Setting and recall · 場面と復習

Unit 14 · Chapter opener|3|6.source_text: A weekday at the office in Kuala Lumpur: Encik Tanaka and Cik Mei Ling plan the weekend hike. The weather is cloudy, Mei Ling has to work on Saturday, so they move the hike to Sunday, agree a rain plan and write a message to their friends. All names, plans and times are fictional.

Unit 14 · Chapter opener|3|7.source_text: クアラルンプールの平日のオフィス。田中さんとメイリンさんが週末のハイキングの計画を立てます。空は曇りで、メイリンさんは土曜日に仕事があるので日曜日に延ばし、雨の日の計画を決めて友だちにメッセージを書きます。名前・計画・時刻はすべて架空です。

Unit 14 · Chapter opener|3|8.source_text: Without notes, from chapters 5, 7 and 13: say one thing you must do with perlu, one question with Kenapa …? and its answer with sebab, and one thing you have not done yet with belum. / 第5章・第7章・第13章の復習：perlu でしなければならないことを一つ、Kenapa …? の質問と sebab の答えを一組、belum でまだしていないことを一つ言いましょう。

Unit 14 · Chapter opener|3|9.source_text: Recall prompt: Saya perlu … Kenapa …? Sebab … Saya belum …

Unit 14 · Chapter opener|3|10.source_text: Write one question for Tanya Cikgu before you look at the new words. / 新しい単語を見る前に、Tanya Cikgu への質問を一つ書きましょう。

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|0.source_text: Pattern box: Kalau ___ , kita makan di kafe.  (condition: kalau, written jika)

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|1.source_text: 1. A: Kalau hujan, apa kita buat? B: Kalau hujan, kita makan di kafe.
target_spans: Kalau hujan, kita makan di kafe.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|2.source_text: 2. A: Kalau tidak hujan, kita buat apa? B: Kalau tidak hujan, kita mendaki.
target_spans: Kalau tidak hujan, kita buat apa?

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|3.source_text: 3. A: Kalau awak penat, awak buat apa? B: Kalau saya penat, saya berehat.
target_spans: Kalau awak penat, awak buat apa?

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|4.source_text: 4. A: Bila kita makan di kafe? B: Kalau hujan.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|5.source_text: 5. A: Bila awak mendaki? B: Bila cuaca cerah.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|6.source_text: 6. A: Apa kata Puan Aini? B: Puan Aini kata, kalau hujan, kita tangguhkan. Bila cuaca cerah, kita mendaki.
target_spans: Puan Aini kata, kalau hujan, kita tangguhkan. Bila cuaca cerah, kita mendaki.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|7.source_text: Explanation: Kalau + a clause says the condition, then a comma, then what follows: Kalau hujan, kita makan di kafe. (the Kata-Kata frame). Nothing like "then" comes after the comma. Kalau tidak hujan is the opposite condition. kalau is what people say, and jika is the standard word for a message or a notice: Jika hujan, kita tangguhkan. Both mean "if". Compare bila and apabila: bila (chapter 4) is "when" in everyday speech (Bila cuaca cerah, kita mendaki.), and apabila is the standard word for writing. Kalau is if (it may or may not happen); bila and apabila are when (it will happen at some point). At the start of a question Bila …? still asks "when?"
target_spans: Kalau hujan, kita makan di kafe.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|8.source_text: 説明：Kalau ＋ 節で条件を言い、コンマのあとに結果を続けます：Kalau hujan, kita makan di kafe.（Kata-Kata の文型）。コンマのあとに「それなら」にあたる語は入りません。Kalau tidak hujan は反対の条件です。kalau は話すときの語で、jika はメッセージや掲示の標準語です：Jika hujan, kita tangguhkan. どちらも「もし」です。bila と apabila も同じです：bila（第4章）は日常の「〜するとき」（Bila cuaca cerah, kita mendaki.）、apabila は書くときの標準語です。Kalau は起こるかどうか分からない「もし」、bila・apabila はいつか起こる「〜するとき」です。文頭の Bila …? は「いつ？」のままです。
target_spans: Kalau hujan, kita makan di kafe.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|9.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese has four ways to say if: 〜たら, 〜ば, 〜なら and 〜と. Malay uses kalau for all of them, and the result comes after a comma with no extra word. Keep bila (when it happens) apart from kalau (if it happens): 雨が降ったら is kalau hujan, 晴れたとき is bila cuaca cerah.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|10.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語には「もし」を表す形が四つあります（〜たら・〜ば・〜なら・〜と）。マレー語はすべて kalau で言い、結果はコンマのあとに余計な語なしで続けます。bila（起こるとき）と kalau（起こるなら）を分けてください：「雨が降ったら」は kalau hujan、「晴れたとき」は bila cuaca cerah です。

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|12.source_text: Pattern box: Saya tidak datang kerana saya ___ . / Saya bangun awal supaya saya tidak ___ .  (reason and purpose)
target_spans: Saya bangun awal supaya saya tidak

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|13.source_text: 1. A: Kenapa awak tidak datang? B: Saya tidak datang kerana saya bekerja.
target_spans: Saya tidak datang kerana saya bekerja.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|0.source_text: 2. A: Kenapa cik tidak boleh datang pada hari Sabtu? B: Sebab saya bekerja.
target_spans: Kenapa cik tidak boleh datang pada hari Sabtu?

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|1.source_text: 3. A: Kenapa awak bangun awal? B: Saya bangun awal supaya saya tidak lambat.
target_spans: Saya bangun awal supaya saya tidak lambat.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|2.source_text: 4. A: Kenapa awak datang awal? B: Saya datang awal supaya kita tidak lambat.
target_spans: Saya datang awal supaya kita tidak lambat.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|3.source_text: 5. A: Kenapa Mei Ling menangguhkan rancangan mendaki? B: Mei Ling menangguhkan rancangan mendaki kerana dia bekerja.
target_spans: Kenapa Mei Ling menangguhkan rancangan mendaki?
Mei Ling menangguhkan rancangan mendaki kerana dia bekerja.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|4.source_text: 6. A: Apa tujuan mesej ini? B: Supaya kawan kita tahu rancangan itu.
target_spans: Supaya kawan kita tahu rancangan itu.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|5.source_text: Explanation: kerana (chapter 5) and sebab (chapter 5) both give the reason: the main clause comes first and the reason after it, Saya tidak datang kerana saya bekerja. (the Kata-Kata frame). kerana is the standard word, sebab is just as common in speech, and the answer to Kenapa …? can start with either. supaya gives the purpose, "so that": Saya bangun awal supaya saya tidak lambat. (the Kata-Kata frame). The clause after supaya has its own subject (saya, kita) and is often negative. tujuan is the purpose as a noun: Apa tujuan mesej ini? Do not use supaya for a reason, and do not use kerana for a purpose.
target_spans: Saya tidak datang kerana saya bekerja.
Saya bangun awal supaya saya tidak lambat.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|6.source_text: 説明：kerana（第5章）と sebab（第5章）はどちらも理由を言います。主節が先で、理由があとに来ます：Saya tidak datang kerana saya bekerja.（Kata-Kata の文型）。kerana は標準語、sebab は話し言葉でも同じようによく使い、Kenapa …? への答えはどちらで始めてもかまいません。supaya は目的の「〜ように」です：Saya bangun awal supaya saya tidak lambat.（Kata-Kata の文型）。supaya のあとの節には自分の主語（saya・kita）があり、否定になることがよくあります。tujuan は名詞の「目的」です：Apa tujuan mesej ini? 理由に supaya を、目的に kerana を使わないでください。
target_spans: Saya tidak datang kerana saya bekerja.
Saya bangun awal supaya saya tidak lambat.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|7.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese ので and から give a reason; ために and ように give a purpose. Malay keeps the pairs apart: kerana and sebab are ので・から, supaya is ように. A learner who says Saya tidak datang supaya saya bekerja has said the purpose by mistake.
target_spans: Saya tidak datang supaya saya bekerja

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|8.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「ので」「から」は理由、「ために」「ように」は目的です。マレー語も分けます：kerana・sebab が「ので・から」、supaya が「ように」。Saya tidak datang supaya saya bekerja と言うと、うっかり目的を言ってしまいます。
target_spans: Saya tidak datang supaya saya bekerja

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|11.source_text: 1. A: Hujan. Awak masih mahu berjalan kaki? B: Ya. Walaupun hujan, saya mahu berjalan kaki.
target_spans: Hujan. Awak masih mahu berjalan kaki?
Ya. Walaupun hujan, saya mahu berjalan kaki.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|12.source_text: 2. A: Awak penat. Awak masih mahu mendaki? B: Ya. Walaupun saya penat, saya suka mendaki.
target_spans: Awak penat. Awak masih mahu mendaki?
Ya. Walaupun saya penat, saya suka mendaki.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|13.source_text: 3. A: Hari ini panas. Awak masih mahu pergi? B: Ya. Walaupun panas, saya mahu pergi.
target_spans: Hari ini panas. Awak masih mahu pergi?
Ya. Walaupun panas, saya mahu pergi.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|14.source_text: 4. A: Walaupun hujan, kita mendaki? B: Tidak. Kalau hujan, kita makan di kafe.
target_spans: Tidak. Kalau hujan, kita makan di kafe.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|0.source_text: 5. A: Awak penat. Awak mahu balik? B: Tidak. Walaupun penat, saya mahu makan di kafe dengan kawan.
target_spans: Tidak. Walaupun penat, saya mahu makan di kafe dengan kawan.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|1.source_text: 6. A: Siapa yang membatalkan rancangan mendaki? B: Cik Mei Ling membatalkan rancangan mendaki kerana hujan. Namun kita masih makan di kafe.
target_spans: Cik Mei Ling membatalkan rancangan mendaki kerana hujan. Namun kita masih makan di kafe.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|2.source_text: Explanation: walaupun + a clause says what is true although something else is true: Walaupun hujan, saya mahu berjalan kaki. (the Kata-Kata frame). The comma comes after the first clause and the surprising part follows. Do not add tetapi in the second clause, because walaupun already carries the contrast. For two separate sentences, tetapi (chapter 5; spoken tapi) is the everyday word and namun is the written one: Rancangan mendaki batal. Namun kita masih makan di kafe. Kalau is not the same as walaupun: kalau hujan is a condition, walaupun hujan says the rain is no obstacle.
target_spans: Walaupun hujan, saya mahu berjalan kaki.
Rancangan mendaki batal. Namun kita masih makan di kafe.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|3.source_text: 説明：walaupun ＋ 節で、別のことが事実であってもこうだ、という対比を言います：Walaupun hujan, saya mahu berjalan kaki.（Kata-Kata の文型）。最初の節のあとにコンマを置き、意外な部分が続きます。後ろの節に tetapi は足しません。walaupun がすでに対比を表しているからです。二つの別々の文では、日常語は tetapi（第5章；話し言葉は tapi）、書き言葉は namun です：Rancangan mendaki batal. Namun kita masih makan di kafe. Kalau と walaupun は違います。kalau hujan は条件、walaupun hujan は「雨でも関係ない」です。
target_spans: Walaupun hujan, saya mahu berjalan kaki.
Rancangan mendaki batal. Namun kita masih makan di kafe.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|4.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese のに, けれども and 〜ても all point at contrast. In Malay walaupun opens the first clause and there is no tetapi in the second: 雨なのに歩く is Walaupun hujan, saya berjalan. For 雨が降っても use walaupun hujan too, but 雨が降ったら is kalau hujan.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|5.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「のに」「けれども」「〜ても」はどれも対比を示します。マレー語では walaupun が最初の節を始め、後ろの節に tetapi は入りません：「雨なのに歩く」は Walaupun hujan, saya berjalan。「雨が降っても」も walaupun hujan ですが、「雨が降ったら」は kalau hujan です。

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|7.source_text: Pattern box: Dia makan sambil ___ .  (two things at once; also semasa and sejak)

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|8.source_text: 1. A: Dia makan sambil buat apa? B: Dia makan sambil membaca surat khabar.
target_spans: Dia makan sambil membaca surat khabar.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|9.source_text: 2. A: Awak minum teh sambil buat apa? B: Saya minum teh sambil bercakap dengan kawan.
target_spans: Awak minum teh sambil buat apa?
Saya minum teh sambil bercakap dengan kawan.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|10.source_text: 3. A: Boleh kita bercakap sambil berjalan? B: Boleh. Kita boleh bercakap sambil berjalan.
target_spans: Boleh. Kita boleh bercakap sambil berjalan.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|11.source_text: 4. A: Awak makan sambil bekerja? B: Tidak. Saya makan dulu, kemudian saya bekerja.
target_spans: Tidak. Saya makan dulu, kemudian saya bekerja.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|12.source_text: 5. A: Semasa mendaki, awak buat apa? B: Semasa mendaki, saya minum air dan berehat.
target_spans: Semasa mendaki, saya minum air dan berehat.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|0.source_text: 6. A: Sejak bila awak suka mendaki? B: Sejak bulan lepas.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|1.source_text: Explanation: sambil + a verb says that one person does two things at the same time, and the person is the same for both: Dia makan sambil membaca surat khabar. (the Kata-Kata frame). semasa (during, when) is for a period or an event: Semasa mendaki, kita minum air. sejak (since) names the point where something started: Sejak bulan lepas saya suka mendaki. All three are learned as they are. When two people do two different things, say two sentences, not sambil.
target_spans: Dia makan sambil membaca surat khabar.
Sejak bulan lepas saya suka mendaki.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|2.source_text: 説明：sambil ＋ 動詞は、同じ人が同時に二つのことをする、という意味です：Dia makan sambil membaca surat khabar.（Kata-Kata の文型）。semasa（〜の間に）は期間や出来事に使います：Semasa mendaki, kita minum air. sejak（〜以来）は始まりの時点を言います：Sejak bulan lepas saya suka mendaki. 三つともそのまま覚えます。二人が別々のことをするときは sambil ではなく、文を二つにします。
target_spans: Dia makan sambil membaca surat khabar.
Sejak bulan lepas saya suka mendaki.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|3.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 〜ながら is one verb form. Malay puts sambil between the two actions and keeps both verbs plain: 食べながら読む is makan sambil membaca. 〜の間に is semasa and 〜以来 is sejak.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|4.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「〜ながら」は動詞の形です。マレー語は二つの動作のあいだに sambil を置き、どちらの動詞も形を変えません：「食べながら読む」は makan sambil membaca。「〜の間に」は semasa、「〜以来」は sejak です。

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|6.source_text: Pattern box: Mula-mula kita ___ , kemudian kita ___ , akhirnya kita ___ .  (sequence)

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|7.source_text: 1. A: Apa rancangan kita? B: Mula-mula kita berjumpa di stesen. Kemudian kita mendaki. Akhirnya kita makan di kafe.
target_spans: Mula-mula kita berjumpa di stesen. Kemudian kita mendaki. Akhirnya kita makan di kafe.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|8.source_text: 2. A: Awak buat apa pagi ini? B: Mula-mula saya bangun, kemudian saya makan, akhirnya saya pergi bekerja.
target_spans: Mula-mula saya bangun, kemudian saya makan, akhirnya saya pergi bekerja.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|9.source_text: 3. A: Apa dalam mesej itu? B: Mula-mula berjumpa di stesen. Seterusnya mendaki. Akhirnya makan di kafe.
target_spans: Mula-mula berjumpa di stesen. Seterusnya mendaki. Akhirnya makan di kafe.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|10.source_text: 4. A: Akhirnya awak sampai! B: Ya, akhirnya saya sampai. Maaf, saya lambat.
target_spans: Ya, akhirnya saya sampai. Maaf, saya lambat.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|11.source_text: 5. A: Kita tangguhkan rancangan mendaki, ya? B: Ya. Mula-mula kita tangguhkan, kemudian kita tulis mesej untuk kawan kita.
target_spans: Ya. Mula-mula kita tangguhkan, kemudian kita tulis mesej untuk kawan kita.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|12.source_text: 6. A: Mula-mula kita buat apa? B: Mula-mula kita berjumpa di stesen pukul tujuh.
target_spans: Mula-mula kita berjumpa di stesen pukul tujuh.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|0.source_text: Explanation: mula-mula, kemudian and akhirnya give the order: first, then, finally. Mula-mula kita berjumpa di stesen. Kemudian kita mendaki. Akhirnya kita makan di kafe. (Kata-Kata lines). mula-mula is learned as a whole word, and akhirnya is akhir + -nya, also a whole word. kemudian (chapter 7) is the everyday "then"; in a formal message or a notice the word is seterusnya (next). In speech you may also hear lepas tu, which this course only asks you to recognise. Each step is a short sentence with the same subject, so say it again or leave it out when it is clear.
target_spans: Mula-mula kita berjumpa di stesen. Kemudian kita mendaki. Akhirnya kita makan di kafe.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|1.source_text: 説明：mula-mula・kemudian・akhirnya は順序を言います：まず・それから・最後に。Mula-mula kita berjumpa di stesen. Kemudian kita mendaki. Akhirnya kita makan di kafe.（Kata-Kata の文）。mula-mula は一語として、akhirnya は akhir ＋ -nya ですがやはり一語として覚えます。kemudian（第7章）は日常の「それから」で、改まったメッセージや掲示では seterusnya（次に）を使います。話し言葉では lepas tu も聞こえますが、このコースでは聞いて分かればよい語です。各段階は主語が同じ短い文で、分かるときは主語を繰り返すか省きます。
target_spans: Mula-mula kita berjumpa di stesen. Kemudian kita mendaki. Akhirnya kita makan di kafe.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|2.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese まず, それから and 最後に are the same three steps. Malay needs no connecting verb form: each step is a plain sentence. Do not use kemudian for 〜のあとで when another event comes first (selepas is for that).

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|3.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「まず」「それから」「最後に」と同じ三つの段階です。マレー語は動詞の形をつなぎ変えず、各段階を素の文にします。ほかの出来事が先にあるときの「〜のあとで」には kemudian ではなく selepas を使います。

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|0.source_text: Model each A line; learners answer as B, then swap. Explain the rule only after they have used the pattern.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|1.source_text: Pattern IDs are the Kata-Kata chapter 14 frames f01 to f06 (pattern 2 shows f02 and f03 together, reason and purpose). Explanations and Japanese comparisons are drafts.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|2.source_text: Pattern 1: kalau + a clause, a comma, then the result. Check that no word for "then" follows the comma, that tidak hujan is the opposite condition, and that bila is "when" in speech. Accept jika and apabila in a written line, and ask for kalau and bila when the learner speaks.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|3.source_text: Pattern 2: kerana and sebab for the reason, supaya for the purpose. If a learner says supaya for a reason, give the situation (the reason for staying away) and ask which word fits. Accept sebab in speech.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|4.source_text: Pattern 3: walaupun + a clause, a comma, then the surprising part, with no tetapi in the second clause. Check walaupun hujan (rain is no obstacle) against kalau hujan (a condition).

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|5.source_text: Pattern 4: sambil for two actions by one person at once; semasa and sejak as whole words. Check that both verbs stay plain.

Unit 14 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|6.source_text: Pattern 5: mula-mula, kemudian, akhirnya in order. Accept seterusnya in a written line and ask for kemudian in speech.

■ Japanese bridge · 日本語との橋渡し
sudah menulis ≈ もう書いた · akan berjumpa ≈ 会う予定 · sedang membaca ≈ 読んでいるところ · belum mendaki ≈ まだ登っていない · masih bekerja ≈ まだ働いている · baru menulis ≈ 書いたばかり

Japanese changes the verb ending (書いた / 書いていない); Malay puts the marker in front and keeps the verb (menulis). belum is まだ〜ていない, sudah is もう〜た. / 日本語は動詞の語尾が変わります。マレー語はマーカーを前に置き、動詞（menulis）はそのままです。belum は「まだ〜ていない」、sudah は「もう〜た」です。

1. Ask what you do if it rains. (apa)
2. Ask who wrote the message. (siapa)
3. Ask where you meet. (di mana)
4. Ask formally whether the hike is still on. (Adakah)
5. Ask politely whether you may move it to Sunday. (Bolehkah)
6. Ask how many choices there are. (berapa)
7. Ask when the hike starts. (bila)
8. Ask what time you meet. (pukul berapa)
9. Ask on what day you hike. (hari apa)
10. Ask how you get to the station. (bagaimana; spoken macam mana)
11. Ask why the hike is put off. (kenapa; also mengapa or apa sebab; the answer starts with sebab or kerana)
12. Ask which day is better. (yang mana)
13. Ask where you go after the hike. (ke mana)
14. Ask where your friend is from. (dari mana)
15. Ask how far the station is. (berapa jauh)
16. Ask how long the hike is. (berapa lama)
17. Ask how many cups of tea there are. (berapa with a counter)
18. Ask who made the plan. (siapa with oleh)

Unit 14 · Culture and usage note|2|0.source_text: Read about the everyday and the written words for if and when, the difference between putting a plan off and cancelling it, and the general custom of arranging outings in a group chat.

Unit 14 · Culture and usage note|3|0.source_text: There are two Malays for "if" and "when", and both are right. People say kalau and bila when they talk; a message, a notice or a letter may say jika and apabila. The same goes for tetapi and namun, jadi and oleh itu, kemudian and seterusnya. In the scene Tanaka hears the difference himself: Mei Ling writes Jika hujan, kita tangguhkan, and in speech they say Kalau hujan, kita tangguhkan. Use the everyday word to speak and the standard word to write something formal.

Unit 14 · Culture and usage note|3|1.source_text: A plan can change in two ways, and Malay names them separately. Tangguhkan puts the plan off to another day (the hike moves to Sunday), and batalkan cancels it (the hike is off). A change of plan is easier to accept when you give the reason with kerana or sebab and a new choice: Ada dua pilihan. A Janji! is a light promise between friends, and the other person takes it seriously.

Unit 14 · Culture and usage note|3|2.source_text: General knowledge, not a rule and not a checked fact: friends and colleagues in Malaysia often arrange an outing in a group chat, and a message about a change usually gives the reason and the new plan in a few short lines. The plans in this course are fictional.

Unit 14 · Culture and usage note|3|3.source_text: Japanese learners often use one word for every reason. Keep them apart: kerana and sebab for ので・から, supaya for ように, and walaupun for のに. And a Japanese 〜たら, 〜ば, 〜なら and 〜と are all kalau in Malay.

Unit 14 · Culture and usage note|3|5.source_text: 「もし」と「〜するとき」にはマレー語が二通りあり、どちらも正しい言い方です。話すときは kalau と bila、メッセージ・掲示・手紙では jika と apabila を使うことがあります。tetapi と namun、jadi と oleh itu、kemudian と seterusnya も同じです。場面の中で田中さんもその違いに気づきます：メイリンさんは Jika hujan, kita tangguhkan と書き、話すときは Kalau hujan, kita tangguhkan と言います。話すときは日常の語を、改まって書くときは標準の語を使います。

Unit 14 · Culture and usage note|3|6.source_text: 予定の変更には二通りあり、マレー語は別々の語で言います。Tangguhkan は別の日に延ばすこと（ハイキングを日曜日に延ばす）、batalkan は取りやめること（ハイキングは中止）です。予定を変えるときは、kerana か sebab で理由を言い、新しい選択肢を出すと受け入れられやすくなります：Ada dua pilihan. Janji! は友だち同士の軽い約束ですが、相手は本気で受け取ります。

Unit 14 · Culture and usage note|3|7.source_text: 一般的な知識であり、規則でも確認済みの事実でもありません：マレーシアでは、友人や同僚がグループチャットで外出の約束をすることがよくあり、変更のメッセージは、理由と新しい予定を短い数行で伝えるのがふつうです。このコースの予定はすべて架空です。

Unit 14 · Culture and usage note|3|8.source_text: 日本人の学習者は、理由をどれも同じ語で言いがちです。kerana・sebab は「ので・から」、supaya は「ように」、walaupun は「のに」と分けてください。また、日本語の「〜たら」「〜ば」「〜なら」「〜と」は、マレー語ではどれも kalau です。

Unit 14 · Teaching plan and answer key|3.source_text: Before Block A: Kata-Kata Sedia Kelas c14 (30 cards, frames ms-c14-f01 and ms-c14-f02).

After Block D: the Kata-Kata chapter 14 deck with spaced review, frames ms-c14-f01, ms-c14-f02, ms-c14-f03, ms-c14-f04, ms-c14-f05, ms-c14-f06 in the frame drill and Susun Ayat; about 3 hours of self-study for this unit (planning figure).
Hanashishou (Stage 2): the plan links chapter 14 to the work and social scenes with plans and changes. Their Malay is not yet tagged by chapter (build step 6), so do not assign them yet.
Next: the writing block after unit 14 (explain and rearrange a plan), then the review block after chapter 15 and unit 15 (Kata-Kata c15).
■ Block A · Words and patterns (45 min)
Goal: I can say a condition with kalau, a reason with kerana or sebab, a purpose with supaya and a contrast with walaupun.
0–5 Recall: chapters 5, 7 and 13 (Kenapa …? with sebab, perlu, belum) from the opener prompts.
10–20 Vocabulary focus: core words first, with each root; recognition and revision words are only pointed out.

20–40 Pattern focus: patterns 1 and 2 first (kalau, kerana / supaya), question and answer before the rule; then the vocabulary in three groups with each whole word and its root (joining ideas 10, the order of a plan 3, plans and changes 9). Draw the ladder: everyday kalau, bila, tetapi, jadi, kemudian beside the written jika, apabila, namun, oleh itu, seterusnya.
■ Block B · Drills and conversation (45 min)
Goal: I can plan a weekend outing with a friend: a rain plan, a reason I cannot come, a choice of two days and the order of the day.
0–5 Recall: say one reason with kerana and one condition with kalau.
5–25 Drill ladder in order: pattern table, substitution, transformation (written to everyday first), question and answer, question-word choice, short dialogues, then the markers drill.
25–40 Model conversation, gapped form, then the changed-facts variant.

Unit 14 · Teaching plan and answer key|4.source_text: Goal: I can follow a phone call about a changed plan, read a message in written Malay, and put a plan off or cancel it with a reason.
0–5 Recall: each learner says one rain plan and one reason for staying away.
5–20 Listening: read the questions, two readings, check, then shadow three lines.
30–45 Task with role cards; announce the change of plan halfway.
■ Block D · Review and test (45 min)
Goal: I can choose between kalau and walaupun, kerana and supaya, and between the everyday and the written words, and correct a short sentence.
0–15 Mixed review: cumulative question-word drill (chapters 1 to 14), then the markers drill with new cues and a check of kerana against supaya and kalau against walaupun.
35–45 Preview: the writing block after unit 14 (explain and rearrange a plan), then unit 15 (lost and found; Kata-Kata c15).
Goal: I can handle a short role-play about a changed outing, including a second change of plan.
0–5 Recall: say three sentences about a weekend plan with kalau, kerana and supaya.

5–15 Scene listening: read the Kata-Kata scenario lines ms-c14-s01 to ms-c14-s15 (Tanaka and Cik Mei Ling plan the hike) twice; learners tick kalau, kerana, supaya, walaupun, sambil, tangguhkan and batalkan when they hear them, and listen for the message language in lines 13 and 14.
15–30 Role-play in pairs: pairs play the same scene with their own fictional outing, reason and day, without the script.
30–40 Changed situation: a changed day: it rains on Sunday too; one cancels the outing, the other asks the time of the meal and makes a promise.
40–45 Culture and usage note discussion, and the home-practice briefing.

Unit 14 · Teaching plan and answer key|5.source_text: Load: 29 core words in three groups (joining ideas 10, the order of a plan and agreeing it 5, plans and changes 14), no recognition word, and revision of if, because and but, weather and the hike, the plan and talking. Suggested order: Block A the first group with patterns 1 and 2; Block B the second and third groups with patterns 3 to 5. If the pilot shows 29 is too many, the natural cut is: kalau / jika, kerana, supaya, walaupun, sambil, mula-mula, akhirnya, tangguhkan, batalkan, pilihan first; the rest second.

Written against spoken (Sam, 13 Nov 2026): the everyday words are what people say: kalau, bila (for "when"), tetapi or spoken tapi, jadi, kemudian (spoken lepas tu, recognition only). The standard words are for a message or a notice: jika, apabila, namun, oleh itu, seterusnya. bila as "when" is everyday and apabila is standard. The scene models it in lines s13 and s14: do not correct Kalau or bila in speech and do not ask for jika in a conversation.

kerana (standard) or sebab (everyday) for the reason and supaya for the purpose; do not swap them. walaupun opens the first clause and takes no tetapi in the second; kalau hujan (a condition) is not walaupun hujan (rain is no obstacle). sambil is two actions by one person; semasa and sejak are whole words.

Whole words and roots: walaupun (walau), akhirnya (akhir + -nya), mula-mula (repeated words come in Stage 3), seterusnya (terus), semasa (masa), tujuan (tuju), pilihan (pilih), keputusan (putus) and perubahan (ubah) are each learned whole. tangguh and batal are the roots of tangguhkan and batalkan (cards ms-c14-018 to -022).

The -kan rule from chapter 12 (Sam): tangguhkan and batalkan appear in kita sentences and requests (Kita batalkan rancangan mendaki., Boleh kita tangguhkan ke hari Ahad?), never after sudah, sedang, belum, akan, baru or masih. A third person (a doer who is not kita and not the speaker) takes the standard forms menangguhkan and membatalkan (Sam, 14 Nov 2026; both are ledger rows, L-1294 and L-1295): Mei Ling menangguhkan rancangan mendaki kerana dia bekerja., Puan Aini membatalkan mesyuarat itu. The bare tangguhkan and batalkan stay for requests, offers and kita plans. Rancangan mendaki batal. stays for the intransitive. baiklah is one word (an agreement or the start of a plan, as in Baiklah, kita buat begini.); the standard form is the same in speech, so no register pair is taught.
target_spans: Boleh kita tangguhkan ke hari Ahad?
Mei Ling menangguhkan rancangan mendaki kerana dia bekerja.

Unit 14 · Teaching plan and answer key|5.source_text: tangguhkan and batalkan take a noun object, not a verb: tangguhkan rancangan mendaki, batalkan rancangan mendaki (a verb such as mendaki does not follow them), and Rancangan mendaki batal. for the intransitive. A written notice gives the object (Oleh itu, kita tangguhkan rancangan itu ke hari Ahad.); a short spoken reply may drop it (Jika hujan, kita tangguhkan., Kita tangguhkan ke hari Ahad.).
target_spans: Oleh itu, kita tangguhkan rancangan itu ke hari Ahad.

Unit 14 · Teaching plan and answer key|6.source_text: kami against kita (a common trap): kami leaves the listener out, kita includes the listener. A group-chat message or a notice goes to people who are going too, so it says kita (Kita tangguhkan ke hari Ahad. Namun kita masih makan di kafe.). kami fits an invitation to someone who has not yet said yes (Hujung minggu ini kami mahu mendaki. Puan Aini mahu datang?); once she says yes, the plan is kita. Japanese has one 私たち for both, so learners mix them: the question is whether the listener goes too.
target_spans: Kita tangguhkan ke hari Ahad. Namun kita masih makan di kafe.
Hujung minggu ini kami mahu mendaki. Puan Aini mahu datang?

Unit 14 · Teaching plan and answer key|6.source_text: keputusan is a word for a written notice or a result (Keputusan: hari Ahad.). The casual turns do not use ruling-style words: no keputusan in conversation. The casual dialogue lines may use the everyday bare root after an aspect word, as Kata-Kata does (Saya sudah tulis mesej.); the pattern examples, keys, notices and written texts use the meN- form (menulis).

Where Japanese learners usually slip: (1) supaya for a reason, or kerana for a purpose (ので against ように); (2) tetapi in the second clause after walaupun; (3) a word for "then" after the comma of kalau; (4) bila for "if" and kalau for "when"; (5) jika and apabila in speech, which sounds like a notice; (6) one verb in the sambil sentence given to two different people.

Natural speech: Kalau, bila, tetapi, jadi, Janji! and Baik in conversation; jika, apabila, namun, oleh itu, seterusnya in messages and notices. The casual lines keep kita and a short second sentence. The scene follows Kata-Kata c14 (scenario lines ms-c14-s01 to s15, frames f01 to f06). All names, plans and times are fictional; learners may use an invented outing.
Cumulative question words: chapters 1 to 14. Chapter 14 adds no new question word.

Unit 14 · Teaching plan and answer key|7.source_text: Answer keys are on each component. Japanese text awaits native review.
Standard forms first; spoken forms are labelled. ber- verbs are taught as whole ledger forms, each with its root; no meN- verb (chapter 11) and no suffixed verb form (chapter 12).

The writing block after unit 14 (45 minutes): write a message that changes a plan in six to eight sentences, with a reason, the new day, a rain plan, the order of the day and a purpose, in everyday words for a group chat and in written words for a notice; names and days may be invented.
Fictional model: two messages about the same change, one for a group chat (everyday) and one for a notice at the office (written). All names and plans are invented:

Selamat petang semua. Kita tangguhkan rancangan mendaki ke hari Ahad kerana saya bekerja pada hari Sabtu. Kalau hujan, kita makan di kafe. Mula-mula kita berjumpa di stesen pukul tujuh, kemudian kita mendaki, akhirnya kita makan di kafe. Saya datang awal supaya kita tidak lambat. Janji!

Unit 14 · Writing block · Explain and re.source_text: Notice: the reason first, then the new day, the rain plan and the order. The group chat says kalau and bila; the notice says jika, apabila, namun and oleh itu. / 気づくこと：理由、新しい日、雨の日の計画、順序の順に書きます。グループチャットは kalau・bila、掲示は jika・apabila・namun・oleh itu を使います。
■ Plan · 45 minutes · 進め方
0–5 Recall: say a reason with kerana, a condition with kalau and a purpose with supaya (unit 14).
5–15 Model and notice: read the two messages; underline every connector and say which is everyday and which is written; rewrite Jika hujan, kita batalkan rancangan itu as speech.
target_spans: Jika hujan, kita batalkan rancangan itu

Unit 14 · Writing block · Explain and re.source_text: 15–30 Guided draft: write your own message about a changed outing, first for a group chat, then as a short notice, with the checklist below.
30–40 Peer or teacher feedback with the peer check.
40–45 Rewrite one sentence from the group chat into the written style, and read the group-chat message aloud.
0–5 復習・5–15 例文を読んで気づく・15–30 下書き・30–40 ペアまたは先生の確認・40–45 一文を書き直して音読。
■ Your turn · 自分で
Write six to eight sentences: a message to your group chat about a changed outing, then two sentences of the same news as a notice. Include:
☐ the reason for the change (kerana or sebab), and Ada perubahan rancangan.
☐ the new day, with tangguhkan in a kita sentence (Kita tangguhkan … ke hari …)
☐ a rain plan with kalau (Kalau hujan, kita …), and in the notice jika
☐ the order of the day with mula-mula, kemudian and akhirnya, and a purpose with supaya
予定が変わったことを知らせるグループチャットのメッセージと、同じ知らせを短い掲示にした二文を、6〜8文で書きましょう。変更の理由、新しい日、雨の日の計画、一日の順序、目的を入れます。名前・日・場所は架空でかまいません。
■ Peer check · 互いに確認
☐ kerana or sebab gives a reason, supaya a purpose (not the other way round).
☐ A comma follows the kalau, jika and walaupun clause, and no word for "then" follows it.
☐ The group chat uses kalau and bila; the notice uses jika, apabila, namun or oleh itu (and not both in one text).
☐ tangguhkan and batalkan are in kita sentences or a request, not after sudah, sedang, belum or akan; the partner can answer one question about the message.
☐ 理由と目的の語、コンマ、日常の語と書き言葉の語の使い分け、tangguhkan・batalkan の使い方を確認し、パートナーが質問を一つします。

Model: Any six to eight correct sentences that cover the checklist. Model: Selamat petang semua. Kita tangguhkan rancangan mendaki ke hari Ahad kerana saya bekerja pada hari Sabtu. Kalau hujan, kita makan di kafe. Mula-mula kita berjumpa di stesen, kemudian kita mendaki, akhirnya kita makan di kafe. Saya datang awal supaya kita tidak lambat. Janji! Notice: PENGUMUMAN. Ada perubahan rancangan. Oleh itu, kita tangguhkan rancangan itu ke hari Ahad. Jika hujan, kita batalkan rancangan itu.
target_spans: Selamat petang semua. Kita tangguhkan rancangan mendaki ke hari Ahad kerana saya bekerja pada hari Sabtu. Kalau hujan, kita makan di kafe. Mula-mula kita berjumpa di stesen, kemudian kita mendaki, akhirnya kita makan di kafe. Saya datang awal supaya kita tidak lambat. Janji!
PENGUMUMAN. Ada perubahan rancangan. Oleh itu, kita tangguhkan rancangan itu ke hari Ahad. Jika hujan, kita batalkan rancangan itu.

Unit 14 · Writing block · Explain and re.source_text: Mark for the task first (the reason, the new day, the rain plan, the order, the purpose), then for form (the comma, the choice of everyday or written words, tangguhkan and batalkan in a kita sentence). Accept jika in the group chat in a first draft but ask for kalau once in the rewrite; accept the everyday bare root in a first draft (Kita tulis mesej) but ask for the meN- form in the notice.
Names, days and places are fictional. Do not ask anyone to share a real address or phone number.
This is the extra 45-minute writing block after unit 14.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|7.source_text: Explanation: ___ saya hilang. says that something of mine is lost: the thing first, then saya (my), then hilang (the Kata-Kata frame): Dompet saya hilang. hilang means you cannot find it. The thing is the subject: you do not say saya hilang dompet. barang hilang is lost property, and kaunter barang hilang is the lost-property counter. Add where and when after the thing: Beg tangan saya hilang di stesen. Barang saya hilang tadi. Do not use hilang for something you left behind by accident; chapter 16 teaches that.
target_spans: Beg tangan saya hilang di stesen.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|8.source_text: 説明：___ saya hilang. は私の〜がなくなった、という意味です：物が先、次に saya（私の）、最後に hilang（Kata-Kata の文型）：Dompet saya hilang. hilang は見つからないことです。なくなった物が主語で、saya hilang dompet とは言いません。barang hilang は遺失物、kaunter barang hilang は遺失物の窓口です。場所や時はあとに足します：Beg tangan saya hilang di stesen. Barang saya hilang tadi. うっかり置き忘れたときには hilang を使いません。それは第16章で学びます。
target_spans: Beg tangan saya hilang di stesen.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|9.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese says 財布をなくした with a doer who loses it. Malay makes the wallet the subject: the wallet is lost. 私の財布 puts the owner first; Malay puts it after the thing: dompet saya. A learner who says saya hilang has said that "I" am missing.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|10.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語は「財布をなくした」と、なくした人を主語にして言います。マレー語は財布を主語にして「財布がなくなった」と言います。「私の財布」は持ち主が先ですが、マレー語は物のあとに saya を置きます：dompet saya。saya hilang と言うと、「私が行方不明だ」という意味になります。

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|12.source_text: Pattern box: Saya mencari ___ yang ada ___ . / Lelaki yang memakai ___ .  (the thing or person that has / wears)

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|13.source_text: 1. A: Awak mencari apa? B: Saya mencari beg yang ada zip.
target_spans: Saya mencari beg yang ada zip.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|14.source_text: 2. A: Beg yang mana? B: Beg yang ada tali panjang.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|15.source_text: 3. A: Siapa lelaki itu? B: Lelaki yang memakai cermin mata.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|0.source_text: 4. A: Perempuan yang mana? B: Perempuan yang memakai topi.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|1.source_text: 5. A: Awak mencari dompet yang mana? B: Dompet yang ada satu poket kecil.
target_spans: Dompet yang ada satu poket kecil.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|2.source_text: 6. A: Tetamu kita yang mana? B: Lelaki yang memakai baju berjalur.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|3.source_text: Explanation: Say the thing or the person first, then yang, then a short clause that tells which one: Saya mencari beg yang ada zip. (the Kata-Kata frame) and Lelaki yang memakai cermin mata. (the Kata-Kata frame). yang ada ___ says what the thing has, and yang memakai ___ says what the person wears. yang is one word for "who", "which" and "that", for things and for people, and it stands between the noun and the description. The clause is short and has its own verb: ada, memakai, membawa. Without yang, beg ada zip is a whole sentence (the bag has a zip), not a description of the bag.
target_spans: Saya mencari beg yang ada zip.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|4.source_text: 説明：まず物か人を言い、次に yang、そのあとに、どれかを示す短い節を置きます：Saya mencari beg yang ada zip.（Kata-Kata の文型）、Lelaki yang memakai cermin mata.（Kata-Kata の文型）。yang ada ___ は持っているもの、yang memakai ___ は身につけているものを言います。yang は「〜する（人・物）」にあたる一語で、物にも人にも使い、名詞と説明のあいだに置きます。節は短く、ada・memakai・membawa のような動詞を持ちます。yang がないと beg ada zip は「そのバッグはファスナーがある」という一つの文になり、バッグの説明にはなりません。
target_spans: Saya mencari beg yang ada zip.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|5.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese puts the whole description before the noun: ファスナーが付いているバッグ, 眼鏡をかけている男性. Malay reverses it: the noun first, then yang and the clause: beg yang ada zip, lelaki yang memakai cermin mata. Japanese needs no linking word, so yang is the word learners forget.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|6.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語は説明全体を名詞の前に置きます：「ファスナーが付いているバッグ」「眼鏡をかけている男性」。マレー語は逆で、名詞が先、次に yang と節：beg yang ada zip、lelaki yang memakai cermin mata。日本語には結ぶ語が要らないので、yang は忘れやすい語です。

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|8.source_text: Pattern box: Beg itu berwarna ___ dan ada ___ .  (colour and features)

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|9.source_text: 1. A: Apa warna beg itu? B: Beg itu berwarna hitam dan ada tali panjang.
target_spans: Beg itu berwarna hitam dan ada tali panjang.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|10.source_text: 2. A: Apa warna dompet itu? B: Hitam. Dompet kulit. Ada zip dan satu poket kecil.
target_spans: Hitam. Dompet kulit. Ada zip dan satu poket kecil.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|11.source_text: 3. A: Baju lelaki itu berwarna apa? B: Baju itu putih dan berjalur.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|12.source_text: 4. A: Topi perempuan itu berwarna apa? B: Topi itu berwarna merah.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|13.source_text: 5. A: Beg itu besar atau kecil? B: Beg itu kecil dan berwarna biru.
target_spans: Beg itu kecil dan berwarna biru.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|14.source_text: 6. A: Apa lagi ciri beg itu? B: Ada zip dan dua poket.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|0.source_text: Explanation: berwarna + a colour word gives the colour: Beg itu berwarna hitam. dan ada ___ adds what it has: Beg itu berwarna hitam dan ada tali panjang. (the Kata-Kata frame). Ask the colour with Apa warna ___ itu? or berwarna apa?. The colour word alone also works in everyday speech (Hitam., Beg itu hitam., warna hitam). berjalur (striped) is learned whole. ciri is a feature: Apa ciri beg itu? ada names a feature the thing has: ada zip, ada satu poket kecil, ada tali panjang. Two features are usually enough to find one bag.
target_spans: Beg itu berwarna hitam dan ada tali panjang.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|1.source_text: 説明：berwarna ＋色の語で色を言います：Beg itu berwarna hitam. dan ada ___ で持っているものを足します：Beg itu berwarna hitam dan ada tali panjang.（Kata-Kata の文型）。色は Apa warna ___ itu? か berwarna apa? でたずねます。日常では色の語だけでもかまいません（Hitam.・Beg itu hitam.・warna hitam）。berjalur（しま模様の）は一語として覚えます。ciri は特徴です：Apa ciri beg itu? ada はその物が持つ特徴を言います：ada zip・ada satu poket kecil・ada tali panjang。バッグを見つけるには、特徴が二つあればたいてい十分です。
target_spans: Beg itu berwarna hitam dan ada tali panjang.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|2.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese has the adjective 黒い and the noun 黒色, and says バッグは黒で、ひもが長い with に・で・が. Malay says berwarna hitam (is black-coloured) and uses ada (has) for every feature where Japanese says 付き or 〜がある: ファスナー付き is ada zip.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|3.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語には形容詞の「黒い」と名詞の「黒色」があり、「バッグは黒で、ひもが長い」と言います。マレー語は berwarna hitam と言い、持っている特徴は日本語の「〜付き」「〜がある」にあたる ada で言います：「ファスナー付き」は ada zip。

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|5.source_text: Pattern box: Bentuknya ___ , seperti ___ .  (shape and likeness; seperti itu and seperti ini)

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|6.source_text: 1. A: Bagaimana bentuk dompet itu? B: Bentuknya segi empat, seperti kotak.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|7.source_text: 2. A: Bagaimana bentuk beg itu? B: Bulat, seperti bola.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|8.source_text: 3. A: Seperti ini? B: Ya, seperti itu, tetapi ada zip.
target_spans: Ya, seperti itu, tetapi ada zip.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|9.source_text: 4. A: Dompet awak seperti ini? B: Tidak, bukan seperti ini. Dompet saya segi empat.
target_spans: Tidak, bukan seperti ini. Dompet saya segi empat.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|10.source_text: 5. A: Bagaimana bentuk meja di kafe itu? B: Bulat. Seperti pinggan besar.
target_spans: Bagaimana bentuk meja di kafe itu?

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|11.source_text: 6. A: Beg itu seperti beg awak? B: Ya, seperti beg saya. Warna beg itu pun sama.
target_spans: Ya, seperti beg saya. Warna beg itu pun sama.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|0.source_text: Explanation: bentuk is shape, and bentuknya (-nya, chapter 2) is "its shape": Bentuknya segi empat, seperti kotak. (the Kata-Kata frame). seperti + a noun says what it looks like: seperti kotak, seperti bola. seperti ini is "like this one" (the thing is near the speaker or in the hand), and seperti itu is "like that one": Seperti ini? Ya, seperti itu, tetapi ada zip. (Kata-Kata lines). seperti is the standard word. In speech people say macam (chapter 5); the spoken macam tu for seperti itu comes in chapter 17, so this unit only names it. segi empat and bulat tell the shape: four-sided or round.
target_spans: Ya, seperti itu, tetapi ada zip.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|1.source_text: 説明：bentuk は形、bentuknya（-nya、第2章）は「その形」です：Bentuknya segi empat, seperti kotak.（Kata-Kata の文型）。seperti ＋名詞で何に似ているかを言います：seperti kotak・seperti bola。seperti ini は「これのような」（話し手の近くや手にある物）、seperti itu は「それのような」です：Seperti ini? Ya, seperti itu, tetapi ada zip.（Kata-Kata の文）。seperti は標準の語です。話すときは macam（第5章）を使い、seperti itu にあたる話し言葉の macam tu は第17章なので、このユニットでは名前だけ出します。segi empat と bulat は形を言います：四角か丸です。
target_spans: Ya, seperti itu, tetapi ada zip.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|2.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 〜のような and 〜みたい both mean seperti; そのような is seperti itu and このような is seperti ini. Japanese says 形は四角で、箱のようです with a ような that changes form; Malay keeps seperti as it is and puts the noun after it.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|3.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「〜のような」「〜みたい」はどちらも seperti です。「そのような」は seperti itu、「このような」は seperti ini。日本語は「箱のようです」と「ような」が形を変えますが、マレー語は seperti の形を変えず、あとに名詞を置きます。

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|5.source_text: Pattern box: Yang mana satu? Yang ___ atau yang ___ ?  (which one of two)

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|6.source_text: 1. A: Yang mana satu? Yang ada zip atau yang tidak ada zip? B: Yang ada zip.
target_spans: Yang mana satu? Yang ada zip atau yang tidak ada zip?

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|7.source_text: 2. A: Beg yang mana? Yang besar atau yang kecil? B: Yang kecil.
target_spans: Beg yang mana? Yang besar atau yang kecil?

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|8.source_text: 3. A: Lelaki yang mana? Yang memakai topi atau yang memakai cermin mata? B: Yang memakai cermin mata.
target_spans: Lelaki yang mana? Yang memakai topi atau yang memakai cermin mata?

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|9.source_text: 4. A: Yang mana satu? Yang berwarna hitam atau yang berwarna biru? B: Yang berwarna biru. Yang itu!
target_spans: Yang mana satu? Yang berwarna hitam atau yang berwarna biru?

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|10.source_text: 5. A: Perempuan yang mana? Yang tinggi atau yang pendek? B: Yang tinggi.
target_spans: Perempuan yang mana? Yang tinggi atau yang pendek?

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|11.source_text: 6. A: Yang mana satu, encik? B: Yang itu! Yang ada zip.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|0.source_text: Explanation: Yang mana satu? asks which one of two or more things or people. Offer the choice with Yang ___ atau yang ___? (the Kata-Kata frame): Yang ada zip atau yang tidak ada zip? The answer is Yang + the feature, and the noun is left out because it is already clear: Yang ada zip. Yang itu! points at the one. tidak ada is the opposite of ada: yang tidak ada zip. yang mana was taught in chapter 6; now it picks one by its description.
target_spans: Yang ada zip atau yang tidak ada zip?

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|1.source_text: 説明：Yang mana satu? は、二つ以上の中からどれかをたずねます。Yang ___ atau yang ___?（Kata-Kata の文型）で選択肢を出します：Yang ada zip atau yang tidak ada zip? 答えは Yang ＋特徴で、名詞は分かっているので省きます：Yang ada zip. Yang itu! はその一つを指します。tidak ada は ada の反対です：yang tidak ada zip。yang mana は第6章で学びました。ここでは特徴で一つを選びます。
target_spans: Yang ada zip atau yang tidak ada zip?

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|2.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese asks どれ? and answers with の: 黒いの, ファスナー付きのやつ. Malay does the same with yang: yang hitam, yang ada zip. The Japanese の (the one) is yang, and the noun can be dropped after it.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|3.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語は「どれ？」とたずね、「の」で答えます：「黒いの」「ファスナー付きのやつ」。マレー語も yang で同じことをします：yang hitam・yang ada zip。日本語の「の」（その物）にあたるのが yang で、そのあとの名詞は省けます。

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|0.source_text: Model each A line; learners answer as B, then swap. Explain the rule only after they have used the pattern.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|1.source_text: Pattern IDs are the Kata-Kata chapter 15 frames f01 to f06 (pattern 2 shows f01 and f03 together, the thing or person that has or wears; the patterns run f02, f01 and f03, f04, f06, f05). Explanations and Japanese comparisons are drafts.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|2.source_text: Pattern 1: the thing comes first, then saya, then hilang. If a learner says saya hilang dompet, give the situation (a wallet that cannot be found) and ask who or what is lost. Accept hilang for something you cannot find; if a learner means something left behind by accident, say that chapter 16 has a word for it.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|3.source_text: Pattern 2: the noun, then yang, then a short clause with ada, memakai or membawa. Check that yang is not left out before ada or a verb, and that the description is not put before the noun.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|4.source_text: Pattern 3: berwarna + a colour, then dan ada + a feature. Accept hitam or warna hitam in a quick answer. Check apa warna for the question.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|5.source_text: Pattern 4: bentuknya + segi empat or bulat, then seperti + a noun; seperti ini for the thing in front of you and seperti itu for the one that is not. Accept macam in speech; do not teach macam tu yet.

Unit 15 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|6.source_text: Pattern 5: Yang mana satu? then Yang ___ atau yang ___?. The answer is Yang + a feature, with no noun. Check that tidak ada is the opposite of ada.

9. Ask on what day the wallet was lost. (hari apa)
10. Ask how the wallet looks. (bagaimana; spoken macam mana)
11. Ask why the owner is looking for the bag. (kenapa; also mengapa or apa sebab; the answer starts with sebab or kerana)

13. Ask where the visitors go next. (ke mana)

Unit 15 · Culture and usage note|1|0.source_text: No Malay explainer for Stage 2 units: explainers and rubrics are in Japanese or English only, as in Stage 1 (Sam, 13 Nov 2026). Select 日本語 or English.

Unit 15 · Culture and usage note|2|0.source_text: Read about the description before the noun against yang after it, how to talk at a lost-property counter, the general knowledge sentence, and where Japanese learners slip with yang.

Unit 15 · Culture and usage note|3|0.source_text: In Japanese the description comes before the noun: 黒い財布, 眼鏡をかけている男性. Malay puts the noun first and the description after it: dompet hitam, lelaki yang memakai cermin mata. A single adjective can follow the noun by itself, while a clause with a verb or ada needs yang (beg yang ada zip). yang also stands for "the one" when the noun is left out: Yang ada zip.

Unit 15 · Culture and usage note|3|1.source_text: At a lost-property counter people start with what can be seen, not with a brand: the colour, the material, the shape and one small feature such as a zip or a pocket. Staff often hold something up and ask Seperti ini? A good answer says Ya, seperti itu, tetapi … and names the difference. One clear difference helps the counter more than a plain "no".

Unit 15 · Culture and usage note|3|2.source_text: General knowledge, not a rule and not a checked fact: stations, offices and shopping centres in Malaysia often have a counter for lost property, and staff may ask for a description and a form before they hand something back. What each place asks for differs, so ask at the counter. The items, places and times in this course are fictional.

Unit 15 · Culture and usage note|3|3.source_text: Japanese learners often drop yang before ada or a verb, or put the description before the noun as in Japanese. They may also add yang to every adjective. dompet hitam and dompet yang hitam are both heard, but beg yang ada zip needs yang. And one verb, memakai, covers glasses, clothes, a hat and shoes, where Japanese changes the verb each time.

Unit 15 · Culture and usage note|3|5.source_text: 日本語では説明が名詞の前に来ます：「黒い財布」「眼鏡をかけている男性」。マレー語は名詞が先で、説明があとに来ます：dompet hitam、lelaki yang memakai cermin mata。形容詞が一つなら名詞のすぐあとに置けますが、動詞や ada のある節には yang が要ります（beg yang ada zip）。名詞を省くと、yang は「その一つ」にもなります：Yang ada zip.

Unit 15 · Culture and usage note|3|6.source_text: 遺失物の窓口では、ブランドからではなく、目に見えること、つまり色・材料・形、そしてファスナーやポケットのような小さな特徴から話します。窓口の人が物を見せて Seperti ini? とたずねることもよくあります。良い答えは Ya, seperti itu, tetapi … と違いを言うことです。はっきりした違いを一つ言うほうが、ただ「違います」と言うより窓口の助けになります。

Unit 15 · Culture and usage note|3|7.source_text: 一般的な知識であり、規則でも確認済みの事実でもありません：マレーシアの駅・会社・ショッピングセンターには遺失物の窓口があることが多く、物を返す前に、特徴をたずねたり書類を書かせたりすることがあります。場所によって違うので、窓口で聞いてください。このコースの物・場所・時刻はすべて架空です。

Unit 15 · Culture and usage note|4|0.source_text: 日本人の学習者は、ada や動詞の前の yang を落としたり、日本語のように説明を名詞の前に置いたりしがちです。形容詞ごとに yang を付けすぎることもあります。dompet hitam も dompet yang hitam も聞かれますが、beg yang ada zip には yang が要ります。また、めがね・服・帽子・靴のどれにも、日本語は動詞を変えますが、マレー語は memakai の一語です。

■ Block A · Words and patterns (45 min)
Goal: I can say that something of mine is lost and describe it with yang, a colour and a feature.
0–5 Recall: chapters 5, 8 and 14 (a colour, a piece of clothing, a counter, kerana) from the opener prompts.

20–40 Pattern focus: patterns 1 and 2 first (___ saya hilang, yang ada and yang memakai), question and answer before the rule; then the vocabulary in four groups with each whole word and its root (lost things 6, parts and materials 5, colour, shape and likeness 6, people and what they wear 4). Draw the order: Japanese 黒い財布 against Malay dompet hitam and dompet yang hitam.
■ Block B · Drills and conversation (45 min)
Goal: I can describe a wallet or a bag by colour, shape and features, and say which one with Yang mana satu?.
0–5 Recall: say what is lost and give one colour.
5–25 Drill ladder in order: pattern table, substitution, transformation (join with yang first), question and answer, question-word choice, short dialogues, then the markers drill.
25–40 Model conversation, gapped form, then the changed-facts variant.

Unit 15 · Teaching plan and answer key|4.source_text: Goal: I can follow a call that describes two visitors, read a lost-property form and tell a person by what they wear.
