■ Block D · Review and test (45 min)
Goal: I can decide when yang is needed, use memakai for what people wear, and correct a short description.
0–15 Mixed review: cumulative question-word drill (chapters 1 to 15), then the markers drill with new cues and a check of yang against no yang.
35–45 Preview: the review block after chapter 15 (chapters 13 to 15 and earlier verb contrasts), then unit 16 (accidents and complaints; Kata-Kata c16).
Goal: I can handle a short role-play at a lost-property counter or at a station, including a second item that looks the same.
0–5 Recall: say three sentences that describe a bag or a person with yang, berwarna and seperti.

5–15 Scene listening: read the Kata-Kata scenario lines ms-c15-s01 to ms-c15-s17 (the lost-property counter, then the visitors) twice; learners tick hilang, yang, memakai, berwarna and seperti when they hear them, and listen for Yang itu! in line 9.
15–30 Role-play in pairs: pairs play the counter scene with their own fictional item, colour and features, without the script; then swap and describe a visitor at a station.
30–40 Changed situation: a changed item: a second bag looks the same; one asks Yang mana satu?, the other chooses by one feature and names something inside.

Unit 15 · Teaching plan and answer key|5.source_text: Load: 23 core words in four groups (lost things 7, parts and materials 5, colour, shape and likeness 7, people and what they wear 4), no recognition word, and revision of describing, clothes and papers, places and people, and talking. Suggested order: Block A the first two groups with patterns 1 and 2; Block B the last two groups with patterns 3 to 5. If the pilot shows 23 is too many, the natural cut is: hilang, dompet, beg tangan, zip, berwarna, bentuk, seperti, lelaki, perempuan, memakai first; the rest second.

yang is the connector Japanese does not need. Japanese puts the whole description before the noun and links it with nothing: 黒い財布, 眼鏡をかけている男性. Malay puts the noun first and joins the description with yang: dompet yang hitam and dompet hitam both exist (the first stresses "the black one" against another), and lelaki yang memakai cermin mata needs yang because the description has a verb. yang is one word for "who", "which" and "that", for people and things.

When yang can be dropped: a single adjective straight after the noun (dompet hitam, beg besar, lelaki tinggi). When it cannot: a clause with a verb or ada (beg yang ada zip, perempuan yang memakai topi), because beg ada zip is a whole sentence ("the bag has a zip"). yang stays when the noun is left out (Yang ada zip., Yang itu!) and after yang mana when one of two is chosen. A learner who drops yang before an adjective is understood; a learner who drops it before ada is not.

memakai covers glasses, clothes, a hat and shoes (memakai cermin mata, memakai baju, memakai topi, memakai kasut), where Japanese changes the verb: かける for glasses, 着る for clothes, かぶる for a hat and はく for shoes and trousers. It is the standard form of the everyday pakai (chapter 4): a dialogue may use pakai, and the pattern examples and keys use memakai. memakai also means "to use", which this unit does not drill.

hilang (lost) against tertinggal (left behind), which chapter 16 teaches: Dompet saya hilang. means you cannot find the wallet; tertinggal is for something you left somewhere by accident. Keep to hilang in this unit (the plan asks for hilang here and tertinggal in chapter 16). If a learner says tertinggal, accept it and say the word comes next chapter.

seperti and seperti itu / seperti ini: seperti is the standard word, and everyday speech says macam (chapter 5). seperti itu is the standard form of the spoken macam tu, which chapter 17 teaches, so it is only named here. ini is the thing near the speaker or in the hand, itu the one that is not.

Unit 15 · Teaching plan and answer key|6.source_text: Whole words and roots: berjalur (ber- + jalur) and berwarna (ber- + warna) are each learned whole; memakai is me- + pakai with the p dropped; bentuknya is bentuk + -nya. ciri may be printed doubled, ciri-ciri, on forms: recognise both (repeated words come in Stage 3). beg tangan, cermin mata, nombor plat and segi empat are learned as phrases (cards ms-c15-007, -017, -009, -012).

The -kan and bare-root rules from chapters 12 to 14 still hold: a dialogue line may keep Kata-Kata's everyday bare root (Saya sudah jumpa dia.), and the pattern examples, keys and written forms use the meN- form (mencari, membawa, memakai). A request takes the plain root (Tolong cari telefon saya.). dari is for places (dari Jepun) and daripada for people and organisations.

Where Japanese learners usually slip: (1) leaving out yang before ada or a verb; (2) putting the description before the noun; (3) saya hilang for "I lost it" (it says "I am missing"); (4) one verb for each kind of clothing instead of memakai; (5) seperti followed by a clause instead of a noun; (6) answering Yang mana satu? with the noun again instead of Yang ___.

Natural speech: Yang itu!, Seperti ini? and Ya, seperti itu, tetapi … at the counter; memakai, yang and berwarna in a description; the form says Ciri (often printed doubled, ciri-ciri) and Sila ambil …. The scene follows Kata-Kata c15 (scenario lines ms-c15-s01 to s17, frames f01 to f06); turn 11 of the model joins s11 and s12. All names, items and times are fictional; learners may use an invented item.
Cumulative question words: chapters 1 to 15. Chapter 15 adds no new question word; yang mana (chapter 6) now picks one by its description.

Unit 15 · Review block · Chapters 13 to.source_text: Notice: belum and sudah stand in front of the verb; perlu says what you must do and supaya why; yang opens a description after the noun; a ber- verb has no object (bekerja, berjumpa), a meN- verb takes the thing (mendaftar, menunggu doktor), a request takes the plain root (Tolong hubungi …) and -i points at a person or place. / 気づくこと：belum・sudah は動詞の前、perlu はすべきこと、supaya は目的、yang は名詞のあとの説明を始めます。ber- の動詞は目的語をとらず（bekerja・berjumpa）、meN- の動詞は物をすぐあとに置き（mendaftar・menunggu doktor）、依頼は素の語根（Tolong hubungi …）、-i は人や場所へ向かう動作です。
■ Plan · 45 minutes · 進め方
0–5 Recall: say one thing you have not done yet with belum and describe one thing in the room with yang.
5–15 Mixed input: read the model; underline every yang clause, every ber- verb, meN- verb and -i verb, and say why each marker or connector is there.
15–30 Alternating role task: in pairs, one is a visitor who has lost a bag and one is the receptionist; swap after seven minutes (task below).
30–40 Changed situation: the receptionist says the doctor comes later and there are two choices; the visitor chooses with a reason and describes a second item.
40–45 Self-check against the list below, then one thing to practise at home.
0–5 復習・5–15 混合の入力・15–30 役割交代のタスク・30–40 状況の変更・40–45 自己チェック。

Part 1 (15 min, alternating): A is a visitor at a clinic reception who has lost a bag (Beg saya hilang.), describes it with yang, berwarna and seperti, says what A has not done yet (Saya belum mendaftar.) and asks permission (Boleh saya …?). B is the receptionist and asks the colour, asks Yang mana satu?, says what A needs to do and gives a reason. After seven minutes swap.
Part 2 (10 min, changed situation): B says Maaf, doktor datang pukul empat. Ada dua pilihan: tunggu atau datang esok. A chooses with kerana or kalau and says one more thing about the bag.
target_spans: Maaf, doktor datang pukul empat. Ada dua pilihan: tunggu atau datang esok.

Unit 15 · Review block · Chapters 13 to.source_text: Part 3 (5 min): write three sentences about a lost item of your own: one with yang, one with belum and one with a meN- verb.
パート1：交代で来院者と受付を演じます。パート2：状況が変わり、来院者は理由か条件をつけて選び、バッグについてもう一つ言います。パート3：なくした物について、yang・belum・meN- の動詞を一つずつ使った3文を書きます。
■ Peer check · 互いに確認
☐ yang is in front of ada or a verb (beg yang ada zip), and the description comes after the noun.
☐ belum stands in front of the verb, and the verb keeps its form (belum mendaftar).
☐ A ber- verb has no object, and a meN- verb has the thing right after it (mencari beg, menunggu doktor).
☐ A request takes the plain root (Tolong hubungi …), and perlu or supaya gives the need or the purpose.
☐ Yang mana satu? is answered with Yang ___. and one feature.

Model: Any natural exchange that follows the checklist. Model: Beg saya hilang. Saya mencari beg yang berwarna biru dan ada tali panjang. Saya belum mendaftar, jadi saya perlu mendaftar dulu. Kalau doktor sibuk, saya menunggu di sini. Yang ada zip, ya.
target_spans: Beg saya hilang. Saya mencari beg yang berwarna biru dan ada tali panjang. Saya belum mendaftar, jadi saya perlu mendaftar dulu. Kalau doktor sibuk, saya menunggu di sini. Yang ada zip, ya.

Accept the everyday bare root in speech (daftar, panggil), but ask for the standard form once in the written part.

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|4.source_text: 4. A: Awak tertinggal apa di bilik mesyuarat? B: Saya tertinggal fail saya di bilik mesyuarat.

Saya tertinggal fail saya di bilik mesyuarat.

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|5.source_text: 5. A: Kunci awak tertinggal di dalam? B: Betul, kunci saya tertinggal di dalam bilik.
target_spans: Betul, kunci saya tertinggal di dalam bilik.

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|6.source_text: 6. A: Bila awak tertinggal kunci itu? B: Tadi pagi. Kunci saya tertinggal di dalam rumah.
target_spans: Tadi pagi. Kunci saya tertinggal di dalam rumah.

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|7.source_text: Explanation: tertinggal is ter- + tinggal (chapter 2): to be left behind, by accident, without meaning to. Saya tertinggal ___ di ___. (the Kata-Kata frame): you are the one who left it, and you say what and where: Saya tertinggal telefon di pejabat. The thing can also be the subject: Kunci saya tertinggal di dalam rumah. (Kata-Kata line s01): my key was left inside the flat. tertinggal is not hilang (chapter 15): hilang means you cannot find it; tertinggal means you know where you left it, but you did not mean to.
target_spans: Kunci saya tertinggal di dalam rumah.

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|8.source_text: 説明：tertinggal は ter-＋tinggal（第2章）で、うっかり、そのつもりなく置いてきた、という意味です。Saya tertinggal ___ di ___.（Kata-Kata の文型）：自分が置き忘れた人で、何をどこに、と言います：Saya tertinggal telefon di pejabat. 物を主語にもできます：Kunci saya tertinggal di dalam rumah.（Kata-Kata の s01）：私の鍵が家の中に残っている。tertinggal は hilang（第15章）とは違います：hilang は見つからないこと、tertinggal はどこに置いたか分かっていて、わざとではないことです。
target_spans: Kunci saya tertinggal di dalam rumah.

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|9.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 〜を置き忘れた and 〜が家に残っている are two sentences with two different shapes. Malay says both with tertinggal: Saya tertinggal telefon di pejabat. and Kunci saya tertinggal di dalam rumah. There is no word for しまった: ter- carries "by accident, without meaning to".
target_spans: Kunci saya tertinggal di dalam rumah.

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|10.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「〜を置き忘れた」と「〜が家に残っている」は形の違う二つの文ですが、マレー語はどちらも tertinggal で言います：Saya tertinggal telefon di pejabat.・Kunci saya tertinggal di dalam rumah. 「しまった」にあたる語はなく、ter- が「うっかり、そのつもりなく」を表します。
target_spans: Kunci saya tertinggal di dalam rumah.

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|1.source_text: 6. A: Jangan risau. B: Terima kasih. Maaf, saya tersangkut di jalan yang sesak.
target_spans: Terima kasih. Maaf, saya tersangkut di jalan yang sesak.

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|2.source_text: Explanation: To say sorry for a small accident, say Maaf, and then saya and the ter- verb: Maaf, saya terlupa. (the Kata-Kata frame). The ter- verb already says "by accident, without meaning to", so you need no more. The usual answer is short and kind: Jangan risau. (Kata-Kata line s07). The verbs for this pattern: terlupa (forgot), terlepas (missed), tersilap (got it wrong), tertidur (fell asleep), tersangkut (got stuck). Add what you will do next if you can: Maaf, saya terlupa. Saya hantar sekarang.
target_spans: Maaf, saya terlupa. Saya hantar sekarang.

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|3.source_text: 説明：小さな失敗を謝るときは、Maaf, のあとに saya と ter- の動詞を言います：Maaf, saya terlupa.（Kata-Kata の文型）。ter- の動詞がすでに「うっかり、そのつもりなく」を表すので、それ以上は要りません。返事は短くやさしく：Jangan risau.（Kata-Kata の s07）。この文型の動詞：terlupa（忘れた）・terlepas（逃した）・tersilap（間違えた）・tertidur（寝てしまった）・tersangkut（動けなくなった）。できれば次にすることも足します：Maaf, saya terlupa. Saya hantar sekarang.
target_spans: Maaf, saya terlupa. Saya hantar sekarang.

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|4.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese says すみません、うっかり忘れてしまいました, with うっかり and てしまう both marking the slip. Malay needs neither: Maaf, saya terlupa. is the whole apology. ter- takes the place of うっかり〜てしまう, and a long apology is not expected for a small slip.

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|5.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語は「すみません、うっかり忘れてしまいました」と、「うっかり」と「〜てしまう」の両方で失敗を示します。マレー語はどちらも要らず、Maaf, saya terlupa. で謝罪は十分です。ter- が「うっかり〜てしまう」の代わりをし、小さな失敗に長い謝罪は求められません。

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|14.source_text: Explanation: tidak sengaja means "by accident, not on purpose" (the spoken form is tak sengaja). With a ter- verb it adds emphasis: Saya tidak sengaja terlanggar kerusi. (the Kata-Kata frame). ter- already says it was not meant; tidak sengaja says it once more, which helps when someone might think you did it on purpose. Awak tidak sengaja. (Kata-Kata line s09) is how the other person says: "I know it was not on purpose." tidak sengaja can also stand alone: Ya, saya tidak sengaja.

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|0.source_text: 説明：tidak sengaja は「うっかり・わざとではなく」という意味です（話し言葉は tak sengaja）。ter- の動詞と一緒に使うと強調になります：Saya tidak sengaja terlanggar kerusi.（Kata-Kata の文型）。ter- がすでに「そのつもりはなかった」を表しますが、tidak sengaja はそれをもう一度言うので、わざとだと思われそうなときに役に立ちます。Awak tidak sengaja.（Kata-Kata の s09）は、相手が「わざとではないと分かっています」と言う言い方です。tidak sengaja だけでも言えます：Ya, saya tidak sengaja.

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|1.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 〜するつもりはなかった and うっかり are both near tidak sengaja. Malay does not need it with ter-, but a learner who adds it is not wrong: it is a polite way to say that nothing was meant.

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|2.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「〜するつもりはなかった」「うっかり」はどちらも tidak sengaja に近い言い方です。マレー語では ter- と一緒なら要りませんが、足しても間違いではなく、悪気がなかったことを丁寧に伝える言い方です。

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|11.source_text: Explanation: When a thing is the subject, ter- says what happened to it: Air kopi tertumpah di meja. (the Kata-Kata frame). The same ter- can name a state that lasts: Pintu terkunci. (the door is locked), Talian terputus. (the line is cut off), tercedera (hurt), terbakar (burnt). A state is not an action: nobody is locking the door now. After the state you can ask for help: Pintu terkunci. Boleh tolong hubungi pejabat pengurusan? (the Kata-Kata frame). tolong + the plain root is the request.
target_spans: Pintu terkunci. Boleh tolong hubungi pejabat pengurusan?

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|12.source_text: 説明：物が主語のとき、ter- はその物に何が起きたかを言います：Air kopi tertumpah di meja.（Kata-Kata の文型）。同じ ter- が、続いている状態も言えます：Pintu terkunci.（ドアに鍵がかかっている）・Talian terputus.（回線が切れている）・tercedera（けがをしている）・terbakar（焼けている）。状態は動作ではありません。いま鍵をかけている人はいません。状態を言ったあとで助けを頼めます：Pintu terkunci. Boleh tolong hubungi pejabat pengurusan?（Kata-Kata の文型）。tolong＋素の語根が依頼です。
target_spans: Pintu terkunci. Boleh tolong hubungi pejabat pengurusan?

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|0.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 鍵がかかっている (a state, with ている) and 鍵をかけてしまった (an action, with てしまう) are two forms. Malay terkunci can be either: Pintu terkunci. is the state. Compare the 〜ている feeling of terkunci, terputus and tercedera with the 〜てしまった feeling of terlupa and terlepas.

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|1.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「鍵がかかっている」（状態、ている）と「鍵をかけてしまった」（動作、てしまう）は別の形です。マレー語の terkunci はどちらにもなれますが、Pintu terkunci. は状態です。terkunci・terputus・tercedera の「〜ている」の感じと、terlupa・terlepas の「〜てしまった」の感じを比べましょう。

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|10.source_text: Explanation: ter- has two meanings. In front of an adjective it means "the most": termurah (the cheapest), terbesar (the biggest), terbaik (the best): chapter 6. In front of a verb it means "by accident, without meaning to": tertinggal, terlupa, terlepas: this chapter. The Kata-Kata frame puts both in one sentence: Yang ini termurah, tetapi dompet saya tertinggal di rumah. Look at the root: murah, besar and baik describe things (adjectives), so ter- means "the most"; tinggal, lupa and lepas are actions, so ter- means "by accident". Learn each ter- word as a word: not every ter- form is on this list, and the prefix alone does not tell you the meaning.
target_spans: Yang ini termurah, tetapi dompet saya tertinggal di rumah.

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|11.source_text: 説明：ter- には二つの意味があります。形容詞の前では「最も」：termurah（一番安い）・terbesar（一番大きい）・terbaik（一番よい）：第6章。動詞の前では「うっかり、そのつもりなく」：tertinggal・terlupa・terlepas：この章です。Kata-Kata の文型は両方を一つの文に入れます：Yang ini termurah, tetapi dompet saya tertinggal di rumah. 語根を見ましょう：murah・besar・baik は物の様子（形容詞）なので ter- は「最も」、tinggal・lupa・lepas は動作なので ter- は「うっかり」です。ter- の語は一つずつ覚えます：ter- の形がすべてこの表にあるわけではなく、接頭辞だけでは意味は決まりません。
target_spans: Yang ini termurah, tetapi dompet saya tertinggal di rumah.

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|0.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese keeps the two ideas apart: 一番〜 (the most) and うっかり〜てしまう (by accident). Malay uses one prefix for both, so the root decides. A learner who reads terbesar as "accidentally big" or tertinggal as "the most left" has mixed them.

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|1.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語は「一番〜」（最も）と「うっかり〜てしまう」（偶然）をはっきり分けます。マレー語は一つの接頭辞で両方を言うので、語根が決め手になります。terbesar を「うっかり大きい」、tertinggal を「一番残っている」と読むと、二つを混ぜています。

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|1.source_text: Pattern IDs are the Kata-Kata chapter 16 frames f01 to f06 (pattern 4 shows f03 and f06 together, a thing as the subject; the patterns run f01, f02, f04, f03 and f06, f05). Explanations and Japanese comparisons are drafts.

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|2.source_text: Pattern 1: tertinggal + the thing + di + the place; the thing can also be the subject (Kunci saya tertinggal …). If a learner says hilang for something left at home, give the situation (you know where it is) and say that hilang is for something you cannot find.

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|3.source_text: Pattern 2: Maaf, saya + a ter- verb. Accept a short Maaf. as a first try, then ask for the verb. Check that the verb is a ter- verb for a small slip (terlupa, terlepas, tersilap, tertidur, tersangkut).

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|4.source_text: Pattern 3: Saya tidak sengaja + a ter- verb. Accept the spoken tak sengaja in a quick answer; ask for tidak sengaja once in the written part. Do not mark the sentence without tidak sengaja wrong: ter- already says "by accident".

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|5.source_text: Pattern 4: a thing + tertumpah or another ter- word (a result or a state), then a request with Boleh tolong. Check that terkunci and terputus are used for a state, with no doer. Accept Boleh tolong hubungi …? with the plain root after tolong.

Unit 16 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|6.source_text: Pattern 5: Yang ini + termurah, terbesar or terbaik, then tetapi + the thing + tertinggal + the place. Ask the learner which ter- says "the most" and which says "by accident", and why (the root).

Unit 16 · Culture and usage note|1|0.source_text: No Malay explainer for Stage 2 units: explainers and rubrics are in Japanese or English only, as in Stage 1 (Sam, 13 Nov 2026). Select 日本語 or English.

Unit 16 · Culture and usage note|2|0.source_text: Read about うっかり〜てしまった against ter-, how an apology depends on who is responsible, the general knowledge sentence, and where Japanese learners slip with ter-.

Unit 16 · Culture and usage note|3|0.source_text: Japanese marks a slip twice: うっかり before the verb and 〜てしまった after it. Malay marks it once, inside the verb: ter- says "by accident, without meaning to". So Maaf, saya terlupa. is a complete apology. A long, formal apology for a small slip can even sound too heavy; the other person usually answers Jangan risau.

Unit 16 · Culture and usage note|3|1.source_text: The apology depends on who is responsible. A short Maaf, saya terlupa. is right for your own slip. When it is not your fault, say what happened without blame: Pintu terkunci. or Talian terputus. These sentences state a fact and leave the doer out, which is the polite way to report a problem to a guard or an office: first what happened, then what you ask for.

Unit 16 · Culture and usage note|3|2.source_text: General knowledge, not a rule and not a checked fact: condominiums in Malaysia often have a guardhouse and a management office, and a resident who is locked out usually tells the guard first, who then contacts the office. Practice differs from place to place, so ask at the guardhouse. The names, units and times in this course are fictional.

Unit 16 · Culture and usage note|3|3.source_text: Japanese learners often use tertinggal where Japanese says なくした, or put ter- on any adjective to mean "too much". The two ter- meanings of this chapter are only these: "the most" before an adjective (termurah) and "by accident" before a verb (tertinggal). When you report an injury at a clinic counter, name only what you can see, as Mr Tanaka does, and let the staff do the rest.

Unit 16 · Culture and usage note|3|5.source_text: 日本語は失敗を二回示します：動詞の前の「うっかり」と、あとの「〜てしまった」。マレー語は一回で、動詞の中に示します：ter- が「うっかり、そのつもりなく」を表します。ですから Maaf, saya terlupa. だけで謝罪は十分です。小さな失敗に長く改まった謝罪をすると、かえって重く聞こえることがあり、相手はたいてい Jangan risau. と答えます。

Unit 16 · Culture and usage note|3|6.source_text: 謝り方は、だれに責任があるかで変わります。自分の失敗なら短く Maaf, saya terlupa. で十分です。自分のせいではないときは、責めずに起きたことを言います：Pintu terkunci.・Talian terputus. これらは事実を述べるだけで、した人を言いません。警備員や事務所に問題を伝える丁寧な言い方です：まず何が起きたか、次に何を頼みたいかを言います。

Unit 16 · Culture and usage note|3|7.source_text: 一般的な知識であり、規則でも確認済みの事実でもありません：マレーシアのコンドミニアムには警備員室と管理事務所があることが多く、鍵を中に残して入れなくなった住人は、まず警備員に話し、警備員が事務所に連絡するのが普通です。やり方は場所によって違うので、警備員室で聞いてください。このコースの名前・部屋・時刻はすべて架空です。

Unit 16 · Culture and usage note|4|0.source_text: 日本人の学習者は、日本語で「なくした」と言うところに tertinggal を使ったり、形容詞に ter- を付けて「〜すぎる」の意味にしたりしがちです。この章の ter- の意味は二つだけです：形容詞の前では「最も」（termurah）、動詞の前では「うっかり」（tertinggal）。クリニックの受付でけがを伝えるときは、田中さんのように見えることだけを言い、あとはスタッフに任せます。

Unit 16 · Teaching plan and answer key|3.source_text: Before Block A: Kata-Kata Sedia Kelas c16 (31 cards, frames ms-c16-f01 and ms-c16-f02).

After Block D: the Kata-Kata chapter 16 deck with spaced review, frames ms-c16-f01, ms-c16-f02, ms-c16-f03, ms-c16-f04, ms-c16-f05, ms-c16-f06 in the frame drill and Susun Ayat; about 3 hours of self-study for this unit (planning figure).

Hanashishou (Stage 2): the plan links chapter 16 to the guardhouse, lost-wallet and clinic-visit scenes, and offers a missed-bus scene as optional recycling. Their Malay is not yet tagged by chapter (build step 6), so do not assign them yet.
Next: the writing block after chapter 16 (a brief factual incident message), then unit 17 (Kata-Kata c17).
■ Block A · Words and patterns (45 min)
Goal: I can say what I left behind or forgot by accident with tertinggal and terlupa, and apologise with Maaf, saya ___..
0–5 Recall: chapters 1, 6 and 15 (an apology, termurah, hilang) from the opener prompts.
10–20 Vocabulary focus: core words first, with each root; recognition and revision words are only pointed out.

20–40 Pattern focus: patterns 1 and 2 first (Saya tertinggal ___ di ___, Maaf, saya ___), question and answer before the rule; then the vocabulary in four groups with each ter- word and its root and the root's chapter (ter- accidents 9, ter- states and results 5, by accident, an accident, the key and the spill 4, what you see 5). Draw the two ter- side by side: termurah (the most) against tertinggal (by accident).
■ Block B · Drills and conversation (45 min)
Goal: I can say what spilt, slipped, broke or was cut off with a ter- verb, say tidak sengaja for emphasis, and tell termurah from tertinggal.
0–5 Recall: say one thing you forgot or left behind with ter-.

5–25 Drill ladder in order: pattern table, substitution, transformation (the state, the thing as the subject, the two ter- first), question and answer, question-word choice, short dialogues, then the markers drill.
25–40 Model conversation, gapped form, then the changed-facts variant.

Unit 16 · Teaching plan and answer key|4.source_text: Goal: I can follow a call that explains why a colleague is late, read a clinic form and tell a guard a door is locked.
0–5 Recall: each learner tells a partner one small slip of this week in two sentences with Maaf and a ter- verb.
5–20 Listening: read the questions, two readings, check, then shadow three lines.
30–45 Task with role cards; announce the change of plan halfway.
■ Block D · Review and test (45 min)
Goal: I can choose between the two ter- meanings, between tertinggal and hilang, and between a state (terkunci) and an action.
0–15 Mixed review: cumulative question-word drill (chapters 1 to 16), then the markers drill with new cues and a check of the two ter- meanings.
35–45 Preview: the writing block after chapter 16 (a brief factual incident message), then unit 17 (standard and spoken choices, particles, invitations and refusals; Kata-Kata c17).
Goal: I can handle a short role-play at a guardhouse or a clinic counter, including a change such as an office that is not open.
0–5 Recall: say three sentences: one tertinggal, one Maaf, saya … and one Pintu terkunci.

5–15 Scene listening: read the Kata-Kata scenario lines ms-c16-s01 to ms-c16-s11 (the model: the locked door and the spilt coffee) and then the clinic scene ms-c16-s12 to s17 (the Block E dialogue below) twice; learners tick tertinggal, terlupa, terlepas, tersangkut, tertumpah, tergelincir and tidak sengaja when they hear them, and listen for Jangan risau. in lines 7 and 9.

15–30 Role-play in pairs: pairs play the guardhouse scene with their own unit and key, without the script; then swap and play a spill with a colleague. Do not role-play any medical advice: the clinic part stops at the receptionist's Sila tunggu sekejap.
30–40 Changed situation: a changed fact: the management office is not open yet; A asks to wait in the lobby and says tidak sengaja once more.
40–45 Culture and usage note discussion, and the home-practice briefing.

Unit 16 · Teaching plan and answer key|5.source_text: ■ What to listen for · 注意点

Load: 27 core words in five groups (ter- accidents 9, ter- states and results 5, by accident, an accident, the key and the spill 4, what you see 5, what happened and what to say 4), no recognition word, and revision of the chapter 6 ter-, sorry and the reply, things and places, moving about and time, and office and clinic. Suggested order: Block A the first two groups with patterns 1 and 2; Block B the last two groups with patterns 3 to 5. If the pilot shows 27 is too many, the natural cut is: tertinggal, terlupa, terlepas, tertumpah, terkunci, tidak sengaja, kunci, bengkak, luka, lebam first; the rest second.

ter- accident against ter- superlative: ter- + an adjective (chapter 6: termurah, terbesar, terbaik) means "the most"; ter- + a verb (this chapter: tertinggal, terlupa, terlepas) means "by accident, without meaning to". The Kata-Kata cards for this chapter say it on the first card: not the ter- of termurah and terbaik. Teach the two side by side with Yang ini termurah, tetapi dompet saya tertinggal di rumah. Do not tell learners to guess the meaning of any other ter- word from the prefix: the plan says to learn each form as a word. Ability and idiom readings of ter- are outside this chapter.
target_spans: Yang ini termurah, tetapi dompet saya tertinggal di rumah.

Unit 16 · Teaching plan and answer key|5.source_text: tertinggal (left behind) against hilang (lost, chapter 15): Dompet saya hilang. means you cannot find the wallet; Saya tertinggal dompet di rumah. means you know where it is and you did not mean to leave it. The chapter 15 unit used hilang and only named tertinggal; from here learners choose between them by one question: "do I know where it is?"

Apologising in Malay against Japanese うっかり〜てしまいました: Japanese marks the slip twice (うっかり, 〜てしまう). Malay marks it once, in the verb: Maaf, saya terlupa. is the whole apology, and the answer is Jangan risau. Do not ask for a longer apology for a small slip, and do not teach a formula for blame: if it is not your fault, state what happened (Pintu terkunci., Talian terputus.) and make the request.

Unit 16 · Teaching plan and answer key|6.source_text: terkunci as a state, not an action: Pintu terkunci. means the door is locked now; nobody is locking it. terputus, tercedera and terbakar are the same: a state that lasts. The Japanese 〜ている feeling is close (鍵がかかっている, 切れている, けがをしている), while terlupa and terlepas feel like 〜てしまった. A state can take masih (Pintu itu masih terkunci.); an accident takes baru (Encik Tanaka baru tergelincir.). An accident ter- verb rarely takes sudah or sedang; masih and baru are fine, and masih also goes with a place: Kunci saya masih di dalam rumah.
target_spans: Kunci saya masih di dalam rumah.

Unit 16 · Teaching plan and answer key|6.source_text: tidak sengaja with a ter- verb adds emphasis, and does not change the meaning: Saya tidak sengaja terlanggar kerusi. The spoken form is tak sengaja. Do not mark a ter- sentence without it wrong. Awak tidak sengaja. is also what you say to someone else who did something small (Kata-Kata s09).

Whole words and roots: each ter- word is learned whole, with its root as the card note gives it: tertinggal (ter- + tinggal, chapter 2), terlupa (lupa, chapter 4), tertidur (tidur, chapter 4), terlepas (lepas, chapter 4), tertumpah (tumpah, this chapter), terkunci (kunci, this chapter); jatuh, silap, langgar, gelincir, cedera, bakar, putus and sangkut are not class cards. kemalangan is a whole word (ke-an words come in Stage 3; the root malang is not taught alone); Malaysian Malay says kemalangan, not the Indonesian word.

The clinic scene (safety): learners say only what they can see: bengkak, luka kecil, lebam. The receptionist registers Mr Tanaka (Encik perlu daftar dulu. Ini borang.) and asks him to wait (Sila tunggu sekejap.). The unit gives no diagnosis, no treatment advice and no medicine, and learners must not be asked to name a cause or a remedy. If a learner asks what to do for an injury, say that it is a question for the doctor.
target_spans: Encik perlu daftar dulu. Ini borang.

Unit 16 · Teaching plan and answer key|6.source_text: The -kan and bare-root rules from chapters 12 to 15 still hold: a dialogue line may keep Kata-Kata's everyday bare root (Saya hubungi pejabat pengurusan., Encik perlu daftar dulu.), and the pattern examples, keys and written forms use the meN- form (menunggu, mendaftar, menghubungi). A request takes the plain root (Boleh tolong hubungi …?). tangguhkan and batalkan take a noun object (tangguhkan rancangan); this unit does not use them. dari is for places and daripada for people and organisations.

Where Japanese learners usually slip: (1) hilang for something left behind; (2) ter- on an adjective to mean "too" or "very"; (3) reading terbesar as accidental; (4) an apology that is too long for a small slip; (5) putting a doer into a state sentence (Saya terkunci means "I am locked in"); (6) tidak sengaja without a verb (Saya tidak sengaja kunci).

Unit 16 · Teaching plan and answer key|7.source_text: Natural speech: Maaf, saya terlupa. and Jangan risau.; Pintu terkunci.; Hati-hati, lantai licin.; Awak tidak sengaja.; the spoken tak sengaja. The scene follows Kata-Kata c16 (scenario lines ms-c16-s01 to s17, frames f01 to f06); the model ends at the office scene (s11) and the clinic scene (s12 to s17) is its own short dialogue in Block E, because turns are not joined across a scene change. terjatuh takes ke for the movement (Cawan itu terjatuh ke lantai.), while tertumpah and tergelincir take di for where it happened (tertumpah di meja, tergelincir di tangga); the Kata-Kata line Air kopi tertumpah di meja. stays as it is. All names, units and times are fictional; learners may use an invented flat or an invented cup.
Cumulative question words: chapters 1 to 16. Chapter 16 adds no new question word.

Unit 16 · Teaching plan and answer key|8.source_text: Answer keys are on each component. Japanese text awaits native review.
Standard forms first; spoken forms are labelled. ber- verbs are taught as whole ledger forms, each with its root; no meN- verb (chapter 11) and no suffixed verb form (chapter 12).

Unit 16 · Writing block · A brief factua.source_text: ユニット16のあとの書く練習（45分）：小さな出来事を、だれがどこで・何が起きたか・見えること・頼みを一つ入れて4〜6文の事実のメッセージに書きます。責めたり助言したりしません。名前や部屋は架空でかまいません。
（日本語は下書きです。ネイティブ・スピーカーの確認待ち）
No Malay explainer for Stage 2 units: explainers and rubrics are in Japanese or English only, as in Stage 1 (Sam, 13 Nov 2026). Select 日本語 or English.

The writing block after unit 16 (45 minutes): write a brief factual incident message in four to six sentences with who and where, what happened with a ter- verb, what you can see and one request; no blame and no advice; names and units may be invented.
Fictional model: two short factual messages about small incidents, one to the management office (a key left inside) and one to a colleague (a spill). All names and units are invented:

Selamat petang. Saya Mei Ling dari Blok C, unit 5-2. Kunci saya tertinggal di dalam rumah dan pintu terkunci. Saya tidak sengaja terlupa kunci tadi. Boleh tolong hubungi pengawal? Saya menunggu di lobi. Terima kasih.
target_spans: Selamat petang. Saya Mei Ling dari Blok C, unit 5-2. Kunci saya tertinggal di dalam rumah dan pintu terkunci. Saya tidak sengaja terlupa kunci tadi. Boleh tolong hubungi pengawal? Saya menunggu di lobi. Terima kasih.

Unit 16 · Writing block · A brief factua.source_text: Encik Tanaka, maaf. Air kopi saya tertumpah di meja dan cawan saya pecah. Saya tidak sengaja. Lantai licin. Boleh tolong ambil tisu? Terima kasih.
target_spans: Encik Tanaka, maaf. Air kopi saya tertumpah di meja dan cawan saya pecah. Saya tidak sengaja. Lantai licin. Boleh tolong ambil tisu? Terima kasih.

Unit 16 · Writing block · A brief factua.source_text: Notice: who and where first, then what happened with a ter- verb, then tidak sengaja if it matters, then one request with Boleh tolong. The message states facts; it does not blame anyone and gives no advice. / 気づくこと：まずだれがどこで、次に ter- の動詞で何が起きたか、必要なら tidak sengaja、最後に Boleh tolong で頼みを一つ書きます。事実だけを書き、だれも責めず、助言もしません。
■ Plan · 45 minutes · 進め方
0–5 Recall: say one thing you left behind with tertinggal and one Maaf, saya … (unit 16).
5–15 Model and notice: read the two messages; underline every ter- verb and say which is an action and which is a state; rewrite Pintu terkunci as Saya terlupa kunci and say how the meaning changes.
15–30 Guided draft: write your own message about a small incident (a key, a spill, a missed bus) with the checklist below.
30–40 Peer or teacher feedback with the peer check.
40–45 Rewrite one sentence to remove any blame or advice, and read the message aloud.
0–5 復習・5–15 例文を読んで気づく・15–30 下書き・30–40 ペアまたは先生の確認・40–45 一文を書き直して音読。
■ Your turn · 自分で
Write four to six sentences: a message to the management office or to a colleague about a small incident (fictional). Include:
☐ who you are and where (Saya …, Blok B, unit …)
☐ what happened, with a ter- verb or state (tertinggal, terkunci, tertumpah, tergelincir, pecah)
☐ tidak sengaja if you want to say it was not on purpose, and one thing you can see (bengkak, luka kecil, lebam, licin)
☐ one practical request with Boleh tolong …?, and Terima kasih.
小さな出来事について、管理事務所か同僚あての短い事実のメッセージを4〜6文で書きましょう。だれがどこで、何が起きたか、見えること、頼みを一つ入れます。名前・部屋・場所は架空でかまいません。医者の診断や助言は書きません。
■ Peer check · 互いに確認
☐ The message says what happened with a ter- verb or a state, and does not use hilang for something left behind.
☐ tidak sengaja stands in front of the ter- verb, or the message does without it.
☐ It states facts only: no blame, no guess about a cause, no advice; an injury is described only by what you can see.
☐ One request with Boleh tolong …? and the plain root after tolong; the partner can say what is asked of whom.
☐ 事実だけか、責めていないか、頼みが一つか、hilang と tertinggal の使い分けを確認し、パートナーが質問を一つします。

Model: Any four to six correct sentences that cover the checklist. Model: Selamat petang. Saya Mei Ling dari Blok C, unit 5-2. Kunci saya tertinggal di dalam rumah dan pintu terkunci. Saya tidak sengaja terlupa kunci tadi. Boleh tolong hubungi pengawal? Saya menunggu di lobi. Terima kasih.
target_spans: Selamat petang. Saya Mei Ling dari Blok C, unit 5-2. Kunci saya tertinggal di dalam rumah dan pintu terkunci. Saya tidak sengaja terlupa kunci tadi. Boleh tolong hubungi pengawal? Saya menunggu di lobi. Terima kasih.

Unit 16 · Writing block · A brief factua.source_text: Mark for the task first (who and where, what happened, a request), then for form (the ter- verb, tidak sengaja in front of it, tertinggal against hilang, the plain root after tolong). Accept a short Maaf. in a first draft but ask for the ter- verb once in the rewrite; accept the everyday bare root in a first draft (Saya hubungi pengawal) but ask for the written form in the message.

Names, units and places are fictional. Do not ask anyone to share a real address, flat number or phone number. Do not mark or comment on any medical content: the message may only say what is visible (bengkak, luka kecil, lebam).
This is the extra 45-minute writing block after unit 16.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|0.source_text: Pattern box: Sudikah encik ___ ?  (a polite invitation)

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|1.source_text: 1. A: Ini jemputan makan malam pejabat. Sudikah encik datang? Sila balas sebelum hari Rabu. B: Terima kasih, Puan Aini. Pukul berapa?
target_spans: Ini jemputan makan malam pejabat. Sudikah encik datang? Sila balas sebelum hari Rabu.
Terima kasih, Puan Aini. Pukul berapa?

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|2.source_text: 2. A: Sudikah puan makan dengan kami hari Jumaat? B: Terima kasih. Saya lapang pada hari Jumaat.
target_spans: Sudikah puan makan dengan kami hari Jumaat?
Terima kasih. Saya lapang pada hari Jumaat.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|3.source_text: 3. A: Boleh cik singgah di pejabat dulu? B: Boleh. Saya singgah pukul enam.
target_spans: Boleh cik singgah di pejabat dulu?

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|4.source_text: 4. A: Sudikah encik datang ke rumah saya hujung minggu ini? B: Terima kasih atas jemputan puan. Saya akan datang.
target_spans: Sudikah encik datang ke rumah saya hujung minggu ini?
Terima kasih atas jemputan puan. Saya akan datang.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|5.source_text: 5. A: Bos belanja. Sudikah encik datang? B: Siapa lagi yang datang?

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|6.source_text: 6. A: Saya mahu ajak encik makan malam. Sudikah encik datang? B: Terima kasih. Saya setuju.
target_spans: Saya mahu ajak encik makan malam. Sudikah encik datang?

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|7.source_text: Explanation: sudi is polite: you ask the other person, never about yourself. Sudikah encik datang? (the Kata-Kata frame) means "would you be willing to come?" and is for someone senior, a client or someone you do not know well. The same invitation can be written on a card as a jemputan. With kami (we, not you) the host speaks for a group: Sudikah puan makan dengan kami?; kita (we, with you) comes after the answer: Kita pergi sama-sama. ajak is friendlier: Saya ajak encik makan malam. A written invitation from a person is jemputan daripada Puan Aini (daripada for people and offices, never dari).

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|8.source_text: 説明：sudi はていねいな言い方で、相手にたずねるときに使い、自分のことには使いません。Sudikah encik datang?（Kata-Kata の文型）は「いらっしゃいませんか」で、目上の人・お客・あまり親しくない人に使います。同じ誘いをカードに書いたものが jemputan です。kami（相手を含まない私たち）はホストが仲間を代表して言うとき：Sudikah puan makan dengan kami?；kita（相手を含む私たち）は返事のあとで：Kita pergi sama-sama. ajak はもっとくだけた言い方：Saya ajak encik makan malam. 人からの書いた招待は jemputan daripada Puan Aini（人や事務所には daripada、dari は使わない）。

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|9.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese いらっしゃいませんか and 来ませんか are two politeness levels in one verb. Malay shows the level with the word: sudi (polite), mari (standard), jom (friends), ajak (friendly). A learner who says Saya sudi datang about themselves has used it the wrong way round.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|10.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「いらっしゃいませんか」と「来ませんか」は一つの動詞の中の二つの丁寧さです。マレー語は言葉でレベルを示します：sudi（ていねい）・mari（標準）・jom（友人）・ajak（親しい）。Saya sudi datang と自分のことに使うと、逆の使い方になります。

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|0.source_text: Pattern box: Sayangnya saya tidak ___ . Lain kali, ya?  (declining softly, with a reason)

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|1.source_text: 1. A: Sudikah encik datang pada hari Sabtu? B: Sayangnya hari Sabtu saya tidak lapang. Lain kali, ya?
target_spans: Sudikah encik datang pada hari Sabtu?
Sayangnya hari Sabtu saya tidak lapang. Lain kali, ya?

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|2.source_text: 2. A: Sudikah cik makan malam dengan kami? B: Malangnya saya ada mesyuarat. Lain kali, ya?
target_spans: Sudikah cik makan malam dengan kami?
Malangnya saya ada mesyuarat. Lain kali, ya?

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|3.source_text: 3. A: Mari kita makan di kafe itu. B: Terima kasih. Sayangnya saya tidak boleh tahan pedas.
target_spans: Mari kita makan di kafe itu.
Terima kasih. Sayangnya saya tidak boleh tahan pedas.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|4.source_text: 4. A: Sudikah puan datang? B: Saya segan untuk menolak jemputan encik, tetapi saya tidak lapang.
target_spans: Saya segan untuk menolak jemputan encik, tetapi saya tidak lapang.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|5.source_text: 5. A: Sudikah encik datang hari Sabtu atau hari Ahad? B: Sayangnya saya tidak lapang hari Sabtu dan hari Ahad.
target_spans: Sudikah encik datang hari Sabtu atau hari Ahad?
Sayangnya saya tidak lapang hari Sabtu dan hari Ahad.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|6.source_text: 6. A: Sayangnya saya tidak lapang hari ini. B: Tidak mengapa. Lain kali, ya?
target_spans: Sayangnya saya tidak lapang hari ini.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|7.source_text: Explanation: To decline kindly, do three things: soften the start with Sayangnya or Malangnya (a pity, unfortunately), give a reason (saya tidak lapang, saya ada mesyuarat, saya tidak boleh tahan pedas), and offer another time: Lain kali, ya? (the Kata-Kata frame). Saya segan untuk menolak jemputan puan. (Kata-Kata line s04) says that you are reluctant to say no, which shows that you value the invitation. menolak is tolak (chapter 9, push) with meN-: here it means to decline. Say the reason plainly; do not leave the sentence unfinished.
target_spans: Saya segan untuk menolak jemputan puan.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|8.source_text: 説明：親切に断るには三つのことをします：Sayangnya・Malangnya（残念ながら）で始めてやわらげ、理由を言い（saya tidak lapang・saya ada mesyuarat・saya tidak boleh tahan pedas）、別の機会を示す：Lain kali, ya?（Kata-Kata の文型）。Saya segan untuk menolak jemputan puan.（Kata-Kata の s04）は、断りにくいと伝え、お誘いを大切に思っていることを示します。menolak は tolak（第9章、押す）に meN- が付いた形で、ここでは「断る」です。理由ははっきり言い、文を途中でやめません。
target_spans: Saya segan untuk menolak jemputan puan.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|9.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese ちょっと… leaves the refusal unsaid and trusts the listener to understand. Malay softens but still says it: Sayangnya … and a reason, then another time. A reply that is only Susah or silence can leave the host unsure; a clear reason and Lain kali, ya? is both polite and understood.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|10.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「ちょっと…」は断りを言わずに相手の察しに任せます。マレー語はやわらげても断りを言います：Sayangnya … と理由、そのあと別の機会。Susah だけの返事や沈黙では主催者が分からないことがあり、はっきりした理由と Lain kali, ya? が、ていねいで伝わる言い方です。

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|12.source_text: Pattern box: Bagaimana kalau ___ ?  (suggesting another time or place)

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|13.source_text: 1. A: Hari Sabtu saya tidak lapang. B: Bagaimana kalau hari Jumaat?

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|0.source_text: 2. A: Makanan di kafe itu pedas. B: Bagaimana kalau kita makan di kedai lain?
target_spans: Bagaimana kalau kita makan di kedai lain?

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|1.source_text: 3. A: Kita makan pukul tujuh? B: Bagaimana kalau pukul lapan?

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|2.source_text: 4. A: Hari Jumaat saya tidak boleh datang. B: Bagaimana kalau hari Isnin?
target_spans: Hari Jumaat saya tidak boleh datang.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|3.source_text: 5. A: Bagaimana kalau kita makan di rumah saya? B: Itu cadangan yang bagus.
target_spans: Bagaimana kalau kita makan di rumah saya?

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|4.source_text: 6. A: Tempat itu jauh. B: Bagaimana kalau kita naik teksi?

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|5.source_text: Explanation: Bagaimana kalau …? (the Kata-Kata frame) offers an alternative: how about …? The spoken form is Macam mana kalau …?. The suggestion is a cadangan, and the answer can praise it: Itu cadangan yang bagus. After a refusal, a suggestion keeps the plan alive: Hari Sabtu saya tidak lapang. Bagaimana kalau hari Jumaat? The host answers either way; a suggestion is not a promise.
target_spans: Hari Sabtu saya tidak lapang. Bagaimana kalau hari Jumaat?

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|6.source_text: 説明：Bagaimana kalau …?（Kata-Kata の文型）は代案を出す言い方で、「〜はいかがですか」です。話し言葉は Macam mana kalau …?。提案は cadangan で、答えでほめられます：Itu cadangan yang bagus. 断ったあとに提案すると、話が続きます：Hari Sabtu saya tidak lapang. Bagaimana kalau hari Jumaat? 主催者はどちらの答えもでき、提案は約束ではありません。
target_spans: Hari Sabtu saya tidak lapang. Bagaimana kalau hari Jumaat?

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|7.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 〜はどうですか and 〜でもいいですか are close to Bagaimana kalau …?. Malay keeps kalau (if) in the question, so the suggestion is "what if we …?". The same kalau is the condition of chapter 14.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|8.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「〜はどうですか」「〜でもいいですか」が Bagaimana kalau …? に近い言い方です。マレー語は質問の中に kalau（もし）を残すので、「〜したらどうか」という提案になります。この kalau は第14章の条件と同じです。

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|10.source_text: Pattern box: ___ ! Hari Jumaat, pukul tujuh. / Tidak mengapa. ___  (saying yes, and taking a no kindly)
target_spans: ! Hari Jumaat, pukul tujuh. / Tidak mengapa.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|11.source_text: 1. A: Bos setuju. Hari Jumaat, pukul tujuh. B: Setuju! Hari Jumaat, pukul tujuh.
target_spans: Bos setuju. Hari Jumaat, pukul tujuh.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|12.source_text: 2. A: Kita makan di kedai mamak? B: Setuju! Mari kita pergi.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|13.source_text: 3. A: Sayangnya saya tidak lapang hari ini. B: Tidak mengapa. Kita cuba lain kali.
target_spans: Sayangnya saya tidak lapang hari ini.
Tidak mengapa. Kita cuba lain kali.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|14.source_text: 4. A: Maaf, saya tidak boleh datang. B: Tidak mengapa. Lain kali, ya?

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|15.source_text: 5. A: Hari Jumaat, pukul tujuh. Setuju? B: Set!

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|16.source_text: 6. A: Maaf, saya tidak lapang. B: Takpe. Kita cari hari lain.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|0.source_text: Explanation: To say yes, say Setuju! (the Kata-Kata frame) and repeat the day and the time, so that both people know the plan: Setuju! Hari Jumaat, pukul tujuh. To take a no kindly, say Tidak mengapa. and add one thing: Kita cuba lain kali. (the Kata-Kata frame). In everyday speech with friends and colleagues, Setuju! becomes Set! and Tidak mengapa. becomes Takpe. or Tak apa. The standard forms are for writing and for people you do not know well; the spoken forms are for friends, colleagues and the mamak. Learn to hear both, say the one that fits, and write the standard form.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|1.source_text: 説明：賛成するときは Setuju!（Kata-Kata の文型）と言い、日と時刻をくり返して二人の予定を確かめます：Setuju! Hari Jumaat, pukul tujuh. 断りを快く受けるときは Tidak mengapa. と言い、もう一言足します：Kita cuba lain kali.（Kata-Kata の文型）。友人や同僚との日常の会話では、Setuju! が Set!、Tidak mengapa. が Takpe. や Tak apa. になります。標準形は書くときと、あまり親しくない人に使い、話し言葉は友人・同僚・マミ屋台で使います。両方を聞き取れるようにし、場面に合う方を言い、書くときは標準形を書きます。

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|2.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese switches between ですます and くだけた形 without changing the words much. Malay changes the words themselves: Tidak mengapa. and Takpe. are not the same register. Japanese 大丈夫です and いいよ are the nearest, but a learner should choose the Malay form by the listener, not by the Japanese.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|3.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語は言葉をあまり変えずに「ですます」と「くだけた形」を切り替えます。マレー語は言葉そのものが変わります：Tidak mengapa. と Takpe. は同じ場面の言い方ではありません。「大丈夫です」と「いいよ」が近い訳ですが、日本語ではなく聞き手によってマレー語の形を選びます。

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|5.source_text: Pattern box: Jom makan kat ___ ni!  (friends and colleagues, spoken)

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|6.source_text: 1. A: Jom makan kat kafe ni! B: Jom! Saya lapar.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|7.source_text: 2. A: Jom makan kat kedai mamak tu! B: Set!
target_spans: Jom makan kat kedai mamak tu!

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|8.source_text: 3. A: Kedai mamak tu di mana? B: Kat depan pejabat tu. Dekat sahaja.
target_spans: Kat depan pejabat tu. Dekat sahaja.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|9.source_text: 4. A: Jom minum kat kafe ni! Saya belanja! B: Terima kasih! Saya minum teh. Saya belanja minggu depan.
target_spans: Jom minum kat kafe ni! Saya belanja!
Terima kasih! Saya minum teh. Saya belanja minggu depan.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|10.source_text: 5. A: Makanan kat sini pedas. B: Saya tak tahan pedas. Saya tak nak pedas.
target_spans: Saya tak tahan pedas. Saya tak nak pedas.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|11.source_text: 6. A: Macam tu boleh? B: Boleh. Takpe.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|0.source_text: Explanation: This pattern is spoken Malay for friends and colleagues (the Kata-Kata frame): jom (let's), kat for the standard di, and ni or tu after the noun for ini or itu: kafe ni, kedai mamak tu. The standard version is Mari makan di kafe ini. The spoken pairs of this chapter are: tidak mengapa / takpe, tidak boleh tahan / tak tahan, setuju / set, seperti itu / macam tu, di / kat, ini / ni, itu / tu. Saya belanja! says that you pay. For a dislike, the everyday ways are Saya tak nak pedas. and Saya tak suka pedas.; Saya tidak boleh tahan pedas. is the standard form.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|1.source_text: 説明：この文型は友人や同僚との話し言葉です（Kata-Kata の文型）：jom（〜しよう）、標準形 di の代わりの kat、ini・itu の代わりに名詞のあとに置く ni・tu：kafe ni・kedai mamak tu。標準形は Mari makan di kafe ini. です。この章の話し言葉の組は：tidak mengapa / takpe、tidak boleh tahan / tak tahan、setuju / set、seperti itu / macam tu、di / kat、ini / ni、itu / tu。Saya belanja! は自分が払うという意味です。苦手なものを言う日常の言い方は Saya tak nak pedas.・Saya tak suka pedas.、標準形は Saya tidak boleh tahan pedas. です。

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|2.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese friends say 行こうよ, ここで食べよう with a casual ending. Malay changes three small words: di to kat, ini to ni, itu to tu. They are easy to hear but easy to over-use: in an email, a form or a client meeting, write di, ini, itu.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|3.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語では友人どうし「行こうよ」「ここで食べよう」とくだけた語尾にします。マレー語は三つの小さな語が変わります：di が kat、ini が ni、itu が tu。聞き取りやすい反面、使いすぎやすく、メール・書類・お客様との会議では di・ini・itu と書きます。

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|0.source_text: Model each A line; learners answer as B, then swap. Explain the rule only after they have used the pattern.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|1.source_text: Pattern IDs are the Kata-Kata chapter 17 frames f01 to f06 (pattern 4 shows f04 and f05 together, saying yes and taking a no kindly; the patterns run f01, f02, f03, f04 and f05, f06). Explanations and Japanese comparisons are drafts.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|2.source_text: Pattern 1: Sudikah encik + a verb + ?. Check that sudi is used to ask the other person, and that kami is used for a group that does not include the listener. Accept Jom or Mari in a friendly invitation and say that Sudikah is for a senior person.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|3.source_text: Pattern 2: Sayangnya or Malangnya + saya tidak or saya ada + a reason, then Lain kali, ya?. Check that the reason is given and the sentence is finished. Accept a short Maaf, saya tidak lapang. as a first try.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|4.source_text: Pattern 3: Bagaimana kalau + a day, a time or a place. Accept the spoken Macam mana kalau …? in a quick answer and ask for Bagaimana in the written part.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|5.source_text: Pattern 4: Setuju! + the day and the time, or Tidak mengapa. + one more sentence. Accept the spoken Set!, Takpe. and Tak apa. in a quick answer; ask for the standard form once in the written part. Do not ask for lah or kan.

Unit 17 · Pattern and grammar focus|8|6.source_text: Pattern 5: Jom makan kat + the place + ni or tu. Say that this pattern is spoken, for friends and colleagues, and ask learners to say the standard version (Mari makan di kafe ini.) once.

Unit 17 · Cumulative question-word drill.source_text: 第1章から第17章までの疑問語をすべて使って質問します。
（日本語は下書きです。ネイティブ・スピーカーの確認待ち）
No Malay explainer for Stage 2 units: explainers and rubrics are in Japanese or English only, as in Stage 1 (Sam, 13 Nov 2026). Select 日本語 or English.
Ask questions with every question word taught so far (chapters 1 to 17).

Chapters 1 to 17: apa / siapa / di mana / Siapakah (-kah) / Apakah (-kah) / di manakah (-kah) / Adakah / Bolehkah / berapa / bila / pukul berapa / hari apa / bagaimana (spoken: macam mana) / kenapa (= mengapa, apa sebab; answer: sebab or kerana) / yang mana / ke mana / dari mana / berapa jauh / berapa lama / berapa with a counter (Berapa biji?) / siapa with oleh (Kek ini dibuat oleh siapa?)

Chapter 17 adds no new question word. The invitation questions use the ones you know: Siapa yang belanja?, Makan malam itu di mana?, Pukul berapa?, Kenapa encik tidak boleh datang?, Bagaimana kalau hari Jumaat? (spoken Macam mana kalau …?) / 第17章で新しい疑問語は増えません。誘いの質問は知っている疑問語で作ります：Siapa yang belanja?、Makan malam itu di mana?、Pukul berapa?、Kenapa encik tidak boleh datang?、Bagaimana kalau hari Jumaat?（話し言葉は Macam mana kalau …?）
1. Ask what the invitation is for. (apa)
2. Ask who is treating. (siapa)
3. Ask where the dinner is. (di mana)
4. Ask formally whether the boss agrees. (Adakah)
5. Ask politely whether you may bring a friend. (Bolehkah)
6. Ask how many people are coming. (berapa)
7. Ask when the dinner is. (bila)
8. Ask what time the dinner starts. (pukul berapa)
9. Ask on what day the dinner is. (hari apa)
10. Ask how about Friday. (bagaimana; spoken macam mana)
11. Ask why the person cannot come. (kenapa; also mengapa or apa sebab; the answer starts with sebab or kerana)
12. Ask which café. (yang mana)
13. Ask where everyone goes after dinner. (ke mana)
14. Ask where Mr Tanaka comes from. (dari mana)
15. Ask how far the mamak stall is. (berapa jauh)
16. Ask how long the dinner lasts. (berapa lama)
17. Ask how many dishes of nasi lemak. (berapa with a counter)
18. Ask who made the food. (siapa with oleh)

Unit 17 · Culture and usage note|2|0.source_text: Read about when to use the standard and the spoken form, ちょっと… against Sayangnya …, lah and kan, and the general knowledge sentence.

Unit 17 · Culture and usage note|3|0.source_text: Malay speakers move between two registers. With friends and colleagues, and at an everyday stall, people say takpe, kat, ni, tu and Set!. In emails, forms, notices and meetings with clients, the standard forms are used: tidak mengapa, di, ini, itu, setuju. A learner should understand the spoken forms, use them with friends and colleagues, and write the standard forms.

Unit 17 · Culture and usage note|3|1.source_text: Japanese ちょっと… leaves a refusal unsaid and trusts the listener to guess. Malay softens a refusal but still says it: Sayangnya …, a reason, and then another time: Lain kali, ya? A reply that gives no reason can leave the host unsure; Saya segan untuk menolak jemputan puan. shows that you value the invitation.
target_spans: Saya segan untuk menolak jemputan puan.

Unit 17 · Culture and usage note|3|2.source_text: lah and kan are everyday particles. lah softens or stresses what is said, and its meaning depends on the tone; kan asks the listener to agree. Japanese learners often add lah to every sentence, which sounds odd, and neither is a copy of よ or ね. You must understand them but never need to say them: a sentence without them is correct. In writing, lah joins the word: Takpelah.

Unit 17 · Culture and usage note|3|3.source_text: General knowledge, not a rule and not a checked fact: colleagues in Malaysia often eat together at casual stalls near the office, and the person who invites often says Saya belanja! belanja means to treat someone, not to spend money (that is berbelanja). Accept kindly, and offer Saya belanja minggu depan. Names and places in this course are fictional.

Unit 17 · Culture and usage note|3|5.source_text: マレー語の話し手は二つのレジスターを使い分けます。友人や同僚と、また日常の屋台では takpe・kat・ni・tu・Set! と言います。メール・書類・お知らせ・お客様との会議では標準形 tidak mengapa・di・ini・itu・setuju を使います。学習者は、話し言葉を聞いて分かり、友人や同僚には使い、書くときは標準形を書きます。

Unit 17 · Culture and usage note|3|6.source_text: 日本語の「ちょっと…」は断りを言わずに相手の察しに任せます。マレー語は断りをやわらげても、断りは言います：Sayangnya …、理由、そして別の機会：Lain kali, ya? 理由のない返事では主催者が分からないことがあります。Saya segan untuk menolak jemputan puan. は、お誘いを大切に思っていることを示します。
target_spans: Saya segan untuk menolak jemputan puan.

Unit 17 · Culture and usage note|3|7.source_text: lah と kan は日常の助詞です。lah は語調をやわらげたり強めたりし、意味は語調によります。kan は聞き手に同意を求めます。日本人の学習者はすべての文に lah を付けがちで、不自然に聞こえます。どちらも「よ」や「ね」の写しではありません。聞いて分かる必要はあっても、自分で言う必要はなく、なくても文は正しいです。書くときは lah は語に続けます：Takpelah.

Unit 17 · Culture and usage note|3|8.source_text: 一般的な知識であり、規則でも確認済みの事実でもありません：マレーシアの同僚は、職場の近くの気軽な屋台で一緒に食べることがよくあり、誘った人は Saya belanja! とよく言います。belanja は「おごる」で、「お金を使う」ではありません（それは berbelanja）。快く受け、Saya belanja minggu depan. と返します。このコースの名前と場所はすべて架空です。

After Block D: the Kata-Kata chapter 17 deck with spaced review, frames ms-c17-f01, ms-c17-f02, ms-c17-f03, ms-c17-f04, ms-c17-f05, ms-c17-f06 in the frame drill and Susun Ayat; about 3 hours of self-study for this unit (planning figure).

■ Block A · Words and patterns (45 min)
Goal: I can invite someone politely with Sudikah encik …?, and say yes (Setuju!) or no (Sayangnya saya tidak …) with a reason.
0–5 Recall: chapters 1, 14 and 15 (tidak / tak, kalau, seperti itu) from the opener prompts.
10–20 Vocabulary focus: core words first, with each root; recognition and revision words are only pointed out.

20–40 Pattern focus: patterns 1 and 2 first (Sudikah encik ___?, Sayangnya saya tidak ___. Lain kali, ya?), question and answer before the rule; then the vocabulary in four groups, the standard form always before the spoken one (invitations 8, accepting and declining 6, standard and spoken pairs 8, two particles 2). Put the pairs on the board in two columns, standard on the left, spoken on the right.

Unit 17 · Teaching plan and answer key|3.source_text: ■ Block B · Drills and conversation (45 min)
Goal: I can suggest another time with Bagaimana kalau …?, take a refusal kindly, and tell the standard forms from the spoken ones, such as tidak mengapa and its spoken partner.
0–5 Recall: say one invitation and one polite refusal with a reason.

5–25 Drill ladder in order: pattern table, substitution, transformation (standard to spoken and back, then refuse softly), question and answer, question-word choice, short dialogues, then the markers drill.
25–40 Model conversation, gapped form, then the changed-facts variant.

Unit 17 · Teaching plan and answer key|4.source_text: Goal: I can follow a lunch invitation that is moved, read a written invitation and reply to it in standard Malay, and invite a colleague and answer a refusal.
0–5 Recall: each learner invites a partner to eat somewhere (fictional) and the partner refuses kindly in two sentences.
5–20 Listening: read the questions, two readings, check, then shadow three lines.
20–30 Reading and writing.
30–45 Task with role cards; announce the change of plan halfway.
■ Block D · Review and test (45 min)
Goal: I can choose the standard or the spoken form to suit the listener, tell belanja from berbelanja, and recognise lah and kan without having to say them.
0–15 Mixed review: cumulative question-word drill (chapters 1 to 17), then the markers drill with new cues and a check of the standard and spoken pairs.
15–25 Unit test (low-stakes).
25–35 Self-check and feedback.
35–45 Preview: chapter 18 (the integrated review of chapters 10 to 17; there is no new word), then the fast course for chapter 17 if needed.
■ Block E · Scene transfer (45 min)
Goal: I can play an invitation, a refusal and a new plan in two registers, with a friend and with a senior colleague, including a change of day.
0–5 Recall: say three sentences: one Sudikah …?, one Sayangnya … and one Bagaimana kalau …?

5–15 Scene listening: read the Kata-Kata scenario lines ms-c17-s01 to ms-c17-s16 (the dinner invitation, the café and the talk about takpe, lah and kan) and then the mamak scene ms-c17-s17 to s20 (the Block E dialogue below) twice; learners tick takpe, kat, ni, tu, macam tu, tidak boleh tahan and Set! when they hear them, and notice lah and kan without having to say them.

15–30 Role-play in pairs: pairs play the invitation twice: first to a senior colleague in standard Malay, then to a friend in spoken Malay; then swap. Do not ask learners to use lah or kan, and do not ask for a medical reason for a refusal.

Unit 17 · Teaching plan and answer key|5.source_text: ■ What to listen for · 注意点

Load: 25 core words in four groups (invitations 8, accepting and declining 7, standard and spoken pairs 8, two particles 2), no recognition word, and revision of the Stage 1 spoken forms, food and the café, plans, days and the office. Suggested order: Block A the first two groups with patterns 1 and 2; Block B the pairs and the particles with patterns 3 to 5. If the pilot shows 25 is too many, the natural cut is: sudi, lapang, setuju, menolak, sayangnya, lain kali, tidak mengapa, tidak boleh tahan, jemputan first; the rest second.

Standard first, always: the standard form is taught before its spoken form, and the spoken form is labelled "spoken". The pairs of this chapter: tidak mengapa / takpe or tak apa; tidak boleh tahan / tak tahan; seperti itu / macam tu; di / kat; ini / ni; itu / tu; setuju / set; and jom against mari. Learners must understand the spoken forms, may use them with friends and colleagues, and write the standard forms. The spoken form is never marked wrong in conversation and the standard form is always right.

When to use the spoken forms and when not: use them with friends, with colleagues you know and at the mamak; do not use them in emails, forms, notices or meetings with clients, or with someone you meet for the first time. When in doubt, use the standard form: nobody is offended by it. takpe is a slang short form of tak apa, which is the spoken form of tidak mengapa (the Kata-Kata card says "recognise only" for takpe).

tidak boleh tahan against boleh tahan: Saya tidak boleh tahan pedas. means "I can't stand spicy food"; boleh tahan (chapter 5) means "not bad": a different expression. The spoken form is tak tahan; for a plain dislike say Saya tak nak pedas. or Saya tak suka pedas. Learners give only a taste or a plain reason; do not ask for or discuss a medical reason for refusing food.

lah and kan are recognition only (Sam, R4): you hear them, you may say them, and no key, task or test requires them. lah softens or stresses, and its meaning depends on the tone (Takpelah. is softer, Bolehlah. is a reluctant yes); in writing it joins the word. kan asks the listener to agree, and it is not the suffix -kan (chapter 12). Japanese learners over-use lah, often on every sentence; tell them that a sentence without lah is correct and that it is not a copy of よ or ね. Do not mark a sentence without them wrong.

Unit 17 · Teaching plan and answer key|6.source_text: Polite refusal in Malaysia against Japanese ちょっと…: soften (Sayangnya …, Malangnya …), give a reason, and offer another time (Lain kali, ya?). Saying only Susah or nothing leaves the host unsure; a clear but soft no is both polite and understood. Saya segan untuk menolak jemputan puan. is a polite way to say that you are reluctant. The teacher stays with this teaching hypothesis: it is not a rule of Malaysian manners and is not source-checked.
target_spans: Saya segan untuk menolak jemputan puan.

Unit 17 · Teaching plan and answer key|6.source_text: belanja means to treat someone (to pay for them), not to spend money: Bos belanja. Saya belanja! The chapter 10 word berbelanja is to spend money or shop. A learner who says Saya belanja di pasar for shopping has mixed them. Saya belanja minggu depan. is the kind answer to a treat. menolak is tolak (chapter 9, push) with meN-; here it means to decline.

jom, mari, ajak, jemput and sudi are different tones, not shortenings of one another: Sudikah encik datang? (polite, to a senior person), Mari kita pergi. (standard), Jom makan! (friends), Saya ajak encik. (friendly), Ini jemputan daripada Puan Aini. (a written invitation). sudi asks the other person and is not used about yourself.

sudi is very polite and belongs to invitations (Sudikah encik datang?); boleh is the casual, common choice in an everyday request (Boleh cik singgah di pejabat dulu?). Teach sudi for a senior person, a client or a formal invitation, and boleh for colleagues and friends (Sam, 14 Nov 2026).
target_spans: Boleh cik singgah di pejabat dulu?

Unit 17 · Teaching plan and answer key|6.source_text: Lain kali, ya? is a soft no, the same job as Japanese また今度: it closes the matter kindly and promises no day (Sam, 14 Nov 2026). When the writer really offers a new day, say the day (Bagaimana kalau hari Khamis?) and do not add Lain kali, ya?; the reading and the writing model do exactly that. Use Lain kali, ya? when you decline and no new day is meant.

kami against kita in invitations: Sudikah puan makan dengan kami? (the host speaks for a group; kami does not include the listener) and Kita pergi sama-sama. (all of us together; kita includes the listener).

The -kan and bare-root rules from chapters 12 to 16 still hold: a dialogue line may keep Kata-Kata's everyday bare root (Saya tanya bos dulu., Kita pergi sama-sama.), and a request takes the plain root; the written reply and the pattern examples use menerima and menghantar. tangguhkan and batalkan are not used in this unit. dari is for places and daripada for people and offices (jemputan daripada Puan Aini).

The Kata-Kata Sedia Kelas list for this chapter also names a Dunia card about a festival open house; this unit teaches no festival and no faith-specific expression, and the only invitations are to an office dinner, a café and the mamak. The unit uses no religious greeting or reply.

Unit 17 · Teaching plan and answer key|7.source_text: Where Japanese learners usually slip: (1) sudi about themselves; (2) lah on every sentence; (3) belanja for spending; (4) the spoken form with a client or in an email; (5) a refusal with no reason (Susah); (6) boleh tahan for "can't stand"; (7) kami for "all of us".

Natural speech: Jom makan kat kafe ni!, Takpe., Set!, Saya tak tahan pedas., Macam tu boleh?; and in standard speech Sudikah encik datang?, Tidak mengapa., Setuju!, Lain kali, ya? The scene follows Kata-Kata c17 (scenario lines ms-c17-s01 to s20, frames f01 to f06). The model is s01 to s16, one line to a turn, with no turn joined across a scene change (s07 and s08 are both Puan Aini, who asks the boss in between); the mamak scene (s17 to s20) is the Block E dialogue. The inner … of lines s13 and s15 are shown as ‘…’. All names, places and times are fictional.
Cumulative question words: chapters 1 to 17. Chapter 17 adds no new question word.

Unit 17 · Teaching plan and answer key|8.source_text: Answer keys are on each component. Japanese text awaits native review.
Standard forms first; spoken forms are labelled. ber- verbs are taught as whole ledger forms, each with its root; no meN- verb (chapter 11) and no suffixed verb form (chapter 12).

Chapter 10 · Fast-course summary pack|5|.source_text: 4 · Saya berasal dari ___. Saya bekerja di ___.  e.g. Saya berasal dari Osaka. / Saya bekerja di Kuala Lumpur.
5 · Saya sudah / belum (ber- verb).  e.g. Saya sudah berkahwin. / Saya belum berkenalan dengan jiran.

Remember: ber- has no nasal sound changes; it is spelt be- before r and in bekerja, and bel- only in belajar. A ber- verb never changes; the markers do the work. bertolak is set off (not push); berhenti kerja is quit a job. In speech you will hear the root (kerja, sarapan, pindah); write the ber- form.
ber- には鼻音の変化がなく、r の前と bekerja で be-、belajar だけ bel- になります。ber- の動詞は形が変わらず、マーカーが時を表します。bertolak は「出発する」（「押す」ではない）、berhenti kerja は「仕事を辞める」です。話し言葉では語根（kerja・sarapan・pindah）も聞きますが、書くときは ber- の形を使います。

Chapter 12 · Fast-course summary pack|5|.source_text: 1 · Tolong ___ bungkusan ini.  e.g. Tolong simpankan bungkusan ini. / Tolong hantarkan bungkusan itu.
2 · Boleh ___ mesej itu?  e.g. Boleh tunjukkan mesej itu? / Boleh bawakan beg saya?
3 · Saya mahu ambil ___.  e.g. Saya mahu ambil bungkusan. / Boleh ambilkan bungkusan saya?
4 · Boleh hubungi ___ ?  e.g. Boleh hubungi juruteknik? / Juruteknik sedang membaiki paip.
5 · Ada kebocoran di ___ saya.  e.g. Ada kebocoran di siling saya. / Tolong matikan lampu itu dulu.

Remember: -kan on a root means do it for someone or make it happen (simpan → simpankan, mati → matikan); -i points at a person or place (hubungi). Two k in letakkan and tunjukkan; berikan is beri + -kan, not ber- + ikan; bersihkan is bersih + -kan. In speech you will hear the root alone (simpan, tutup); say the -kan form. After sudah, sedang, belum or akan, or with a third-person doer, use the meN- verb: menyimpan, menghantar.

-kan は語根に付いて「誰かのためにする」「そうなるようにする」を表し（simpan → simpankan、mati → matikan）、-i は人や場所へ向かう動作です（hubungi）。letakkan と tunjukkan は k が二つで、berikan は beri ＋ -kan（ber- ＋ ikan ではありません）、bersihkan は bersih ＋ -kan です。話し言葉では語根だけも聞きますが、言うときは -kan の形を使います。sudah・sedang・belum・akan のあと、または三人称の動作主のときは meN- の動詞（menyimpan・menghantar）を使います。

Chapter 13 · Fast-course summary pack|4|.source_text: 5 · Tidak dibenarkan ___ di sini.  e.g. Tidak dibenarkan minum di sini. / Borang ini wajib diisi.

Remember: belum is not yet, tidak is not; perlu is a step you take, patut is advice and mesti or wajib is a must; tidak perlu is not having to and tidak boleh is not allowed. On a sign you read tidak dibenarkan or dilarang; in speech you say tidak boleh. For your health follow your own doctor and pharmacist.

Chapter 17 · Fast-course summary pack|3|.source_text: I can invite someone politely with Sudikah encik …?. / Sudikah encik …? でていねいに誘える。
I can decline with Sayangnya …, a reason and Lain kali, ya?. / Sayangnya …・理由・Lain kali, ya? で断れる。
I can suggest another time with Bagaimana kalau …? and say Setuju!. / Bagaimana kalau …? で別の機会を提案し、Setuju! と言える。
I can tell the standard forms from the spoken ones, and I recognise lah and kan without having to say them. / 標準形と話し言葉を区別でき、lah と kan は自分で言わなくても聞いて分かる。
■ Core words · 基本の25語
jemputan — invitation · 招待・招待状  [L-1265]
ajak — To invite along; to ask someone to come (informal) · （気軽に）誘う  [L-0689]
sudi — To be willing; glad to (polite) · 喜んで〜する（ていねい）  [L-0828]
lapang — Free (not busy) · 手が空いている、暇な  [L-0656]
belanja — To treat someone (pay for them) · おごる、ごちそうする  [L-0717]
singgah — To drop in; to stop by · 立ち寄る  [L-0748]
cadangan — suggestion · 提案  [L-1257]
lain kali — another time · また今度  [L-1260]
setuju — agree · 賛成する  [L-1255]
menolak — to decline, to refuse (also to push) · 断る  [L-1256]
segan — hesitant / shy · 遠慮する・気が引ける  [L-1258]
sayangnya — what a pity · 残念なことに  [L-1259]
malangnya — Unfortunately · 残念ながら、あいにく  [L-0787]
tidak mengapa — never mind; it is all right (standard; spoken takpe / tak apa) · 大丈夫・かまわない（標準；話し言葉は takpe / tak apa）  [L-1261]
tidak boleh tahan — can't stand; can't handle, e.g. spicy food (standard; spoken tak tahan) · 耐えられない・苦手だ、例えば辛いもの（標準；話し言葉は tak tahan）  [L-1267]
tak tahan — Can't handle; can't stand (informal) · 耐えられない、苦手だ（くだけた言い方）  [L-0690]
set — "Deal!" / "Agreed!" (everyday speech) · 「決まり！」（日常の話し言葉）  [L-0703]
kat — at, in (spoken; standard di) · 〜で・〜に（話し言葉；標準は di）  [L-1252]
ni — this (spoken; standard ini) · これ・この（話し言葉；標準は ini）  [L-1263]

Chapter 17 · Fast-course summary pack|4|.source_text: tu — that (spoken; standard itu) · それ・その（話し言葉；標準は itu）  [L-1264]
macam tu — like that (spoken; standard seperti itu) · そんなふうに（話し言葉；標準は seperti itu）  [L-1262]
takpe — never mind (spoken short form of tak apa; standard tidak mengapa) · 大丈夫（話し言葉、tak apa の短縮形；標準は tidak mengapa）  [L-1266]
lah — softening or emphasis particle (spoken; meaning depends on tone) · 語調を調整する助詞（話し言葉・文脈による）  [L-1254]
kan — "right?", "isn't it?" (confirmation particle, spoken) · 〜でしょう・〜よね（話し言葉）  [L-1253]
balas — to reply · 返事をする、返信する  [L-1302]

Chapter 17 · Fast-course summary pack|4|.source_text: Remember: standard first. tidak mengapa is spoken takpe or tak apa; tidak boleh tahan is spoken tak tahan; setuju is spoken set; di is spoken kat; ini is spoken ni; itu is spoken tu; seperti itu is spoken macam tu. Use the spoken forms with friends and colleagues, and write the standard forms. belanja means to treat, not to spend.
標準形が先です。tidak mengapa の話し言葉は takpe・tak apa、tidak boleh tahan は tak tahan、setuju は set、di は kat、ini は ni、itu は tu、seperti itu は macam tu。友人や同僚には話し言葉を使い、書くときは標準形を書きます。belanja は「おごる」で、「お金を使う」ではありません。
